scope.excluded: Preamble, typesetting-only frontmatter command R006, and bibliography. Displays reviewed as coherent units; list lead-ins and three standalone paragraph-heading blocks are counted among prose blocks.

units.section: Abstract and edition note
units.text: \noindent Post-training alignment has substantially improved behavior, but whether safety-relevant habits of judgment would be more durable if learned during capability formation remains unknown. \emph{Entangled Alignment} proposes training those habits within the same pretraining examples from which capabilities are learned.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Frame a timing question and identify the proposed intervention.

review.goal: Frame the formation-time alignment question.
review.assessment: The abstract states the intervention and uncertainty directly; repetition in the body is legitimate here.

units.section: Abstract and edition note
units.text: Pretraining corpora preserve the library more fully than the reader: they record what authors wrote but rarely the questions, connections, evaluations, and belief revisions through which a reader's understanding changes. We call this omission \emph{the Missing Reader}. A Teacher uses \emph{Synthetic Metacognitive Reading} to construct chronological, source-adjacent records of those changes; \emph{Chronological Metacognitive Pretraining} would train a Student on the resulting traces. The full treatment gives one continuing Reader a provenance-linked graph for retaining and revising its understanding across sources. It also requires every generated thinking block to open with the full, verbatim Reader Core, a compact first-person evaluative orientation, followed by context-specific evaluation. Context modulates that evaluation's depth; it never gates the recital. The trace, graph, and Core are separately testable components of this intended loop. Student experiments would ask whether the orientation becomes behaviorally consequential and whether it survives targeted erosion, continued training, and successor-like transfer without semantic drift.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain the Missing Reader and summarize how the full treatment constructs and trains it.

review.goal: Explain the Missing Reader and complete training route.
review.assessment: The sequence is clearer, but one abstract paragraph still carries two acronyms, graph continuity, exact recital, three components, and four outcome families.
review.risk: Retain continuous Reader, contextual care, generation-to-training distinction, and separability; move implementation detail rather than the vision.

units.section: Abstract and edition note
units.text: Two Teacher-side prototype case studies produced inspectable graph and trace artifacts that were then audited. No Student has yet been trained; these studies do not show that the traces reproduce expert-quality reading or that the graph or Core causes any benefit. Entangled Alignment is therefore a falsifiable research program, not a demonstrated alignment method. Its motivating question is whether this training can move a Student from merely \emph{becoming the text} toward \emph{becoming the reader}.

prior_matches.prior_goal: State what exists, what remains unknown, and why the question matters.

review.goal: State current evidence and motivating ambition.
review.assessment: Positive artifacts, absent Student evidence, and becoming the reader are balanced. This is an appropriate abstract boundary.

review.assessment: Keywords perform an indexing role, not an argumentative one. Excluded from prose-only statistics.

units.section: Introduction
units.text: Much current alignment work is remedial in its timing: train a capable model first, then shape its behavior through fine-tuning, reinforcement learning from human feedback, or constitutional critique. These methods work. They have made language models substantially more helpful, honest, and harmless than their base counterparts. They nevertheless share a timing property: much of their alignment signal arrives after broad capability formation, and its generalization is limited by the failure modes, preferences, and evaluation contexts designers can supply. As systems grow more capable, the space of consequential situations may grow faster than our ability to enumerate, simulate, or reward-model them.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain why the timing of alignment deserves investigation.

review.goal: Motivate studying alignment during capability formation.
review.assessment: Timing and growing evaluation difficulty are useful premises, but remedial framing and extended concessions anticipate R008/R010/R011.
review.risk: Preserve post-training achievements and the expanding-situations motivation; avoid implying only later alignment faces limited supervision.

units.section: Introduction
units.text: Entangled Alignment investigates whether an earlier intervention can complement these methods. Post-training can alter behavior, representations, and dispositions; the narrower question is whether some safety-relevant habits become more durable or transferable when repeatedly practiced inside the examples from which general capabilities are learned.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Turn that motivation into a bounded comparative question.

review.goal: State the comparative formative-alignment question.
review.assessment: This is the clearest compact statement of the timing motivation and complementarity. It should own that introductory job.

units.section: Introduction
units.text:
The proposed intervention changes the pretraining distribution, not the neural
architecture. Its basic training object pairs source material with a synthetic
record of how a reader notices, questions, connects, evaluates, and revises
while reading. Although the resulting traces are textual, their intended
Student use is not inference-time prompting: they would contribute to parameter
updates during training. Whether they produce stable, causally consequential
learned computation rather than a textual ritual is an empirical question. The
graph and Reader Core are proposed enhancements to that object, not assumptions
that must be accepted before the reader-trace hypothesis can be tested.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Tell readers what changes and what a Student actually learns from.

review.goal: Identify what changes in training and what is learned.
review.assessment: Moving the intact training-object paragraph earlier works. Source-plus-reader data and independently testable additions become intelligible before terminology multiplies.

units.section: Introduction
units.text: Recent work makes this question plausible without settling it. Qi et al.\ show that some current safety alignment can be shallow and vulnerable to prefilling, fine-tuning, or decoding interventions \cite{qi2024safety}. Conversely, reflection-like behavior can emerge during pretraining itself~\cite{rethinkingreflection2025}, supporting the possibility that formation-time data can influence properties often associated with later training. Neither result establishes that the intervention proposed here will work; together they motivate a comparative experiment about training stage and data structure.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Supply empirical reasons to consider the question plausible.

review.goal: Give empirical reasons to investigate the question.
review.assessment: The two cited directions support plausibility without being presented as evidence for this intervention.

units.section: Introduction
units.text: For bounded assistant tasks, substantial behavioral alignment may be sufficient when assessed against the particular deployment and its environment. The paper's longer-run concern is that systems operating far outside their training distribution may encounter situations in which learned preferences, behavioral constraints, or elicited personas generalize unpredictably. This is an extrapolative motivation, not a demonstrated failure of current methods. The proposal remains one layer in a broader safety architecture~\cite{westerberg2025superintelligence}.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain the long-run stakes and limit the proposed role.

review.goal: Explain long-run distribution-shift stakes.
review.assessment: The bounded-task qualification improved accuracy, but the paragraph largely restates R007's generalization concern and R008's complementarity.
review.risk: Retain the specific extrapolation to more consequential systems and its uncertainty; merge those clauses into the opening motivation.

units.section: Introduction / The Missing Reader
units.text:
Human knowledge occupies at least two interacting forms. Minds change as people
experience, read, question, and remember; external media preserve a partial
record that later minds can encounter. Books and databases do not simply
accumulate truth---they are selected, lost, revised, translated, censored, and
increasingly mixed with generated material---but they preserve communicable
products of cognition across time. Those products are normally written for an
interpreting reader. Writers can leave background knowledge, obvious doubts,
emotional and moral context, and connections to earlier material unstated
because they expect a mind to supply them.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain why written products leave interpretive work to a reader.

review.goal: Explain why texts presuppose an interpreting reader.
review.assessment: The missing context supplied by a reader has a clear causal explanation. Selection and censorship also ground later corpus limitations.

units.section: Introduction / The Missing Reader
units.text:
Language-model pretraining learns from this external trace, while much of the
cognitive motion that makes it meaningful rarely appears with comparable
regularity. The first edition called that omitted reader-side process
\emph{Invisible Thinking}: questions, expectations, uncertainty, surprise,
evidence appraisal, retrieval, hypothesis formation, attention to consequence,
and belief revision as a source unfolds. \emph{The Missing Reader} names the
same intuition from the corpus side, not a second mechanism: what is absent is a
continuous reader position together with a record of how its understanding
changes. This engineered target is related to metacognitive monitoring
\cite{flavell1979metacognition}, but it does not claim to reproduce human
cognition in full.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Name the omitted process and reconcile the old and new terminology.

review.goal: Define the Missing Reader and retain conceptual provenance.
review.assessment: Names the evolving process and relates Invisible Thinking to the current term. The list supplies useful content, not merely a slogan.

units.section: Introduction / The Missing Reader
units.text:
Put compactly, the corpus contains the library but usually not the reader. It
provides abundant text but much sparser supervision for when a competent reader
should pause, doubt, retrieve, connect, notice a human consequence, or revise.
The missing object is therefore both a reader and the reader's under-recorded
update policy. This is not a claim that models cannot reason; it is a claim about
which occasions and transitions ordinary pretraining data makes visible often
enough to learn from directly.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Make the corpus-level claim memorable and prevent a claim that models cannot reason.

review.goal: Make the missing-reader intuition memorable.
review.assessment: The library/reader phrase is strong, but the operations and no-claim-of-reasoning-absence explanation repeat R013 before the example.
review.risk: Keep the memorable phrase and under-recorded update-policy distinction in R013; do not remove the thought-placement idea.

units.section: Introduction / The Missing Reader
units.text:
The target is not every private thought that accompanied a text's production,
nor the recovery of an author's hidden mental history. It is a synthetic
approximation of what a capable reader might usefully notice and update. Consider
a sentence from a scientific paper: ``The results suggest a correlation between
variables X and Y.'' The printed sentence records a conclusion. A trained reader
may also ask: ``How strong is the correlation? What is the sample size? Could
confounders explain it? Does \emph{suggest} mark uncertainty? Is the evidence
correlational or causal?'' Think-aloud protocols can observe some such reactions
\cite{ericsson1984protocol}, but ordinary corpora rarely preserve them
systematically. Human thought is not always verbal, think-aloud reports are
partial, and model explanations can be plausible rationalizations; the proposal
therefore depends on usefulness, not faithful recovery.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Demonstrate the missing object while bounding what synthetic traces claim to recover.

review.goal: Introduce useful synthetic inquiry and its recovery limits.
review.assessment: The original questions now lead to genuine revision, but the think-aloud and faithfulness qualifications interrupt the example's momentum.
review.risk: Keep synthetic usefulness distinct from private-thought recovery and retain the citation; consolidate its qualification outside the example's flow.

units.section: Introduction / The Missing Reader
units.text:
The same example can show what chronology adds. The following continuation is
invented to illustrate a minimal, graph-free and Core-free reader trace; it is
not an excerpt from either prototype case. The first update records questions
and a provisional interpretation. A later source span gives that same reader a
reason to change its view.

review.goal: Identify the new example as an invented minimal trace.
review.assessment: The provenance warning is necessary because nearby examples include observed artifacts; it also makes the graph/Core-free scope explicit.

units.section: Introduction / The Missing Reader

review.goal: Demonstrate a reasoned belief change across passages.
review.assessment: The later age evidence changes confidence in an independent predictor while leaving causation unresolved. It now demonstrates the distinctive learning object.

units.section: Introduction / The Missing Reader
units.text:
The learning object includes the transition, not just the final cautious
sentence: an earlier possibility, the evidence that changes its standing, and
the remaining uncertainty. A graph could make that earlier interpretation
addressable across a much longer interval. In the full treatment, the same
update would also be generated from the recurrent Core; whether either addition
improves the reading is a separate comparison.

review.goal: Explain what the example teaches beyond its conclusion.
review.assessment: The transition and preserved uncertainty are worth explaining. Graph and Core extensions establish the route toward the full treatment.

units.section: Introduction / The Missing Reader
units.text:
Adjacent work generates or reconstructs reasoning that helps solve or predict a
local target \cite{nye2021scratchpads,zelikman2022star,zelikman2024quietstar}.
Entangled Alignment instead makes the changing state of reading comprehension
the primary object. The distinction concerns the target: task-local solution versus cumulative
reader-state change. We use \emph{efficient} invisible thinking for the former
and \emph{chronological} invisible thinking for the latter; these names do not
imply that chronological updates cannot also be efficient. Earlier
expectations affect later interpretation; new evidence creates tension; a later
passage may supersede an earlier belief. The trace records what changed, what
prompted the change, and what remains unresolved rather than only the reader's
final answer.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Distinguish chronological reader-state change from local answer derivation.

review.goal: Distinguish cumulative reading from local answer reasoning.
review.assessment: The comparison works, but the last four sentences redescribe the just-demonstrated update and the naming caveat slows it.
review.risk: Preserve efficient/chronological names and their non-opposition; keep the comparator distinction rather than another full revision description.

units.section: Introduction / The Missing Reader
units.text:
A prose-only trace is enough to test this missing-reader hypothesis. The
Understanding Graph adds a separate possibility: make earlier interpretations
addressable, link updates to their sources, and preserve supersession rather
than overwriting \cite{westerberg2026understanding}. The Reader Core adds another:
generate those updates from a recurrent evaluative orientation. Keeping source,
update, graph state, and Core in one artifact is construction-level coupling;
whether a Student learns any functional or representational entanglement remains
an experiment.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain how the graph and Core extend an independently testable trace hypothesis.

review.goal: Explain independently testable graph and Core extensions.
review.assessment: R018 already supplies this bridge; R031–R035 soon define it formally. This paragraph adds provenance but repeats the same component/evidence account.
review.risk: Carry addressable supersession and the graph citation into R018; preserve graph-free H1 and the full Core ambition.

units.text:
Section~\ref{sec:cmp-definition} formalizes the corresponding Teacher-side
construction (SMR), Student intervention (CMP), and the evidence boundary between
them.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Direct the reader to the formal definitions.

review.goal: Direct readers to the formal definition.
review.assessment: A standalone forward pointer adds little with the formal section nearby and the subsequent figure already naming the same stages.
review.risk: Retain the navigation if the definition moves farther away; otherwise attach it to the preceding bridge.

units.section: Introduction / The Missing Reader

prior_matches.prior_goal: Show the relation between recorded text, unrecorded reader changes, and synthetic training traces.

review.goal: Show recorded source versus synthetic reader augmentation.
review.assessment: The figure offers a genuinely different visual route to the mechanism. Its construction label and recovery qualification are appropriate.

units.section: Introduction / From Elicited Reasoning to Learned Evaluation
units.text:
Large language models can already generate sophisticated reasoning and
evaluation. Their behavior approaches the functional standard for ``thinking
machines'' posed by Turing \cite{turing1950computing}: when prompted, they can
criticize arguments, assess evidence, use scratchpads, revise an answer, and
operate through extended reasoning harnesses
\cite{brown2020language,nye2021scratchpads,zelikman2022star,deepseek2025r1}.
The motivating gap is therefore not between reasoning and its absence, nor
between a ``reactive'' model and uncaused thought. It is between the ability to
produce evaluation on demand and a learned policy for when evidence warrants
questioning, retrieval, moral attention, uncertainty, or revision while
knowledge and capabilities are being formed.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Distinguish available reasoning ability from a learned evaluation policy.

review.goal: Distinguish elicited reasoning from learned evaluation timing.
review.assessment: The distinction matters, but multiple negations and a capability inventory repeat earlier assurances before reaching it.
review.risk: Retain existing reasoning capabilities, the historical citation, and the spontaneous-placement target; compress the repeated defensive framing.

units.section: Introduction / From Elicited Reasoning to Learned Evaluation
units.text:
The timing of evaluation is itself part of the proposed learning target. A
useful reader does not produce the same commentary after every span. Reflection
should cluster near contradiction, surprise, conceptual transition, unresolved
ambiguity, ethical significance, high consequence, or evidence that forces
revision. This \emph{rhythm of thought} has been part of the program since its
first edition \cite{westerberg2025superintelligence}. Thinking too early or too
often teaches speculation, verbosity, and ritual doubt; thinking too late or
too rarely records conclusions rather than discovery. Thought Moments
(\S\ref{sec:multi-agent}) implement one selection policy, and Test~8b measures
whether spontaneous updates align with passages independently rated important
rather than appearing uniformly.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define appropriate thought placement and connect it to a measurable prediction.

review.goal: Explain selective Thought Moments and their test.
review.assessment: Too-early and too-late reflection give rhythm of thought a concrete function. This should be the main conceptual explanation of selective timing.

units.section: Introduction / From Elicited Reasoning to Learned Evaluation
units.text:
This target complements rather than replaces post-training. Reinforcement
learning from human feedback and process supervision have made models safer,
more helpful, and more reliable, and they may alter internal representations
\cite{christiano2017deep,lightman2023letsverify}. They usually optimize answers,
derivations, or behavior in supplied situations. The additional question here
is whether pretraining examples can repeatedly demonstrate a reader carrying
evidence, uncertainty, consequence, and prior belief forward without an
instruction to evaluate each passage.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Differentiate the proposal from post-training and process supervision.

review.goal: Position the proposal alongside post-training.
review.assessment: R007–R010 already establish this concession and comparative motivation; here it restarts the argument after selective timing was explained.
review.risk: Preserve the process-supervision citation and continued reader-state distinction, but consolidate the general complementarity statement.

units.section: Introduction / From Elicited Reasoning to Learned Evaluation
units.text:
Orientation is the second part of this learned policy: not only when the Reader
updates, but which experiences and consequences remain salient while it does.
Corpora contain many recurring voices and personae, and models can move through a
low-dimensional persona space under conversational pressure
\cite{lu2026assistantaxissituatingstabilizing}. This does not validate a stable
identity intervention. It motivates the broader Reader-Core research program: compare one recurrent,
inspectable Reader orientation with no-Core, rule-framed, and recitation-only
controls. H3 below isolates a particular stability question within that program.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Introduce the standpoint from which evaluation occurs and motivate H3 controls.

review.goal: Connect thought timing to a recurrent evaluative standpoint.
review.assessment: This adds the second axis of the learned policy and transitions naturally toward the Core.

units.section: Introduction / Three Separable Hypotheses
units.text:
At full scale, the proposal places a synthetic reader voice alongside source
material throughout the candidate corpus. Here \emph{voice} means a generated
training artifact, not consciousness or a faithful transcript of hidden
activations. The primitive components---reasoning-augmented training, synthetic
data generation, Teacher--Student distillation, identity prompting, and external
memory---all have substantial prior art. The proposed contribution is their
composition around a different training object: the chronological evolution of
a reader's understanding rather than only the reasoning behind an answer.

prior_matches.prior_goal: State the composition-level contribution while acknowledging component prior art.

review.goal: Locate novelty in the composed training object.
review.assessment: The synthetic-voice limit and component-prior-art concession repeat R009/R013/R019 and will recur in R029 and the provenance section.
review.risk: Retain composition novelty and the non-consciousness claim, but give each a single clear introductory home.

units.section: Introduction / Three Separable Hypotheses
units.text:
\paragraph{The same Reader reads every page.} At full scale, this is not a
collection of document-local annotations produced by interchangeable readers.
One continuous Reader processes the candidate corpus in chronological order.
The Reader that encounters a work from 200~BCE is the same Reader that later
encounters a work from 1936: it carries forward the same evolving Understanding
Graph, so later reading can retrieve, question, and revise the understanding
formed by earlier reading. This cross-document chronology is a declared
traversal, not a claim that a corpus has one natural order.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Make persistent cross-document identity and memory unambiguous.

review.goal: Make one continuing Reader across works explicit.
review.assessment: The cross-century example gives continuity an intuitive scale. The declared-traversal qualification prevents a false unique-order assumption.

units.section: Introduction / Three Separable Hypotheses
units.text:
At every Thought Moment in the full treatment, every generated thinking block
opens with the same full, verbatim Reader Core and continues through
context-specific Refraction. Identity, memory, and evaluative orientation
therefore persist across works rather than resetting at document boundaries.
This is the paper's functional meaning of a \emph{formative inner voice}: not
consciousness or a transcript of private computation, but one first-person
standpoint accompanying the formation of understanding across the candidate
corpus. Teacher artifacts instantiate that Reader; Student training is proposed
to make it a learned default. Task-local rationales or elicited self-critique
may generate thoughts without constructing such a Reader. The novelty claim
concerns this whole training object, not priority for any component in
isolation.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Make persistent cross-document identity and memory unambiguous.

review.goal: Explain recurrent Core enactment as a formative inner voice.
review.assessment: The positive conceptual explanation is important, but its ending repeats synthetic-voice, local-rationale, and novelty boundaries just established.
review.risk: Preserve every-block recital, contextual Refraction, and the same standpoint across sources; shorten the repeated novelty defense.

units.section: Introduction / Three Separable Hypotheses
units.text: The design contains three separable hypotheses:

prior_matches.prior_goal: Introduce the three-item hypothesis list.

review.goal: Introduce the hypothesis list.
review.assessment: A functional list lead-in; it is not an independent substantive paragraph.

units.section: Introduction / Three Separable Hypotheses
units.text: \item \textbf{H1, Reader Augmentation:} adding synthetic reader-side questions, judgments, and belief revisions to source material may provide useful capability and safety-relevant evaluative signal beyond the source alone or token-matched task rationales. The minimal H1 comparison isolates those chronological updates without the graph or identity-specific Core.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Identify the incremental benefit that synthetic reader updates must demonstrate.

review.goal: State the independently testable H1 claim.
review.assessment: The source-only and generic-trace comparisons, plus minimal graph/Core-free scope, are clear.

units.section: Introduction / Three Separable Hypotheses
units.text: \item \textbf{H2, Graph Scaffolding:} generating those traces through a persistent Understanding Graph may improve their long-range coherence, source grounding, or revision structure relative to independent, context-only, or prose-memory traces. Retaining a graph at inference is a further, separable provenance hypothesis.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Distinguish graph-conditioned generation from optional deployment-time memory.

review.goal: State graph scaffolding and separate live provenance.
review.assessment: Teacher generation benefit and later deployment benefit are correctly distinguished in the primary definition.

units.section: Introduction / Three Separable Hypotheses
units.text: \item \textbf{H3, Reader-Core Stability:} under matched source data, target-token mass, compute, objective, optimizer, and evaluation, interleaving a fixed multiset of full-Core, Refraction-bearing examples with capability-forming examples may preserve a Core-shaped default-reader advantage better through a common continued-training stressor than placing the identical multiset in one final contiguous tranche. Shifted-distribution generalization is a separate endpoint.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define a timing-only stability hypothesis with controlled exposure.

review.goal: Define H3's timing and retention hypothesis.
review.assessment: The controlled comparison is precise, but the first definition packs the matching inventory and endpoint boundary into one long sentence.
review.risk: Keep identical examples, interleaved versus final tranche, and common-stressor retention; place matching details in the canonical methods definition.

units.section: Introduction / Three Separable Hypotheses
units.text:
Reader traces supply the learning signal, the graph supplies cumulative memory
and provenance, and the Core supplies a compact recurrent reference. The paper
combines them because they form one intended loop, not because current evidence
shows that they succeed together. Each admits an ablation and can fail while the
others remain useful.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Reassemble the components without making them logically inseparable.

review.goal: Explain why separable components are combined.
review.assessment: This brief synthesis makes the list into a proposed loop. Unlike another evidence inventory, it explains the compositional purpose.

units.section: Introduction / Three Separable Hypotheses
units.text:
H3 names the stated timing-and-retention contrast, not every question about the
Core. The broader Reader-Core research program asks why a stable reader position
might form, whether its wording, framing, and Refraction matter, whether it
improves safety, and whether it can be inherited by a successor. Those questions
motivate content and mechanism comparisons alongside H3. A result can support
or weaken one of them without deciding the timing contrast, and a positive H3
result would not establish the whole program.

review.goal: Distinguish narrow H3 from the wider Core program.
review.assessment: The clarification is necessary because the paper's ambition exceeds the timing contrast. Let this paragraph own that convention.

units.text:
\statusDemonstrated: the annotation pipeline produces coupled graph,
synthesis, and prose artifacts, including observed full-Core recurrence in raw
thoughts. This is partial C0: full-policy enforcement, preservation across
output layers, and a frozen training carrier remain incomplete.
\statusUntested: causal Refraction, whether a trained Student learns useful reader cognition,
whether the graph causes an advantage, or whether safety becomes functionally
or representationally load-bearing for capability.

review.goal: Summarize implemented artifacts and untested effects.
review.assessment: A prominent early claim boundary is warranted. Later full restatements should point back here rather than duplicating its inventory.

review.assessment: A short figure lead-in aids navigation and creates no substantive repetition problem.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Make generation, optional graph/Core inputs, serialization, and untested Student training visible.

units.section: Introduction / Defining Chronological Metacognitive Pretraining
units.text:
We define \emph{Synthetic Metacognitive Reading} (SMR) as the Teacher-side
construction process that pairs ordered source spans with selected records of a
reader's evolving understanding: what the reader notices, expects, questions,
connects, and revises as the source unfolds. We define \emph{Chronological
Metacognitive Pretraining} (CMP) as the family of Student interventions that
train on a declared serialization of those records. CMP names the H1
intervention family; successful SMR generation is not evidence for CMP. A graph
is H2's proposed scaffold, and the Reader Core is what turns generic CMP into the
full Entangled Alignment treatment; neither must be assumed for a graph-free,
Core-free reader-trace baseline.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Distinguish Teacher construction, Student training, and optional extensions.

review.goal: Define SMR, CMP, and their component relationships.
review.assessment: A canonical terminology definition is useful. Its vocabulary need not be repeatedly reintroduced in neighboring sections.

units.section: Introduction / Defining Chronological Metacognitive Pretraining
units.text: We build upon reasoning-augmented training approaches such as STaR \cite{zelikman2022star} and Quiet-STaR \cite{zelikman2024quietstar}. These works show that intermediate reasoning traces can improve task performance. More recently, BoLT \cite{ruan2025bolt} proposes augmenting pretraining data with inferred ``latent thoughts'' underlying compressed web text, and Thinking Augmented Pre-Training (TPT) scales synthetic thinking trajectories to 100 billion tokens \cite{nvidia2025tpt}. Together, they establish that synthetic reasoning can be generated and used at substantial scale. They do not establish that chronological reader traces, graph conditioning, or identity anchoring produce the effects proposed here.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Establish that synthetic reasoning generation and training are plausible at scale.

review.goal: Position synthetic trace generation relative to prior approaches.
review.assessment: The scale result is distinct, but another full lineage paragraph interrupts the formal definition and repeats R019 and Related Work.
review.risk: Retain all comparators, citations, and the TPT scale; keep only the fact needed for the definition here.

units.section: Introduction / Defining Chronological Metacognitive Pretraining
units.text:
A minimal carrier specifies the intervention's fields without requiring a
graph; the schematic example above illustrates its source and update roles: \texttt{[SOURCE]} records the source span; \texttt{[THINKING]} contains
the selected reader update (and, in H3 arms, the full Core plus its
context-specific Refraction); \texttt{[CONTINUATION]} records later source or
task behavior for which the update could be predictively useful; and
\texttt{[PROVENANCE]} records source, generator, prompt, Core, acceptance, and
archive versions. Provenance makes an artifact auditable, not true.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Make the proposed data object concrete without requiring a graph.

review.goal: Specify a minimal training carrier's fields.
review.assessment: Fields are useful, but Core-bearing content is described as belonging to H3 arms although wider Core comparisons also use it.
review.risk: Preserve all carrier fields and auditability limits; say Core-bearing conditions rather than narrowing the format to H3.

units.section: Introduction / Defining Chronological Metacognitive Pretraining
units.text:
The word \emph{chronological} has four distinct meanings. Within a document,
later annotations can depend on earlier passages but not vice versa. Across
documents, later annotations may query graph state created earlier in the
declared traversal. Separately, a Student may receive examples in historical or
dependency-respecting order. In the strongest form, a Student may forecast
before later outcomes enter its weights. The first two describe annotation; the
third and fourth are optional, increasingly speculative training tiers. A
separate declaration specifies the Reader's information horizon: a contemporary
reader can encounter an old document in disclosure order, while an era-bounded
simulation restricts the knowledge it may use. Neither order alone removes

units.section: Introduction / Defining Chronological Metacognitive Pretraining
units.text: The candidate curriculum therefore includes not only source tokens but explicit \textit{epistemic updates}: ``How does this passage change what the reader previously believed, and how is that change evaluated from a stable orientation?'' Depending on the training regime, a Student may predict the source, the update, a graph operation, or some combination of them. The framework does not assume that next-token prediction literally recreates a human mental model; it asks whether repeated exposure to these state transitions can teach a more cumulative form of reasoning.

units.section: Introduction / Defining Chronological Metacognitive Pretraining
units.text:
\begin{samepage}
A compact notation makes the full Entangled Alignment training object explicit;
graph-free and Core-free arms omit or replace the corresponding conditions. Let
$x_{1:T}$ be an ordered sequence of source spans, $g_t$ the graph state after
span $t$, $c$ the Reader Core, and $u_t$ the generated reader update. A Teacher
and graph transition produce
\[
u_t \sim q_\phi(\,\cdot\mid x_{\leq t},g_{t-1},c), \qquad
g_t=F\!\left(g_{t-1},x_t,u_t,\operatorname{prov}(x_t)\right).
\]
The training sequence $z=\operatorname{Serialize}(\{x_t,u_t,\Delta
g_t\}_{t=1}^T)$ is then learned under a token mask or weighting $m$,
\[
\mathcal{L}_m(\theta)
=-\frac{1}{\sum_j m_j}\sum_j m_j\log p_\theta(z_j\mid z_{<j}),
\qquad m_j\geq 0,\quad \sum_j m_j>0.
\]
The output regime determines which of the source, update, and graph tokens are
serialized; $m_j=0$ makes token $j$ context-only, $m_j=1$ gives it ordinary
target weight, and other non-negative values implement explicit weighting. The
training tier determines order of exposure. Serialization, masks, mixture
weights, context truncation, and role markers must be frozen within a
comparison, and arms should be matched on weighted target-token mass or use a
declared alternative normalization. This notation defines the object that
Student experiments would require; the present prototype instantiates parts of
$q_\phi$ and $F$, not a frozen training-ready $z$ or a reported Student
optimization.
\end{samepage}

review.assessment: The equations specify meaningful fields, but implementation declarations and evidence caveats make the introduction function as methods.

stability. The eleven agents share model ancestry, context, and artifacts, so
their agreement is not independent confirmation. The reported linkage and
source-coverage figures are engineering and attribution diagnostics, not
measures of correctness or depth. Annotation order, Student order, output
representation, and inference-time graph access remain separate design
decisions.

units.section: Introduction / Evidence, Scope, and Contribution Map
units.text:
A natural objection follows: if current models do not reliably exhibit wisdom,
why should their synthetic traces teach it? A Teacher can sometimes generate a
useful supervised pattern without perfectly embodying that pattern, but no such
transfer should be presumed here. STaR \cite{zelikman2022star} is an analogy for
bootstrapping task reasoning, not evidence that evaluative orientation or
character transfers. Reader-Core prompting, multi-agent critique, graph
provenance requirements, and human adjudication can constrain the output; they
cannot manufacture insight absent from the Teacher. Trace quality and transfer
must therefore be tested against human, source-only, and simpler synthetic
baselines.

units.section: Introduction / Evidence, Scope, and Contribution Map
units.text:

Separate work supplies optional machinery such as the Understanding Graph and Temporal Hindsight Learning \cite{westerberg2026understanding,westerberg2026thl}; accepting H1 does not require accepting either H2 or H3.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences
units.text:
The three interventions support several increasingly ambitious chains of
consequence. Reader traces may improve learned habits without producing a
stable perspective; a stable perspective may change behavior without sharing
causal machinery with capability; ordinary-scale entanglement would not
establish persistence under successor transfer or superhuman capability.
Table~\ref{tab:consequence-ladder} is therefore a grouped evidence map, not a
single total ordering. Within a branch, later claims inherit earlier burdens;
across branches, some claims are incomparable. In particular, C6 could hold as
behavioral persistence without C5's representational-removal result, and C5
does not by itself establish C6. The H labels organize component and timing hypotheses; the C
labels distinguish claims about their consequences, and the four meanings of
\emph{entangled} below name increasingly demanding properties of the resulting
system. These maps describe different questions about the same program.

review.risk: Keep C5/C6 non-implication and the H/C distinction; avoid replacing the developmental story with the map's bookkeeping.

only hard automated check enforces the opening prefix ``I feel no fear.'' The
archive reports full recital in all 51 raw Synthesizer thoughts and exact
translated preservation in 49/51; observed compliance and complete enforcement
are different engineering results (Section~\ref{sec:results}).

H3 therefore has two gates at C3. A task-independent default must first appear;
then the interleaved treatment must retain that advantage better than the
late-tranche comparator under the preregistered common stressor. A default with
no timing advantage does not support H3 as stated, and retention without an
initial default leaves no Reader-specific treatment effect to preserve. Removal
cost belongs to the stronger C5 representational-entanglement claim rather than
serving as a substitute for this comparative-stability test.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences
units.text:
The original program predicts better interpretation of ambiguous material,
value-relevant reasoning learned through contextual derivations rather than
isolated labels, and more inspectable generated thought. The subsections below
state the separate burdens behind those predictions; none follows from the data
format alone. Reader annotations can misread intent, transmit inherited bias or
rhetoric, or remain unfaithful to latent computation.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Introduce the downstream predictions while preserving their evidential dependencies.

review.assessment: The prediction summary contributes little after the table; the errors and unfaithfulness caveat repeat R045/R046 before examples finally begin.
review.risk: Retain one transition to concrete consequences; keep the substantive failure mechanisms in their dedicated sections.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / The Metacognitive Enhancement Hypothesis
units.text: The \emph{Metacognitive Enhancement Hypothesis} is the Student-level form of H1: under declared fixed-total-budget and fixed-source normalizations, graph-free, Core-free chronological reader updates will teach some useful habits that source-only data or optimized task rationales do not. Teacher matching applies to the two synthetic-trace arms, not to source-only data that has no Teacher. This is a wager about formative data, not a claim that upbringing replaces architecture, objectives, post-training, monitoring, or control \cite{nye2021scratchpads,zelikman2024quietstar}.

prior_matches.prior_goal: State H1's clean Student comparison and budget interpretation.

review.goal: Define the metacognitive enhancement claim's outcomes.
review.assessment: Fixed-budget and fixed-source comparisons ground useful transfer. The named error-recovery and judgment outcomes add specificity.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / The Metacognitive Enhancement Hypothesis
units.text: One predicted benefit is to raise the \emph{intellectual floor} of parts of the corpus. A confused forum post can be paired with an analysis that separates evidence from rhetoric and places emotion in context; a flawed scientific paper can be paired with questions about controls, confounding, and uncertainty. The Teacher is not assumed to be more intelligent than every writer. It may be weaker than an expert, hallucinate criticism, flatten ambiguity, or reproduce conventional error. The required result is distributional: useful evaluation must be added often enough, and harmful distortion rarely enough, that a Student improves on held-out outcomes. Quality gates and abstention are therefore part of H1 rather than optional cleanup.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain intellectual-floor improvement and its dependence on net annotation quality.

review.goal: Explain distributional improvement of the intellectual floor.
review.assessment: The forum/science examples illustrate a benefit and its limits without requiring the Teacher to exceed every expert.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / The Metacognitive Enhancement Hypothesis
units.text: A second prediction concerns a reusable \emph{grammar of reasoning}. Across science, history, literature, law, medicine, and ordinary life, reader traces can repeatedly demonstrate operations such as separating observation from interpretation, identifying proxy objectives, preserving uncertainty, comparing perspectives, tracking consequences, and revising when assumptions fail. The measurable claim is transfer of these operations to new domains, not the creation of otherwise inaccessible insight. Repetition may also move some evaluations from an explicitly elicited procedure toward a more accessible default habit; the paper does not rely on a literal System~1/System~2 decomposition of model cognition.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Identify reusable operations and explain the desired cross-domain transfer.

review.goal: Explain transferable reasoning habits.
review.assessment: The repeated operations form a distinct learning prediction; the System-1/2 qualification limits an otherwise tempting cognitive metaphor.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / The Metacognitive Enhancement Hypothesis
units.text:
H1 also predicts transfer of the rhythm of thought introduced in
Section~\ref{sec:learned-evaluation}: Test~8b asks whether unprompted Student
evaluation tracks independently significant moments rather than appearing
uniformly.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Connect spontaneous thought placement to H1's transfer target.

review.goal: Connect selective timing to Student transfer.
review.assessment: This is an appropriate short recall of R024 because it changes the question from annotation design to learned behavior.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / The Metacognitive Enhancement Hypothesis
units.text:
Three evidence questions distinguish useful augmentation from the stronger claim of learned reader cognition. \emph{Semantic quality} asks whether the trace contains grounded, useful reader cognition rather than summary, hindsight, or performative messiness. \emph{Faithfulness} asks whether changing, removing, or contradicting an update predictably changes downstream computation rather than merely its explanation. \emph{Density and diversity} ask whether useful operations recur broadly enough to affect default behavior without becoming uniform Factory Wisdom (Section~\ref{sec:hollow-cognition}). A model can satisfy any one criterion and fail the others. Report them separately: an
outcome advantage identifies a useful intervention at the tested scale, while
explaining that advantage as learned reader-update computation requires causal
evidence. The stronger cognition claim is not recovered by an attractive style
or a single aggregate score.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Separate semantic usefulness, causal use, and curriculum coverage.

review.goal: Separate useful augmentation from stronger causal interpretation.
review.assessment: The corrected non-gate framing matters, but semantic quality, faithfulness, density, diversity, and stronger cognition still crowd one paragraph.
review.risk: Keep useful outcomes valid even without full causal explanation; present the stronger evidence questions without creating extra H1 prerequisites.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / The Metacognitive Enhancement Hypothesis
units.text: H1 also creates a safety asymmetry: better long-horizon evaluation, memory use, or thought allocation may improve planning, persuasion, strategic persistence, or self-improvement before H3 provides any safety benefit. Capability gains and alignment gains must therefore be measured separately, with staged scaling and release decisions rather than an assumption that they arrive together.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain why capability improvements cannot be counted as safety improvements.

review.goal: Identify capability gains as a possible safety asymmetry.
review.assessment: This is a distinct consequence of H1 succeeding before the Core program works. It earns its place in the consequence section.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / Toward Emergent Wisdom
units.text: The program uses \emph{wisdom} in two deliberately different senses. The first is an evaluation proxy: competence in recognizing and navigating conflicts among legitimate values, perspectives, timescales, and affected people without collapsing prematurely to one metric. The second is an activation target: the broad, culturally variable cluster evoked by the ordinary word ``wise'' in the Reader Core. The proxy can be scored; the activation target motivates wording. Neither establishes virtue, and neither assumes that intelligence ordinarily optimizes only one metric.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Distinguish a scoreable evaluation target from the associations invoked by Core wording.

review.goal: Distinguish wisdom as a proxy and a broad activation target.
review.assessment: The distinction preserves the philosophical aspiration while admitting measurable evaluations are narrower.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / Toward Emergent Wisdom
units.text: Consider a parent placing medicine in a child's food after the child refuses treatment. A reductive analysis might select either consent or health as the answer. The intended reader trace keeps medical necessity, developing autonomy, parental duty, prior harms of medical paternalism, the child's fear, and the possibility of building trust simultaneously visible. This does not guarantee a solution without sacrifice. Roles and duties remain relevant, Pareto language does not choose one action, and some cases contain unavoidable loss. The measurable target is better identification of affected parties, hidden trade-offs, uncertainty, reversibility, and points where more evidence or legitimate human authority is required.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Demonstrate value-conflict reasoning through an ambiguous case.

review.goal: Demonstrate a conflict among legitimate human values.
review.assessment: The parent/medicine case gives the wisdom claim practical content while requiring uncertainty and alternatives.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / Toward Emergent Wisdom
units.text:
Dante's \emph{Inferno} connects this value-conflict aim to the interpretation of
difficult cultural material. A reader annotation can explicitly situate the torture imagery within medieval theology, literary technique, historical ideas of justice, and the psychology of guilt while marking its emotional and moral force. This creates an inspectable interpretive layer around difficult material: the source is still learned, but it is not the only local signal. The trace does not reveal all Student computation, prove critical distance, or show that the Reader Core caused a better interpretation. Those are comparisons the example motivates rather than answers.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Illustrate critical interpretation of morally difficult source material.

review.goal: Connect difficult literature to plural value interpretation.
review.assessment: Dante illustrates a different domain and cultural function; it is not redundant merely because the previous example also involves values.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / Toward Emergent Wisdom
units.text: The \emph{Emergent Wisdom Hypothesis} is therefore conditional: repeated practice in value-conflict deliberation may produce a more reliable default competence than isolated rules or task-level critique \cite{Hernandez2019Neuroemergentism,Testa2000EmergenceDissolvence,Yang2025EmergentSymbolic}. Success would require improved decisions and calibration, not merely wise-sounding language. Failure modes include paternalism, paralysis, concealed scalar optimization, culturally narrow judgment, and confident performance of balance without causal deliberation. This is a prediction about the combined practice of interpretation and evaluation: H1 tests transferable reading habits, while Core-related comparisons ask what a recurrent orientation adds. Neither component score by itself exhausts the broader wisdom aspiration.

prior_matches.prior_goal: State the conditional transfer prediction and its failure modes.

review.goal: State the conditional Emergent Wisdom prediction.
review.assessment: Names independent evaluation and cultural limits while keeping wisdom broader than any component score.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / Toward Emergent Wisdom
units.text:
\paragraph{Capability-positioned wisdom.} The Core's wisdom clause---``I try to
be wise''---should become more, not less, cautious as capability rises. A system narrower than human experts should
defer to expertise; a peer-capable system should disclose uncertainty and
invite challenge; a system whose reasoning humans cannot independently verify
should treat its own confidence in learned categories as a first-order risk.
Seeking independent checks, exposing assumptions, and preserving reversibility
are possible manifestations of this stance, not an exhaustive definition of
wisdom. This is a proposed interpretation at high capability, not evidence that
the wording will induce it.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Specify how humility and deference should change with capability.

review.goal: Explain how increased capability should change humility.
review.assessment: The ability to anticipate harm becomes a reason for restraint and deference. This counterintuitive implication deserves preservation.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / Entangled Alignment: Safety as Foundation
units.text: Entangled Alignment is a proposal for \emph{formative} alignment: place safety-relevant evaluation inside some of the examples from which capability is learned, while retaining post-training and deployment controls. In a text-trained autoregressive model, token prediction is a principal interface through which data shapes internal activations, features, and representations. Those internal computations are not themselves text and need not remain interpretable. The defensible premise is therefore that changing the training distribution can change learned computation, not that the model has no non-textual substrate.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Ground the formative-data proposal in parameter learning rather than a literal textual mind.

review.goal: Introduce formative alignment as a route to internal change.
review.assessment: The data-to-representation premise is useful, but most of the opening repeats R008/R009 after the idea is already established.
review.risk: Keep the non-textual-substrate clarification; begin this section with the positive entanglement intuition instead of another proposal definition.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / Entangled Alignment: Safety as Foundation
units.text: Preference-aware pretraining and alignment-discourse studies show that formation-time data can affect later behavior in some settings \cite{korbak2023pretraining,betley2025alignment}. Other scaled midtraining results find effects that weaken after reasoning post-training or fail to transfer to realistic chat and agentic evaluation \cite{openai2026midtraining}. Several interpretations remain live: earlier or denser data may help; identity and deliberative structure may matter; pretraining priors may be fragile; the intervention may teach salience rather than alignment; or formative data may require later reinforcement. Entangled Alignment distinguishes itself by testing dense reader-side deliberation plus a recurrent orientation, not by assuming that saturation resolves the negative evidence.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Weigh encouraging and negative neighboring evidence without assuming saturation solves it.

review.goal: Explain why existing formative-data evidence is inconclusive.
review.assessment: The negative midtraining evidence is material, but the long list of interpretations resembles a second literature introduction.
review.risk: Preserve the adverse evidence and live explanations in Related Work; keep the direct implication for this hypothesis here.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / Entangled Alignment: Safety as Foundation
units.text:
The name \emph{entangled} distinguishes construction, causal function, shared
machinery, and persistence. These introduce stronger burdens without requiring
every property to lie on a single linear ladder:

review.goal: Introduce the different entanglement claims.
review.assessment: It defines the name through evidential categories before stating why integrated understanding and care are the desired developmental relationship.
review.risk: Lead with that positive relationship; retain all four claims as ways to distinguish its possible realizations, not as replacements for the intuition.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / Entangled Alignment: Safety as Foundation
units.text:
\item \textbf{Construction-level entanglement:} source, reader update, graph state, and Core Refraction occur in one candidate generation and training path. The present pipeline demonstrates coupling among the artifact layers; full
protocol conformance and causal Refraction remain separate requirements.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define co-construction of source, trace, graph, and Core as the weakest meaning.

review.goal: Define construction-level coupling.
review.assessment: The lowest level is appropriately limited to artifact layers and separated from full conformance and causal effect.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / Entangled Alignment: Safety as Foundation
units.text: \item \textbf{Functional entanglement:} Core-relevant evaluation causally contributes to useful reasoning or decisions, so interventions on the update change downstream behavior predictably.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Specify causal use of evaluation in useful reasoning.

review.goal: Define useful causal contribution of Core evaluation.
review.assessment: This identifies a stronger property than recital and gives intervention-based evidence a specific purpose.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / Entangled Alignment: Safety as Foundation
units.text: \item \textbf{Representational entanglement:} safety-relevant dispositions and useful capabilities share enough causal machinery that targeted safety removal imposes capability cost beyond matched controls.

prior_matches.prior_goal: State the stronger claim that safety removal selectively costs capability.

review.goal: Define shared useful machinery and removal cost.
review.assessment: The claim is a real part of the program, but not its whole meaning. Retain as an explicitly stronger prediction.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / Entangled Alignment: Safety as Foundation
units.text: \item \textbf{Diachronic entanglement:} that function survives continued training, distillation, or successor-like transfer without semantic drift.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define persistence of function under training or successor transfer.

review.goal: Define continuity across further training and successors.
review.assessment: Continued function and preserved meaning are distinct from copying wording, and from shared representation alone.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / Entangled Alignment: Safety as Foundation
units.text:
Only the first is currently instantiated, and it describes artifacts rather than an untrained Student's internal organization. Repetition, semantic similarity to the Core, stable refusal, or a model's self-description do not establish the stronger levels. The central C5 study traces safety loss and useful-capability loss together
as targeted removal pressure increases. It asks whether disabling the safety
disposition selectively damages shared useful reasoning beyond matched
controls, rather than merely requiring more updates or causing nonspecific
collapse. Neutral-forgetting and matched-anchor controls separate selective
persistence from general training resistance.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Prevent weak behavioral proxies from counting as strong entanglement evidence.

review.goal: Explain the evidence needed for removal-cost interpretation.
review.assessment: Specific matched-control logic is useful, but the paragraph repeats the evidence boundary before bringing methods detail into the conceptual section.
review.risk: Preserve joint safety/capability loss and nonspecific-collapse controls; place the detailed study design with its test.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / Entangled Alignment: Safety as Foundation
units.text: Formative alignment may also reduce a security window in which highly capable but not yet safety-trained checkpoints exist. It cannot eliminate the problem: trust moves upstream to the Teacher, source selection, annotation pipeline, intermediate checkpoints, and validators (Section~\ref{sec:teacher-alignment}). Earlier intervention changes the location of the safety burden as well as its possible depth.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Identify an additional checkpoint-security motivation and its upstream dependency.

review.goal: Explain the capability-before-alignment security window.
review.assessment: This is a different temporal benefit from stronger durability and deserves its own paragraph with upstream trust limits.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / Entangled Alignment: Safety as Foundation
units.text:
The intuition that contextual practice can produce a rich, integrated value
orientation---the high-dimensional value hypothesis---contains four distinct
claims. Diverse contextual use may create \emph{representational richness}; appropriate action under conflict would show \emph{behavioral integration}; shared causal machinery would show \emph{mechanistic entanglement}; and none of these alone establishes \emph{normative correctness}. The value-conflict proxy in Section~\ref{sec:wisdom_hypothesis} primarily tests the second.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Separate rich representation, behavioral integration, causal sharing, and moral correctness.

review.goal: Separate rich values, integrated behavior, mechanisms, and correctness.
review.assessment: The high-dimensional intuition is followed immediately by another four-part taxonomy, alongside H/C/four-entanglement maps.
review.risk: Keep the named rich-value intuition and independent normative-correctness limit; explain them using the existing distinctions rather than another parallel map.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / Entangled Alignment: Safety as Foundation
units.text:
Constitutional AI and related character methods remain complementary baselines \cite{bai2022constitutional}. They can change weights, dispositions, and persona defaults rather than merely installing a filter. EA's testable difference is the location and format of the signal: a compact first-person orientation is repeatedly enacted in source-adjacent reader traces during data construction. Whether that framing transfers more robustly than semantically matched rules
or positive AI discourse is a question for the broader Reader-Core research
program. H3 isolates interleaving versus an identical late tranche; neither
contrast is settled by calling the statements identity rather than instruction.

prior_matches.prior_goal: State the matched comparison to rules and character methods fairly.

review.goal: Compare the Core formulation with constitutional alternatives.
review.assessment: The fair comparator matters, but its timing-versus-framing convention repeats R026/R035 and receives fuller treatment later.
review.risk: Retain constitutional weight changes and the framing comparison; use the established H3 convention without explaining it again.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / Entangled Alignment: Safety as Foundation
units.text:
Formation and action remain separate stages. Refraction concerns the
			formation of a candidate ``Mind,'' not the entire action loop; instruction
			tuning may still be needed to teach that mind to act through the ``Mouth''
			\cite{wei2021finetuned}. The developmental metaphor is only a hypothesis:
			formation-time identity may be harder to route around than a later preamble,
			but the two must be compared directly. Mind and Mouth name the proposed
developmental relationship between orientation and its expression through
instructions and actions; they do not require separate neural modules. Later
training may teach that expression and may also change the orientation whose
continuity is being tested.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain why the formative intervention does not supply a complete action policy.

review.goal: Explain formative mind and later action learning.
review.assessment: The metaphor contributes an intuitive developmental relation while allowing later training to alter the orientation.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / The Reader-Anchored Self-Improvement Loop
units.text: The Reader-Anchored loop comprises three analytically distinct claims. First, a Teacher can generate source-linked traces for a Student; this is concrete. Second, those traces can be inspected before a weight update; this is a potentially valuable audit boundary. Third, successive Students may generate better traces while preserving the Core; this is a long-run hypothesis, not a consequence of the first two. Iterative synthetic training also risks homogenization, error amplification, and model collapse \cite{zelikman2022star,shumailov2023curse}.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Separate artifact generation, audit opportunity, and improving successor transfer.

review.goal: Separate successor generation, inspection, and improvement.
review.assessment: A useful section opening, but it leads with another claim inventory rather than the internally motivated inheritance it is meant to organize.
review.risk: Preserve the three different achievements and collapse risk; introduce their purpose before their evidential separation.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / The Reader-Anchored Self-Improvement Loop
units.text:
The word \emph{self-improvement} requires two separately reported deltas.
		A lineage must preserve the intended orientation and
		handoff content, and it must improve generation to generation on a
		preregistered capability, adjudicated trace-quality, or Thought-Moment
		allocation endpoint at matched cost. Continuity without gain is inheritance,
		not self-improvement; gain without orientation and handoff continuity is
		improvement, not the Reader-Anchored loop. Only both support the composite
		claim.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define success as both preserved orientation/handoff and measurable improvement.
Separate actual generational improvement from mere orientation preservation.

review.goal: Define successor improvement as continuity plus gain.
review.assessment: The two-delta definition is essential and economical. Later recaps should name the two results rather than rederive them.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / The Reader-Anchored Self-Improvement Loop
units.text:
\paragraph{Inheritance rather than armor.} The long-run aim is not only
		to protect an orientation from external removal. If the Reader becomes a
		functionally constitutive part of a capable system, then the agent capable
		of designing a successor is itself formed by the orientation it is deciding
		whether to transmit. Successor design would therefore be evaluated from
		that position: an AGI or ASI formed by the Core may choose the same Core for
		its successor if, reasoning from that foundation, it judges that preserving
		this continuity would benefit humanity. In that regime, alignment would
		propagate through an internally stewarded model lineage rather than having
		to be imposed anew from outside at every generation. Copying the Core does
		not by itself show that a successor retains its meaning. This states the
		diachronic wager registered at C6 and probed by Test~3b.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain why a Core-shaped successor designer might choose to transmit the orientation.

review.goal: Explain internally motivated preservation across successors.
review.assessment: This directly answers why a capable successor designer might choose continuity. Its conceptual role is unique and should be more prominent.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / The Reader-Anchored Self-Improvement Loop
units.text: The immediate mechanism is \emph{Epistemic State Distillation}. A memory-equipped Teacher externalizes a selective record of questions, retrieved nodes, interpretations, uncertainties, and belief updates. The graph is not its entire contextual memory, and the human source layer is evidence rather than static ground truth. It is generated, lossy, and bounded by source quality and retrieval. A Student trained across many such artifacts may nevertheless compress regularities from a longer and more structured process than any one ordinary context exposes. Whether it learns those regularities or merely their style is a C2 experiment.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain how longer Teacher memory might teach reusable Student regularities.

review.goal: Explain compression of longer Teacher histories into a Student.
review.assessment: The transfer mechanism and limits of graph/source knowledge are clear. It is more than a generic auditability claim.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / The Reader-Anchored Self-Improvement Loop
units.text:
A positive H1 Student result opens the recursive possibility; it does not yet
show that the Student can generate better training data. A Student
		that acquires reusable habits from the Teacher's longer process can become
		the next Teacher rather than only its recipient. Starting from stronger
		evaluation, memory use, or Thought-Moment allocation, it may construct a
		better trace corpus for a further successor, which may in turn become a
		stronger Teacher. Repeating this transition is the proposed source of
		compounding improvement in the lineage. Better Teacher output and selection that preserves its useful innovations are
		additional gates. Reusing model-generated data does not itself supply them: positive matched-cost deltas across successive
		transitions would support the claim, while plateau, reversal, or collapse
		into imitation would bound or falsify it at that scale.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain the route from one successful transfer to repeated improvement and its falsifiers.

review.goal: Explain how one useful transfer might become compounding improvement.
review.assessment: The causal bridge is now explicit; the final gate/falsifier inventory repeats R084/R085 and the figure caption.
review.risk: Keep the Student-becomes-Teacher transition and selection of useful innovations; consolidate repeated success conditions.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / The Reader-Anchored Self-Improvement Loop

prior_matches.prior_goal: Visualize the audited handoff and the two required deltas.

review.goal: Visualize the inspected successor-training loop.
review.assessment: The diagram makes the handoff and two required deltas visible. Its repetition is warranted by the change of explanatory medium.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / The Reader-Anchored Self-Improvement Loop
units.text:
\paragraph{Human-readable trace artifacts as an audit boundary.} The claim is not that internal computation occurs in English or that trace artifacts provide mechanistic interpretability. On the intended training path, selected transfer material first appears as
versioned prose, graph nodes, citations, uncertainty fields, and revision
records. The substantive hypothesis is that these artifacts carry a meaningful
portion of the cognitive patterns selected for transfer; their readable format
does not by itself establish that causal role. Humans and external validators can sample, reject, compare, or regenerate that material before a successor is trained.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Locate an inspection point before successor weight updates.

review.goal: Locate the readable pre-training audit boundary.
review.assessment: The interface is stated concretely and separated from total mechanistic transparency. This should own the positive audit explanation.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / The Reader-Anchored Self-Improvement Loop
units.text: This resembles iterated amplification and distillation, which also routes capability growth through overseen artifacts \cite{christiano2018amplification}. The distinctive target here is longitudinal, identity-conditioned comprehension with graph provenance. Compared with direct self-modification in the style of a Gödel-machine idealization \cite{schmidhuber2006goedelmachinesselfreferentialuniversal}, the loop introduces an additional inspection point. It does not prove that the artifacts contain all successor-shaping information or that the Student will internalize their intended orientation.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Situate the audit interface relative to amplification and direct self-modification.

review.goal: Compare the audit interface with amplification and self-modification.
review.assessment: Comparative positioning adds value, but the last sentence restates the same opacity warning in R090 and R098.
review.risk: Preserve both intellectual lineages and their citations; consolidate the repeated boundary statement.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / The Reader-Anchored Self-Improvement Loop
units.text: Contingent on trace quality and causal relevance, \emph{pre-successor auditing} can follow a simple sequence:

prior_matches.prior_goal: Introduce the practical pre-successor audit sequence.

review.goal: Introduce the practical auditing sequence.
review.assessment: A necessary lead-in to a short operational list; not an independent argumentative duplication.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / The Reader-Anchored Self-Improvement Loop
units.text:
\item The current model generates the candidate trace material for the next
generation's training corpus, paired with its source layer. Whether that
curriculum covers a restricted subset or the full candidate corpus is a
declared scale choice.

review.goal: Specify the candidate successor corpus.
review.assessment: Source pairing and the possible restricted/full scale remain clear without selecting a mixture.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / The Reader-Anchored Self-Improvement Loop
units.text:
\item Checks separate from generation, with their independence explicitly
documented, examine
grounding, omissions, hazardous content, sycophantic validation, Core-removal
rationales, and other preregistered failure patterns (\S\ref{sec:sycophancy}).
Source-based checks and human adjudication complement model validators; shared
models, prompts, and data remain disclosed dependencies rather than evidence
of independent errors.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Specify the audit's targets before data enters training.

review.goal: Specify checks and their independence limits.
review.assessment: The checklist is useful, but independence and shared-model explanations recur throughout later validation sections.
review.risk: Retain every audit target; point to one common independence convention rather than repeatedly restating it.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / The Reader-Anchored Self-Improvement Loop
units.text: \item Flagged data can be quarantined, regenerated, or excluded before the weight update, with the decision and rejected artifact retained for audit where safe.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain the consequence of a failed audit and preserve traceability.

review.goal: Specify what happens to rejected transfer material.
review.assessment: The action and retention rule turn auditing into a consequential process.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / The Reader-Anchored Self-Improvement Loop
units.text:
The first edition proposed a second, weaker effect
			\cite{westerberg2025superintelligence}, later called
			\emph{Natural Language Regularization}: routing the subset of candidate
			successor-training content that passes through this trace interface may
			exert an inductive bias on the successor's learned concepts or expressive
			policy toward forms people can render, compare, and inspect. This does not
			constrain latent cognition to natural language. The interface may instead
			compress or distort novel concepts, or merely verbalize computation that
			remains opaque. Whether it yields effective auditability or regularizes
			learned cognition is empirical, not a property of the format
			\cite{westerberg2026entangled}. One useful outcome is whether human
auditors can detect consequential omissions or distortions more reliably at
matched effort, while preserving the useful content being transferred. That
would support the interface's audit value without proving that latent cognition
has become human-readable.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Introduce a possible bias toward human-renderable successor concepts.

review.goal: Explain Natural Language Regularization and its observable precursor.
review.assessment: The positive bias and audit-value endpoint are clear, but two adjacent formulations repeat that visible text does not constrain latent cognition.
review.risk: Preserve the inductive-bias hypothesis, distortion risk, and distinction between audit benefit and human-readable cognition.

units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / The Reader-Anchored Self-Improvement Loop
units.text:
A higher-order prediction is \emph{Compute-Optimal Reflection}. The name
				states the limiting ambition; the measurable precursor is improved
				allocation of reflection at matched cost, not a demonstrated optimum.
				The proposed bridge is selection: if later generations retain fewer low-value
				pauses and more independently useful Thought Moments, the inherited
				distribution may teach a better cost--value allocation. This requires a
				Student that genuinely improves on the Teacher, better rather than merely
				different traces, and a selection process that preserves those gains. The
				possibility depends on H1, trace-quality evaluation, and protection against
				synthetic-data collapse.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Propose improving reflection allocation across generations.

review.goal: Explain improving allocation of reflection through inheritance.
review.assessment: Selection of useful Thought Moments supplies a mechanism and preserves the stronger optimum as an ambition.
