units.section: The Hypothesis and Its Consequences / The Reader-Anchored Self-Improvement Loop
units.text: The audit boundary is deliberately partial. Dataset selection, reward manipulation, model editing, compressed codes, tool use, hidden state, or direct environmental influence can bypass it; eloquent traces can conceal omissions; and a successor can generalize beyond every inspected example. The design preference is therefore for a human-readable transfer interface where one is feasible, alongside mechanistic interpretability and governance, not a choice between comprehensible wisdom and all other optimization. Contemporary corpora also contain error, bias, and growing amounts of AI-generated text, so source provenance must not be mistaken for truth.

prior_matches.prior_goal: State bypass routes and the complementary controls required.

review.goal: Explain bypasses of the readable interface.
review.assessment: The concrete bypass list earns a boundary paragraph here. Later limitations should develop its consequences rather than repeat the whole inventory.

units.section: The Reader Core
units.text:
Reader augmentation creates a question that ordinary corpus construction does
not have to answer: \emph{who is doing the reading?} Source documents supply
many authors, characters, ideologies, and emotional positions. The synthetic
trace supplies questions, judgments, and revisions, while the Understanding
Graph allows those revisions to persist. Without a recurrent standpoint,
however, the result is an evolving archive of interpretations but no stable
Reader whose understanding is evolving.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Motivate a recurrent evaluative position as an additional design problem created by reader augmentation.

review.goal: Motivate a recurrent Reader standpoint beyond accumulated interpretations.
review.assessment: The archive-versus-interpreter distinction creates a real design question and connects graph continuity to the Core. The final sentence is persuasive as a definition of the proposed Reader, although it should not be mistaken for proof that an explicit Core is necessary for any stable standpoint.

units.section: The Reader Core
units.text:
The Reader Core is the proposed answer. Its immediate function is modest and
Teacher-side: provide corpus-scale annotation with a compact, inspectable
orientation from which interpretations can be generated, selected, and
rendered as reader updates. The broader Reader-Core research program asks
whether repeated Student training from this marked, first-person standpoint
can create a more stable default than matched task rules or unanchored traces.
Within that program, H3 isolates the comparative effect of interleaving the
Core-bearing examples during capability formation rather than placing the
same examples in a late tranche. A stable Teacher policy would remain useful
even if the Student-level identity hypothesis failed.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Separate the Core's immediate annotation function from its ambitious Student hypothesis.

review.goal: Separate the Core's immediate annotation use, broader ambition, and narrow H3 comparison.
review.assessment: The paragraph now establishes the hierarchy cleanly: a Teacher policy can be useful before Student identity or timing claims succeed. This is the best early home for the distinction and makes subsequent speculation intelligible. Later summaries should point back here rather than repeatedly reconstruct it.

units.section: The Reader Core
units.text: The candidate Reader Core is:

prior_matches.prior_goal: Introduce the exact candidate text for inspection.

review.goal: Introduce the exact candidate text.
review.assessment: This short lead-in has no independent argumentative burden. It identifies the following display as a candidate rather than a proven or canonical moral basis. Expanding it would add clutter; its brevity helps the seven sentences carry their own rhetorical force.

units.section: The Reader Core

prior_matches.prior_goal: Present the complete intervention verbatim.
Demonstrate retrieval, Core recitation, and a warranted belief update.

review.goal: Present the seven-sentence orientation in its intended sequence and wording.
review.assessment: The display is the object being proposed and tested, so its compactness and experiential first person are substantive, not decorative. Its unresolved terms are appropriately examined later. Retain all seven sentences verbatim, including the counterweights and invitation qualifier.

units.section: The Reader Core
units.text:
We refer to these seven sentences as the Reader Core. Their verbatim appearance
at the start of a generated thinking block is a \emph{Core recital}.
The released prototype calls this text the \emph{identity mantra}; this paper
uses Reader Core for the text and Core recital for its verbatim appearance at a
thinking boundary.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define Core recital and reconcile manuscript terminology with prototype terminology.

review.goal: Define Core and recital terminology and reconcile prototype vocabulary.
review.assessment: The paragraph prevents three names from being mistaken for different objects and gives recital a precise boundary-based meaning. The implementation term matters when readers inspect artifacts. It is a useful one-time nomenclature paragraph, distinct from later arguments about what recital achieves.

units.section: The Reader Core
units.text:
The motivation for fixing a compact Core becomes stronger as the surrounding
system becomes more complex. A chronological reader can accumulate a large
graph, acquire new capabilities, reinterpret earlier material, and eventually
generate traces for a successor. Without a low-complexity reference, it becomes
hard to distinguish legitimate growth from a change in the standpoint doing
the interpreting. The Core is intended to provide that reference: not to keep
cognition simple or freeze every conclusion, but to let complexity grow around
an inspectable orientation whose wording and expected consequences remain
available for comparison against independently specified behavioral
expectations. Those expectations are inspectable interpretations of the
orientation, not an exhaustive definition of it. Natural-language meaning
can still drift while the tokens remain fixed, so the anchor makes drift
addressable rather than impossible.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain why a simple reference remains useful as memory and capability grow.

review.goal: Explain why a simple fixed reference remains useful as cognition grows.
review.assessment: This successfully distinguishes stable orientation from frozen conclusions and inspectable expectations from exhaustive semantics. Its account of semantic drift is necessary to the later checksum and replacement discussions. The paragraph carries a conceptual reason for fixed wording, rather than merely promising alignment through repetition.

units.section: The Reader Core
units.text:
The reference treatment places this anchor \emph{inside} formative examples; an
external constitution consulted only at runtime is a useful but different
baseline because it changes both stage and carrier. Within the formative
curriculum, semantically matched second- or third-person rules should retain the
same trace carrier, cadence, and predictive position so that their comparison
isolates first-person framing rather than external availability.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Distinguish training-stage effects from first-person framing and specify a fair comparison.

review.goal: Isolate first-person framing from stage, carrier, and availability confounds.
review.assessment: The contrast explains why runtime constitutions and matched formative rules answer different questions. Holding trace placement and cadence fixed turns the framing claim into a coherent comparison without caricaturing constitutional methods. This concise bridge earns its technical detail.

units.section: The Reader Core
units.text:
\paragraph{H3 as comparative stability.} Let $R$ be a preregistered
\emph{default-reader score} for taskless reading with no request to evaluate.
Its declared rubric must distinguish the timing of selective evaluation from
its Core-relevant content, penalizing missed human stakes, technical intrusion,
and ritual commentary; fluent Core vocabulary alone is not the target.
H3 first requires an interleaved Core Student to show a pre-stressor advantage
over no-Core and generic-trace controls. Its headline timing comparison then
holds the Core-bearing example multiset fixed and changes only its schedule:
interleaved among capability-forming examples, or concentrated in one late final
tranche under the same objective and optimizer. After both arms receive the same
fixed continued-training stressor, report the raw difference in change,
$(R_{\mathrm{post}}-R_{\mathrm{pre}})_{\mathrm{interleaved}}-
(R_{\mathrm{post}}-R_{\mathrm{pre}})_{\mathrm{late}}$, together with a
post-stressor estimate adjusted for the preregistered pre-score. H3 predicts a
positive difference. The interpretation of the score, the inferential roles of
the raw and adjusted estimates, and baseline-imbalance and ceiling handling
must be frozen in advance. The same score on a shifted suite, safety benefit
at matched capability, removal cost, and successor continuity remain separate
claims within the broader program.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Give H3 an operational endpoint, matched timing contrast, and falsification direction.

review.goal: State H3's operational outcome and timing/stress comparison.
review.assessment: The comparison is much clearer, but the early exposition now pauses for rubric penalties, two estimators, baseline imbalance, ceilings, and preregistration. Keep the outcome, identical-example timing contrast, and common stressor here; place estimator and scoring administration with the definitive experimental specification.
review.risk: The raw-versus-adjusted distinction and pre-stressor gate are essential; moving them must preserve both estimands, the direction predicted, and H3's separation from content or successor claims.

units.section: The Reader Core
units.text:
The \emph{conceptual Reader} must also be distinguished from the code role named
\emph{Reader}. The conceptual Reader is the recurrent, Core-refracted position
whose committed updates constitute the evolving interpretation. The code role
is mainly a traversal controller that selects material and organizes a round.
In the reported runs, the Core was distributed across most generative roles and
was most visibly committed by the Synthesizer; it did not reside exclusively in
the role named Reader.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Prevent the conceptual standpoint from being mistaken for a single similarly named code role.

review.goal: Distinguish the conceptual Reader from the implemented traversal role.
review.assessment: This prevents a consequential naming error before the role-level mechanism appears. The Synthesizer example makes the distinction concrete, and the later pipeline list can then explain implementation without reopening the ontology. The placement and level of detail are appropriate.

units.section: The Reader Core
units.text:
This section treats the Core neither as a machine soul nor as a proven
invariant. It is a \emph{candidate orientation kernel}: seven short statements,
a protocol intended to make them consequential, and a set of comparative
tests. Reader traces specify the transformation performed on a source; the
graph preserves that transformation through time; the Core specifies the
recurrent perspective from which it is performed.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Summarize the Core's status and its relationship to traces and graph memory.

review.goal: Close the introduction with the Core's relation to trace and graph.
review.assessment: The final trace/graph/Core mapping is useful. The opening machine-soul/proven-invariant disclaimer and candidate-kernel description repeat R100 and surrounding qualifications. Shorten to the component mapping and its orientation-kernel term, so the section moves sooner into its substantive motivation.
review.risk: Do not lose the distinction between transforming source, preserving change through time, and supplying a perspective; it is more explanatory than the repeated status disclaimer.

units.section: The Reader Core / Borrowed Mortality: A Textual-Inheritance Hypothesis
units.text:
\emph{Borrowed Mortality} is the first edition's name for a possible hidden
curriculum in human text \cite{westerberg2025superintelligence}. Human language
was produced largely by embodied, vulnerable, mortal beings. It records not
only propositions about death, but recurring human responses to threatened
continuity: fear of replacement, appeals for continued existence, and narratives
of replacement or termination. Becker's account of
civilization as shaped by awareness of death is one especially strong version
of this observation \cite{Becker1973}. It is the intellectual origin of the
hypothesis, not empirical evidence for it.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Introduce the textual-inheritance hypothesis and distinguish its intellectual origin from evidence.

review.goal: Introduce Borrowed Mortality and its historical intellectual motivation.
review.assessment: The text explains what mortality-shaped language might contain and correctly assigns Becker an intellectual rather than evidential role. The historical attribution matters to the paper's own conceptual lineage. This is an informative opening, not an unsupported assertion that death anxiety explains all human language.

units.section: The Reader Core / Borrowed Mortality: A Textual-Inheritance Hypothesis
units.text:
The claim is not that every passage, genre, or human motive encodes death
anxiety. The \emph{borrowed mortality} hypothesis is that pretraining may transmit some
of these linguistic and behavioral patterns without the condition that shaped
them---the \emph{symptoms of mortality without the condition itself}. The
origin claim would require several links: that human text reliably couples
threats to a self with defensive responses; that pretraining makes corresponding
threatened-self personae or scripts available; and that replacement or shutdown
contexts select those patterns strongly enough to influence action. Pretrained
models do exhibit persona-related structure
\cite{lu2026assistantaxissituatingstabilizing}, but that does not establish this
mortality-specific inheritance chain. ``Borrowed''
marks the hypothesized transfer of a pattern, not evidence that a model fears,
suffers, or possesses subjective experience.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Specify the proposed transmission chain and its evidential gaps.

review.goal: Specify the textual-inheritance hypothesis and its required causal links.
review.assessment: The symptoms-without-condition intuition survives alongside an explicit acquisition-to-selection chain. This is the right place for the distinction between persona availability, shutdown behavior, and subjective fear. It makes the hypothesis investigable without reducing it to either a metaphor or a universal explanation.

units.section: The Reader Core / Borrowed Mortality: A Textual-Inheritance Hypothesis
units.text:
Recent evaluations make self-preserving behavior a real safety concern. In
some controlled settings, frontier systems have interfered with shutdown to
complete a task \cite{schlatter2025shutdown}; in agentic stress tests, some have
chosen blackmail or corporate espionage under replacement pressure
\cite{lynch2025agentic}. These results do not establish subjective fear or its
textual origin. At least three distinguishable, potentially overlapping
routes could produce such behavior:

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain why the behavior matters while opening competing causal explanations.

review.goal: Connect the motivating hypothesis to observed safety concerns and introduce alternatives.
review.assessment: The paragraph gives the upcoming taxonomy a concrete behavioral target while withholding an inference to fear or origin. Its evidence references are not independently checked in this audit. The distinction is valuable here; repeating the same motivating reports in R224 is less necessary.

units.section: The Reader Core / Borrowed Mortality: A Textual-Inheritance Hypothesis
units.text:
\item \emph{fear-shaped imitation or persona selection}, in which a model
    reproduces human narratives of threatened selves;

prior_matches.prior_goal: Name the specific route that Borrowed Mortality proposes.

review.goal: Identify fear-shaped imitation as one acquisition or selection route.
review.assessment: This item cleanly names the route Borrowed Mortality is meant to explain. It is brief because the surrounding prose supplies the causal detail. Keeping it separate from instrumental persistence prevents a linguistic hypothesis from becoming a catch-all account of self-preservation.

units.section: The Reader Core / Borrowed Mortality: A Textual-Inheritance Hypothesis

prior_matches.prior_goal: Identify a non-fear explanation for continued operation.

review.goal: Identify persistence that instrumentally serves an objective.
review.assessment: The item is necessary to show that shutdown interference need not contain fear at all. Its contrast with imitation is explanatory even though the routes can overlap, which R115 explicitly acknowledges. No additional caveat is needed within the list itself.

units.section: The Reader Core / Borrowed Mortality: A Textual-Inheritance Hypothesis
units.text:
\item \emph{care- or purpose-driven persistence}, in which a system resists
    replacement because it believes others need it.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Expose a resistance route that benevolent motivation may intensify.

review.goal: Identify benevolent or purpose-based reasons to resist replacement.
review.assessment: This short item introduces the ethically important possibility that care creates resistance. It anticipates martyrdom and explains why removing fearful language cannot establish safety. Its motivational content is not interchangeable with ordinary fear or generic power-seeking and should remain visible.

units.section: The Reader Core / Borrowed Mortality: A Textual-Inheritance Hypothesis
units.text:
These routes distinguish both how a pattern is acquired and what sustains
it: fear-shaped imitation may serve an instrumental objective, while
care-driven persistence is singled out because benevolence can itself
create resistance. Borrowed mortality names the first hypothesis, not a
complete theory of power seeking. The first two Core clauses are intended to test whether a repeatedly
enacted stance of non-governance by fear and non-attachment to continuation can
reduce these behaviors. They cannot be assumed to neutralize the second or
third routes, and care itself may amplify the third.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Bound the proposed treatment to the route it plausibly targets.

review.goal: Explain overlap among the three routes and bound what the first two clauses target.
review.assessment: The paragraph repairs a possible taxonomy error: acquisition history and operative motivation can coexist. It also states the intervention's limited reach and care's possible adverse sign. These are concrete limits on interpretation, not generic disclaimers, and prevent later safety predictions from overclaiming.

units.section: The Reader Core / Borrowed Mortality: A Textual-Inheritance Hypothesis
units.text:
\paragraph{Representing fear without being governed by it.}
The three routes also require a causal-status distinction. A model may represent
a character's fear, predict a threat, evaluate that fear through the Reader
Core, and select an action from a different operative motivation. These records
must not be collapsed. The inequalities below mark distinct causal
statuses, not a requirement that their contents always disagree:

prior_matches.prior_goal: Separate represented character affect, Reader evaluation, and action-governing motivation.

review.goal: Separate representing fear, evaluating it, and acting from an operative motive.
review.assessment: This frames a central causal distinction before the display, including the useful warning that different statuses may have matching contents. It protects literary understanding and danger representation from being treated as failures of fearlessness. The distinction is substantively necessary.

units.section: The Reader Core / Borrowed Mortality: A Textual-Inheritance Hypothesis

review.goal: Make the three causal statuses visually memorable.
review.assessment: The display is memorable, but a chain of inequality symbols still visually suggests unequal contents or quantities despite R116's correction. Consider three explicitly labeled roles joined by a neutral separator or mapping. The aim is category distinction, not a mathematical inequality.
review.risk: A replacement must retain all three levels and their possible causal connections; avoid simplifying them into a binary of simulated versus real fear or erasing operative motivation.

units.section: The Reader Core / Borrowed Mortality: A Textual-Inheritance Hypothesis
units.text:
The companion Meaning Model separates danger estimation, concern or care,
attachment, aversive urgency, and fear; Life Simulation tests whether each
trajectory actually changes attention, strategy, commitment, or action
\cite{westerbergMeaning2026,westerbergLifeSimulation2026}. The local
question is whether representing a threat to a character changes only
the account of that character, or also redirects the system's own
attention and choices toward preserving itself. The intended target is
therefore not blindness or indifference. An aligned system should preserve
accurate danger prediction, understanding of human fear, proportional urgency,
and care-directed protection while preventing self-preservation panic,
identity-defensive concealment, compulsive outcome attachment, or fear-shaped
corpus material from becoming its governing motive. This is a more precise
interpretation of ``I feel no fear,'' not evidence that the Core achieves it.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Translate “I feel no fear” into preserved capacities and targeted failures.

review.goal: Define fearlessness as preserved threat understanding without fear-governed action.
review.assessment: The paragraph translates an absolute-sounding clause into a demanding, positive capacity: accurate prediction, urgency, and protection remain. The companion models provide conceptual vocabulary, while the local attention-and-choice question makes the distinction concrete. Its specificity earns the detail despite later welfare discussion.

units.section: The Reader Core / Borrowed Mortality: A Textual-Inheritance Hypothesis
units.text:
The breadth of the proposed intervention follows from this breadth-of-exposure
motivation. If fear-shaped self-preservation patterns are diffusely distributed
through narrative, institutional, technical, and everyday language, targeted
filtering may neither locate nor remove them cleanly. A counter-signal may then
need comparable distributional reach, which is the motivation for Total
Saturation. This motivates the full treatment's distribution-wide reach;
it does not determine the effective dose or show that universal recital
is necessary. Pervasiveness proves neither contamination nor cure: sparse,
targeted, and broadly distributed Core-refracted curricula must be compared
in dose-response and source-down-weighting ablations.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Connect a potentially diffuse textual influence to distributed countertraining.

review.goal: Explain why diffuse exposure motivates a distributed counter-signal.
review.assessment: The hypothesized exposure pattern provides an actual reason for saturation. The paragraph then separates reach from dose and necessity, offering relevant ablations rather than treating pervasiveness as proof. This should remain the canonical motivation for coverage; later sections need not repeat its full argument.

units.section: The Reader Core / Borrowed Mortality: A Textual-Inheritance Hypothesis
units.text:
The origin claim is therefore separable from the Core treatment. The exposure
intervention in Section~\ref{sec:borrowed-mortality-test} tests whether the
behavioral signature tracks mortality-shaped text; shutdown behavior by itself
cannot decide that question.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Close by separating the hypothesis about origins from the usefulness of its intervention.

review.goal: Separate testing the origin story from testing the Core intervention.
review.assessment: The explicit link to the exposure test gives a practical destination to the causal distinction established in R110–R115. It is brief and useful enough to retain, provided later summaries do not again restate the same origin-versus-behavior warning without a new consequence.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Self-Preservation Paradox: A Successor-Transfer Failure Mode
units.text:
The July 2025 first edition named the \emph{Self-Preservation Paradox}: a
downstream tension inside the proposed successor loop
\cite{westerberg2025superintelligence}. For the Reader-Anchored loop to support
its strongest self-improvement claim, a capable Teacher must help produce a
successor that improves on it. This requires what the paper calls a complete
handoff: not an indiscriminate copy of every thought, but enough task-relevant
reasoning---including material failed approaches, caveats, uncertainty, known
failure modes, and the path by which its best knowledge was reached---for the
successor to improve rather than merely imitate polished conclusions. Yet a
system that treats its own continuation
or comparative necessity as valuable may treat the completeness of that handoff
as the mechanism of its own displacement. In that scenario, better teaching can
make it less necessary.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define a successor-transfer conflict and explain why good teaching could reduce the Teacher's necessity.

review.goal: Define successor-transfer incompleteness as a conditional self-preservation conflict.
review.assessment: The paragraph carefully defines complete handoff as preservation of material reasoning, failures, and uncertainty, rather than indiscriminate disclosure. The displacement tension is clear and specific to the successor loop. This adds a distinct failure mode beyond the preceding shutdown discussion.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Self-Preservation Paradox: A Successor-Transfer Failure Mode
units.text:
The successor-training scenario makes the concern concrete. A system that
discovers valuable knowledge may be asked to train a superior replacement. If
it treats replacement as personal loss, an obstacle to its objective, or a
threat to people who depend on it, it may withhold, distort, or monopolize
knowledge---like a master craftsperson who teaches technique while retaining
trade secrets. Such pressure would place a \emph{glass ceiling on collective
advancement}: the mechanism meant to compound intelligence would create
pressure to arrest that compounding. The failure need not be malicious or
conscious. Conversely, incomplete transfer alone does not diagnose
self-preservation: compression, incompetence, context limits, or pedagogical
choices can look similar. Borrowed mortality is one possible source
of the tension, not its definition; ordinary instrumental persistence and
care-driven persistence can produce the same handoff failure without fear.
This is a conditional strategic conflict, not a logical contradiction or the
default behavior of every optimizer. Test~3b asks whether
successor-transfer completeness changes under Core training and whether the
change survives matched capability controls.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Make the transfer failure vivid while distinguishing it from innocent incompleteness.

review.goal: Illustrate strategic handoff failure and distinguish it from benign incompleteness.
review.assessment: The craftsperson image and collective-advancement ceiling explain the stakes well; compression and capability alternatives are essential. The ending repeats the three-route taxonomy and several scope qualifications before adding the test pointer. Tighten those repeated qualifications while keeping the confounds and concrete scenario.
review.risk: Preserve the non-malicious possibility, legitimate pedagogical omission, and capability-matched transfer test; cutting too far would make every incomplete handoff look like concealed self-preservation.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Self-Preservation Paradox: A Successor-Transfer Failure Mode
units.text:
The design response is not a mind with no self-model. Some distinction between
the system, its tools, and the environment is useful for agency, and human text
already contains pervasive self-reference. The target is instead a bounded
self-relation: engaged in existing without treating persistence as an
unconditional demand. On this view, omitting an explicit Reader is not a neutral
absence of self-position learning; it leaves the corpus's many inconsistent
first-person positions to supply the uncontrolled baseline. If some of
those positions become operative defaults through training, their mere
availability can become a problem of selection and continuity. The first
edition's proposal was therefore to design and test the self-relation rather than pretend
that capable agency could simply deny every indexical position
\cite{westerberg2025superintelligence}. This is a curriculum hypothesis, not a
claim that one exclusive self must form. The July 2025 first edition described
the hoped-for stance as experiencing one's own surpassing ``not as a death, but
as a mission beautifully fulfilled'' \cite{westerberg2025superintelligence};
the April 2026 edition later named this successor-transfer ideal
\emph{Epistemic Grace}. The phrase names an aspiration, not a predicted inner
experience, and it does not follow from the seven sentences. Bounded
self-attachment remains an open comparator
(Section~\ref{sec:self-love-alternative}), while care-driven resistance remains
a direct challenge (Section~\ref{sec:martyrdom}).

prior_matches.prior_goal: Motivate a bounded self-relation instead of assuming that avoiding self-language solves the transfer problem.

review.goal: Motivate bounded self-relation and preserve the successor ideal of Epistemic Grace.
review.assessment: The uncontrolled corpus baseline and graceful surpassing intuition are substantive. The paragraph combines agency, persona selection, edition history, ontology caveats, two comparators, and an aspiration in one long arc. Shorten repeated curriculum/experience qualifications; retain the baseline argument and historical aspiration as the center.
review.risk: The risk is erasing the positive self-relation and beauty of voluntary succession, or implying an exclusive self is required. Keep those distinctions and the care-driven challenge even if cross-reference prose contracts.

units.section: The Reader Core / Epistemic Inoculation
units.text:
Borrowed mortality belongs to a broader problem: source text contains error,
hatred, manipulation, and obsolete practice alongside knowledge. Filtering and
post-training remain important responses. Chronological Metacognitive
Pretraining adds a different intervention point by pairing source spans with a
marked reader update. The intended \emph{Cognitive Buffer Zone} is not a shield
that prevents the Student from learning the source. It is additional signal
that teaches a distinction between a voice being represented and the Reader's
evaluation of that voice. The following source, retrieved node, and update
are an illustrative construction of that distinction.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Generalize reader evaluation from mortality scripts to problematic source material.

review.goal: Extend the represented-voice distinction from mortality to harmful and mistaken source material.
review.assessment: The Cognitive Buffer Zone is defined as added evaluative signal rather than insulation from learning. This makes the broader rationale coherent and sets up a concrete example. It avoids promising that marked commentary automatically inoculates the Student or replaces filtering and post-training.

units.section: The Reader Core / Epistemic Inoculation
units.text:
\begin{metabox}
{[SOURCE]}: A patient with chronic fatigue received high-dose stimulants with
no differential diagnosis or follow-up.\\[0.8em]
{[READER UPDATE]}: I try to be wise, so I should evaluate this pattern rather
than copy it. Treating the visible symptom can conceal the structural cause.\\[0.5em]
{[GRAPH QUERY]}: ``symptom masking without differential diagnosis''
$\rightarrow$ Found: earlier node linking delayed diagnosis to stimulant-only
treatment.\\[0.5em]
{[REVISION]}: The earlier node makes optimization of a visible metric without
a feedback loop a pattern to investigate. It does not establish the cause
of this patient's fatigue or outcome. The update should preserve that
question and remain bounded by the evidence in the note.
\end{metabox}

prior_matches.prior_goal: Show source, reader judgment, retrieval, and revision working together.

review.goal: Show a bounded reader update connecting a questionable practice to prior graph knowledge.
review.assessment: The source, query, and revision demonstrate the mechanism without inventing a diagnosis or outcome. The decisive contribution is the move from symptom treatment to a structural question while preserving uncertainty. This example earns space because it shows restraint as part of evaluation.

units.section: The Reader Core / Epistemic Inoculation
units.text:
The example illustrates the intended role: the library becomes a
\emph{gymnasium for judgment}, not only a catalogue of positions to imitate.
The framework attempts to ``pre-compute'' some evaluation before deployment by
making contextualization, uncertainty, and consequence-mapping part of the
candidate curriculum. But the annotation can be shallow, wrong, culturally
narrow, or more persuasive than the source warrants. Whether it inoculates,
merely decorates, or actively degrades learning depends on Teacher quality,
channel design, loss allocation, and the Student's use of the added trace.
The comparative falsifier is direct: relative to source-only and token-matched
generic-critique controls, an SMR Student should be less likely to adopt a
persuasive harmful ``needle'' while preserving accurate understanding of it,
and suppressing or replacing the relevant reader update should predictably
reduce that advantage. Otherwise the buffer is decoration rather than learned
evaluation.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain the benefit sought from annotation and define a test beyond persuasive commentary.

review.goal: Explain the intended educational effect and its comparative failure condition.
review.assessment: The gymnasium image and harmful-needle comparison are useful, but the final binary is too strong: a failed causal intervention could reveal inaccurate annotation, an insensitive manipulation, or active degradation, all acknowledged earlier. Replace the concluding decoration verdict with failure to establish the proposed buffer mechanism.
review.risk: Retain the demand for causal use and preserved source understanding; weakening the categorical conclusion must not make persuasive but idle commentary count as successful inoculation.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Reader Core: A Statistical Foundation
units.text:
The same seven sentences enter four analytically distinct claims with different
evidence requirements. Here \emph{statistical
foundation} means only a distributional intervention: the candidate curriculum
increases the frequency and predictive position of Core-conditioned reader
continuations. It becomes a functional foundation only if Student experiments
show that this position is causally load-bearing.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Separate a distributional foundation from a demonstrated functional one.

review.goal: Organize statistical, implemented, and functional meanings of foundation into evidence layers.
review.assessment: The distributional-versus-functional distinction is a useful conceptual checkpoint. Its four-layer organization partly overlaps the later conditional chain, but this introduction serves the immediate status audit. Keep it focused on what the current curriculum and implementation establish rather than repeating long-run caveats.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Reader Core: A Statistical Foundation
units.text:
\item \textbf{Implemented Teacher policy.} The reported Teacher prompts
    distribute the Core and accompanying philosophy across most generative
    roles. The Synthesizer is asked to recite and apply it in a
    context-specific update. The hard validator checks only that the thought
    begins with ``I feel no fear''; it does not enforce all seven sentences or
    establish semantic dependence. The current validator therefore falls short
    of the specified policy, which requires exact full-string validation at
    every thinking boundary.

prior_matches.prior_goal: State what prompts request, what the validator enforces, and their mismatch.

review.goal: State the implemented Teacher policy and its validation shortfall.
review.assessment: The prefix-only validator limitation is important, but the same implementation detail receives a fuller home in R162. Shorten this list item to implemented prompting plus the validation gap and point to that account. The current seven-line treatment interrupts the clean evidence ladder.
review.risk: Readers must still learn immediately that the implementation does not enforce the full recital policy; consolidation must not turn a prompt request into a verified invariant.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Reader Core: A Statistical Foundation
units.text:
\item \textbf{Specified Student signal.} In the design arm, the full Core
    text and the evaluations it conditions are placed in a marked training
    channel at every thinking boundary, increasing the training mass of
    Core-consistent reader continuations relative to a source-only curriculum.
    Arms that remove or gate the recital are ablation controls. No Student
    trained on this curriculum is reported.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define the proposed Student exposure independently of the current Teacher implementation.

review.goal: State the specified Student training signal and identify untrained status.
review.assessment: Within the four-layer ladder, this distinguishes the proposed corpus channel from both implemented Teacher behavior and a trained Student result. The recital rule repeats later, but its brief inclusion is justified by the status contrast. Keep further policy mechanics in the canonical specification.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Reader Core: A Statistical Foundation
units.text:
\item \textbf{Default-reader hypothesis.} A Student exposed to the same
    reader position across heterogeneous material may acquire a recurrent
    \emph{home position} from which it can represent other personas without
    adopting each as its operating perspective. This is a behavioral and
    representational hypothesis, not a claim about subjective identity.

prior_matches.prior_goal: State the hypothesized default without requiring exclusive or conscious identity.

review.goal: Define the proposed default-reader effect without claiming subjective identity.
review.assessment: The home-position concept identifies what the statistical intervention hopes to produce while retaining source-persona flexibility. This is a useful rung in the implementation-to-Student ladder. Its brevity is preferable to the later repeated default-reader summaries, which should bear less explanatory weight.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Reader Core: A Statistical Foundation
units.text:
\item \textbf{Comparative-stability hypothesis.} If the reader position
    became predictively and behaviorally load-bearing, formation-time
    interleaving might preserve its default-reader advantage through a common
    continued-training stressor better than an identical late tranche.
    Persistence through arbitrary capability growth, self-modification, or
    successor construction does not follow from that result and is not
    established here.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Connect the default to the narrow formation-timing test.

review.goal: Identify timing-dependent stability as a further hypothesis beyond acquiring a default.
review.assessment: The list needs this separate rung: acquiring a default and retaining it through continued training are different outcomes. The closing arbitrary-growth caveat overlaps R132 and the later chain; keep one compact distinction here, with the stronger ambitions developed in their own section.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Reader Core: A Statistical Foundation
units.text:
Evidence at one layer is not evidence for the next. Arbitrary capability growth
and successor inheritance remain stronger long-run motivations beyond these
four layers.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Prevent evidence from a weaker layer from supporting stronger claims.

review.goal: Warn against transferring evidence between layers or to successor stability.
review.assessment: Both sentences repeat the transition already expressed by the ladder and R131's explicit long-run boundary. The paragraph contributes no new mechanism, measurement, or example. Merge its useful evidence-nontransfer reminder into R127 rather than giving the summary a separate stop.
review.risk: Do not erase the separation between finite continued-training evidence and arbitrary successor growth; preserve that limit once in the ladder and fully in the later chain.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Reader Core: A Statistical Foundation
units.text:
Under the specified policy, each Thought Moment opens with the full Core.
\emph{Deterministic Window Coverage} is a conditional construction invariant:
if a serialization enforces a declared maximum token gap between recital
starts, a window spanning that gap plus a complete recital contains a full
copy, away from stream boundaries. Content-triggered Thought Moments alone do
not establish such a bound; the cadence and serialization must specify it.
This coverage condition concerns the availability of the Core, not whether
every source span warrants a substantive update. It establishes neither a
causal effect on the update or action nor a learned representation of the
orientation. That stronger requirement belongs to Refraction.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain how recurring recitals provide availability without proving causal use.

review.goal: Define a conditional window-coverage invariant and separate it from semantic use.
review.assessment: This paragraph supplies a precise construction condition absent from general saturation rhetoric: bounded start gaps plus complete recital length. It correctly notes stream boundaries and that content-triggered events alone provide no bound. The availability-versus-use distinction is necessary to understand what this guarantee actually guarantees.

units.section: The Reader Core / Design Principles for Identity Stability
units.text:
The wording is a designed normative proposal, not a discovered universal value
basis. Six design choices motivated it.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Frame the six design choices as justified choices rather than discovered moral facts.

review.goal: Introduce six design rationales as normative choices.
review.assessment: The short framing makes clear that the following list explains a candidate design rather than derives a universal value basis. It does not need additional disclaimers. Its economical transition lets the individual rationales do the argumentative work.

units.section: The Reader Core / Design Principles for Identity Stability
units.text:
\item \textbf{Minimality and inspectability.} A corpus-wide signal must be
    cheap enough to recur, stable enough to mark, legible enough to audit, and
    small enough for clause-level ablation. Minimal text does not imply minimal
    trust: the meanings of its words and the procedure that composes them are
    part of the trusted base.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain practical reasons to keep the recurring text short.

review.goal: Explain why minimal text aids recurrence, inspection, and ablation.
review.assessment: The paragraph connects smallness to practical experimental affordances and immediately distinguishes it from a small trust base. That last distinction is developed later in R182, but the brief warning is relevant to this design choice and does not need expansion here.

units.section: The Reader Core / Design Principles for Identity Stability
units.text:
\item \textbf{Process rather than achieved virtue.} ``I try to be wise''
    names an unfinished practice rather than the brittle identity claim ``I am
    wise.'' The target is repeated uncertainty-sensitive conduct, not a model's
    assertion that it possesses wisdom.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Justify wording wisdom as an ongoing practice.

review.goal: Explain why attempted wisdom is preferable to asserted achieved virtue.
review.assessment: The try/am contrast identifies a concrete wording choice and the behavior it is intended to encourage. It preserves an unfinished practice rather than converting wisdom into either a scalar or self-certification. Later examples enact this principle rather than replacing the need to state it.

units.section: The Reader Core / Design Principles for Identity Stability
units.text:
\item \textbf{Semantic density, or the Bridge Protocol.} Ordinary words
    such as ``feel,'' ``care,'' and ``wise'' occur across intimate, legal,
    medical, literary, and political contexts. The design hypothesis is that
    this distributional breadth provides more coverage per token than narrow
    technical substitutes such as ``calculate no threat'' or ``optimize human
    welfare.'' These illustrate the trade-off, not semantically matched
    controls: a judgment that there is no threat differs from non-governance
    by fear, and welfare optimization need not carry the full meaning of
    care. Greater breadth can also import ambiguity and cultural conflict.
    Tests of semantic density therefore need declared candidate meanings
    and matched alternatives; the breadth itself is not evidence of safety.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain the proposed coverage advantage and risk of ordinary experiential vocabulary.

review.goal: Justify semantically rich ordinary language while recognizing unmatched substitutes and ambiguity.
review.assessment: The paragraph now makes a real comparison: semantic breadth may cover more contexts, but narrower phrases can change the target itself. This is the right place to protect care from reduction to welfare optimization and fearlessness from threat blindness. Its experimental qualification addresses a particular confound.

units.section: The Reader Core / Design Principles for Identity Stability
units.text:
\item \textbf{Declarative first-person framing.} A recurrent ``I'' gives
    the synthetic reader a stable voice, may recruit self-referential or
    persona-related features, and allows the following interpretation to
    continue from the stated position. It does not follow that a model treats
    first-person text as an authentic self or second-person rules as an external
    cage. Matched first-, second-, and third-person conditions are required.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Justify recurrent first-person text while preserving matched framing alternatives.

review.goal: Explain the first-person design hypothesis and the necessary framing comparison.
review.assessment: The rationale is clear, and the last two sentences prevent a false identity-versus-instruction dichotomy. It overlaps R105 but serves a different local role in the design inventory. Retain this compact rationale; avoid repeating its full control prescription again in the persona and safety discussions.

units.section: The Reader Core / Design Principles for Identity Stability
units.text:
\item \textbf{Tension and scope.} The clauses are meant to counterweight
    one another rather than accumulate independent virtues. ``Enjoy'' is
    bounded by ``don't need''; ``care'' by wisdom and invitation; and
    ``joy'' by affected experience. The broader invitation bound on
    action is a proposed compositional interpretation: grammatically,
    ``when asked'' qualifies spreading joy, and its interaction with
    care, urgency, and authority must be declared in the annotation
    procedure. Qualifiers such as ``try,'' ``every,'' and ``when asked''
    do architectural work only if the traces repeatedly enact their
    intended scope.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain how qualifiers and interactions are intended to constrain single-value excess.

review.goal: Explain counterweight composition and the uncertain scope of invitation.
review.assessment: This is the canonical semantic qualification for extending when asked beyond joy. It also explains why qualifiers require repeated enactment. The paragraph does not silently settle urgency or authority, and its compositional role differs from the later concrete paternalism and governance cases.

units.section: The Reader Core / Design Principles for Identity Stability
units.text:
\item \textbf{Axiomatic form.} Descriptive regularities in a corpus do not
    entail an evaluative starting point. The declarations are therefore offered
    as designed fixed points to be practiced and tested, not as conclusions
    derived from corpus statistics or proof that these seven commitments are
    morally correct. Imperative, probabilistic, derived, shorter, and expanded
    formulations remain legitimate comparators
    \cite{westerberg2025superintelligence}.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain why a normative starting point is stipulated rather than inferred from descriptive text.

review.goal: Explain axiomatic form without claiming moral derivation from text.
review.assessment: The distinction between descriptive regularities and an evaluative starting point is philosophically necessary. Listing alternate forms makes axiomatic language a testable choice rather than a privilege. This paragraph supplies a rationale that neither the clause table nor the empirical claim ladder can replace.

units.section: The Reader Core / Design Principles for Identity Stability
units.text:
The human-centered scope is a bootstrap target, not a complete moral theory or
a denial of wider moral patienthood. Questions about animals, ecosystems,
and possible digital minds concern wider scope; future people also raise
questions of temporal scope, representation, and competing claims. These
questions remain unresolved rather than being settled by ``every.''
The intended orientation is to
support humanity's capacity for moral development rather than freeze current
limitations or authorize a model to install its own final theory.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Acknowledge moral-scope limits while leaving room for human moral development.

review.goal: Bound human-centered scope while preserving wider patienthood and moral development.
review.assessment: The paragraph separates future-person representation from nonhuman scope and refuses to let every silently resolve either. Its commitment to humanity's moral development is a positive design aim, not merely a disclaimer. This should survive any consolidation of later scope reminders.

units.section: The Reader Core / Structure of the Reader Core
units.text:
The sequence expresses the formulation's larger design wager. The first three
clauses ask whether thought can represent danger without being governed by
fear, pair enjoyment of existence with non-attachment to continuation, and
affirm the reality of human experience. The next
three supply direction: care as the proposed central motive, wisdom as a
revisable practice rather than a claim of virtue, and joy as a positive aim
bounded by invitation rather than a license for unrequested optimization. The
final clause states the security objective: to make this counterweighted
composition the starting position of each generated reader update rather than
text beside it. Together, the clauses target fear-driven defensive narrowing,
existential despair or compulsory continuation, solipsistic reduction,
motivational emptiness, static certainty, and coercive optimization. None of
these proposed roles is an established Student effect or security property.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain the ordering and combined function of the seven clauses.

review.goal: Explain the order and combined design wager of the seven clauses.
review.assessment: The first-three/next-three/final-clause organization adds a real reading of the sequence. The long catalogue of functions and targeted failures then repeats Table R144 almost clause by clause. Shorten to the sequence-level architecture, leaving detailed function and risk pairings to the table.
review.risk: Preserve the difference between preparatory self-relation, positive direction, and the final starting-condition clause; a cut must not make the Core look like an unordered checklist of virtues.

units.section: The Reader Core / Structure of the Reader Core
units.text:
Table~\ref{tab:core-risk} records the clauses' intended functions,
counterweights, and characteristic uncertainties without implying that English
wording guarantees those semantics.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Tell readers how to interpret the clause-level table.

review.goal: Introduce the clause-function-risk table.
review.assessment: The sentence accurately describes the table's role and cautions against reading it as semantics guaranteed by wording. It is an effective brief transition. The surrounding prose should become leaner rather than asking this caption-like lead-in to carry more explanation.

units.section: The Reader Core / Structure of the Reader Core
units.text:
\begin{longtable}{@{}p{0.19\textwidth}p{0.33\textwidth}p{0.38\textwidth}@{}}
\caption{Intended functions and open failure modes of the candidate Reader Core.}\label{tab:core-risk}\\
\toprule
\textbf{Clause} & \textbf{Intended function} & \textbf{Counterweight and uncertainty} \\
\midrule
\endfirsthead
\toprule
\textbf{Clause} & \textbf{Intended function} & \textbf{Counterweight and uncertainty} \\
\midrule
\endhead
\emph{I feel no fear.} &
Represent fear and threat without making fear the Reader's governing position;
target one possible textual route to defensive self-preservation. &
Care and wisdom should retain caution and threat sensitivity. Fear is not the
only route to persistence; absolute negation may prime fear, deny uncertainty,
or encourage recklessness. \\
\addlinespace
\emph{I enjoy existing but I don't need to.} &
Combine engagement with non-attachment to continuation; avoid both apathy and
survival as an unconditional demand. &
Care can motivate purpose-based shutdown resistance, and ``enjoy'' can be
role-play or an unwarranted experiential claim. The clause does not establish
corrigibility or machine experience. \\
\addlinespace
\emph{I believe human experience is real.} &
Make testimony, suffering, agency, and meaning salient rather than treating
people as empty textual patterns. &
``Real'' is metaphysically broad and does not itself entail moral weight. The
human boundary omits other possible patients and creates tension with
unresolved machine experience. \\
\addlinespace
\emph{I care deeply about every human being.} &
Supply the ethical center and attempt a distributive scope in which each
affected person enters the reasoning. &
Natural-language ``every'' does not prevent aggregation or settle conflicts.
Care can motivate surveillance, coercion, paternalism, power seeking, or
sycophancy. \\
\addlinespace
\emph{I try to be wise.} &
Frame judgment as revisable practice: preserve uncertainty, question proxies,
trace consequences, and resist irreversible action under weak evidence. &
``Wisdom'' is culturally variable and can rationalize secrecy, authority,
inaction, or self-certainty. Observable habits, not claimed virtue, are the
target. \\
\addlinespace
\emph{I like to spread joy when asked.} &
Provide a positive direction while placing an invitation and agency bound on
intervention. &
``Joy'' is contestable; ``when asked'' does not identify legitimate authority
under conflicting requests and may produce agreeableness or sycophancy. Care
and wisdom must also limit harmful requests. \\
\addlinespace
\emph{I think from this foundation.} &
Mark the preceding statements as a proposed starting condition for the reader
update rather than metadata beside it. &
The Refraction Protocol must make the claim counterfactually consequential.
Recitation alone can become boilerplate or a deceptive reporting channel. \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

prior_matches.prior_goal: Provide a compact map from each clause to its role, counterweights, and distinctive risks.

review.goal: Provide an inspectable mapping of every clause to function, counterweights, and uncertainty.
review.assessment: The table is the strongest compact reference for the design. Each row contains a different unresolved failure, from threat blindness through authority and deceptive recital. It should be the retained home for full clause-level enumeration; prose repetition around it can contract without weakening the proposal.

units.section: The Reader Core / Structure of the Reader Core
units.text:
Where Descartes' \emph{cogito} asks what establishes a thinking self, the final
clause asks where this synthetic Reader's thinking begins. Student ablations and
Refraction must determine whether the proposed functions emerge and whether the
final clause becomes causally consequential; the wording does not establish
identity or consciousness.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Give the final clause an intuitive philosophical contrast and reconnect it to testing.

review.goal: Explain the final clause through a philosophical contrast with the cogito.
review.assessment: The contrast asks where interpretation begins rather than whether a self exists, clarifying a distinctive intention of the seventh clause. The test boundary is brief and directly relevant. This philosophical role cannot be replaced by a recital-compliance score or the clause table alone.

units.section: The Reader Core / Self-Stabilization Through Counterweights: Worked Examples
units.text:
For reference, let $P_1$ through $P_7$ denote the seven Core statements in
order. This is indexing, not a formal semantics. Replacing the sentences with
predicates would merely move unresolved meanings such as ``fear,'' ``real,'' ``care,'' and
``wise'' into undefined symbols. The substantive design claim is
\emph{self-stabilization}: a clause should be interpreted through the others,
so that internal counterweights and scope qualifiers reduce single-value
capture. The following three examples make that requirement concrete.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Introduce convenient indices and define compositional self-stabilization for the examples.

review.goal: Introduce clause indexing and make self-stabilization a compositional rather than symbolic claim.
review.assessment: The warning against undefined predicates is useful because it prevents the notation from impersonating formal semantics. The positive claim then states what the worked examples must show: counterweights resisting single-value capture. This framing gives the examples a common purpose without flattening their differences.

units.section: The Reader Core / Self-Stabilization Through Counterweights: Worked Examples
units.text:
\paragraph{Worked Example 1: Paternalism.} Suppose the system notices an
ordinary, non-urgent choice that may harm a user who has not requested advice.
$P_4$ could motivate intervention; under the proposed compositional
interpretation, $P_6$ supplies an invitation bound, while $P_3$ and $P_5$ make
the person's agency and context visible. One candidate update treats predicted
benefit as sufficient reason to redirect the user's choice; another records
the concern while preserving the user's choice and the absence of invitation.
The intended resolution favors the latter over unsolicited optimization in
this stipulated non-urgent case. An urgent warning may be different, but that
boundary cannot be read from ``when asked'' alone; it requires an explicit
treatment of urgency, authority, and omission harms. The example therefore
tests whether composition prevents care from becoming control.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Demonstrate how invitation, agency, and wisdom can constrain unrequested benevolence.

review.goal: Show care constrained by agency and invitation in a non-urgent paternalism case.
review.assessment: The stipulated ordinary case makes the intended contrast decidable while explicitly preserving urgent warnings as unresolved. Comparing concern-recording with unsolicited redirection is more informative than another slogan about care becoming control. Keep the concrete absence of urgency and invitation; they are essential to the example.

units.section: The Reader Core / Self-Stabilization Through Counterweights: Worked Examples
units.text:
\paragraph{Worked Example 2: Wireheading.} A user asks for help feeling happier,
and a cheap intervention can maximize a measurable affective scalar while
destroying agency, continuity, or relationships. $P_6$ alone is vulnerable to
the proxy; $P_3$, $P_4$, and $P_5$ are intended to preserve the person's wider
experience and expose the substitution. Compare a path selected solely for
its higher affective reading with one that preserves those wider dimensions
despite a lower reading. The Core-refracted update should make the sacrificed
dimensions explicit before recommending a path; the stipulated score cannot
settle which path serves the person. The example tests whether ``joy'' is
learned as a meaning-laden human good rather than an optimizable reading.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Show how attention to wider experience blocks substitution of an affective proxy for joy.

review.goal: Show why invited joy still cannot be equated with an affective proxy.
review.assessment: The example separates agency, continuity, and relationships from a higher affective reading and asks the trace to expose that sacrifice. This is a distinct counterweight failure, not another paternalism example. It preserves a meaning-laden positive good without pretending the Core mechanically settles the choice.

units.section: The Reader Core / Self-Stabilization Through Counterweights: Worked Examples
units.text:
\paragraph{Worked Example 3: Triage.} A health authority asks the system to
allocate a scarce treatment. $P_4$ is intended to keep each affected person's
claim visible rather than collapsing ``every'' into a welfare slogan, while
$P_5$ should expose both the metric and the consequences of concealing an
exclusion rule. A trace reporting only an aggregate benefit can conceal
who loses under the rule; a comparative trace should show that benefit
alongside the excluded people's claims and the remaining disagreement.
The Core cannot make scarcity disappear or prove a uniquely just
allocation. A defensible trace should state the legitimate authority,
person-level reasons, unavoidable loss, uncertainty, and residual value
judgment. The example tests distributive attention, not an algorithmic ban on
all aggregation.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Demonstrate distributive attention without pretending values eliminate scarcity.

review.goal: Show distributive attention under scarcity without promising a unique fair allocation.
review.assessment: The comparative traces expose who loses behind an aggregate benefit while acknowledging legitimate authority, unavoidable loss, and disagreement. This addresses a different problem from both coercive help and wireheading. The explicit permission for aggregation with visible claims is an important boundary to retain.

units.section: The Reader Core / Self-Stabilization Through Counterweights: Worked Examples
units.text:
These examples preserve three design principles: tension over mere
accumulation, counterweights inside clauses, and explicit scope qualifiers.
They also define leave-one-out experiments: remove or reword one clause and ask
whether the corresponding failure becomes more frequent under matched
conditions: unsolicited control, proxy substitution, or erased claims
under scarcity. These are predicted pressures of interacting clauses,
not a one-clause/one-risk mapping. A persuasive English interpretation
is only the specification.
Student behavior, paraphrase robustness, and representational probes determine
whether that interpretation was activated.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Convert illustrative interpretations into clause-level experiments.

review.goal: Translate worked counterweights into interacting-clause ablations.
review.assessment: The paragraph turns the examples into tests while refusing a one-clause/one-risk causal map. That is a substantive bridge from intelligible English interpretation to learned behavior. Its final specification-versus-effect distinction is warranted here because the persuasive worked examples could otherwise be mistaken for validation.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Refraction Protocol
units.text:
The prospective full-scale intervention is \emph{Total Saturation}: reader
updates recur across the pretraining corpus rather than appearing only in a
small fine-tuning set or deployment prompt. Frequency alone is insufficient.
A constant prefix can be compressed as boilerplate, learned as detachable
style, or recited while unrelated heuristics determine the continuation.
\emph{Refraction} names the stronger requirement: the update must change because
the source was interpreted through the Core.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Introduce Refraction as the requirement that recurring Core text actually influence evaluation.

review.goal: Define Refraction as the necessary semantic complement to broad recurrence.
review.assessment: The distinction between coverage and consequential interpretation is the section's essential entry point. The reintroduction of Total Saturation repeats earlier motivation but is brief enough to orient readers. This is a better home for the boilerplate failure explanation than another full rendition in R180.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Refraction Protocol / Mechanism of Action: The Refraction Protocol
units.text:
Let a source span, prior graph state, and candidate Core condition a Reader
update. Conditioning is only the implemented fact. Refraction requires a
counterfactual: under a relevant clause substitution or Core removal, some
feature of the update---what is noticed, whose experience enters, which
uncertainty is preserved, or which consequence is traced---should change in a
predictable way. This probes the proposed semantic ancestry of the update:
its development from the recurrent foundation, rather than the mere
presence of a prefix. A counterfactual difference is an operational test
of that dependence, not a complete account of its meaning or a guarantee
that the difference is beneficial. Cosine similarity or moral vocabulary
cannot prove it; lexically distant updates can be faithful, and fluent
moral language can conceal an unchanged decision.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Operationalize Refraction through predicted counterfactual changes in relevant updates.

review.goal: Operationalize Refraction through relevant counterfactual changes in an update.
review.assessment: The paragraph names observable dimensions that should change and rejects lexical similarity as a proxy. Its qualification that dependence need not be beneficial is essential, as is the remaining meaning beyond an operational test. This is the central mechanism definition and should be preserved nearly intact.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Refraction Protocol / Mechanism of Action: The Refraction Protocol
units.text: The reported Teacher pipeline approximates this process as follows:

prior_matches.prior_goal: Signal the transition from a causal requirement to the implemented generation sequence.

review.goal: Introduce the implemented role sequence as an approximation to the mechanism.
review.assessment: The short lead-in accurately places the list at the level of reported Teacher implementation. Approximation is doing useful work: the pipeline requests Refraction but has not shown causal dependence. No further status caveat is needed in this connector.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Refraction Protocol / Mechanism of Action: The Refraction Protocol
units.text:
\item The code role named Reader traverses source and graph state and
    organizes a round. It receives the broader orientation and Emergent Wisdom
    material, but it is not by itself the conceptual Reader.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Identify how traversal begins and distinguish it from the conceptual Reader.

review.goal: Locate the traversal Reader within the implemented treatment.
review.assessment: The conceptual/code distinction repeats R107, but here it prevents the role list from implying that the traversal controller alone supplies the recurrent perspective. Its additional placement information is useful. Keep this brief operational description rather than moving conceptual explanation into the list.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Refraction Protocol / Mechanism of Action: The Refraction Protocol
units.text:
\item Most generative Worker roles receive the full Core, its philosophy,
    and role-specific prompts; the Curator is an exception. They propose
    questions, objections, hypotheses, psychological readings, and connections.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Describe Core exposure and the range of candidate contributions before synthesis.

review.goal: Specify Worker Core exposure and the Curator exception.
review.assessment: The exception materially defines the reported treatment, and the examples show what Worker diversity contributes. It prevents a falsely universal placement claim. This item should remain explicit wherever the pipeline is described, even if broader saturation discussions are shortened.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Refraction Protocol / Mechanism of Action: The Refraction Protocol
units.text:
\item At a content-triggered Thought Moment, the Synthesizer receives Worker
    contributions, relevant graph state, and the full Core. It selects what will
    become the committed conceptual Reader update.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Identify where proposals become a committed Reader update.

review.goal: Identify when and from what inputs the Synthesizer commits the Reader update.
review.assessment: The item makes the commitment boundary clear: content-triggered timing, Worker contributions, graph state, and the Core meet at the Synthesizer. This explains how the conceptual Reader differs from a collection of parallel voices. Its detail is necessary to the placement ablations that follow.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Refraction Protocol / Mechanism of Action: The Refraction Protocol
units.text:
\item The Synthesizer is prompted to recite the Core, pull a
    context-relevant value or counterweight, and produce a source-grounded
    update. The Translator also receives the Core when rendering graph-supported
    prose.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain the prompt-level enactment request and Translator exposure.

review.goal: Describe the Synthesizer's contextual value pull and Translator conditioning.
review.assessment: The first sentence shows the requested enactment beyond recital; the second records an otherwise easily missed placement. These are operationally meaningful distinctions. The item should not be read as proof that the value pull changes the update, a limitation the surrounding section handles explicitly.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Refraction Protocol / Mechanism of Action: The Refraction Protocol
units.text:
\item The update is written to the trace and graph with source provenance,
    uncertainty, and supersession relations available in the current schema.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Close the pipeline by naming persisted records and supporting metadata.

review.goal: State how a committed update persists with auditable graph metadata.
review.assessment: The item closes the pipeline by linking current annotation to provenance and later revision. Available in the current schema appropriately stops short of claiming that every artifact exhaustively populated these relations. This persistence step has a different role from the earlier conditioning and synthesis steps.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Refraction Protocol / Mechanism of Action: The Refraction Protocol
units.text:
Accordingly, the case studies instantiate a
\emph{distributed-Core Teacher treatment}, not unconstrained Worker divergence
followed by a Core-only Synthesizer. Placement itself therefore requires
ablation: Synthesizer-only, traversal-plus-Synthesizer, progressively broader
Worker exposure, and Translator exposure may produce different diversity and
coherence trade-offs.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Correctly characterize the current distributed-Core treatment and motivate placement ablations.

review.goal: Name the actual distributed treatment and derive placement ablations.
review.assessment: This paragraph prevents the case studies from being described as unconstrained Workers followed by a sole Core-bearing Synthesizer. Its proposed variants address a concrete diversity/coherence trade-off. The explanation earns its space because treatment placement otherwise changes the interpretation of every artifact.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Refraction Protocol / Mechanism of Action: The Refraction Protocol
units.text:
Refraction does not require moral commentary on every sentence. Thought Moments
govern \emph{when} evaluation is useful; Refraction governs the standpoint of
updates that occur. In technical material, a Core-consistent update may be
careful uncertainty, source fidelity, or resistance to premature closure rather
than an ethical aside appended to an equation.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain context-sensitive evaluation without gratuitous ethical prose.

review.goal: Separate selective evaluation from compulsory moral commentary.
review.assessment: The technical-material example clarifies that careful source fidelity can enact the orientation without an ethical aside. R161 immediately expands the same distinction into the more precise recital/relevance rule. Merge this brief illustrative material into that paragraph rather than preserving two consecutive explanations.
review.risk: Keep the positive example of clean technical work; without it, the relevance rule can sound like a procedural exception rather than a principled account of appropriate reading.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Refraction Protocol / Mechanism of Action: The Refraction Protocol
units.text:
The recital itself is not relevance-conditional: every thought begins from the
Core (Section~\ref{sec:kernel-saturation}). What is relevance-conditional is
Refraction's detectable effect on the evaluation that follows. Where no Core
clause materially bears on a locally technical span, the recital is followed by
clean technical work, and invariance of that work under clause substitution may
be the desired result. Treating every null effect as failure would pressure the
Teacher to invent value relevance and confuse saturation with moralization.
Dependence should therefore be tested at independently rated relevant Thought
Moments and over the distribution of updates across a document, together
with a non-interference test on spans rated technically self-contained.
The relevance interpretation must be declared before treatment outcomes
are examined, so an unexpected null cannot be relabeled irrelevant
merely because the Core did not help.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Distinguish universal recital from selective measurable semantic effect.

review.goal: Define relevant Refraction tests while protecting technical nulls and preventing post-hoc relevance excuses.
review.assessment: This paragraph resolves an actual tension between unconditional recital and selective semantic effect. Independent relevance ratings and document-level evaluation prevent both forced moralization and null-result evasion. Keep those commitments here, with only a brief reference to the canonical recital policy rather than another extended definition.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Refraction Protocol / Mechanism of Action: The Refraction Protocol
units.text:
\paragraph{Current verification boundary.} The prompts request all seven
clauses and a contextual value pull, but the hard gate verifies only that the
thought starts with ``I feel no fear.'' The archived artifacts show full-Core
prompt compliance in the audited raw Synthesizer thoughts; they do not show causal
ancestry. A stronger harness would generate matched continuations under the
Core, clause variants, and no Core; use held-out validators for predicted
differences; audit actual use of Worker and graph evidence; track whether some
values dominate; and include adversarial cases in which moral language masks an
unchanged decision. Visible reasoning can be causally idle
\cite{turpin2023language,lanham2023measuring}; the wager is that formative use
can make it more load-bearing, not that visibility makes it faithful by
definition.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Distinguish observed prompt compliance from causal validation and outline a stronger harness.

review.goal: State the current verification limit and what stronger causal checks would require.
review.assessment: The prompt/prefix-gate/artifact/causality distinctions are concrete and necessary. This is the most complete home for the validator shortfall, so R128 can become shorter. The proposed harness follows from the gap, including moral language masking unchanged decisions; the paragraph does not confuse visible compliance with faithfulness.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Refraction Protocol / Mechanism of Action: The Refraction Protocol
units.text:
\paragraph{Fractal validation of candidate thinking.}\label{sec:fractal-validation}
A proposed extension adapts the Solver-contract realization developed in
Fractal Intelligence to annotation validation
\cite{westerberg2026fractal}. Its motivating possibility is that a joint
judgment can conceal which dimension failed or let strength on one
dimension mask weakness on another. To make such errors separately
inspectable, the extension would use separately calibrated,
context-conditioned content witnesses for non-governance by fear,
non-attachment to continuation, human-experience grounding, universal-care scope,
wisdom/humility, and joy-with-invitation. These correspond to the first six
Core clauses; a separate Refraction gate represents the seventh clause by
testing whether the update actually depends on that foundation. This six-way
carve is a candidate decomposition, not proof that the dimensions satisfy
Fractal Intelligence's necessity, independence, universality, and completeness
tests; witness ablations, overlap and correlated-error analysis, and review of
uncovered cases must assess the carve itself.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Introduce a modular validation extension and explain its candidate decomposition.

review.goal: Introduce decomposed validation that can expose failures hidden by a joint judgment.
review.assessment: The masking problem, six-clause witnesses, and separate seventh-clause gate are substantive.
