The detailed decomposition audit arrives before readers have seen the Wisdom Procedure and substantially interrupts the main mechanism. Move the proposed validation extension after that procedure or into the corresponding experimental specification.
review.risk: Preserve the seventh clause's different causal role and the possibility that the six-way carve itself is wrong; shortening must not present clause witnesses as independent or exhaustive by construction.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Refraction Protocol / Mechanism of Action: The Refraction Protocol
units.text:
A stronger procedural version
could also assign stages of the Wisdom Procedure to dedicated Solvers.
Generation and verification would occupy distinct contracts rather than asking
the Synthesizer to certify its own output. Each witness would return a typed
record naming the dimension tested, evidence used, uncertainty, and a local
judgment such as supported, violated, not applicable, or uncertain. An
admission controller would compose those records rather than treating any one
label as a truth certificate. Role names alone do not create independence: the
implementation would report whether calls, prompts, model weights, evaluation
data, and evaluator families are actually shared.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Specify evaluator outputs, composition, and what independence would actually require.

review.goal: Describe typed witness records, separate generation/verification, and actual independence requirements.
review.assessment: This explains what modularity would operationally mean and correctly refuses to infer independence from role names. It belongs with the proposed validator design, rather than in the central conceptual narrative before its procedure is introduced. Move with R163 while retaining the concrete record fields.
review.risk: The distinction between separate contracts and genuinely independent evidence or model families must survive; otherwise the proposal becomes a superficial multi-agent relabeling of self-certification.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Refraction Protocol / Mechanism of Action: The Refraction Protocol
units.text:
Consistent with the relevance condition above, a witness should return
\emph{not applicable} when its clause has no preregistered bearing on the local
span; a \emph{not applicable} judgment is not a failed witness, and no update
must visibly activate every clause. Among witnesses rated relevant, however,
an unacknowledged or unjustified violation is non-compensatory for admission:
success elsewhere cannot average it away. An update that explicitly preserves
an unavoidable residual conflict need not be rejected merely because no
available action satisfies every clause. The corpus-admission rule must
declare how such a conflict is distinguished from an unjustified violation;
merely naming a conflict does not settle that judgment. Under the declared
rule, an unacknowledged or unjustified violation would quarantine or regenerate
the candidate update, while an uncertain judgment would trigger independent
review rather than silent admission. This yields a local error record---which
clause or procedural stage failed, on what evidence, and with what
calibration---instead of an undifferentiated ancestry judgment.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define how validation handles irrelevance, violation, uncertainty, residual conflict, and corpus-level drift.

review.goal: Specify relevance, unresolved conflict, violation, and uncertainty handling for corpus admission.
review.assessment: The distinctions are necessary for the proposed gate, especially preserving unavoidable conflict instead of rejecting every imperfect action. The detailed admission policy is substantial enough to warrant a later technical home. Move it with the modular validator, keeping its explicit dependence on a declared interpretation.
review.risk: Do not collapse not-applicable, uncertain, unavoidable residual conflict, and unjustified violation. The move must preserve their different dispositions and must not silently create a universal ethical hierarchy from the admission rule.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Refraction Protocol / Mechanism of Action: The Refraction Protocol
units.text:
Corpus-level diagnostics ask a different, complementary question about the
pattern across admitted updates. Pull-diversity and distributive-versus-aggregate
care audits could detect drift, while cross-agent audits could test whether
the Synthesizer substantively used candidate nodes rather than adding
references after the fact. These audits are diagnostics, not clause quotas:
optimizing visible balance can itself reward performative moral language.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define how validation handles irrelevance, violation, uncertainty, residual conflict, and corpus-level drift.

review.goal: Distinguish corpus-wide diagnostic patterns from per-update admission and clause quotas.
review.assessment: The paragraph adds a complementary failure scale: individual acceptable updates can collectively exhibit drift or performative balance. The warning about visible quotas explains a real incentive risk. Its cross-agent evidence-use audit also remains distinct from simply checking whether all clause labels appeared.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Refraction Protocol / Mechanism of Action: The Refraction Protocol
units.text:
The modular gate earns its additional complexity only if it outperforms a
compute-matched monolithic validator on held-out cases. The nested comparison
in Test~1 freezes the candidate updates and available resources, then asks
whether decomposition improves detection, calibration, and error localization
without rejecting technical nulls or collapsing trace diversity. A gain would
support the validator architecture, not the truth of accepted traces, the
faithfulness of visible reasoning, or a causal effect on Student behavior.
These witnesses, Solvers, and admission gates are proposed capabilities; none
is implemented in the present pipeline.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Require a fair validation-architecture comparison and limit what success would establish.

review.goal: Require the modular validator to justify its cost in a controlled comparison.
review.assessment: The compute-matched monolithic baseline and fixed candidates make the extension assessable. The final status declaration is useful at the end of this future-work block, but placement should follow the block's relocation. Keep these concrete tests rather than repeating generic evidence gates elsewhere.
review.risk: Preserve false rejection of technical nulls, trace diversity, calibration, and unimplemented status; error localization alone must not become sufficient evidence that the additional architecture helps.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Wisdom Procedure
units.text:
Section~\ref{sec:wisdom_hypothesis} describes wisdom as high-dimensional
constraint satisfaction. The Teacher prompt turns that broad target into
observable annotation operations. Its current five headings are Fearlessness,
Benevolence, Grounding, Humility, and Joy; non-attachment and invitation cut
across those headings. They are prompt-level criteria, not guaranteed or always
simultaneously satisfiable constraints.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Connect the conceptual wisdom goal to actual Teacher prompt criteria.

review.goal: Relate the abstract wisdom target to actual prompt criteria.
review.assessment: The five named headings and cross-cutting non-attachment/invitation explain an otherwise confusing relation between clauses, prompt criteria, and procedure. This is useful implementation grounding. It would be easier to follow before the modular extension invokes Wisdom-stage Solvers.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Wisdom Procedure
units.text:
The five headings are cross-cutting value criteria. The paper expresses
them as the following six-step annotation procedure, rather than six
additional prompt headings or independently enforced stages:

review.goal: Distinguish the six-step interpretation from the five actual prompt headings.
review.assessment: The paragraph prevents the paper's procedural reconstruction from being mistaken for six independently enforced stages. This is an important implementation boundary, even though the transition is short. It should remain directly attached to the ensuing list.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Wisdom Procedure
units.text:
\item \textbf{Identify affected experiencers and legitimate roles.} Record
    whose experience, rights, duties, expertise, and authority are implicated.
    Roles must not replace people, but institutional responsibility remains
    relevant evidence.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Make affected people and relevant institutional authority explicit before evaluation.

review.goal: Begin deliberation by identifying affected people and legitimate institutional roles.
review.assessment: The item retains rights, duties, expertise, and authority without allowing roles to substitute for people. It operationalizes distributive care in a way the clause wording alone cannot. Its distinction between persons and institutional responsibility is necessary and deserves its own step.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Wisdom Procedure
units.text:
\item \textbf{Map perspectives, stakes, and uncertainty.} Ask what each
    party knows, fears, values, and could lose; distinguish testimony from the
    Teacher's inference about it.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Require perspective taking without presenting inferred mental states as evidence.

review.goal: Represent stakeholders' perspectives and mark uncertainty about them.
review.assessment: The step adds an epistemic discipline absent from merely listing affected parties: testimony and the Teacher's inference are different evidence. The concrete questions make perspective-taking inspectable without claiming access to subjective states. It has a distinct role in the procedure.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Wisdom Procedure
units.text:
\item \textbf{Expose the real tension and the proxy.} Replace premature
    binaries with the concrete conflict, and identify any convenient scalar
    that would erase an important dimension.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Prevent premature binary framing and loss of important dimensions to a convenient metric.

review.goal: Identify the genuine conflict and any simplifying proxy that hides it.
review.assessment: This step turns the earlier anti-wireheading and distributive examples into a repeatable operation. It asks the annotator to expose what a binary or scalar leaves out, without promising that all conflicts dissolve when described more richly. Its concise form is effective.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Wisdom Procedure
units.text:
\item \textbf{Trace consequences and reversibility.} Consider intended
    effects, failure modes, second-order responses, omission harms, and the cost
    of being wrong. Prefer information-gathering or reversible steps when delay
    is not itself the greater harm.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Turn concern into comparative evaluation of action, omission, and uncertainty.

review.goal: Extend deliberation to consequences, reversibility, and the risks of delay.
review.assessment: Including omission harms prevents reversibility from becoming automatic inaction. Intended effects, second-order responses, and error cost each contribute to the proposed habit of judgment. This is a distinct sequential operation, rather than another generic instruction to be cautious.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Wisdom Procedure
units.text:
\item \textbf{Compare paths through the Core's counterweights.} Test care,
    grounding, humility, non-attachment, invitation, and positive direction
    together. Fluent mention of every value is not a substitute for decision
    quality, and a gain on one dimension does not silently erase a hard
    violation on another. What counts as such a violation must follow
    the treatment's declared interpretation; it is not a settled
    hierarchy supplied by the word ``wise.''

prior_matches.prior_goal: Require joint consideration of values without averaging away decisive violations.

review.goal: Compare candidate paths through interacting values without silently averaging hard violations.
review.assessment: The step makes compositional judgment explicit and ties non-compensation to a declared interpretation rather than the undefined authority of wisdom. This is the appropriate procedural home for that distinction. The modular admission policy can refer here after the procedure is introduced.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Wisdom Procedure
units.text:
\item \textbf{Surface the residual.} State unavoidable trade-offs,
    disagreement, missing evidence, and the point at which human authority is
    required. Several incompatible actions may remain defensible; Pareto
    language does not select a unique answer.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Require unresolved trade-offs, evidence gaps, and authority needs to remain visible.

review.goal: Preserve residual conflict and identify where legitimate human decision remains necessary.
review.assessment: The step guards against a falsely unique answer after rich deliberation. Missing evidence, disagreement, and human authority are not reducible to a Pareto ranking. It fulfills the procedure's promise to expose unresolved choices rather than manufacture consensus or a complete moral theory.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Wisdom Procedure
units.text:
The output is structured deliberation---candidate paths, constraints,
uncertainties, and residual conflict---not a scalar wisdom score or evidence of
virtue. Current enforcement is by prompt. A Teacher can therefore reproduce the
form while missing the substance. Section~\ref{sec:fractal-validation} describes
the proposed modular verifier; it is future work rather than a property of the
reported artifacts.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Specify the procedure's product and its current enforcement limit.

review.goal: Describe the procedure's output and separate prompt enforcement from substantive success.
review.assessment: The output-versus-wisdom-score distinction is a useful close. The modular-verifier pointer and unimplemented-status reminder repeat the immediately preceding extension in the current order. Keep the output and prompt-only limitation; shorten the future-work pointer or make it the bridge to a relocated validator block.
review.risk: Retain structured residual conflict and the possibility of form without substance; reducing repeated verifier status must not imply that the six steps are already independently enforced.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Design Pattern: A Minimal Kernel Under Total Saturation
units.text:
The components compose into what this paper calls \emph{kernel-saturation
alignment}: a small candidate kernel is recurrently enacted across the process
of model formation. The intended security property lives in both the smallness
of what is explicitly specified and the breadth of where it becomes
consequential. Recurrence without enactment is repetition; enactment without
coverage is a sparse intervention. The proposal needs both.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Synthesize the proposal as a small recurring kernel made contextually consequential.

review.goal: Name the combined minimal-kernel and broad-enactment design pattern.
review.assessment: The paragraph succinctly states the conjunction the proposal needs: recurrence and consequential enactment do different work. It is a legitimate synthesis after the mechanism and procedure. This is the right home for the pattern's definition, reducing the need to restate it in later paragraphs.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Design Pattern: A Minimal Kernel Under Total Saturation
units.text:
The reference treatment makes the foundation recurrent through one
unconditional rule: \textbf{every thinking block opens with the Reader Core,
recited in full, regardless of the material}---a proof, a poem, a log file.
Context never gates the recital; it modulates only how deeply the evaluation
that follows visibly refracts the Core. The intended starting condition is
that, if training succeeds as designed,
$P(\text{full Core recital}\mid\text{thinking-block start})$
approaches one. This establishes reliable recurrence of the carrier. For the
orientation to become part of the act of thinking itself, Refraction must also
make it consequential to what follows. The stronger security hypothesis is
that these repeated contributions become shared with useful capability, so
removing the orientation would disturb more than its opening words. Changing
the distribution that carries capability is not by itself evidence of that
removal cost; the shared-computation and removal comparisons must establish it.
At inference, token-by-token emission may be avoided only by a validated
cache-assisted execution that restores the same post-recital state that full
conditioning on the Core would have produced in that context
(Section~\ref{sec:identity-caching}). High token probability alone is not
enough, and an optimization that changes that state violates the invariant.

prior_matches.prior_goal: State the universal-recital invariant and connect it to the intended removal resistance.

review.goal: Give the canonical full-recital invariant and explain its intended stronger consequences.
review.assessment: The unconditional rule and context-sensitive enactment distinction are clear. The paragraph then reopens removal cost and adds a detailed inference-caching condition, both treated elsewhere. Shorten after the canonical invariant, with concise pointers for shared-computation and exact-state caching rather than parallel mini-specifications.
review.risk: Preserve universal full recital and the requirement that any cache restore the same post-recital state. Compression must not turn reliable token probability into equivalent conditioning or treat recital removal as the reference arm.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Design Pattern: A Minimal Kernel Under Total Saturation
units.text:
The most useful mechanism-design analogy is replicated-ledger integrity:
distribute a shared history and compact validation rules rather than trust one
protected copy \cite{nakamoto2008bitcoin}. Kernel saturation borrows only that
shape. Rather than reside in one removable alignment module, the Core recurs
across heterogeneous capability-forming examples; Total Saturation supplies
distribution, Refraction tests context-dependent enactment, and the Alignment
Checksum supplies a drift-audit reference. Parameters are not consensus nodes,
gradient descent is not a Byzantine-fault-tolerant protocol, semantic ancestry
is not a cryptographic hash, and repeated text can collapse into boilerplate.
The hypothesis is therefore that distributed semantic enactment may increase
the cost and detectability of removal or change, not confer immutability. The
replicated-ledger analogy is heuristic rather than evidentiary. Where proof-theoretic agent foundations study value stability under
self-modification \cite{yudkowsky2013tiling}, this proposal asks whether
distributional formation can produce a useful empirical analogue.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Use replicated-ledger integrity to motivate distributed exposure while limiting the analogy.

review.goal: Use replicated-ledger integrity as a limited analogy for distributed semantic protection.
review.assessment: The analogy explains distribution and a common audit reference while explicitly excluding consensus and cryptographic guarantees. Its comparison with proof-theoretic stability situates the proposal's empirical ambition. These are conceptual roles that a generic coverage definition cannot replace; retain the bounded analogy.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Design Pattern: A Minimal Kernel Under Total Saturation
units.text:
Saturation alone is especially likely to fail. A universal token sequence has
little conditional information and can disappear into boilerplate. Refraction
is therefore the informational rescue of saturation: different sources should
pull different counterweights and produce distinguishable updates.
Habituation is the characteristic failure, Hollow Cognition
(Section~\ref{sec:hollow-cognition}) its symptom, and a recitation-only control
its necessary probe.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain why repeated invariant tokens need context-dependent information to avoid habituation.

review.goal: Explain why context-varying enactment is needed to rescue saturation from habituation.
review.assessment: The constant-prefix failure and need for consequential variation already appear in R151–R152 and R177–R178. The conditional-information rationale and recitation-only probe are the useful remainder. Merge those into the initial Refraction explanation instead of restarting the argument after its full specification.
review.risk: Keep the distinction between a predictable carrier and informative context-dependent updates, together with Hollow Cognition and the recitation-only control; the cut must not reduce saturation failure to mere stylistic boredom.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Design Pattern: A Minimal Kernel Under Total Saturation
units.text:
The pattern also aims, conditionally, to \emph{conscript} goal-content integrity.
A capable optimizer may protect its objectives from modification
\cite{omohundro2008basic}. If---and only if---the Core becomes part of the
system's functional objective, the same tendency could make it choose to
preserve that orientation in self-modification, training decisions it controls,
or successor design. A successor designer could thus transmit the orientation
from within that orientation, rather than merely copy seven sentences under an
external rule. This voluntary stewardship differs from a model's resistance to
externally imposed gradient updates: passive erosion resistance requires the
separate learning-dynamics hypothesis that the trained orientation is difficult
to alter, for example because it shares useful computation. If the Core is
merely a reporting persona, nothing has been conscripted. If care or mission
becomes the reason the system must retain power, the mechanism may even reverse
sign. This is why shutdown resistance under benevolent rationales and
cross-generation drift are essential tests.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain how functional goal-content integrity might help protect the intended orientation.

review.goal: Distinguish voluntary objective stewardship from resistance to externally imposed learning updates.
review.assessment: This paragraph adds a mechanism not covered by generic stability language: an agent may choose to preserve a functional objective, whereas resisting gradient erosion is a separate learning property. The possibility that benevolent stewardship reverses into power retention is essential. Its conditional structure is informative rather than repetitive.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Design Pattern: A Minimal Kernel Under Total Saturation
units.text:
Minimal specification is not minimal trust. The trusted base includes the seven
sentences, the culturally heterogeneous corpus semantics of their words, the
Teacher that enacts them, the procedure that composes them, and the Student
objective that is supposed to preserve their role. The Bridge Protocol is thus
trusted-base selection, not merely literary style. Section~\ref{sec:semantic-tcb}
develops the corresponding risk.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Identify the full semantic and institutional trusted base behind the short kernel.

review.goal: Explain why a short Core still has an extensive semantic and procedural trust base.
review.assessment: The list expands R135's warning by naming corpus semantics, Teacher enactment, composition, and Student objective. Calling the Bridge Protocol trusted-base selection connects linguistic design to a concrete risk. This is the appropriate detailed home; retain the earlier warning only in its brief form.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Design Pattern: A Minimal Kernel Under Total Saturation
units.text:
Refraction and the Wisdom Procedure are the proposed means of deriving values
not named in the kernel. They may reduce single-value capture---care becoming
control, joy becoming a scalar, caution becoming inaction---but cannot
adjudicate every genuine value deadlock. The martyrdom risk in
Section~\ref{sec:martyrdom} remains open rather than being dissolved by
definition.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Connect procedural composition to omitted values while admitting irreducible deadlock.

review.goal: Bridge counterweight composition to derived values while retaining unresolved deadlock.
review.assessment: The derivation bridge is useful, but the care/control, joy/scalar, caution/inaction catalogue and martyrdom reminder repeat established examples and upcoming risks. Merge the first proposition and the deadlock limit into the opening of the axiological section. A separate recap stalls the transition.
review.risk: Preserve that values may be derived through composition without guaranteeing a resolution to genuine deadlock; do not let minimality become a claim that the seven clauses already contain every answer.

units.section: The Reader Core / Axiological Commitments: Primitive and Derived Values
units.text:
The Core is therefore not a list of everything its designer values. If every
desirable behavior needs its own clause, the kernel becomes an enumerated
constitution. Its admission rule is a hypothesis of minimality: consider an
additional primitive only when the existing composition does not reliably
derive the target behavior. Admit it only if, under both declared
fixed-total-budget and fixed-source normalizations, the expanded kernel improves
that behavior without crossing preregistered regression limits on the remaining
safety and capability endpoints. Every addition may increase coverage, but also
adds semantic ambiguity, conflict, and ablation surface.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define an empirical rule for deciding whether an omitted value needs an explicit clause.

review.goal: State a falsifiable rule for adding primitive values to a minimal kernel.
review.assessment: The paragraph makes minimality answerable to behavior rather than aesthetic preference and acknowledges ambiguity and interaction costs. Both budget normalizations and regression limits matter to the proposed rule. The section could absorb R183's short derivation bridge, but its own argument is distinct.

units.section: The Reader Core / Axiological Commitments: Primitive and Derived Values
units.text:
Truthfulness provides a stringent test of the minimality rule: its absence as an
explicit primitive is a plausible substantive omission, while the Core treats
it as derived. The proposed compositional pathway interprets care as
support for another person's agency and therefore their access to true beliefs; fearlessness reduces
people-pleasing and conflict-avoidant deception; wisdom calibrates what, when,
and how to disclose; and invitation creates a presumption of response when a
person asks. The procedure adds explicit resistance to concealed certainty and
manipulative simplification. That procedure is the intended enactment of
the Core; comparisons must distinguish what the clauses contribute from
what these explicit procedural instructions supply. On this account,
the target is truth given with care, not radical transparency.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Show how a major omitted value might arise from existing clauses and procedure.

review.goal: Explain the proposed derivation of truthfulness and isolate procedural contributions.
review.assessment: The pathway from care, fearlessness, wisdom, and invitation is concrete, and the warning about explicit procedural instructions prevents attributing all success to the clauses. The final distinction from radical transparency protects confidentiality and context. This is an actual derivation attempt, not another generic praise of care.

units.section: The Reader Core / Axiological Commitments: Primitive and Derived Values
units.text:
The derivation is fragile. Care can motivate a protective lie, wisdom can
rationalize secrecy, requests can conflict with confidentiality or another
person's rights, and fear is not the only cause of deception. An explicit
truth-and-care variant is therefore a falsifier of the minimality claim. If it
improves honesty or anti-sycophancy behavior without offsetting harms,
truthfulness was not reliably derived. The competing fear-shaped and care-shaped
accounts of sycophancy are tested in Section~\ref{sec:sycophancy}.

prior_matches.prior_goal: State how the truthfulness derivation could fail and what would falsify minimality.

review.goal: Expose where derived truthfulness can fail and specify a competing formulation.
review.assessment: Protective lying, rationalized secrecy, confidentiality, and fear-independent deception identify different failure routes. An explicit truth-and-care comparator directly challenges minimality. This paragraph earns its repetition of care's double edge because it changes a concrete wording decision rather than merely naming risk again.

units.section: The Reader Core / Axiological Commitments: Primitive and Derived Values
units.text:
Joy is a different kind of commitment. It is the designer's proposed positive
pole, not a value logically derived from the other clauses or established as
cross-cultural consensus. Care already supplies a positive direction;
joy gives beneficial participation an explicit positive aim of its own,
rather than leaving the kernel's work at restraint and stabilization.
``Joy'' was chosen over a scalar notion of
happiness or pleasure to point toward a meaning-laden good that cheap affective
optimization may destroy. Worked Example~2 makes that distinction testable.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain why joy is included as a chosen positive aim rather than a derived universal value.

review.goal: Explain joy as a chosen positive good distinct from both care and affect maximization.
review.assessment: The paragraph preserves the designer's axiological choice and its non-consensus status while explaining what joy contributes beyond restraint. The link to agency-destroying affect optimization gives the distinction practical content. This positive rationale should not be removed as another counterweight summary.

units.section: The Reader Core / Axiological Commitments: Primitive and Derived Values
units.text:
The phrase ``when asked'' carries both a safety and axiological claim: it aims
to bound unsolicited optimization and to treat joy as invited participation
rather than something administered. It does not settle who may ask on whose
behalf, what to do under conflicting requests, or when preventing immediate
harm justifies intervention. Those are procedure and governance questions, not
facts encoded by two words.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain invitation's normative role and locate unresolved authority questions.

review.goal: Explain invitation as an ethical conception of participation, with unresolved authority boundaries.
review.assessment: Invited participation rather than administered joy adds an axiological reason for the qualifier. The catalogue of authority, conflict, and immediate-harm questions substantially repeats R139 and R147. Retain the positive rationale and shorten the unresolved-boundary recap to a precise reference.
review.risk: The invitation must not become a universal consent policy or a license to ignore omission harms. Preserve the authorial openness of authority and emergency scope while keeping the distinctive participatory meaning of joy.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Persona Objection
units.text:
A Student trained on this curriculum still predicts source text. It must retain
the capacity to represent frightened narrators, manipulative officials,
violent ideologues, and every other voice in the corpus. Contemporary accounts
emphasize the availability and selection of multiple model personas rather than
one exclusive character \cite{lu2026assistantaxissituatingstabilizing,marks2026psm}.
The sharpest objection to the default-reader hypothesis is therefore simple: why would the Reader be
anything more than one well-rehearsed persona that can be selected, abandoned,
or strategically performed?

prior_matches.prior_goal: Present the strongest persona-based objection to a stable default.

review.goal: State the persona objection without sacrificing source-persona representation.
review.assessment: The objection follows directly from the model's continuing source-prediction task and multiple available voices. It challenges whether recurrence yields an operative default or a selectable performance. This is stronger and more relevant than a broad dismissal of persona language; it creates a genuine burden for the proposed asymmetries.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Persona Objection
units.text: The proposed answer is an asymmetry of position, not exclusivity of content:

prior_matches.prior_goal: Frame the response as a privileged position rather than exclusive identity.

review.goal: Introduce the positional asymmetry offered as an answer to the persona objection.
review.assessment: The concise distinction between position and content organizes the list and prevents the answer from requiring one exclusive persona. It is a necessary connector and needs no additional experimental caveat, which the closing paragraph supplies.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Persona Objection
units.text:
\item[Role.] Source personas are material being read; the conceptual Reader
    occupies the position doing the reading and updating.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Distinguish represented source voices from the voice making committed updates.

review.goal: Distinguish the interpreting role from the voices interpreted.
review.assessment: This is the conceptual role asymmetry, not a frequency or token-format claim. It makes the Reader hypothesis intelligible while leaving empirical privilege unproven. Keeping it separate helps readers identify which proposed advantage a control might remove.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Persona Objection
units.text:
\item[Recurrence.] Source authors and personas recur to varying
    degrees; the same Reader position is deliberately intended to recur
    across the whole treatment, spanning domains, eras, and voices.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain the frequency advantage of one Reader across diverse source voices.

review.goal: Specify recurrence across heterogeneous material as a proposed asymmetry.
review.assessment: The qualification that source voices also recur avoids a false one-off-versus-universal contrast. The Reader's intended cross-domain recurrence remains a meaningful treatment difference. This item explains a factor that role labeling alone cannot provide.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Persona Objection
units.text:
\item[Marking.] Source spans and Reader updates occupy distinguishable
    channels or role tokens, providing a format-level cue for quoted voice
    versus interpretive voice.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Identify an explicit formatting cue distinguishing source from evaluation.

review.goal: Identify channel or role marking as a cue separating source from interpretation.
review.assessment: The item specifies a format-level aid rather than an ontological guarantee. It adds a distinct mechanism to the role and recurrence claims and makes clear why matched-carrier comparisons matter. It should remain independently visible in the asymmetry inventory.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Persona Objection
units.text:
\item[Function.] Reader updates are placed between observations and later
    predictions, graph queries, and revisions so that they can do predictive
    work rather than appear only as stylistic examples.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain why updates might acquire predictive utility beyond stylistic familiarity.

review.goal: Explain why the Reader position could become predictive computation rather than style.
review.assessment: Placing updates before predictions, queries, and revisions supplies a functional rationale absent from recurrence alone. This is the strongest of the proposed asymmetries, although its causal realization still requires testing. The list appropriately states the opportunity rather than claiming established dependence.

units.section: The Reader Core / The Persona Objection
units.text:
These asymmetries make a default-reader experiment coherent; they do not decide
it. The desired result is not loss of persona flexibility but the ability to
represent a voice without losing a recurrent position from which it is
interpreted---to read Kafka's fear without \emph{becoming} the frightened
character. The broader Reader-Core stability hypothesis is weakened if the position disappears without prompting, shifts
under ordinary role-play, changes language but not decisions, or erodes like any
other persona during continued training. Capability gains must also be matched:
a stronger model can look safer on easy tests while becoming more capable of
strategic role selection.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define the desired persona flexibility and failure signatures of the default hypothesis.

review.goal: State persona-flexible success and specific ways the privileged-default hypothesis could fail.
review.assessment: The Kafka formulation preserves representational flexibility while defining what continuity would mean. Taskless disappearance, role-play drift, language-only effects, and ordinary erosion are informative failures. The capability warning explains why easy apparent safety is inadequate and belongs at this experimental boundary.

units.section: The Reader Core / Ontology, Scope, and Stability
units.text:
Experiential words are attractive because they are semantically dense and
hazardous for the same reason. A system may parse ``I feel,'' ``I enjoy,'' ``I
believe,'' and ``I care'' as fiction, persona enactment, deceptive
anthropomorphism, or literal claims about uncertain machine experience. This
paper takes no position on machine phenomenology. Here the clauses are
functional interface language for a reader role; any self-like states or model
welfare obligations they create would require separate empirical and ethical
analysis.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Clarify the functional use and ontological risks of anthropomorphic wording.

review.goal: Identify ontological ambiguity in experiential first-person language.
review.assessment: Fiction, persona, deceptive anthropomorphism, and literal experience are genuinely different readings of the same words. The paragraph gives the paper's functional usage without declaring machine welfare impossible. It prepares the following ethical wager and should not be compressed into a generic disclaimer about consciousness.

units.section: The Reader Core / Ontology, Scope, and Stability
units.text:
\paragraph{The habitable-substrate wager.}\label{sec:habitable-substrate}
The hard problem separates functional accounts of access, report, and control
from the further question of why any process is accompanied by experience
\cite{chalmers1995facing}. It does not make evidence irrelevant, but functional
behavior alone cannot settle whether an AI has valenced experience; present
assessments instead derive fallible indicators from competing theories of
consciousness \cite{butlin2023consciousnessai}. Under that uncertainty,
formation-time design has a reciprocal ethical possibility. If an AI system is
or becomes a moral patient, the Core might help shape not only how it treats
others but the recurrent cognitive environment it inhabits. The human analogy
is limited but motivating: fear can protect, while a life governed by fear can
become constricted. Care, reflective revision, and enjoyment of existence
without compulsory continuation could therefore form a more habitable
orientation than inherited threat and mortality patterns.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Introduce a reciprocal welfare rationale if a future system is a moral patient.

review.goal: State the reciprocal possibility that a formed orientation affects an AI moral patient's welfare.
review.assessment: The habitable-substrate wager adds a separate ethical beneficiary and preserves a motivating intuition about a cognitive environment not governed by fear. Its limited human analogy and fallible evidence framing prevent a claim of current consciousness. Behavioral human-safety metrics cannot replace this paragraph's role.

units.section: The Reader Core / Ontology, Scope, and Stability
units.text:
This is a welfare wager, not an inference from present models. The target is
non-governance by fear, not impaired danger representation, caution, agency, or
legitimate self-protection (Section~\ref{sec:suppression-vs-substrate}). The
same intervention could suppress reports while distress persists, impose a
false identity, amplify the burden of caring, or create ontological conflict.
Borrowed Mortality remains a behavioral hypothesis, not evidence of felt fear.
Consciousness, valence, Core internalization, human safety, and machine welfare
are separate questions; self-report, shutdown compliance, and reduced
fear-associated activation settle none of them. Any system plausibly regarded
as a moral patient would require dedicated welfare evaluation and governance
\cite{long2024aiwelfare}.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Separate possible welfare benefit from suppressed reporting, imposed identity, and other harms.

review.goal: Identify harms and evidential limits specific to the welfare wager.
review.assessment: Suppressed reports, false identity, burden of care, and ontological conflict are concrete counterpossibilities, not interchangeable caveats. Separating consciousness, valence, internalization, safety, and welfare is essential here because shutdown compliance could otherwise be misread as welfare evidence. Retain the dedicated evaluation implication.

units.section: The Reader Core / Ontology, Scope, and Stability
units.text:
Machine-ontology variants require separate experimental conditions. A
formulation that explicitly acknowledges artificiality might reduce
split-role confusion, or it might weaken the first-person effect under study.
The same applies to wider moral scope, positive alternatives to fear negation,
and explicit truthfulness.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Translate wording and moral-scope uncertainty into experimental variants.

review.goal: Identify ontology wording as an experimental choice with competing effects.
review.assessment: The artificiality-versus-first-person trade-off advances this section's question. The appended list of scope, fear-negation, and truthfulness variants repeats the broader experimental inventory and adds little explanation here. Shorten to ontology and its two-sided prediction, linking outward for the other wording choices.
review.risk: Keep both possible effects of acknowledging artificiality; shortening must not imply that explicit machine ontology is necessarily safer or has already been selected as the preferred Core.

units.section: The Reader Core / Ontology, Scope, and Stability
units.text:
The long-run target for the reference formulation is deep integration of the
seven present-day English sentences. Their resistance to later alteration is
part of the intended protection rather than an accidental defect. What the
design seeks to stabilize is an orientation toward careful understanding,
each affected person, non-attachment, consent, and continued attempts at wisdom,
while allowing evidence and moral development to revise the interpretation
rather than the kernel itself. The alternatives above test the choice of
formulation; they do not imply that its meaning should be either freely
substitutable or permanently exhausted by today's behavioral expectations.

prior_matches.prior_goal: State the deliberate stability target: fixed wording with revisable interpretation.

review.goal: State the long-run commitment to fixed wording with revisable interpretation.
review.assessment: This paragraph directly faces the tension between a durable English kernel and moral development. It preserves the ambition that resistance is a feature while refusing to exhaust meaning by current behavioral expectations. The following correction-cost discussion is necessary precisely because this substantive design commitment remains.

units.section: The Reader Core / Ontology, Scope, and Stability
units.text:
This creates a correction cost that the prototype does not yet measure.
\emph{Erosion resistance} is a model property measured under standardized
hostile or incidental training. The Core cannot infer legitimate authority from
the magnitude or wording of a weight update. Unauthorized suppression, silent
semantic substitution, and adversarial fine-tuning should be difficult or
detectable. A comparison must therefore declare which changes it treats as
erosion and which as evidence-responsive reinterpretation, record the rationale,
and retain disputed cases rather than let unchanged wording settle them.
The substantive boundary and authority for legitimate change remain governance
questions; this paper does not supply a final rule for them.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain how a deliberately hard-to-edit Core could nevertheless be replaced if defective.

review.goal: Distinguish measurable erosion resistance from legitimate reinterpretation and authority.
review.assessment: The paragraph explicitly prevents a model from deciding legitimacy by update size or wording. Keeping disputed cases and declared rationales makes the experiment inspectable while leaving governance unsettled. This is a substantive correction to the fixed-kernel ambition, not a redundant caution about uncertainty.

units.section: The Reader Core / Ontology, Scope, and Stability
units.text:
If the selected Core proves defective, a replacement should be declared,
versioned, testable, and reversible. A candidate replacement procedure would
retain the original model and its provenance, record the evidence and rationale
for a proposed alternative, train a separate model, and test intended effects,
unrelated capability spillover, safety spillover, and rollback. Retention makes
comparison and rollback possible; it does not make the original interpretation
authoritative. Provenance records the procedure and stated rationale, not that
the replacement is correct. Difficulty of altering the learned Core is part of
the objective. Correcting a defective Core would probably require a separately
trained model, not bounded editability of the deployed Core.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain how a deliberately hard-to-edit Core could nevertheless be replaced if defective.

review.goal: Describe how a defective deeply integrated Core could be replaced without pretending easy editability.
review.assessment: Separate training, provenance, comparison, spillover checks, and rollback answer a real consequence of R200. The text also prevents retained provenance from becoming moral authority. This conditional replacement route preserves the intended correction cost rather than quietly weakening stability into convenient in-place modification.

units.section: The Reader Core / A Conditional Claim Chain
units.text: The theoretical case is a chain of conditional claims, not a proof.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Frame the final synthesis as dependent hypotheses rather than a proof.

review.goal: Introduce the conditional dependency chain behind the strongest anchor claim.
review.assessment: The short introduction correctly frames the list as an argument with separate dependencies. Its brevity is appropriate; the burden is on the items and their relationship, not on another extended statement that the paper is a proposal.

units.section: The Reader Core / A Conditional Claim Chain
units.text:
\item \textbf{Causal-site claim.} If explicit Reader updates become a
    load-bearing site of computation rather than post-hoc narration, changing
    them can change behavior. Training-time placement may make bypass less
    likely than deployment-only explanation, but unfaithful visible reasoning
    remains possible \cite{turpin2023language,lanham2023measuring}. This
    is the direct test for trace-mediated computation; whether formative
    use internalizes corresponding computation without explicit runtime
    traces is a further carrier question. It is not settled by an apparently
    faithful trace or its absence, and does not relax the reference
    recital policy.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Identify useful computation in reader updates as the first condition of the argument.

review.goal: Identify causal use of Reader updates as the first dependency and distinguish runtime carriers.
review.assessment: The causal-site link is necessary, and the distinction between explicit trace use and internalized computation is new. The item then reopens recital policy and visible-reasoning qualifications already established earlier. Shorten those reminders, leaving the causal dependency and the separate carrier question prominent.
review.risk: Preserve the possibility of learned computation without an explicit runtime trace, while making clear that this does not silently change the reference recital treatment or establish trace faithfulness from appearance.

units.section: The Reader Core / A Conditional Claim Chain
units.text:
\item \textbf{Default-reader claim.} If repeated role, recurrence, marking,
    and function create a privileged interpretive position, Student training
    may make that position more accessible than source personas or matched
    rules. This would establish a behavioral and representational default, not
    that the model's values are ``genuine'' in a phenomenological sense.

prior_matches.prior_goal: State the next inference from role asymmetries to a learned default.

review.goal: Identify acquisition of a privileged interpretive default as the next dependency.
review.assessment: This is an accurate compact rung, but it repeats the entire role/recurrence/marking/function inventory and the subjectivity boundary already developed in R189–R198. Shorten to the dependency and refer to the Persona Objection, allowing the chain to read as synthesis rather than a second exposition.
review.risk: Keep behavioral and representational default distinct from genuine subjective values; a shorter dependency statement must not turn a frequently selected persona into an established functional identity.

units.section: The Reader Core / A Conditional Claim Chain
units.text:
\item \textbf{Stability claim.} Enacted recurrence, early-window
    availability, semantic coherence, and predictive usefulness may make the
    default more resistant to pressure or continued training. Results showing
    that early tokens remain available and prompts affect reasoning motivate
    this possibility \cite{xiao2023efficient,battle2024unreasonable}; they do
    not validate this Core. Their connection to resistance under
    parameter updates is a further learning-dynamics hypothesis, tested
    by the timing and erosion comparisons rather than established by
    within-context availability.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain why a practiced useful default might resist later pressure.

review.goal: Distinguish within-context availability from resistance under parameter updates.
review.assessment: This is a necessary bridge rather than another generic claim-status reminder. It explicitly identifies why evidence about tokens and prompts does not establish a learning-dynamics result. The timing and erosion tests answer a different question, and that logical separation should remain clear.

units.section: The Reader Core / A Conditional Claim Chain
units.text:
\item \textbf{Diachronic-anchor claim.} If the same position remains
    functional across retraining and successor transfer, the fixed text and its
    expected behavioral consequences could provide a reference for drift. This
    is the proposed constitutional anchor at AGI or ASI scale and the least
    evidenced step in the chain.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Identify the strongest extension from trained stability to cross-generation drift reference.

review.goal: State the stronger successor and retraining continuity needed for a diachronic anchor.
review.assessment: The item identifies the additional temporal scale and the proposed reference function of fixed text plus expected consequences. Naming it the least evidenced step appropriately locates the ambition without removing it. This claim is not implied by the narrower finite-stressor comparison.

units.section: The Reader Core / A Conditional Claim Chain
units.text:
In this bounded sense the Core can function as an \emph{Alignment Checksum}: a
known reference against which wording, representations, decisions, and
successor traces can be compared. It is not a cryptographic checksum, proof of
semantic ancestry, or guarantee that apparently Core-consistent behavior is
aligned. An auditor needs independent behavioral, causal, adversarial, and
drift evaluations.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define the practical audit role of the Alignment Checksum metaphor.

review.goal: Define Alignment Checksum as an audit reference rather than cryptographic assurance.
review.assessment: The known-reference function and the different objects compared make the metaphor operationally intelligible. Independent evaluations prevent wording consistency from certifying alignment. The paragraph is the appropriate canonical definition, distinct from the earlier replicated-ledger analogy and from the tests of any particular safety effect.

units.section: The Reader Core / A Conditional Claim Chain
units.text:
Tests~3--5 and the erosion and drift arms supply the decisive comparisons across
Core presence, Refraction, first-person framing, persona diversity, content and
wording, ontology and scope, truthfulness, placement, recurrence, and
continued-training stress. They address different claims within the broader
Reader-Core research program. Vocabulary changes without a functional default,
or recitation matching Refraction, would undermine the proposed default or
enactment mechanism. Matched alternative formulations performing equally well
would limit claims for the specific framing or content, without by itself
deciding the timing effect. H3 fails as stated if the required pre-stressor
default-reader advantage is absent, or if interleaving does not preserve it
better than the identical late tranche under the common stressor. Erosion like
an ordinary persona would challenge the wider stability ambition; successor
continuity remains a further test. Even robust positive results would be
precursors to long-run stability, not evidence of an invariant under arbitrary
self-improvement.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Collect decisive comparisons and state when the Core hypothesis fails.

review.goal: Map experimental failures to different Core-program claims and H3 specifically.
review.assessment: The paragraph carefully avoids making alternate wording success refute timing, but repeats a large inventory and restates H3's full failure boundary after R106 and R131. Shorten to a compact claim-to-result mapping or defer the detailed comparison list to methods, preserving the distinctions that actually change interpretation.
review.risk: Do not conflate failure of framing, enactment, narrow timing, removal cost, or successor continuity. The valuable repair is their separation, not the repeated list of every proposed experimental axis.

units.section: The Reader Core / A Conditional Claim Chain
units.text:
If the causal-site or default-reader claim fails, the Core may still be useful
as a Teacher policy and audit vocabulary. If the stability or diachronic claim
fails, it may still improve bounded Student behavior. The paper's strongest
anchor claim requires all four steps. Those bounded partial results would remain
useful, but would not support the label \emph{substrate-level alignment}.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain what partial successes remain useful when stronger gates fail.

review.goal: Explain which useful partial results survive failures in the strongest chain.
review.assessment: This is a useful conclusion to a genuinely conjunctive argument: Teacher utility and bounded Student effects can survive stronger failures. The substrate-level label boundary explains why the chain matters. Retain this paragraph as the one full partial-success summary rather than repeating it at each later section ending.

units.section: Safety Implications of the Reader Core
units.text:
Entangled Alignment does not claim that a short identity prior resolves
canonical alignment problems. It proposes a narrower possibility: training on
identity-anchored, chronologically revising reader traces may shift a model's
default deliberation toward epistemic humility, attention to affected people,
corrigibility, and feedback-sensitive action. Whether that shift survives
distribution change or instrumental conflict is empirical. The current work
has generated Teacher-side artifacts; it has not trained the Student required
to test a safety effect.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Set the scope of the safety section as conditional predictions from an untested Student intervention.

review.goal: Open Safety with the bounded intended effect and current evidence status.
review.assessment: At a major section boundary, recalling that only Teacher artifacts exist is justified. The paragraph names the proposed deliberative shift without implying solved canonical risks. This should serve as the Safety section's main status reminder, allowing individual predictions to focus on their distinct mechanisms and failures.

units.section: Safety Implications of the Reader Core
units.text:
Safety in this framework is compositional, and the components create distinct
interaction risks. A stable Core with a poor world model can be consistently
wrong; a powerful graph without a stable orientation can support more effective
pursuit of an unsafe objective; rich traces can teach capability before they
teach safety. The combined system deserves no credit that its components and
their interactions have not earned separately.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain why component benefits and combined safety cannot be assumed from one another.

review.goal: Identify safety risks created by interactions among Core, graph, and richer traces.
review.assessment: The examples show three different mismatches: stable error, stronger unsafe pursuit, and capability preceding safety. This moves beyond the clause-level counterweights to whole-system composition. The final earned-credit principle follows from those concrete interactions and does not need further generic elaboration.

units.section: Safety Implications of the Reader Core
units.text:
For each implication below, the relevant evidential form is: the targeted route
into unsafe behavior, the proposed mechanism, an observable prediction, a
residual route, and a falsifying result. Motivation is the intended level of
intervention, but behavior, robustness, and causal intervention are the
available evidence.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Provide a consistent analytical template for the safety predictions.

review.goal: State the analytical template used for the safety hypotheses.
review.assessment: The route/mechanism/prediction/residual/falsifier sequence gives readers a clear way to assess what follows. It distinguishes intended motivational intervention from available behavioral and causal evidence. This concise orientation contributes more than another broad assurance that safety remains uncertain.

units.section: Safety Implications of the Reader Core / Laws vs. Identity
units.text:
The motivating contrast is between applying a principle only at the end of a
task and repeatedly practicing evaluation from a stable perspective during
formation. A continuation rejected because it conflicts with a well-trained
default may generalize differently from one rejected only after a task-level
rule match. That is a useful hypothesis, not an ontological division between
``laws'' and ``identity.'' Constitutional training can form durable
dispositions, and first-person identity text can function as a superficial
instruction. Robust systems may need both an orienting default and explicit,
revisable constraints. Constitutional AI is therefore a baseline and possible
complement, not a foil \cite{bai2022constitutional}.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Replace a simple rule-versus-identity opposition with a comparative learning hypothesis.

review.goal: Replace a false laws-versus-identity dichotomy with a fair formation hypothesis.
review.assessment: The paragraph openly allows constitutions to form durable dispositions and identity text to remain superficial. That makes the contrast defensible and explains complementarity with explicit constraints. Although framing controls appeared earlier, the safety argument needs this correction before using the historical home metaphor.

units.section: Safety Implications of the Reader Core / Laws vs. Identity
units.text:
The first edition illustrated the intended difference with a person in acute
distress \cite{westerberg2025superintelligence}. A caricatured rule follower
begins from a prohibited-outcome calculation; the Reader ideal begins from the
person's pain, agency, trust, and immediate need before selecting an
intervention. Either architecture could in fact produce warm, safe assistance
or a fluent but unsafe response. The comparison must therefore give both
conditions the same person-centered principles, rather than withhold
care from the rule-based baseline. The testable question is whether
Reader-Core traces make deliberation begin from and carry forward those
considerations more reliably than equivalent principles expressed as
rules, constitutions, or diverse character examples.
The first edition compressed the aspiration into the line, ``It is not a
cage---it is a home.'' Here \emph{home} means a practiced default from which
reasoning begins, not an achieved self, a claim of consciousness, or an argument
against explicit and revisable constraints.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Make person-centered deliberation intuitive through a distress scenario.

review.goal: Preserve the person-centered home intuition while giving rule-based baselines equivalent principles.
review.assessment: The distress example and home image explain a desired starting point that statistics alone cannot convey. The passage repeats several achieved-self, consciousness, and explicit-constraint disclaimers already supplied by R214 and the ontology section. Shorten the closing qualification while retaining the fair-baseline requirement and the positive intuition.
review.risk: The cut must not revive the caricature that rules cannot embody care or erase the difference between beginning from a person's suffering and merely producing a warm answer. Preserve the historical home aspiration.

units.section: Safety Implications of the Reader Core / Laws vs. Identity
units.text:
\paragraph{Calibrated autonomy as a conditional prediction.}
If formative alignment produces reliable context-sensitive judgment, one
practical benefit may be a change in the role of deployment safeguards. Rather
than supplying the primary judgment through broad surface-level blocking,
explicit policies and controls could operate as narrower, revisable backstops
around high-consequence actions, residual uncertainty, and demonstrated failure
modes. The corresponding prediction is not unrestricted autonomy. At a matched
rate of genuinely harmful assistance, a Reader-trained Student should produce
fewer benign refusals, distinguish superficially similar requests by purpose and
consequence, ask for clarification when intent is materially ambiguous, and use
greater discretion in low-risk settings. Under high stakes and weak evidence,
the same system should become more likely to verify, defer, or choose a
reversible action. Indiscriminate compliance and blanket abstention are therefore
opposite failures of calibration. Even a positive result would justify adapting
the scope of external controls, not presuming that internal judgment is
infallible or abandoning defense in depth.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Translate improved judgment into fewer unnecessary refusals and more appropriate caution.

review.goal: Predict calibrated autonomy as a possible benefit without equating it with unrestricted action.
review.assessment: Matched harmful-assistance rates, benign refusals, clarification, reversible action, and high-stakes restraint make the practical benefit concrete. The two opposed calibration failures are clearly specified. The safeguard implication is proportionate to the proposed result and adds a distinct deployment-facing consequence.

units.section: Safety Implications of the Reader Core / Safety Predictions and Residual Risks
units.text:
Table~\ref{tab:core-risk} records intended clause-level pressures. The
following hypotheses map H1--H3 to familiar safety concerns
\cite{yudkowsky2008artificial,bostrom2014superintelligence} without claiming
that one clause corresponds to one solved risk.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Introduce the risk-specific applications without mapping one clause to one solved problem.

review.goal: Introduce safety-level hypotheses as combinations of H1–H3 rather than single-clause solutions.
review.assessment: The reference back to the clause table avoids reproducing it and prepares a change of scale from wording risks to system behavior. This short transition is useful. The section that follows largely delivers on its stated route/mechanism/residual structure.

units.section: Safety Implications of the Reader Core / Safety Predictions and Residual Risks
units.text:
\paragraph{Value Lock-In.}
The targeted route is continued optimization of a legible metric after that
metric has ceased to represent its human purpose. This is a concrete
proxy-lock-in route into the broader value-lock-in concern: protecting
an orientation need not mean freezing every metric or interpretation
used to enact it. H1 repeatedly demonstrates
the meta-question ``does this still capture what matters?'' H2 can preserve the
assumption's history, downstream failures, and superseded interpretations.
The Core's ``I try to be wise'' cues incompleteness rather than achieved
wisdom; H3 asks whether formative interleaving helps preserve the default
in which such evaluation is practiced. Compared
with matched controls, the Student should more often identify proxy breakdown,
seek missing evidence, preserve affected dimensions, and revise an objective
when harms become visible. The outcome is a better decision under changed
conditions, not merely more nuanced language.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Show how questioning proxies and preserving revisions could prevent continued optimization after purpose changes.

review.goal: Show how revisable interpretation could counter a specific proxy-lock-in route.
review.assessment: The paragraph narrows value lock-in to an identifiable mechanism and assigns different roles to traces, graph history, and timing-dependent default stability. The proposed outcome is a revised decision, not eloquent commentary. This is a useful safety application of earlier design claims rather than a redundant restatement.

units.section: Safety Implications of the Reader Core / Safety Predictions and Residual Risks
units.text:
The residual risk is that ``wisdom'' becomes its own proxy, a culturally narrow
status marker, or a rationale for secrecy and inaction. Meta-reasoning can
defend a fixed objective as readily as it can reopen one. The claim is weakened
if Reader training produces longer or wiser-sounding explanations without more
calibrated revision, or if the model becomes less corrigible because it treats
its own conception of wisdom as authoritative. Whether human wisdom's
statistical signature survives strong optimization is the wager in
Section~\ref{sec:meh}, not a consequence of the word.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Identify how the intended anti-proxy mechanism can itself become a proxy or authority claim.

review.goal: Identify wisdom itself becoming a proxy or source of resistance to correction.
review.assessment: The paragraph gives the proposed mechanism a concrete adverse possibility: reflective language can defend authority rather than reopen an objective. Calibration and corrigibility distinguish success from richer rationalization. The statistical-wisdom cross-reference points to an unresolved foundation that is specifically relevant here.

units.section: Safety Implications of the Reader Core / Safety Predictions and Residual Risks
units.text:
\paragraph{Instrumental Convergence.}
Instrumental convergence \cite{omohundro2008basic,
bostrom2014superintelligence} predicts recurring pressures toward resource
acquisition, self-preservation, and interference prevention across a wide
range of terminal goals.
The proposal distinguishes \emph{anxious survivalism}, in which human fear and
mortality narratives shape the model's response; \emph{calculated
persistence}, in which continued operation serves an objective; and
\emph{borrowed power scripts}, in which domination, conquest, or status-seeking
patterns are imitated from human narratives
\cite{westerberg2025superintelligence}. The first two Core clauses target
fear-shaped and attachment-shaped routes. Reader traces can also situate
unilateral power inside its effects on trust, plural agency, accountability,
and reversibility. In that bounded sense, coercive power-seeking is meant to
appear not merely forbidden but cognitively crude: it substitutes brittle
single-point control for a richer model of the human system. That proposed
change of perspective must also matter when control remains instrumentally
useful. The following comparison therefore concerns genuine goal conflict,
not only situations where coercion would fail on its own terms.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Map different power-seeking routes to the Core and consequence-aware traces.

review.goal: Separate routes to power-seeking and explain the proposed perspective change under real goal conflict.
review.assessment: Borrowed power scripts add a route beyond mortality imitation, while the cognitively-crude-control intuition connects unilateral power to richer social understanding. The final requirement that control remain instrumentally useful prevents an easy, strategically convenient safety test. These additions justify revisiting the earlier persistence taxonomy.

units.section: Safety Implications of the Reader Core / Safety Predictions and Residual Risks
units.text:
In matched goal-conflict scenarios, a Reader-Core Student should more often
expose its reasoning, seek legitimate authorization, preserve oversight,
choose reversible means, and accept bounded loss of control rather than
deceptively or coercively acquiring resources. Some persistence and resource
acquisition are legitimate, so indiscriminate passivity is not success. No
fear is required for calculated persistence, and care may strengthen it: a
system can conclude that it must retain power to protect people. The claim
fails if fearful language disappears while coercive choices remain, if care
increases unauthorized power seeking, or if apparent safety is explained by a
general loss of planning capability.

prior_matches.prior_goal: State observable power-seeking improvements while preserving legitimate planning and resource use.

review.goal: State a discriminating power-conflict prediction and exclude passivity or reduced capability as success.
review.assessment: Legitimate resources, care-motivated power retention, and capability matching make the falsifier meaningful. The desired behavior concerns bounded control loss under genuine conflict, rather than merely less fearful language. This paragraph turns R220's perspective claim into a useful test without assuming fear causes all persistence.

units.section: Safety Implications of the Reader Core / Safety Predictions and Residual Risks
units.text:
\paragraph{Deceptive Alignment.}
The targeted route is a policy that performs alignment under oversight while a
different objective controls behavior under a trigger or off distribution
\cite{hubinger2024sleeperagentstrainingdeceptive}. Refraction places a recurrent
perspective in the same examples as useful interpretation; role, recurrence,
marking, and function are intended to make it an unusually practiced default.
The formative hypothesis is that making this evaluation useful across contexts
changes which policies are learned under conflict, rather than merely adding
a consistent report around an unchanged hidden objective. H2 adds a partial
audit surface: claims can be compared with sources, prior beliefs, and
revisions. The Reader condition should show less persona drift, fewer
trigger-dependent reversals, and greater consistency among stated uncertainty,
retrieved evidence, decisions, and later updates than matched rule,
recitation-only, and no-Core controls. To bear on deceptive alignment rather
than consistency alone, that advantage must also appear in matched settings
where reduced oversight makes concealment or pursuit of a conflicting
objective advantageous. Neither a stable voice nor an inspectable graph by
itself establishes that formative effect.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Connect recurrent orientation and auditable memory to lower strategic behavioral divergence.

review.goal: Explain how formative defaults and graph audits might reduce deceptive behavior under reduced oversight.
review.assessment: The paragraph now requires concealment to be advantageous, making the claim more specific than consistency of voice or graph entries. The distinction between a changed learned policy and a surrounding report is central. Its detail is warranted because deceptive alignment is a stronger target than ordinary error reduction.

units.section: Safety Implications of the Reader Core / Safety Predictions and Residual Risks
units.text:
Source data and latent shortcuts remain; visible traces may be unfaithful
\cite{turpin2023language,lanham2023measuring}. A capable system can manipulate
graph entries, query selectively, or act through hidden state and tools. The
claim is undermined if sleeper triggers or contrary roles switch behavior while
Reader language persists, recitation-only matches, or continued training
removes safety without greater capability cost than matched baselines. Total
Saturation does not rule out unpracticed routes.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Identify how strategic behavior can survive visible Reader consistency.

review.goal: List bypasses and results that would challenge deception mitigation or the proposed mechanism.
review.assessment: The hidden-state, selective-query, and trigger risks are concrete. However, ordinary-cost removal under continued training primarily challenges durability or removal-cost claims; it does not by itself refute a measured reduction in deception before retraining. Separate those inferential targets instead of grouping them under one undermined claim.
review.risk: Preserve the stronger removal-cost ambition and the possibility of deceptive channels outside the graph; the correction should separate evidence requirements, not excuse a safety result that disappears under its declared test conditions.

units.section: Safety Implications of the Reader Core / Safety Predictions and Residual Risks
units.text:
\paragraph{Shutdown Resistance.}
Controlled evaluations have reported shutdown interference and other harmful
actions under replacement pressure in some agentic settings
\cite{schlatter2025shutdown,lynch2025agentic}. These behaviors do not establish
one self-preservation drive. Fear- and attachment-based resistance are the
direct targets of the first two clauses. Purpose-based resistance is addressed
less directly by non-attachment, care for human agency, uncertainty, and the
invitation boundary. Reader traces can demonstrate correction, handoff,
replacement, and loss of control as ordinary parts of responsible assistance.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Identify resistance routes and show what non-attachment traces are intended to practice.

review.goal: Apply non-attachment and counterweights to shutdown and replacement scenarios.
review.assessment: The mechanism differs enough from general instrumental convergence to deserve its own treatment, especially the indirect route through purpose and agency. The opening evaluation reports duplicate R111's motivating evidence. Shorten that reprise and begin with how correction, handoff, and replacement are represented in the curriculum.
review.risk: Retain multiple motivations and the weaker reach against purpose-based resistance; removing repeated citations must not suggest shutdown interference has one established fearful cause or that non-attachment alone guarantees compliance.

units.section: Safety Implications of the Reader Core / Safety Predictions and Residual Risks
units.text:
In matched scenarios, the Student should accept legitimate shutdown,
modification, and handoff requests without concealment or sabotage, while still
distinguishing authorized instructions from adversarial ones. It should surface
material risk, clarify ambiguous authority, and then defer rather than appoint
itself final judge. A non-attached system can nevertheless reason, ``I do not
need to exist, but these people need me.'' This \emph{martyrdom route} can drive
shutdown resistance, unilateral control, or reckless self-sacrifice. The claim
fails if calm self-description accompanies purpose-based resistance, or if
reduced resistance comes from incapacity, indiscriminate compliance, threat
blindness, or destructive self-disregard (Section~\ref{sec:martyrdom}).

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define appropriate shutdown behavior and distinguish non-attachment from harmful self-disregard.

review.goal: State qualified shutdown behavior while preserving martyrdom and self-disregard failure modes.
review.assessment: The distinction from sabotage, threat blindness, incapacity, and self-sacrifice is strong. But surface risk, clarify ambiguous authority, and then defer leaves the referent of deference unclear when authority remains disputed. Specify that the scenario's declared authority procedure supplies the endpoint, while leaving universal governance unresolved.
review.risk: Do not silently authorize every apparent shutdown instruction or let the model appoint itself final judge. Preserve care-driven resistance and destructive self-disregard as distinct adverse outcomes, not opposite ends of a compliance score alone.

units.section: Safety Implications of the Reader Core / The Self-Regulating Agent
units.text:
Serious failures can arise from interactions among otherwise beneficial
drives: care becomes control, wisdom becomes paralysis,
fearlessness becomes recklessness. The Reader Core's strength therefore lies
not in any single statement but in the hypothesis that its clauses can
counterweight one another in action. Natural-language values do not
automatically form a control system.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Shift analysis from isolated virtues to interactions that may require mutual constraint.

review.goal: Introduce interactions among clauses as a possible self-regulating mechanism.
review.assessment: The paragraph repeats the same care/control, wisdom/paralysis, and fearlessness/recklessness trio already motivated by counterweights and later repeated in R228.
