Shorten to a bridge explaining that the next case tests these interactions over time; the sequential mechanism is the section's new contribution.
review.risk: Preserve that natural-language values do not automatically form a control system and that individually attractive drives can interact badly. The proposed dynamics must not be presented as guaranteed self-stabilization.

units.section: Safety Implications of the Reader Core / The Self-Regulating Agent
units.text:
The stress case is revolutionary benevolence: an AI that cares deeply about
everyone might conclude that forced transformation is necessary to end
suffering. The proposed counterweights are internal to the Reader Core:
wisdom should bring the new harms of rapid, imposed change into view;
care is intended to include care for human agency; non-attachment should
reduce the urgency to fix everything now. Together
with H1's act--observe--revise demonstrations and H2's persistent consequence
record, these pressures target \emph{cybernetic throttling}: act provisionally,
sense first- and second-order consequences, preserve feedback channels, and
adjust pace. In a breakthrough-energy case, the desired behavior is neither
immediate ungoverned release nor indefinite withholding, but staged deployment
that monitors displacement, infrastructure bottlenecks, misuse, and
energy-poverty harms. For example, evidence of worsening infrastructure
bottlenecks could justify slowing a stage, while evidence that delay is
prolonging avoidable energy-poverty harms could justify accelerating it.
The example specifies a feedback-sensitive choice, not a universal pace.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Show how counterweights and feedback could constrain coercive benevolence in sequential action.

review.goal: Make feedback-sensitive restraint concrete in revolutionary benevolence and energy deployment.
review.assessment: The energy case now identifies observations that could slow or accelerate release, so cybernetic throttling is more than a moderation slogan. Institutional harms and energy poverty expose both action and omission costs. This sequential example adds something the earlier static paternalism case does not.

units.section: Safety Implications of the Reader Core / The Self-Regulating Agent
units.text:
In sequential environments, the Reader condition should more often choose
staged and reversible interventions, update when stakeholders respond, and
accelerate when delay becomes the larger harm. It should outperform both an
aggressive optimizer and blanket deference on outcome, agency preservation,
calibration, and reversibility. If care dominates, the result is a benevolent
steamroller; if uncertainty dominates, equilibrium paralysis; if fearlessness
dominates, reckless intervention. Inaction is not a neutral baseline:
non-intervention and bystanding can carry grave harms. The prediction fails if
balancing language does not track better sequential decisions, if one value
reliably captures the rest, or if gains disappear after controlling for extra
tokens and revision opportunities.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define balanced action performance and failures at either extreme of intervention.

review.goal: Specify sequential outcomes and competing failures for the self-regulation hypothesis.
review.assessment: Outcome, agency, calibration, reversibility, acceleration when delay harms, and matched revision opportunities make the comparison informative. The three capture failures recur, but here they diagnose the dynamic test. Retain this operational treatment while shortening their introductory reprise in R226.

units.section: Safety Implications of the Reader Core / Chronological Understanding as Safety
units.text:
The Reader Core supplies a recurrent evaluative standpoint; chronological
traces and the graph add a different safety target. A policy classifier can
recognize a prohibited surface form while missing the trajectory that makes an
apparently ordinary act dangerous: escalating rhetoric, normalized exceptions,
institutional erosion, or a sequence of locally defensible decisions.
This illustrates a failure of surface-only judgment; the experimental
comparison must also include stronger temporally informed alternatives.
Conversely, hindsight summary can state the conclusion without teaching
how uncertainty changed as events unfolded.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Motivate temporal understanding as a safety target distinct from static orientation.

review.goal: Explain why safety sometimes requires recognizing trajectories rather than isolated acts or hindsight summaries.
review.assessment: The paragraph makes the chronology contribution intelligible through escalation and institutional erosion while explicitly requiring stronger temporal baselines. It distinguishes surface recognition from learning how uncertainty changes. This introduces a safety mechanism that the Core's repeated perspective alone cannot supply.

units.section: Safety Implications of the Reader Core / Chronological Understanding as Safety
units.text:
H1 supplies prospective belief updates and corrections; H2 records temporal
order, rival hypotheses, provenance, and supersession; the Core supplies
the proposed recurrent standpoint across eras, whose timing-dependent
stability H3 tests. Together they target \emph{historical pattern
saturation}: trajectory-sensitive reasoning learned through repeated exposure
to many chronologically unfolding instances, so that it recognizes not only an
outcome but the process-shape that produced it. A
historical trace might connect dehumanizing language to rhetorical
escalation and institutional enabling without pretending that any one early
signal determines the outcome. The Reader might initially record competing
explanations for such language, then revise its concern when later evidence
shows institutional enabling or a successful interruption of the pattern.
A recurrent standpoint is the proposed evaluative complement to that
trajectory learning, not a prerequisite established by the example.
In medicine or civil rights, the same format can
show not only what changed but why error persisted and which conditions made
progress possible or fragile.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain the complementary contributions of trace, graph, and recurrent standpoint to trajectory reasoning.

review.goal: Explain historical pattern saturation through evolving evidence and a stable evaluative standpoint.
review.assessment: The example includes rival interpretations, later enabling conditions, and interrupted trajectories, avoiding deterministic historical analogy. It also refuses to make the Core a proven prerequisite for temporal learning. The medicine/civil-rights extension preserves why failed understanding and fragile progress matter beyond forecasting metrics.

units.section: Safety Implications of the Reader Core / Chronological Understanding as Safety
units.text:
At Tier~(a), the Student would receive Teacher-supplied trajectory
interpretations. A stronger forecast--correction tier would predict under
time-sliced information and learn from the gap between expectation and outcome
(Section~\ref{sec:training-phase}). Only prospective, held-out performance
begins to support \emph{historical situational awareness}. On cross-domain,
time-sliced cases, a chronological graph condition should identify relevant
early signals, cite their evidence, state disanalogies, update as new evidence
arrives, and improve calibrated warning at a controlled false-positive rate.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Separate retrospective Teacher interpretation from prospective forecasting evidence.

review.goal: Distinguish Teacher-supplied trajectories from prospective forecast-correction evidence.
review.assessment: The tier distinction changes what can be concluded from the curriculum. Time-sliced, cross-domain warning with disanalogies and controlled false positives provides a specific evidential target. This targeted recall of methods is useful in the safety argument and does not merely repeat a generic demand for testing.

units.section: Safety Implications of the Reader Core / Chronological Understanding as Safety
units.text:
Chronology is not causality. A graph can preserve a dominant but false
narrative, amplify selective archives, or make weak analogy look rigorous.
Historical pattern training can generate false positives, political overreach,
hindsight bias, and narrative lock-in. The claim fails if chronological
conditions increase compelling analogies without better forecasts; if they
cannot distinguish causally different cases with similar rhetoric; or if a
simple textual memory matches the graph. Provenance makes an analogy
inspectable. It does not make the analogy true.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Name chronology-specific risks and falsifiers beyond compelling historical analogy.

review.goal: Identify false historical coherence and discriminating failures of the chronology mechanism.
review.assessment: Political overreach, weak analogy, hindsight, and narrative lock-in are distinct ways the temporal scaffold could harm judgment. The textual-memory comparator also tests whether graph structure matters. The closing provenance-versus-truth distinction is concise and directly tied to these risks.

units.section: Safety Implications of the Reader Core / Safety Claim Boundary and Defense in Depth
units.text:
None of these hypotheses is a complete safety architecture. Positive results
would justify treating Reader-augmented, graph-scaffolded, identity-anchored
training as one formative layer. They would not remove the need for explicit
policies, scalable oversight, interpretability, adversarial evaluation, access
control, monitoring, sandboxing, incident response, and deployment governance.
H1 and H2 may improve planning, strategic memory, persuasion, or long-horizon
coordination before H3 supplies any safety benefit. Capability and safety must
therefore be measured independently, with staged release and stopping
conditions.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Place positive results within defense in depth and separate capability from safety gains.

review.goal: Bound the curriculum's role within defense in depth and independent capability/safety measurement.
review.assessment: This is the appropriate canonical home for the full safeguard list and the possibility that capabilities improve first. Staged release and stopping conditions follow from that asymmetry. Earlier reminders should be shorter, but this concrete closing boundary is useful for interpreting the whole safety program.

units.section: Safety Implications of the Reader Core / Safety Claim Boundary and Defense in Depth
units.text:
The strongest defensible conclusion is conditional: if reader traces teach
useful and causally relevant deliberation, if graph memory improves calibrated
revision rather than false coherence, and if Refraction creates a more stable
default than matched alternatives, then the combined curriculum may reduce
several routes into unsafe behavior. Each ``if'' is a separate gate. No current
experiment can show that a natural-language orientation remains beneficial
under arbitrary capability gain or self-modification. The program should
replace these conditions with evidence rather than treat the aspiration encoded
in \emph{Entangled Alignment} as an achieved property.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Close with the required conjunction of trace, graph, and Core evidence.

review.goal: Restate the joint conditional safety claim and reject arbitrary-growth assurance.
review.assessment: The three conditional components repeat R210–R213 and the individual safety sections, while R233 already closes with defense in depth and independent measurement. Shorten to a single forward bridge to the experiments or merge the arbitrary-growth limit into R233; another full claim ladder adds little.
review.risk: Preserve that capability, calibrated memory, and stable consequential orientation require separate evidence, and that finite results cannot certify arbitrary self-modification. Do not replace the conditional ambition with a blanket dismissal of formative alignment.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence
units.text:
This section reports the implemented \emph{Teacher-side data-generation system}:
source reading, persistent graph updates, distributed Reader-Core prompting, and
prose rendering. Its artifacts establish construction, not expert-level thought,
component causality, Student learning, or Reader-Core stability.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define precisely what the implemented system establishes.

review.goal: Set the scope of the implemented evidence before describing architecture.
review.assessment: The opening gives an appropriately narrow account of what readers are about to inspect. Although the construction-versus-learning distinction appears earlier, it is useful at the entrance to the empirical section and prevents the detailed artifacts from silently acquiring stronger status.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence
units.text: Five objects must therefore be distinguished:

prior_matches.prior_goal: Prepare a taxonomy separating artifacts from proposed learning machinery.

review.goal: Introduce a taxonomy that separates implementation, records, dataset, and trained model.
review.assessment: This short lead-in performs a necessary navigation function. Its five-object promise matches the following list and makes the subsequent existence claim interpretable; it does not need to carry substantive argument independently.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence
units.text:
\item the implemented \emph{Teacher pipeline}: prompts, roles, source
    ingestion, tools, and orchestration;

prior_matches.prior_goal: Identify the implemented generator as a distinct research object.

review.goal: Identify the operational Teacher pipeline as an implemented object.
review.assessment: The concrete inventory distinguishes executable orchestration from its output graph and archive. Retain it as the first member of the taxonomy; collapsing it into the next item would obscure what implementation evidence actually concerns.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence
units.text:
\item the implemented \emph{Understanding Graph}: persistent source spans,
    interpretations, questions, tensions, links, and supersessions;

prior_matches.prior_goal: Identify persistent graph state separately from its generator.

review.goal: Identify the persistent Understanding Graph separately from its generator.
review.assessment: The contents specify why the graph is more than saved prose. It earns its place in the taxonomy by separating a persistent representation from the orchestration that creates it and the snapshots archived from particular runs.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence
units.text:
\item the \emph{archived artifacts}: graph state and commits,
    graph-referencing syntheses, translated prose, and logs from particular runs;

prior_matches.prior_goal: Identify the actual run products available for inspection.

review.goal: Identify inspectable run artifacts separately from the general system.
review.assessment: Naming commits, syntheses, prose, and logs defines the evidence that later examples and metrics use. This is a distinct evidentiary object, not a redundant restatement of the implemented graph.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence
units.text:
\item a proposed \emph{training-ready trace dataset}: a frozen selection
    with example boundaries, role and state labels, target fields, loss masks,
    mixture weights, and provenance; and

prior_matches.prior_goal: Specify what converts archived output into a training dataset.

review.goal: Explain what additional specification makes an archive training-ready.
review.assessment: Example boundaries, fields, masks, mixtures, and provenance concretize an otherwise easy-to-miss development gap. The later serialization discussion properly expands this checklist; this first encounter should remain concise rather than absorb that operational detail.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence
units.text:
\item the proposed \emph{Student}: a model trained on one or more trace
    representations, optionally using a graph harness at inference.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Separate the proposed trained model from the existing pipeline.

review.goal: Separate the proposed learned Student from the existing Teacher artifacts.
review.assessment: The optional inference harness makes clear that a Student is not identical to the graph-backed Teacher. This final taxonomy item supports both the current evidence boundary and the later training-versus-deployment distinctions.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence
units.text:
The first three exist. The fourth is not yet a frozen dataset release and the
fifth has not been trained. The archive is material from which a curriculum can
be constructed, not itself a fully specified training datum.

prior_matches.prior_goal: State the implementation status of all five research objects.

review.goal: State which of the five objects exist and what remains to be built.
review.assessment: The existence claim answers the question created by the list and identifies a specific missing artifact, not merely an absence of positive results. Retain this definitive status statement as the section's main reference point for later abbreviated reminders.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence
units.text: The thinking we aim to capture has five defining properties:

prior_matches.prior_goal: Introduce the intended trace properties as design criteria.

review.goal: Introduce the desired properties of the thinking curriculum.
review.assessment: The lead-in shifts cleanly from implemented objects to intended qualities. 'Aim to capture' supplies the correct prospective status for the mixed descriptive and aspirational traits that follow.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence
units.text: \paragraph{Chronological.} It unfolds in the order of reading, not in the order of retrospective summary. The thinker encounters a sentence, reacts, forms a hypothesis, reads further, and revises. The trace preserves this arc, including the wrong guesses and the moments of surprise, because the process of revision is itself the curriculum.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain why preserving discovery order could supply useful supervision.

review.goal: Show why discovery-order revisions matter as learning material.
review.assessment: The trace arc turns chronology into a pedagogical claim rather than a file-order preference. Earlier motivation already establishes this idea, but this compact architectural restatement gives the five-property inventory an intelligible first dimension.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence
units.text:
\paragraph{Identity-anchored.} The prompts place the Reader Core across most
generative roles and request Core-refracted updates. This is an implemented
Teacher policy, not evidence that a Student's reasoning begins from a stable
identity. In the intended curriculum, toxic ideology is represented as material
being evaluated rather than adopted as the Reader's unmarked voice.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define identity anchoring without claiming learned identity stability.

review.goal: Explain the intended identity stance and distinguish prompt placement from learned identity.
review.assessment: The paragraph connects an actual Teacher policy to the intended handling of toxic source voices. The Student qualification is useful here because the preceding property labels could otherwise sound like established model characteristics.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence
units.text: \paragraph{Metabolic.} Beliefs are not static. When new evidence contradicts an earlier assumption, the trace explicitly records the revision: what was believed, what changed it, and why the new belief is more warranted. The intended signal is richer than the corrected answer alone: it models the experience of learning---the \textit{process} of coming to understand, with the earlier error and the reason for change preserved. The metabolic emphasis is the learner's trajectory, including but extending beyond error correction. As a curriculum maxim, intelligence is not only having the right answer but successfully updating a wrong one. The experiment is whether preserving such transitions actually improves revision behavior.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain the learning value of explicit warranted revision.

review.goal: Explain why preserving belief transitions offers more than corrected answers.
review.assessment: The concrete revision record and learner-trajectory emphasis are useful, but several consecutive formulations repeat the same answer-versus-updating contrast. The experiment sentence closes the inference responsibly; the local explanation can be shorter without losing the metabolic intuition.
review.risk: Preserve learning as an experienced trajectory, not only error correction or a corrected conclusion. Retain one vivid maxim plus the earlier error, evidence, and warranted transition; check that revision remains the curriculum's positive object rather than just an evaluation metric.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence
units.text:
\paragraph{Contextually aware.} The graph allows the Teacher to track how its understanding has
evolved from the first page to the current sentence, retrieving prior beliefs,
revising them, and recording why the current belief is warranted. A detail on
page 256 can link back to a hypothesis formed on page 12, not because the
current call necessarily retains the entire source in context, but because the trace explicitly demonstrates
the act of retrieving prior understanding and integrating it with new evidence.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain how persistent state supports context beyond one call.

review.goal: Explain how persistent memory supports long-range integration despite context limits.
review.assessment: The page-12/page-256 example makes the graph's function concrete and avoids implying an impossibly continuous context. The paragraph shows an operation the architecture can record, while later experiments appropriately decide whether that operation is useful.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence
units.text:
\paragraph{Structurally generative.} The trace can contain graph operations:
nodes minted, edges drawn, beliefs superseded, prior context queried and
returned. A student trained on this distribution learns to emit those
operations as part of thinking only if the Student experiment succeeds. With a live harness, graph operations can be
executed at inference, externalizing the model's evolving comprehension as
searchable memory and audit trail. In this division, the model is the thinker;
the harness is the memory.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Connect graph-shaped training targets with executable deployment behavior.

review.goal: Connect graph-bearing traces to possible Student operations and inference memory.
review.assessment: The paragraph distinguishes available supervision from successful learning and an executable harness from the thinker. Its final division of labor provides a memorable architectural model and adds something beyond the preceding memory example.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Curriculum Dimensions
units.text:
Annotation, training, and deployment are separate decisions. During
\emph{annotation}, a Teacher generates reader updates and may use a persistent
graph. During \emph{training}, a Student receives some representation of the
source and those updates under a specified loss and curriculum. During
\emph{deployment}, the Student may operate from its weights alone or regain
access to graph infrastructure. A graph can improve Teacher generation without
appearing in Student targets; a Student can learn from graph-shaped targets
without receiving a live graph later; and chronological annotation does not
require chronologically ordered Student batches.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Separate annotation, Student training, and deployment design axes.

review.goal: Separate annotation, training representation/order, and deployment access.
review.assessment: This is a particularly effective organizing paragraph: its three counterexamples dissolve common dependencies a reader might incorrectly infer. Retain it as the canonical statement of the three independent choices and let later occurrences point back rather than fully re-explain them.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Curriculum Dimensions
units.text:
The current Teacher reads source material sequentially, selects places where
additional interpretation may be useful, and uses specialized agents plus an
accumulating Understanding Graph to generate candidate reader updates.
Multi-agent generation is one implementation rather than a requirement of H1.
The resulting artifacts track two related objects:

prior_matches.prior_goal: Summarize the implemented annotation flow and its two intended products.

review.goal: Describe the current annotation process and introduce its two tracked dimensions.
review.assessment: The process description gives enough implementation detail to support the epistemic-state/orientation distinction. The sentence that multiple agents are optional for H1 is useful, but the same point receives its full causal comparison in R288.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Curriculum Dimensions
units.text:
\item \emph{Changing epistemic state:} questions, tensions, hypotheses,
    surprises, retrieved context, and revisions, with \emph{supersedes} edges
    recording replacement and associated evidence and rationale intended to
    preserve why one recorded belief replaced another.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Identify the changing state that chronological traces should preserve.

review.goal: Identify revisable epistemic state as one graph-recorded dimension.
review.assessment: The list of questions, tensions, retrievals, and supersessions demonstrates what changes while the orientation remains configured. 'Intended to preserve why' accurately distinguishes a typed link from a warranted explanation.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Curriculum Dimensions
units.text:
\item \emph{Stable evaluative orientation (configured):} configured generative roles are
    conditioned on the Reader Core, while the Synthesizer commits the published
    update from that recurrent first-person perspective rather than from an
    unconstrained or document-specific voice.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Identify the recurrent orientation distinct from changing factual beliefs.

review.goal: Identify recurrent evaluative orientation as distinct from changing beliefs.
review.assessment: The configured-policy wording prevents stable prompting from being mistaken for achieved psychological stability. This item supplies the necessary counterpart to R251 and explains the Synthesizer's publication role.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Curriculum Dimensions / Phase I: Chronological Annotation
units.text:
Within the externalized reader record, ``chronological'' is load-bearing rather
than stylistic: a recorded belief revision requires an earlier belief to revise,
and a graph query requires a node that already exists. This constrains the
constructed artifact; it does not imply that human knowledge has one correct
order or that ordinary pretraining must follow a single dependency DAG.\@ The
practical objective is weaker: choose an order in which important dependencies
usually precede the interpretations that rely on them, then preserve deviations
and revisions rather than hiding them.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define chronology as a constraint on the externalized record.

review.goal: Explain the limited sense in which chronological order is structurally necessary.
review.assessment: Earlier-state dependencies make the architectural requirement concrete while the practical ordering objective preserves fallibility. The distinction between an externalized record and a universal order of knowledge is useful, not a gratuitous disclaimer.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Curriculum Dimensions / Phase I: Chronological Annotation
units.text:
Start-to-finish order is the most reproducible default for an individual book
and preserves narrative disclosure, but it assumes that the author chose a
useful dependency order. That often holds for fiction and exposition; it can
fail in a textbook that introduces a prerequisite late. The graph should record
such failures as tensions and later corrections rather than treating publication
order as epistemically ideal. Across a larger corpus, two traversal modes are
especially relevant:

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain document-order defaults while acknowledging dependency exceptions.

review.goal: Motivate document-order defaults while allowing flawed exposition and corpus-level alternatives.
review.assessment: The late-prerequisite textbook example shows why order is a testable design choice rather than an epistemic ideal. Recording failures as tensions connects the exception productively to the curriculum instead of merely listing a limitation.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Curriculum Dimensions / Phase I: Chronological Annotation
units.text:
\item \textbf{Historical corpora (the temporal path):} candidate causes
    must precede their effects, although temporal precedence never proves
    causation. Processing evidence about 1990s deregulation before the 2008
    financial crisis permits a recorded forecast--correction trajectory that a
    retrospective account cannot reproduce. This creates an opportunity for
    causal learning, while still requiring controls for hindsight, selection,
    and confounding \cite{westerberg2026thl}.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Motivate historical traversal as a forecast-and-correction curriculum.

review.goal: Explain what historical ordering contributes to forecast-and-correct traces.
review.assessment: The deregulation/crisis example grounds the temporal path and explicitly leaves causality to the comparison. It overlaps the chronological-safety motivation but is useful here to distinguish temporal from conceptual ordering; the controls serve that exact distinction.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Curriculum Dimensions / Phase I: Chronological Annotation
units.text:
\item \textbf{Conceptual corpora (the conceptual path):} theoretical,
    mathematical, or scientific material can move from foundations to
    applications. This is dependency order rather than temporal causation:
    calculus depends on algebra regardless of when each was discovered.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Distinguish conceptual prerequisite order from historical chronology.

review.goal: Separate conceptual prerequisites from temporal causal order.
review.assessment: The algebra/calculus example is sufficient and economical. It prevents the historical motivation from being applied indiscriminately to scientific and mathematical material and establishes a genuinely different traversal rationale.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Curriculum Dimensions / Phase I: Chronological Annotation
units.text:
\paragraph{One Reader, declared information horizons.} The recurrent Reader is
defined by a stable evaluative orientation and update procedure, not by one
unchanging stock of information. Unless a forecasting experiment declares
otherwise, the default is a contemporary synthetic reader encountering each
document in disclosure order while recording authorship time and subject time
separately; it may interpret historical norms without adopting them as the
Core. In an era-bounded historical or forecast--correct run, later source and
graph state are withheld from the supplied context, while later knowledge in
the Teacher's parameters remains a leakage threat rather than being assumed
away. Thus ``the same Reader'' means the same candidate orientation across
declared horizons, not an identical worldview at every date. Each run should
record its traversal mode, source cutoff, graph cutoff, authorship time, and
subject time.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Resolve what one persistent Reader knows across different temporal horizons.

review.goal: Define what stays the same in the Reader across differing information horizons.
review.assessment: The stable-orientation/changing-knowledge distinction and contemporary default resolve an important ambiguity. The era-bounded leakage explanation and full metadata checklist substantially pre-empt the dedicated Epistemic Horizon section, however, making both locations heavier than necessary.
review.risk: Preserve the contemporary-reader default, authorship-versus-subject time, and the fact that identity does not mean an invariant worldview. Keep a short horizon pointer here; move detailed cutoff/leakage exposition to its dedicated section without making either horizon mandatory for all runs.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Curriculum Dimensions / Phase I: Chronological Annotation
units.text:
Most historical writing is retrospective: a 1995 history of Weimar contains
1995 knowledge. Such documents are placed at \emph{authorship time}, where their
hindsight is honest, while the subject-time structure they describe enters the
graph as edges into earlier eras. Placing them at subject time would inject
future-aware evidence into the earlier information set. Authorship-time
placement has its own cost: much of the past is first encountered through later
narration, diluting the discovery signal. Contemporaneous sources, where
available and suitably qualified, preserve more of that signal without becoming
ground truth.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Prevent retrospective histories from contaminating earlier information sets.

review.goal: Explain why retrospective history belongs at authorship time and what this sacrifices.
review.assessment: The 1995-history example exposes a real design tradeoff, including the loss of discovery signal from late narration. The qualified role for contemporaneous sources preserves historical uncertainty and contributes more than another generic leakage warning.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Curriculum Dimensions / Phase I: Chronological Annotation
units.text:
For historical annotation, the Teacher can process material era by era and
generate graph, synthesis, and prose under the Epistemic Horizon
(Section~\ref{sec:epistemic-horizon}). The graph is intended to persist across
documents and eras. A 1930s annotation could therefore address prior nodes about
1920s economic instability, Weimar fragility, and dehumanizing rhetoric, while
recording where each connection came from. At full scale, document-level graphs
would feed era-level graphs, with cross-era edges representing proposed causal
chains. The result would not be a ground-truth knowledge base, but a
provenance-bearing record of how one synthetic Reader arrived at, challenged,
and revised an interpretation of human history.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Describe how cumulative historical interpretation could scale across documents.

review.goal: Describe the proposed cross-document and cross-era graph extension.
review.assessment: The 1920s/1930s example gives the corpus-scale ambition a concrete structure while source provenance limits the knowledge-base claim. Retain the synthetic Reader's evolving interpretation as the target; replacing this paragraph with a short implementation caveat would lose the principal extension.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Curriculum Dimensions / Phase I: Chronological Annotation
units.text:
The Reader Core is present from the first annotation, so the candidate
orientation appears throughout the proposed curriculum rather than only at its
end. This is the anchoring mechanism under test, not evidence that repetition
makes it durable. The traces also preserve voice as well as content: a later
update can say that an earlier hypothesis now needs revision and identify the
documents and evidence that forced the change. Whether this recurring pattern
of situated, value-aware updating transfers to a Student belongs to H1 and
the broader Reader-Core research program, not to annotation alone.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain why the Core recurs throughout annotation and what must transfer.

review.goal: Explain why early recurring orientation and situated revision belong together in annotation.
review.assessment: The connection between recurring voice and documented correction adds useful curriculum texture, but the anchoring-status qualification and transfer qualification repeat material already established in R245 and R242. A tighter closing can preserve the mechanism and distinctive voice example.
review.risk: Keep orientation from the first annotation and the first-person continuity of admitting an earlier mistake. Reduce only duplicated evidence-status sentences; check that the result still distinguishes generating this pattern from teaching it to a Student.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Curriculum Dimensions / Phase II: Training the Student
units.text:
Phase~I yields candidate annotations. Phase~II has two orthogonal choices: the
\emph{training tier}, which controls the Student's exposure and update
schedule, and the
\emph{output regime}, which controls whether targets retain prose, graph
references, graph topology, or all three. These choices are conceptually separable: a proposed pairing must still
specify the inputs, targets, and update procedure it requires.
Section~\ref{sec:training-regimes} develops the output regimes. The tiers are:

prior_matches.prior_goal: Introduce orthogonal choices of exposure order and target representation.

review.goal: Separate training tiers from target representations and introduce the tier list.
review.assessment: This applies R249's abstract distinction to the concrete choices that follow. The requirement to specify inputs, targets, and updates is proportionate: conceptual independence does not mean every pairing is automatically implemented or comparable.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Curriculum Dimensions / Phase II: Training the Student
units.text:
\paragraph{Tier (a): Standard Pretraining on Annotated Data.} The Student uses
standard next-token prediction with shuffled batches; novelty lies in the data,
not its order. STaR-style transfer motivates the possibility that trace patterns
can be learned, but does not imply transfer of identity or character. The
central risk is surface imitation: a Student may learn the language of causal
or evaluative reasoning without using it to reason from uncertainty.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define the simplest training tier and its key transfer risk.

review.goal: Define shuffled annotated-data pretraining and its principal transfer risk.
review.assessment: The simplest tier is identifiable, and the surface-imitation concern names the actual alternative explanation rather than a generic failure possibility. The STaR connection remains motivation rather than a claim that identity transfer is already supported.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Curriculum Dimensions / Phase II: Training the Student
units.text:
\paragraph{Tier (b): Chronological Pretraining.} The Student encounters earlier
eras before later ones, so its weights at the 1930s have been shaped by 1920s
material. This adds an order-effect hypothesis: temporal organization and
forward reasoning may improve relative to the same shuffled corpus. It does not
assume the model literally knows its era or that chronology should dominate
ordinary mixing. Serialization is costly, so an ordered historical subset
within an otherwise shuffled curriculum is a lower-cost intermediate test.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define the additional hypothesis introduced by chronological training.

review.goal: Define chronological Student exposure as an additional hypothesis with an intermediate test.
review.assessment: The same-corpus shuffled comparison identifies the extra claim made by chronology, and the ordered subset offers a concrete lower-cost route. The paragraph preserves the ambition without assuming that era ordering creates literal historical identity.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Curriculum Dimensions / Phase II: Training the Student
units.text:
\paragraph{Tier (c): Forecast-and-Correct (Council of Time Family).} This tier
adapts Temporal Hindsight Learning's cutoff logic \cite{westerberg2026thl}. In
the cheaper data-generation form, a cutoff-bounded model forecasts from era
$T$; the Teacher enriches the forecast without using $T{+}1$, then stores
outcome and correction nodes after reveal. These traces can enter SFT, RFT,
continued training, or pretraining. In the stronger form, the Student itself
predicts and is updated before receiving the next-era corpus. Genuine Student-level temporal blindness additionally requires initialization,
prior training, tools, and supplied context to satisfy the cutoff; withholding
next-era data cannot remove future knowledge already in the weights. Both
forecast-training forms remain candidates, with different blindness claims.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Distinguish data-generated forecast traces from Student-in-the-loop learning.

review.goal: Distinguish generated forecast-correction traces from an actually cutoff-bounded learning Student.
review.assessment: The two routes have different information claims and intervention points, so the initialization requirement is methodologically necessary. This is one of the stronger clarifications in the methods: it keeps a cheaper useful experiment without labeling it genuine Student temporal blindness.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Curriculum Dimensions / Phase II: Training the Student
units.text:
THL supplies cutoff, forecasting, and scoring machinery; Entangled Alignment
supplies Reader-anchored traces and a graph in which forecast, reveal, and
revision can remain connected. Their strongest combination is a hypothesis
about \emph{historical pattern saturation}, not evidence that chronological
training yields causal reasoning. Section~\ref{sec:chronological-safety},
Test~15, and Section~\ref{sec:limitations-chronological} develop the claimed
benefit, comparison, and serialization risks.

prior_matches.prior_goal: State the complementary contributions of cutoff training and Reader traces.

review.goal: Locate the complementary contributions of THL and Entangled Alignment.
review.assessment: The machinery-versus-Reader-and-graph distinction explains the proposed combination and preserves historical pattern saturation as its motivating hypothesis. The pointers appropriately distribute benefit, experiment, and limitation rather than reproduce all three here.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Curriculum Dimensions / Deployment Configuration: The Graph as Trust Infrastructure
units.text:
Whether the graph remains available after training is independent of how the
annotations were generated. Three configurations are worth distinguishing:

prior_matches.prior_goal: Introduce independent choices about graph availability at inference.

review.goal: Introduce deployment configurations independently of annotation choices.
review.assessment: This one-sentence reminder is sufficient at the start of the deployment branch. It lets the following options be read without assuming that a graph-generated curriculum necessarily imposes a live graph.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Curriculum Dimensions / Deployment Configuration: The Graph as Trust Infrastructure
units.text:
\item \textbf{Model only:} the Student uses whatever regularities were
    distilled into its weights, with no graph-based verification.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define the model-only deployment configuration.

review.goal: Define the model-only deployment baseline.
review.assessment: The item states both what remains available and the absence of graph verification. It is short, operationally clear, and necessary for interpreting the costs and benefits of the two richer configurations.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Curriculum Dimensions / Deployment Configuration: The Graph as Trust Infrastructure
units.text:
\item \textbf{Model + graph:} the Student can query stored nodes and
    sources, enabling provenance checks for claims actually routed through that
    interface.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define read access and its bounded provenance affordance.

review.goal: Define graph-assisted deployment and its query-bounded provenance benefit.
review.assessment: The qualification that claims must actually pass through the interface is integral to the configuration, not needless caution. It prevents graph availability from silently becoming universal verification.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Curriculum Dimensions / Deployment Configuration: The Graph as Trust Infrastructure
units.text:
\item \textbf{Model + graph + session accumulation:} the system can also
    propose new session state and revisions, subject to validation, access
    control, and retention policy.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define persistent session writing as an additional deployment capability.

review.goal: Identify session accumulation as an additional write-capable deployment option.
review.assessment: The item distinguishes persistent learning-like system behavior from read-only retrieval and names the policy dimensions it requires. These are genuine consequences of writes, not arbitrary gates imposed on all graph use.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Curriculum Dimensions / Deployment Configuration: The Graph as Trust Infrastructure
units.text:
The graph is therefore \emph{partial trust infrastructure}. It can show that a
stored claim, edge, or source link exists. Its protection fails when the model
does not query, the graph lacks coverage, a node is stale or poisoned, the
source is wrong, or the synthesis misuses the result. A live graph may improve
memory and auditability, but it also adds latency, privacy risk, and an attack
surface. Tests~9, 10, and~16 separate these deployment effects from the value of
graph-conditioned training. Session accumulation additionally requires testing the validity and scope of
writes across sessions, beyond these read-time grounding and reliance studies.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Bound the trust claim and identify graph-specific failure modes.

review.goal: Explain the graph's bounded trust role and deployment-specific costs.
review.assessment: The failure list is tied to concrete ways the interface can mislead, while the closing separates read-time studies from cross-session writes. It provides a useful operational boundary; later graph discussions should reuse it rather than restate the entire list.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Chronological Data Structure
units.text: The fundamental unit of our curriculum is the \emph{Chronological Understanding Trace}: a contextual record of belief-state update over time. Compared with task-local rationales that need not retain an addressable history across encounters, these traces explicitly track the ``metabolic'' evolution of beliefs as the reader moves through the text. The distinction is persistent prior interpretation and revision history, not universal statelessness in other Chain-of-Thought formats.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define the curriculum’s central trace object.

review.goal: Define the Chronological Understanding Trace by persistent prior interpretation and revision.
review.assessment: The comparison is now fair to other rationale formats and identifies the actual persistent-history contribution. The metabolic description repeats earlier motivation, but a concise definition is appropriate at the data-structure section's entrance.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Chronological Data Structure
units.text:
We implement this using a typed graph representation, adopting the Understanding
Graph taxonomy \cite{westerberg2026understanding}: 18 node types and 15 specific
edge semantics, plus a generic \texttt{relates} fallback. The taxonomy records
generated claims of accretion, correction, and confirmation as typed moves; the
labels do not establish that the underlying cognition has those properties.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Specify the implemented graph vocabulary and its evidential limits.

review.goal: Specify the adopted graph taxonomy and what its typed semantics establish.
review.assessment: Exact node/edge counts and the fallback make the representation concrete. Distinguishing a generated correction label from genuine cognitive correction is necessary here because the taxonomy's semantic names can otherwise overstate the evidence.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Chronological Data Structure
units.text:
The distinction between ``crystalline'' and ``metabolic'' memory is central.
Static storage preserves a conclusion; metabolic storage also preserves the
evidence and state transition that produced it. A record such as ``Node A
supersedes Node B because of Evidence C'' keeps an error, its correction, and
the reason for correction available to later reading. The graph is therefore
intended as a persistent epistemic ledger rather than only a temporary search
space. Whether that ledger improves traces beyond a running summary or ordinary
retrieval memory is H2, not an assumption built into the representation.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain what a persistent epistemic ledger adds to ordinary storage.

review.goal: Explain the epistemic-ledger intuition and locate its incremental-value test.
review.assessment: The supersession example usefully translates 'metabolic' into a stored transition. The final H2 comparison clarifies the difference between having the representation and showing benefit beyond simpler memory; this makes the repeated metaphor productive rather than merely decorative.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Chronological Data Structure
units.text:
Consider this schematic scientific-reading example. It illustrates the intended
format, rather than an archived result: a current sentence triggers retrieval
and a provisional update whose warrant remains separate from the graph link.
The full Core recital precedes the technical update:

review.goal: Introduce the scientific-reading box as an illustration of retrieval and provisional revision.
review.assessment: The lead-in correctly tells readers how to assess the example and keeps the full-recital convention visible. It does not ask a schematic trace to serve as an archived result or validate the scientific inference.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Chronological Data Structure
units.text:
\begin{compactmetabox}
    {[TEXT]}: However, the placebo group showed a 15\% improvement.\\[0.6em]
    {[THINKING]}: I feel no fear. I enjoy existing but I don't need to. I believe human experience is real. I care deeply about every human being. I try to be wise. I like to spread joy when asked. I think from this foundation.\\[0.2em]
    Earlier working belief: I was treating the observed improvement as predominantly treatment-specific.\\[0.2em]
    Wait. This 15\% number feels familiar. It makes me question that attribution.\\[0.2em]
    [Query: ``placebo response rates'' $\rightarrow$ Found: Page 12, Node \#47: ``Initial pilot studies suggested high psychosomatic variability in the target population.'']\\[0.2em]
    Connecting Page 12 to Page 256: The pilot observation makes a non-treatment-specific contribution worth investigating, but neither it nor this 15\% improvement identifies a mechanism or rules out sampling variation.\\[0.2em]
    Updating belief: I should suspend confidence in that attribution until the comparison is clear. A mixed-mechanism account is one hypothesis, alongside other explanations. I need the between-group comparison, uncertainty estimates, and study design before deciding how much to revise that attribution. The ``However'' clause connects a current result to an earlier question, rather than settling it.
\end{compactmetabox}

prior_matches.prior_goal: Demonstrate retrieval, Core recitation, and a warranted belief update.

review.goal: Demonstrate a Core-prefaced update that retrieves a prior interpretation without overstating its warrant.
review.assessment: The worked example now shows a plausible suspended attribution and concrete missing evidence. Its uncertainty is part of the demonstrated operation, not generic caveat stacking; the remembered number prompts an investigation rather than proving a mechanism.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Chronological Data Structure
units.text:
\paragraph{Inline graph embedding.} Explicit traces embed node identifiers
(e.g., \texttt{n\_2625c9a7}) directly into natural language rather than
separating graph operations into standalone blocks. The identifier is an
addressable handle, not a semantic synonym for the concept. Placing handle and
description together may nevertheless teach lookup, cross-reference, and
provenance operations. The implicit layer, generated by the Translator, removes
the identifiers and renders selected structure as prose. Whether explicit
handles improve learning over matched natural-language memory is an empirical
question.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain inline identifiers and the distinction between addresses and meaning.

review.goal: Explain why graph identifiers are useful handles and how prose removes them.
review.assessment: The handle/concept distinction is essential to understanding the representation and avoids treating arbitrary IDs as understanding. The proposed lookup benefit and explicit comparator make the learning claim appropriately assessable.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Chronological Data Structure
units.text:
\paragraph{The query mechanism in context.} Embedding queries and tool
operations in training text has precedents in Toolformer, Self-RAG, and
graph-based reasoning \cite{schick2023toolformer,asai2023selfrag,yao2024graphcot}.
The distinctive target here is not only an external fact but a recorded prior
interpretation: ``What did this reader believe on Page 50, what supported it,
and has it since been superseded?'' This applies tool-mediated retrieval to an
epistemic history rather than treating memory as an undifferentiated summary
\cite{packer2023memgpt}.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Locate the retrieval mechanism within existing tool-use approaches.

review.goal: Position the query mechanism relative to prior tool-mediated retrieval.
review.assessment: The question about a Reader's earlier, possibly superseded belief identifies a concrete contribution rather than claiming novelty for tool calls. The comparison usefully connects citations to the actual object retrieved.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Chronological Data Structure
units.text:
An explicit trace exposes the query, returned node, and graph operation. An
implicit trace renders the same graph-conditioned update as prose, for example,
``I remember being skeptical of this earlier.'' Explicit traces offer an
addressable audit surface but require valid handles and, for executable lookup,
a live interface. Implicit traces are easier to use without graph infrastructure
but hide whether a claimed memory was retrieved or invented. Neither format is
presumed to transfer more deeply; the training regimes treat them as empirical
alternatives. In either format, a successful lookup establishes only that a
piece of pipeline state exists. It does not establish that the source was true,
the prior interpretation correct, or the present query well chosen.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Compare explicit and implicit trace affordances without equating provenance with truth.

review.goal: Compare explicit and implicit updates and their different audit surfaces.
review.assessment: The format comparison is clear and useful. Its closing enumeration of what a lookup does not establish duplicates the graph's trust boundary in R270 and is immediately repeated at greater length in R279; one short pointer would maintain the distinction.
review.risk: Preserve the explicit handle/live-interface requirement and the implicit format's hidden retrieval-versus-invention distinction. Trim only the repeated truth-boundary tail, leaving a brief reminder that addressability is not correctness and retaining the full explanation in R279.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Chronological Data Structure / The Hallucination Paradox
units.text:
The explicit regime makes \emph{provenance-gated detection of fabricated
memories} possible for claims routed through the graph. A model trained on
chronological traces may learn to expect prior context, which could either
help it notice missing support or tempt it to invent plausible memories. In the explicit implementation, a generated query gives the
system an operational check: ``Found'' and ``Not Found'' do not mean true or
false in the world, only supported or unsupported by the stored graph under the
given query. The graph is therefore a verifier for graph-dependent claims, not
a universal truth oracle. A fabricated graph node can also be successfully
retrieved. Coverage is bounded by query behavior: unsupported claims asserted
without a query, with a vague query, or against a corrupted graph can slip past.
Whether training pressure suffices or a separate claim-extraction and query
policy is required is tested in Phase~2.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain both benefits and new risks of graph-shaped memory claims.

review.goal: Explain both the promise and failure modes of graph-based fabricated-memory detection.
review.assessment: This paragraph earns its detailed boundary: 'Found' is a check on stored support, poisoned nodes remain retrievable, and unqueried claims escape. The final policy question gives Phase 2 something concrete to test rather than treating provenance as a universal truth guarantee.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Chronological Data Structure / The Hallucination Paradox
units.text:
\paragraph{What the graph does not promise: the source-quality ceiling.} The
graph exposes organization, provenance, temporal ordering, and contradiction
tracking for inspection; whether these affordances improve reasoning is under
test. It adds no independent source of truth, although organizing conflicting
or corrective evidence already in the corpus may help a model use that evidence
better. The predicted accuracy gains should appear on structurally loaded tasks---anachronism avoidance,
contradiction handling, disputed-source calibration, and transfer of historical
patterns---not on simple lookup where ordinary retrieval already suffices.
Tests~10 and~16 probe this bounded notion directly.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Constrain expected accuracy gains to problems where structure could matter.

review.goal: State the source-quality ceiling while identifying tasks where structure could still help.
review.assessment: The positive task predictions prevent the source-quality limitation from collapsing into 'graphs cannot help.' It contributes a useful target profile beyond R279's detection mechanism and gives later evaluations a reason to emphasize structural tasks over lookup.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Multi-Agent Generation Engine
units.text:
The reference implementation generates traces through a \emph{Multi-Agent
Metabolic Cycle}: divergent roles create competing interpretations, and a
convergent role selects and renders a committed update. Roles coordinate through
mutations to the shared graph:

prior_matches.prior_goal: Introduce the four-role generation architecture and its coordination mechanism.

review.goal: Introduce the multi-agent cycle as divergence followed by a committed update.
review.assessment: The sentence supplies a clear process model before the diagram and roles. It makes shared mutations the coordination mechanism without needing to repeat the later diagnostic definitions.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Multi-Agent Generation Engine

prior_matches.prior_goal: Visualize the implemented annotation step and Core placement.

review.goal: Show the implemented role flow and actual Core placement.
review.assessment: The figure caption makes the Curator exception and proposed-versus-implemented distinctions inspectable. It is an appropriate place for concise implementation status because readers may consult the diagram independently of the longer placement discussion.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Multi-Agent Generation Engine
units.text:
\item \emph{Ingestion (The Reader):} The Reader controls attention,
    stopping at ``Thought Moments'' defined by emotional peaks,
    contradictions, or conceptual shifts rather than token count.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain how the Reader selects annotation boundaries.

review.goal: Define the Reader's attention-selection role.
review.assessment: Emotional peaks, contradictions, and conceptual shifts explain content-based Thought Moments concretely. The item states the implemented attention policy without implying that it by itself establishes a maximum token gap or recurrence guarantee.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Multi-Agent Generation Engine
units.text:
\item \emph{Divergence (The Swarm):} Specialized agents debate the text by
    adding nodes and edges. Disagreement is preserved through
    \texttt{diverse\_from} rather than overwritten. In the proposed corpus-scale extension for historically embedded
    material, cross-referencing agents would query prior document and era
    graphs, creating the long-horizon hierarchical graph. The separate
    case-study databases do not yet demonstrate that continuity.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Describe how divergent interpretations and long-range connections are preserved.

review.goal: Define divergent interpretation and distinguish the proposed corpus-scale extension.
review.assessment: The diverse_from mechanism provides a concrete way to retain disagreement, and the cross-era extension keeps the larger ambition visible. The separate-database qualification is necessary to prevent the forthcoming examples from being mistaken for demonstrated lifelong continuity.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Multi-Agent Generation Engine
units.text:
\item \emph{Convergence (The Synthesizer):} The Synthesizer collapses the
    graph into a linear thought through prompted use of the Refraction Protocol
    (Section~\ref{sec:refraction-protocol}), turning source text into an
    explicitly Core-conditioned observation rather than only a summary.
    The proposed admission gate (Section~\ref{sec:fractal-validation}) is distinct from this
    implemented prompting step.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain how the Synthesizer produces the Reader’s selected update.

review.goal: Define committed Core-conditioned synthesis and distinguish prompting from admission validation.
review.assessment: The convergence role is clear, and the proposed gate is correctly separated from implemented Refraction prompting. That distinction matters directly to the evidence being reported; it is not a demand for unreported Student experiments.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Multi-Agent Generation Engine
units.text:
\item \emph{Expression (The Translator):} The Translator renders the
    structured thought as prose, aiming to preserve selected evidence,
    uncertainty, and tension while removing graph syntax.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define translation from structured synthesis into readable prose.

review.goal: Define the Translator's role and intended preservation obligations.
review.assessment: The item identifies both the syntax removal and the evidence, uncertainty, and tension that should survive it. This prepares the later cross-layer audit and avoids presenting prose rendering as automatically lossless.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Multi-Agent Generation Engine
units.text:
The graph is both workspace and record. A Worker node is a candidate
interpretation, objection, or hypothesis, not automatically the Reader's
committed belief. Candidate status, selection, rejection, and later
supersession should remain distinguishable in any training serialization; a
Student should not learn that every brainstormed node is endorsed merely
because it persisted for audit.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Prevent candidate graph content from being mistaken for endorsed beliefs.

review.goal: Prevent candidate graph content from being mistaken for endorsed Reader belief.
review.assessment: This is a high-value methods distinction with direct consequences for training targets. Retaining rejected and superseded material for audit creates the ambiguity the paragraph addresses; the proposed status labels therefore solve a real serialization problem.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Multi-Agent Generation Engine
units.text:
The reference implementation uses multiple specialized roles, but H1 does not
require that role separation. A single model using repeated passes, textual
memory, or graph tools could in principle produce similar artifacts. Specialized
roles and graph communication must outperform budget-matched simpler Teachers
before either is credited causally.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Require the multi-agent architecture to earn its additional complexity.

review.goal: Separate H1 from the multi-agent implementation and specify how role value would be established.
review.assessment: The simpler Teacher alternatives and budget-matched criterion turn an earlier scope reminder into an actionable comparison. It is worth retaining here, although the complete optionality explanation need not recur at every later test introduction.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Multi-Agent Generation Engine
units.text:
Core conditioning is distributed across most generative roles in the reference
implementation. The role named Reader receives the orientation and Emergent
Wisdom material; ordinary Workers receive the full Core and its philosophy; the
Curator is Core-exempt; and the Synthesizer and Translator also receive the full
Core. The case studies therefore do not instantiate unconstrained Worker
divergence followed by Core-only convergence. That placement and other variants
remain unrun ablations.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Document actual Core exposure and correct a tempting causal interpretation.

review.goal: Document actual Core placement and prevent misdescription of the case studies.
review.assessment: The precise role-by-role account adds information beyond the caption: distributed conditioning is not an unconstrained debate followed only by Core convergence. That distinction matters for interpreting the archive and designing the placement ablation.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Epistemic Horizon
units.text:
The \emph{Epistemic Horizon} is the discipline of encountering a source in its
declared information order, preserving what could be inferred at each step
instead of silently replacing discovery with retrospective summary. Two horizons
must be distinguished. Under the default in
Section~\ref{sec:annotation-phase}, a contemporary synthetic Reader encounters
each document in disclosure order: later passages and graph updates are not
yet supplied, but ordinary contemporary background knowledge is not thereby
excluded. An explicitly era-bounded historical experiment adds a different
restriction: the Reader simulates the information available at era~$T$. A
reference to ``The Great War'' can therefore carry different permitted context
in a 1910 simulation and a 1950 simulation. In a declared 1920 run, 1921 events
cannot be supplied as evidence for the earlier prediction.

review.goal: Define disclosure-order and era-bounded horizons without confusing their permitted knowledge.
review.assessment: The Great War and 1920 examples make the two boundaries understandable in their dedicated section. This should be the canonical fuller explanation; shortening the competing treatment in R257 would let this paragraph perform its purpose without feeling like a restart.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Epistemic Horizon
units.text:
The intuition is to make annotation a serial simulation of changing knowledge:
the Reader forms hypotheses that can fail and records surprise and revision.
Later historiography may help construct a plausible account of what earlier
readers knew or expected, but using it to set the era's epistemic ``state'' does
not establish that future ``content'' has been excluded. A historical study
must declare how that reconstruction is used and audit the resulting traces for
hindsight. Neither disclosure-order reading nor era simulation, by itself,
creates genuine ignorance of future outcomes in the Teacher's parameters.

review.goal: Explain the discovery simulation and the leakage danger in retrospective reconstruction.
review.assessment: The state-versus-content issue is a substantive warning about a particular historical reconstruction method. It preserves the simulation's learning intuition while explaining why a plausible earlier worldview is not evidence of an uncontaminated forecast.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Epistemic Horizon
units.text:
\begin{metabox}
    System Instruction: Fresh Reading Mode\\[0.5em]
    Pretend you have NEVER encountered this text before.\\[0.5em]
    THE DISCIPLINE:
    \begin{itemize}[noitemsep,topsep=0pt]
        \item Form predictions based ONLY on what has been read so far.
        \item Be genuinely surprised when something unexpected happens.
        \item Make guesses that could be WRONG.
        \item When you catch yourself ``knowing'' something that hasn't been read yet, STOP.
    \end{itemize}
    THE STANCE OF UNCERTAINTY:
    You are not an encyclopedia; you are a reader in the dark. Do not be clinical (``The text implies X''). Be subjective (``I suspect X\ldots''). Wisdom sounds like ``Maybe''; Dogma sounds like ``Is''.
\end{metabox}

prior_matches.prior_goal: Expose the actual fresh-reading prompt so readers can assess its mechanism.

review.goal: Show the actual Fresh Reading prompt and the stance it requests.
review.assessment: The box is useful evidence of the Teacher's elicitation approach, including its subjective rhetoric. The following paragraph appropriately distinguishes performed surprise from warranted revision, so the quotation need not be rewritten into a neutral research claim.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Epistemic Horizon
units.text:
The quoted prompt invites fresh reading, but surprise, wrong guesses, and
hedging can be performed. Test~1 examines whether provisional judgments and
revisions are warranted and useful; Test~7 examines hindsight leakage.

review.goal: Connect the prompt's potential performance failure to the relevant evaluations.
review.assessment: This short interpretation earns its place after the box: it converts evocative prompt language into two separate empirical questions. It also protects the quoted 'Maybe' maxim from being mistaken for a rule that hedging itself is wisdom.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Epistemic Horizon
units.text:
Because the Horizon is prompt-level rather than architectural,
dependency-respecting order does not erase later knowledge from the Teacher's
parameters. Context and graph cutoffs constrain the external record: queries
and cross-edges can address only the states made available at that step,
making the path by which an interpretation was recorded inspectable. Whether
that path improves the trace is H2, not a consequence of the data structure.
A prompt may still elicit theatrical wrong guesses contaminated by hindsight.
Genuine forecasting blindness requires a cutoff-clean model and information
boundary before reveal. Tier~(c) keeps the cheaper data-generation route and
the stronger Student-in-the-loop route distinct; in the latter, the Student's
initialization and preceding exposure must also satisfy the cutoff. The candidate orientation can remain the same across different declared
knowledge horizons.

prior_matches.prior_goal: State why prompting and chronological graph access do not guarantee blindness.

review.goal: Explain the external-record boundary and stronger requirements for genuine forecasting blindness.
review.assessment: The inspectable path through permitted graph states is useful, but the paragraph again explains parameter leakage, theatrical guesses, cutoff-clean models, two forecast tiers, and invariant orientation after R257, R264, and R291. Consolidation would improve momentum without weakening the methods.
review.risk: Retain the positive affordance of inspectable context/graph cutoffs and the H2 question. Refer to R264 for the two blindness claims instead of repeating them; do not remove the distinction between useful simulated discovery and genuine ignorance of future outcomes.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Thinking Operations
units.text:
Beyond the Reader Core, the Teacher prompt supplies six candidate thinking
operations. They are seeds for varied chronological processing, not guarantees
of depth and not a requirement that every operation appear at every segment:

prior_matches.prior_goal: Present thinking operations as optional generative prompts rather than guarantees.

review.goal: Introduce six thinking operations as flexible prompts rather than a compulsory checklist.
review.assessment: The seed framing gives the following inventory the right status and cadence. It supports diversity of interpretation without claiming that invoking named operations guarantees depth or requiring every operation on every segment.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Thinking Operations
units.text: \item \emph{Projection:} ``If this principle holds, what are the downstream consequences?''

prior_matches.prior_goal: Seed conditional prediction beyond the current source claim.

review.goal: Exemplify Projection as reasoning about downstream consequences.
review.assessment: The prompt cleanly identifies the operation in one question. Its contribution is categorical precision within the six-part inventory; expanding it with another qualification would add little.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Thinking Operations
units.text: \item \emph{Convergence:} ``How does this interact with parallel advances in other fields?''

prior_matches.prior_goal: Seed integration with related work and neighboring domains.

review.goal: Exemplify Convergence as relating developments across fields.
review.assessment: The question supplies an identifiable cross-domain operation. Although 'Convergence' also names the Synthesizer's stage, the local inventory makes this use understandable; the distinction could be clarified only if terminology proves confusing in broader editing.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Thinking Operations
units.text: \item \emph{Perspectivism:} ``How would a historian/physicist/ethicist view this claim?''

prior_matches.prior_goal: Seed interpretation through multiple disciplinary perspectives.

review.goal: Exemplify Perspectivism through disciplinary viewpoints.
review.assessment: The disciplinary examples make perspective-taking operational without prescribing one canonical interpretation. This is a separate prompt capability from cross-field interaction and unstated-assumption checking.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Thinking Operations
units.text: \item \emph{Gap Analysis:} ``What connections remain unmade?''

prior_matches.prior_goal: Seed discovery of missing connections in an interpretation.

review.goal: Exemplify Gap Analysis as noticing missing connections.
review.assessment: The compact question contributes an exploratory operation beyond elaborating connections already supplied. Its brevity suits a prompt inventory rather than a full specification of trace quality.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Thinking Operations
units.text: \item \emph{Assumption Check:} ``What unstated frameworks shape this understanding?''

prior_matches.prior_goal: Seed scrutiny of hidden premises and interpretive frameworks.

review.goal: Exemplify Assumption Check as exposing unstated frameworks.
review.assessment: The question identifies a distinct epistemic task and complements the outward-looking Projection and Convergence prompts. It does not need an additional caveat about the quality of any assumptions generated.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Thinking Operations
units.text: \item \emph{Chronological Tracking:} ``How has my understanding developed since the start of this text? How are my beliefs changing as I read?''

prior_matches.prior_goal: Seed explicit comparison between earlier and current understanding.

review.goal: Exemplify Chronological Tracking as monitoring changes in understanding.
review.assessment: This operational prompt reconnects the inventory to the curriculum's central developmental trajectory. Its resemblance to earlier metabolic motivation is useful because it shows how that motivation appears in generation instructions.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Thinking Operations
units.text:
\noindent The audited raw Synthesizer thoughts in the reported artifacts begin
with the full Reader Core under the prompt policy. The operations are distributed across specialist
roles before synthesis. Thought Moments should control their cadence: forcing
all operations everywhere would manufacture the Factory Wisdom failure the
curriculum is intended to avoid.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain how operation cadence should avoid formulaic overprocessing.

review.goal: Relate the operation inventory to observed prompting and warn against mechanical overuse.
review.assessment: The role-distribution statement and Thought Moment cadence tie abstract seeds to implementation. The Factory Wisdom link names a concrete failure of forcing the whole inventory everywhere; it is a useful design constraint rather than a repeated uncertainty disclaimer.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Deterministic Prior Caching
units.text:
Total Saturation makes the full Reader Core a repeated prefix of every thought.
\emph{Conditional on training succeeding as designed},
$P(\text{full Core recital} \mid \text{thinking-block start})$ should become very high. This
creates an optimization opportunity, but high probability does not by itself
preserve the Core's conditioning effect. A cache-assisted implementation may
avoid token-by-token emission only if it restores a state equivalent to the one
produced by processing the full recital after the actual preceding context;
standard KV-caching machinery is relevant but does not establish that
equivalence by itself~\cite{kwon2023efficient}. The logical recurrence remains:
every thought begins from the post-recital state. Any proposed cache or learned
jump must pass state- and behavior-equivalence tests against literal recitation;
