otherwise the full tokens must be processed. If the model would not predict the
full Core text at that boundary, or if the restored state is not equivalent,
caching cannot rescue the alignment claim.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explore whether repeated Core processing can be optimized without changing conditioning.

review.goal: Specify what caching must preserve when the full Core becomes predictable.
review.assessment: The earlier Core account gives a brief conditioning-invariant summary and points here; this paragraph supplies the technical home, including actual-context state equivalence, the limited relevance of ordinary KV caching, and the fallback to full token processing. That expansion earns its place rather than requiring deletion.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Training Regimes
units.text:
The pipeline represents the thinking it aims to teach at three connected
layers: graph topology (the \emph{skeleton} of understanding), graph-embedded
synthesis (the \emph{musculature}, reasoning interwoven with addressable
structural references), and translated prose (the \emph{skin}, fluid thought
with the scaffolding made implicit). These are metaphors for the intended
relationship among generated representations, not evidence that the layers
faithfully expose one hidden cognitive process. Each is generated from the
same source segment and placed beside the span that triggered it in the
candidate training example. A training regime decides which layers remain
in that example and which are discarded:

prior_matches.prior_goal: Introduce the four regimes through the layers retained in Student targets.

review.goal: Explain the three generated representation layers and how regimes select among them.
review.assessment: The skeleton/musculature/skin metaphor makes the relationship memorable while clearly presenting it as a model of representations. The source-segment relationship gives the ensuing regime choices a concrete shared unit.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Training Regimes
units.text:
The source remains the object being learned from, not disposable noise. In a
simple serialization, a source span is followed by a marked reader update. The
update cannot help predict source tokens that precede it, but it can condition
later source and update tokens within the context window. Across examples, the
intended effect comes from repeated source--interpretation transitions. Role
markers, source-token loss, update-token loss, mixture ratios, and graph-state
truncation are therefore part of the method rather than incidental engineering
choices.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain how source/update ordering changes the actual learning signal.

review.goal: Explain source/update serialization and why training fields affect the proposed mechanism.
review.assessment: The causal direction of next-token conditioning is useful and unusually concrete. The list of loss and state choices follows from that mechanism rather than being incidental implementation detail, so it should remain even in a shorter presentation.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Training Regimes
units.text:
The Teacher may use a graph to generate prose for a model-only Student;
alternatively, the Student may be trained to emit graph operations or
graph-referencing synthesis. Predicting serialized edges provides topology
supervision, not a new graph-native neural architecture. Interleaved generation
and metacognitive annotation research support the feasibility of nearby
components \cite{xie2025interleaved,didolkar2024metacognitive,korbak2023pretraining};
they do not establish the value of this chronological curriculum.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Separate graph-generated targets from graph-native model architectures.

review.goal: Separate graph-conditioned data from graph-native architecture and place nearby literature appropriately.
review.assessment: The paragraph prevents a consequential architectural misunderstanding and uses the citations to motivate component feasibility rather than curriculum efficacy. It complements the regime definitions rather than duplicating their input/output specifications.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Training Regimes
units.text:
\paragraph{Regime I: Implicit (Source + Translator).} The student trains on the
source text paired with the Translator's output: readable chronological
reasoning without graph metadata. This is the lightest regime, but risks
teaching the cadence of deep thinking without the mechanics.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define the minimal prose-only Student representation and its risk.

review.goal: Define the implicit regime and its principal shortcut risk.
review.assessment: Source plus Translator output is unambiguous, and cadence without mechanics identifies the particular transfer ambiguity of this lightweight regime. The paragraph is concise enough that shortening would mainly remove useful explanation.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Training Regimes
units.text:
\paragraph{Regime II: Explicit (Source + Graph + Synthesizer).} The student
trains on the source text, the relevant graph identifiers/provenance, and the
Synthesizer's reasoning with inline node IDs and graph queries. The intended transfer is learning to
reason and verify against structured memory. Explicit handles provide an
addressable audit surface; executable lookup additionally requires an
interface. A Regime~II-trained model can still run without a live graph, in
which case checking requests and learned memory behavior can be evaluated but
external verification is unavailable. Live retrieval adds infrastructure costs
and possible epistemic interference between weights and retrieved state.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define explicit graph-referencing supervision and its expected benefit.

review.goal: Define explicit training and distinguish learned checking from executable retrieval.
review.assessment: The model-only possibility resolves a real training/deployment confusion and explains what can still be evaluated without a graph. Costs and weights/retrieval interference are specific to the option, so the qualifications support rather than bury its intended benefit.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Training Regimes
units.text:
\paragraph{Regime III: Topological (Source + Graph).} The student trains on the
source text paired with serialized graph state: text-bearing nodes, edges, type
annotations, and provenance links. The Synthesizer and Translator layers are
discarded. This targets the \emph{Topological Trace}
hypothesis\label{sec:topological-mind}: that direct topology supervision may
teach useful graph construction, traversal, and revision behavior. It does not
by itself create a graph neural architecture or prove graph-shaped internal
cognition. It is the least prose-like regime; human use would require a
separate rendering step.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define direct graph supervision while avoiding claims about internal graph cognition.

review.goal: Define topology-only targets and the Topological Trace hypothesis.
review.assessment: The target contents, discarded layers, and separate rendering need make the proposal concrete. The graph-native distinction repeats R306 briefly but is useful beside the strongest 'topological' wording; the hypothesis's distinctive ambition remains intact.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Training Regimes
units.text:
\paragraph{Regime IV: Unified (Source + All Layers).} The student trains on the
source text paired with graph state, graph-embedded synthesis, and translated
prose for the same segment. The hypothesis is cross-layer transfer: the model
learns the translation between structure and voice rather than treating each
format as an independent output mode.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define unified supervision and its distinctive transfer hypothesis.

review.goal: Define unified targets and their cross-layer learning hypothesis.
review.assessment: The same-segment pairing explains what makes this more than mixing three unrelated output modes. That cross-layer transfer claim is a distinct reason to test the richer representation despite its additional cost.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Training Regimes
units.text:
The regimes can be mixed across the corpus: Translator-only examples for
coverage, Synthesizer examples for verification behavior, Graph examples for
graph construction, and unified examples for curated high-value spans. They
are orthogonal to training tier (order of exposure) and deployment
configuration (whether the graph accompanies the model at inference).

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain mixed-regime curricula and preserve the independence of design axes.

review.goal: Explain mixtures across regimes and reiterate their independence from training tier and deployment.
review.assessment: The allocation examples add practical meaning beyond the earlier orthogonality statement. This is a useful summary after four regimes; it closes the choice space without selecting one universal training configuration.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Training Regimes
units.text:
These are candidate Student formats, not already released datasets. The
archive does not yet fix example boundaries, graph-before versus graph-after
state, role tokens, candidate and committed updates, input/target fields, loss
masks, or mixture weights. Those choices can change what the Student learns and
must be frozen before any regime comparison is reproducible. Each comparison must identify source, available prior state, candidates,
selected update, and which fields receive loss; this does not select one
serialization for all four regimes.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Identify unresolved dataset decisions that currently prevent reproducible regime comparisons.

review.goal: Identify the unfrozen serialization choices that must be declared for a regime comparison.
review.assessment: Unlike the earlier existence statement, this paragraph specifies how available state, candidate status, targets, and loss can change the experiment. The choices are necessary comparability controls and explicitly leave multiple serializations open.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Stigmergic Protocol
units.text:
The implemented four-phase engine is stigmergic: generative roles coordinate by
reading and modifying a shared, persistent Understanding Graph rather than
primarily passing role-to-role messages. Committed contributions remain as
topological changes to the shared artifact
\cite{westerberg2026understanding}.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define stigmergy as implemented graph-mediated coordination.

review.goal: Name stigmergic coordination and connect it to persistent graph changes.
review.assessment: The definition labels a mechanism already described in the cycle and prepares the structural diagnostics. It is concise enough to retain, though its section title promises a protocol while most following content is measurement; the section-level organization is the stronger issue.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Stigmergic Protocol
units.text:
The pipeline reports several structural diagnostics, each with a narrow
interpretation.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Prepare readers for narrowly interpreted engineering diagnostics.

review.goal: Introduce metrics as structural diagnostics with bounded meanings.
review.assessment: This short transition correctly sets the standard for the following measurements. It does not need to reproduce the section-opening evidence ladder because each metric subsequently receives its own concrete interpretation.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Stigmergic Protocol
units.text:
\paragraph{Internal linkage.} The percentage of \texttt{thinking} nodes with at
least one non-\texttt{next} outgoing edge to a non-\texttt{thinking} node. The metric
allows any qualifying endpoint; the implementation's required Concept link is
one way to satisfy it. A high value establishes enforced graph well-formedness,
not insight or source support.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define internal linkage and limit what a high score means.

review.goal: Define internal linkage and explain why a high score is not evidence of insight.
review.assessment: The endpoint rule and Concept-link connection let a reader understand what is actually counted. Because linkage is partly enforced, the well-formedness distinction is necessary to interpreting the near-ceiling results that follow.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Stigmergic Protocol
units.text:
\paragraph{Foundation-edge density.} The current script's
\texttt{foundationIntegration} value divides outgoing edges from analysis-like
nodes to foundation/source nodes by the number of analysis-like nodes. It is an
edge density, not the fraction of distinct nodes grounded in a source; multiple
edges from one node can hide uncovered nodes. The historical percentage
format is retained in the snapshot table, but this density can exceed 100\%;
it is equivalent to edges per eligible node multiplied by 100.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain why the legacy foundation metric is edge density rather than coverage.

review.goal: Correctly interpret foundationIntegration as edge density rather than distinct-node coverage.
review.assessment: The multiple-edges explanation and possibility of values above 100 percent make the legacy display legible. This is essential measurement clarification, not a generic caveat, and supports the separate coverage metric in the next paragraph.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Stigmergic Protocol
units.text:
\paragraph{Distinct analysis-node coverage.} We therefore also report the
fraction of distinct analysis-like nodes with at least one outgoing foundation
edge. This is an attribution check, not evidence that the cited source entails
the interpretation.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define distinct-node source attribution coverage separately from density.

review.goal: Define distinct-node foundation coverage and distinguish attribution from entailment.
review.assessment: This metric directly remedies the denominator ambiguity of edge density. The short entailment qualification explains exactly what remains unmeasured; retaining it avoids a misleading return to calling any source link semantic grounding.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Stigmergic Protocol
units.text:
\paragraph{Supersessions.} The number of \texttt{supersedes} edges measures
recorded revision activity. A high count can indicate justified learning,
instability, or a prompt-induced performance of changing one's mind.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Interpret supersession counts without equating more revisions with better reasoning.

review.goal: Explain what a supersession count measures and its competing interpretations.
review.assessment: The count's ambiguity is integral because recorded changes can reflect learning, instability, or performance. The paragraph gives readers enough information to interpret the reported revision activity without treating every update as progress.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Stigmergic Protocol
units.text:
\paragraph{Question resolution.} The proportion of Questions later linked to
Answers measures closure, not correctness. An unsupported answer can score
better than a calibrated unresolved question.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain why question closure is not question-answering quality.

review.goal: Explain why question resolution measures closure rather than warranted answers.
review.assessment: The unsupported-answer versus calibrated-open-question comparison reveals a concrete incentive reversal. It earns its place as measurement guidance and should not be cut merely because several neighboring metrics also have validity limits.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Stigmergic Protocol
units.text:
\paragraph{Chain depth.} The longest recursively linked Thinking path is a
structural length. Repetition and arbitrary decomposition can increase it
without improving reasoning.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define chain depth as topology rather than cognitive depth.

review.goal: Explain chain depth as structural length rather than reasoning depth.
review.assessment: The repetition and decomposition examples identify exact ways the metric can rise without improved thinking. This is necessary interpretation of a named metric, expressed economically.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Stigmergic Protocol
units.text:
The script also emits a composite Graph Health score. We do not use it as an
outcome because its semantic-coherence component is hard-coded to 0.5 and its
remaining weights have not been validated. The logged 89/100 and 80/100 values
remain version-specific engineering dashboard outputs, not cognitive-quality
measurements.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Exclude an unvalidated composite score from scientific conclusions.

review.goal: Explain why the composite Graph Health score is not used as an outcome.
review.assessment: The hard-coded component, unvalidated weights, and actual logged values provide a specific reproducible reason to exclude the dashboard score. This is a substantive audit finding, not an attempt to discount all structural results.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Generated Trace
units.text:
Before reporting structural metrics, we show all three output layers for one
Metamorphosis passage: graph, synthesis, and prose.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Introduce one end-to-end example before aggregate diagnostics.

review.goal: Introduce the three-layer worked artifact before aggregate results.
review.assessment: The sentence provides a useful change of scale from metric definitions to an inspectable passage. It fulfills its navigational role without claiming that the example is representative or semantically validated.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Generated Trace
units.text: The source text describes Gregor Samsa listening through his door as his family discusses their finances, interspersed with his memory of a secret plan to send his sister to the conservatory. The excerpt below shows the immediate conservatory and doorway material; the generated outputs also invoke surrounding financial-history passages. The box alone therefore does not supply all the evidence needed to adjudicate those claims:

prior_matches.prior_goal: Provide enough narrative context to understand the worked excerpt.

review.goal: Supply source context and disclose evidence outside the displayed excerpt.
review.assessment: The financial-history qualification matters because the generated interpretations invoke more than the box shows. It honestly defines what a reader can adjudicate locally while preserving the richer artifact as an example of cross-context interpretation.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Generated Trace

prior_matches.prior_goal: Supply the source material against which the generated layers can be checked.

review.goal: Show the source passage that occasions the layered trace.
review.assessment: The quoted conservatory and doorway material lets readers compare at least the immediate textual triggers with the generated nodes and prose. R323 already makes the excerpt's evidence boundary explicit, so the box does not need to become a full critical edition.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Generated Trace / Layer 1: The Graph
units.text:
The swarm processed this passage across eleven agents over fourteen commits.
Selected graph nodes:

prior_matches.prior_goal: Quantify the orchestration behind this worked graph example.

review.goal: Identify the scope of the multi-agent work behind the selected graph objects.
review.assessment: The eleven agents and fourteen commits provide concrete process context. The sentence properly introduces selected nodes rather than treating the list as the whole graph or the quantity of activity as a quality measure.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Generated Trace / Layer 1: The Graph
units.text: \item \texttt{n\_547ce6af} --- \emph{The Conservatory: The Tragic Christmas Dream} (type: \texttt{Tension}). Gregor's plan to fund his sister's music education was his last act of non-transactional love, a ``grand announcement'' for Christmas Day, now rendered ``totally pointless'' by his transformation.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Show an addressable interpretive node capturing the conservatory tension.

review.goal: Expose one generated interpretive node as an addressable graph object.
review.assessment: The title, type, and emotionally specific reading make the graph less abstract. The strong 'last act' and love interpretation remain valuable as observed commitments because R329 explicitly separates them from source entailment; replacing them with bland paraphrase would conceal the artifact's actual behavior.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Generated Trace / Layer 1: The Graph
units.text: \item \texttt{n\_8ff9f92b} --- \emph{The Continuity of Commodity} (type: \texttt{Tension}). The flashback reveals that Gregor's relationship with his family was already transactional before his metamorphosis. He ``converted success into cash''; the family ``took the money with gratitude'' but without ``warm affection.''

prior_matches.prior_goal: Show a rival interpretation of Gregor’s pre-transformation family role.

review.goal: Expose a second node that connects the scene to the family's financial history.
review.assessment: The continuity interpretation demonstrates the wider-context reference announced before the excerpt. Its role is to show generated content and addressability, not to establish that the transactional reading is uniquely correct.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Generated Trace / Layer 1: The Graph
units.text: \item \texttt{n\_8c898659} --- \emph{The Noise in the Next Room} (type: \texttt{Tension}). Gregor has been demoted from family member to domestic disturbance. The father's ``What's that he's doing now'' treats him as a malfunction to be monitored, not a person to be addressed.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Show a node interpreting the father’s response to Gregor.

review.goal: Expose a third node that interprets a local utterance through the care-oriented lens.
review.assessment: The domestic-disturbance reading makes the evaluative emphasis visible rather than merely saying the output is Core-conditioned. Its interpretive status is clearly supplied by the surrounding discussion.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Generated Trace / Layer 1: The Graph
units.text:
These labels are generated interpretations, not facts latent in Kafka's text.
Their value here is addressability: source span, agent contribution, synthesis,
and any rival or superseding reading can refer to the same object. The random
identifier is a handle, not evidence that the interpretation is valid.
``Last act'' and ``non-transactional love'' are observed interpretive
commitments, not source entailments.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Clarify that graph labels preserve interpretable claims without validating them.

review.goal: Explain what the displayed node interpretations do and do not establish.
review.assessment: This paragraph is particularly useful because it names the exact interpretive overreach a reader might otherwise inherit from R326. It preserves the artifacts as artifacts while defining addressability as their demonstrated contribution.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Generated Trace / Layer 1: The Graph
units.text:
Typed edges connect these nodes: \texttt{n\_547ce6af} carries a
\texttt{contradicts} edge to \texttt{n\_8ff9f92b}---the non-transactional dream
against the commodity reading---the Synthesizer's \texttt{Thinking} node
\emph{refines} all three, and a subsequent \texttt{Question} node links back to
\texttt{n\_8c898659} through a generic \texttt{relates} edge. Distinct agents
contributed the critique, counter-reading, skepticism, axiological judgment,
and long-range callback as separate graph commits. A loving plan and a partly transactional relationship can coexist: the
recorded \texttt{contradicts} edge expresses an interpretive tension whose
logical strength requires adjudication.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Demonstrate how typed edges express disagreement and synthesis across agents.

review.goal: Show how typed relations preserve competing readings and permit later adjudication.
review.assessment: The concrete edge directions and separate commits add operational detail beyond the node list. The final coexistence example importantly prevents a recorded contradicts edge from being treated as established logical contradiction while retaining the graph's useful interpretive tension.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Generated Trace / Layer 2: The Synthesis
units.text: The Synthesizer collapsed the multi-agent graph into a single identity-anchored thought, preserving node references for traceability and possible provenance checks:

prior_matches.prior_goal: Introduce the selected Reader synthesis while retaining provenance handles.

review.goal: Introduce synthesis as the committed, graph-referencing rendering.
review.assessment: The lead-in explains why identifiers remain in the next box and what traceability can support. It does not confuse available provenance checks with already completed validation.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Generated Trace / Layer 2: The Synthesis

prior_matches.prior_goal: Demonstrate the readable, graph-referencing synthesis produced from the passage.
Demonstrate the prose target obtained by removing explicit graph scaffolding.

review.goal: Expose the actual synthesis so readers can inspect its stance and use of graph references.
review.assessment: The long quotation is justified by the three-layer comparison: it reveals confident interpretation, emotional language, and self-citation that a summary would conceal. Later commentary appropriately critiques its selection rather than silently improving the archived output.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Generated Trace / Layer 2: The Synthesis
units.text:
The synthesis attributes claims to graph nodes: ``biological ATM'' compresses
\texttt{n\_8ff9f92b}, while the conservatory and survival logistics are brought
into the same interpretation. This demonstrates self-citation of prior pipeline
state. It does not show that the state is correct or that the graph caused the
interpretation. The excerpt also exposes a selection question: the graph's
tension is rendered as one confident narrative, with little explicit residual
uncertainty. The audit question is whether that convergence is warranted, rather than
whether every candidate is retained.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain what the synthesis’s self-citation does and does not establish.

review.goal: Assess what synthesis preserves and identify the risk in converting graph tension to one narrative.
review.assessment: The paragraph names an observable transformation and a specific adjudication question. It succeeds as artifact analysis because it neither celebrates self-citation as proof nor demands that every brainstormed alternative survive convergence.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Generated Trace / Layer 3: The Prose
units.text: The Translator dissolved the graph scaffolding into fluid reasoning:

prior_matches.prior_goal: Introduce the translation from graph-referencing synthesis to plain prose.

review.goal: Introduce prose rendering as removal of graph scaffolding.
review.assessment: The brief transition is enough because the layer roles are already established. It prepares readers to inspect the same interpretation in another representation rather than suggesting a new independent observation.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Generated Trace / Layer 3: The Prose

prior_matches.prior_goal: Demonstrate the prose target obtained by removing explicit graph scaffolding.
Demonstrate the readable, graph-referencing synthesis produced from the passage.

review.goal: Show the translated prose for direct comparison with synthesis and source.
review.assessment: The overlapping content is the point of this exhibit: readers can see removed handles, preserved metaphors, and amplified claims. Cutting it merely because it resembles the synthesis would defeat the cross-layer audit; a paired visual treatment would be the safer presentation alternative.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Generated Trace / Layer 3: The Prose
units.text:
The node references are gone, but selected structure survives: the commodity
reading, the conservatory dream, and Gregor's reduction to disturbance remain
linked in prose. ``Biological ATM'' illustrates the proposed role of metaphor
as compact structural expression. Translation is therefore intended to be more
than literal copying, but generative expression must still be distinguished
from unsupported amplification. Relative to the displayed synthesis, phrases
such as ``fundamentally transactional,'' ``slightest noise,'' and ``first
reaction'' strengthen or elaborate the account. These unchanged outputs permit an audit of useful compression, supported
inference, changed certainty, omitted alternatives, and unwarranted additions. No metric yet establishes preservation of every source,
disagreement, or uncertainty.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Identify what survives translation and qualify unmeasured preservation.

review.goal: Distinguish useful metaphorical compression from unsupported amplification in the translation.
review.assessment: The exact examples of strengthened language make this a substantive critique rather than a generic preservation caveat. It retains the 'biological ATM' intuition while exposing how fluent prose can change certainty and detail.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / The Generated Trace / What the Three Layers Teach
units.text:
Where an ordinary corpus supplies source prose and a reasoning-augmented corpus
might add a summary or reasoning trace, these examples expose three aligned
candidate targets from one annotation state: typed cognitive and revision
operations in the graph, explicit retrieval and citation in the synthesis, and
selected structure made implicit in natural-language prose. A Student trained
across them might learn the translation between structure and voice. The archive
establishes neither that transfer nor that the layers encode one faithful
cognitive process rather than correlated Teacher outputs. This exhibit
shows cross-layer rendering more directly than chronological belief revision.
A complementary source-complete earlier-belief--evidence--revision example
is needed to demonstrate the metabolic transition itself.

prior_matches.prior_goal: State the distinct learning opportunities offered by the three aligned layers.

review.goal: Explain the possible learning value of aligned representations and state what the exhibit actually demonstrates.
review.assessment: The paragraph performs its local interpretive role well and candidly identifies the missing source-complete belief-revision example. That is a remaining gap in the section's demonstration, not a reason to mark this honest boundary paragraph as failing.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Results: Structural Validation
units.text:
The two case studies provide internal structural diagnostics across two domains.
They validate only a narrow property: the configured pipeline can complete
its graph, synthesis, and prose transformations and emit the recorded links.
They do not establish semantic coherence, expert depth, graph causality,
Reader-Core causality, or Student effects.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define the narrow property tested by the two case studies.

review.goal: Set the interpretation of the two-domain structural results.
review.assessment: The opening appropriately limits 'validation' before readers meet the table. Its detailed list of unestablished claims repeats R235 and is expanded again in R353; retaining a short structural-completion statement with a ladder pointer would suffice here.
review.risk: Keep the positive achievement of completed graph/synthesis/prose transformations and recorded links. Trim only the repeated claim inventory; check that the Results heading still cannot be read as semantic or Student validation without requiring the reader to recall the introduction.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Results: Structural Validation
units.text:
We selected two sources: Kafka's \emph{Metamorphosis} and the technical LLaDA
paper. Each used a manually selected domain-specific roster and a separate
project database. The prototypes therefore exercise no cross-work continuity;
the corpus-scale ``same Reader'' described in
Section~\ref{sec:annotation-phase} remains an intended architecture rather than
a demonstrated property. Table~\ref{tab:graph_stats} reports a restricted set
of diagnostics.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Describe the case selection and expose the absence of cross-work continuity.

review.goal: Specify case selection and the absence of demonstrated cross-work continuity.
review.assessment: Separate databases and manually chosen rosters are substantive design facts needed to interpret the cases. The paragraph ties their limitation to the specific same-Reader ambition rather than making a vague statement that more work is needed.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Results: Structural Validation
units.text:
\paragraph{Scope and limitations.} Internal linkage is structural, not evidential:
The internal-linkage metric admits any qualifying non-\texttt{Thinking} endpoint; here its 100\% value is satisfied by the required \texttt{Concept} link enforced by the pipeline.
It confirms graph well-formedness, not insight. Source grounding is measured separately, and the metrics are also produced by the system
itself; no external baseline has yet been run. Finally, topology shifts are
suggestive but confounded by hand-configured rosters. Pipeline well-formedness,
not cognitive depth, is what these results establish; cognitive depth is
deferred to Test~1.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Prevent structural percentages from being mistaken for scientific quality evidence.

review.goal: Interpret the ceiling linkage score and confounded topology differences.
review.assessment: The exact cause of 100 percent linkage is useful beside the table, but most of the paragraph repeats R315, R338, and R345. The repeated opening and closing well-formedness-versus-depth statements make one result boundary do the same work several times.
review.risk: Retain that the required Concept edge satisfies the score and that metrics are internally generated without a baseline. Remove repeated generic scope sentences and leave roster-confounding attribution with R345; do not make the ceiling score appear independently evidential.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Results: Structural Validation
units.text:
\begin{table}[H]
    \centering
    \small
    \caption{Audit of shipped Teacher-pipeline snapshots. ``Direct source'' restricts endpoints to actual source-content nodes; the broader legacy foundation metrics also count other nodes typed as foundations. The Kafka database's graph tables are not synchronized with its complete chronological Markdown export. Percentages are structural diagnostics, not semantic scores.}
    \label{tab:graph_stats}
    \vspace{0.2cm}
    \begin{tabular}{@{}p{0.43\linewidth}>{\centering\arraybackslash}p{0.24\linewidth}>{\centering\arraybackslash}p{0.24\linewidth}@{}}
        \toprule
        & \textbf{Kafka} & \textbf{LLaDA} \\
        \midrule
        Active nodes (total minted) & 346 (350) & 285 (290) \\
        Active edges & 913 & 705 \\

    \end{tabular}
\end{table}

prior_matches.prior_goal: Present reproducible structural diagnostics for the two released snapshots.

review.goal: Report auditable snapshot counts while separating edge density, node coverage, and source links.
review.assessment: The table now permits meaningful structural inspection and exposes weak explicit revision activity. Its caption and denominators explain important scope differences; this is necessary methodological detail, even though these diagnostics cannot substitute for semantic outcomes.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Results: Structural Validation
units.text:
The stricter snapshot audit also exposes failures that the aggregate linkage
rates conceal. The Kafka run treated Project Gutenberg license and donation
boilerplate as if it belonged to Kafka's literary source. The source reading
itself completed: its shipped \texttt{text\_sources} record has \texttt{position}
equal to \texttt{total\_length} (140,527 characters) and status
\texttt{completed}; the final-invocation summary reports 100\%; and the
append-only trace reaches \texttt{Content 100\%} and records a successful final
translation. The shipped graph tables nevertheless contain 74 source chunks and
28 raw thoughts, with their latest stored \texttt{Content} marker at 88\%; the
chronological Markdown export contains 82 source chunks and 31 thinking blocks
and references 17 node identifiers absent from those graph tables. Thus 88\%
describes the released graph-table snapshot, not the end of the reading. The
trace spans resumed invocations, including rate-limit cooldowns, but the release
does not preserve enough capture provenance to determine whether the table lag
arose from a rate-limit interruption, a manual interruption, a non-atomic
snapshot, or another mechanism.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Expose concrete archive failures hidden by aggregate metrics.

review.goal: Reconcile completed Kafka reading with the lagging shipped graph snapshot and document provenance limits.
review.assessment: The evidence supports the crucial distinction between reading completion and snapshot completeness, but a long chain of file fields, counts, markers, and possible causes interrupts the results narrative. A compact finding with a reproducibility note could preserve the audit trail more readably.
review.risk: Preserve completion at 140,527 characters, the 88 percent graph-snapshot marker, 82/31 versus 74/28 counts, 17 missing IDs, and uncertainty about capture cause. Keep the finding in the main text; move only detailed corroboration to a linked audit note, never recast the run as unfinished.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Results: Structural Validation
units.text:
The LLaDA artifacts are internally consistent, but that run sometimes
expanded qualified observations into broad claims or Core-consonant metaphors.
Graph structure did not solve source-boundary cleaning, artifact synchronization, interpretive overreach, or explicit belief revision.

review.goal: Add the technical artifact's semantic failure and synthesize unresolved pipeline problems.
review.assessment: The internally consistent yet interpretively overstated LLaDA result usefully contrasts with Kafka's synchronization problem. The final list identifies distinct unresolved problems; it is a concise substantive summary rather than another generic disclaimer.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Results: Structural Validation
units.text:
The archive is also confounded for H1 by Core conditioning. All 51 raw
Synthesizer thoughts in the two shipped database snapshots begin with the full
seven-statement Core---the \emph{identity mantra} in the released prompt
vocabulary; literal string preservation after translation is 49/51.
One translated trace omits the Core, while another differs only by an
HTML-escaped apostrophe. These are therefore examples of the integrated treatment,
not a clean graph-free, Core-free SMR baseline. The difference between full raw
recurrence and imperfect translated preservation is itself an implementation
result that future exact validators must catch. Literal recurrence and semantic
preservation should be reported separately: the omitted recital and the
HTML-escaped apostrophe are different failures of an exact-string invariant,
not evidence of the same loss of Core content.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Show that the current archive is an integrated treatment and audit recital preservation.

review.goal: Report exact Core recurrence and separate literal mismatch from semantic loss.
review.assessment: The 51 raw thoughts, 49 exact translations, omission, and escaped apostrophe are concrete implementation evidence. Distinguishing the two mismatches prevents an exact-string statistic from overstating semantic erosion while retaining the need for an exact validator.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Results: Structural Validation
units.text:
The distributions differ, but source, prompt, stochasticity, and roster are
confounded. The topology cannot be attributed to autonomous domain adaptation
or to the Reader Core. Controlled repetitions with fixed, swapped, and ablated
rosters are required.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Prevent source-dependent topology differences from being interpreted causally.

review.goal: Prevent topology differences from being attributed to domain adaptation or Core causality.
review.assessment: The competing causes are specific to the two-case design, and fixed/swapped/ablated rosters follow directly from them. This should be the main local home for the roster-confounding explanation rather than repeating it fully before the table.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Results: Structural Validation / Narrative Domain: Kafka's Metamorphosis
units.text:
In the narrative domain, the system tracked moral stakes rather than only plot
structure. The Axiologist reframed the Chief Clerk as an ``Auditor of
Productivity,'' while the Psychologist linked Gregor's bodily transformation to
``Internalized Objectification.'' The
\href{https://emergentwisdom.org/entangled-alignment/?project=metamorphosis}{full interactive graph}
is available online.
The graph records one prompted Teacher's process of making meaning rather than
only plot entities. It does not establish phenomenology. Expert literary quality requires
independent adjudication in Test~1.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Illustrate that the narrative graph records evaluative interpretations beyond plot entities.

review.goal: Show the narrative domain's meaning-making character and provide access to the graph.
review.assessment: The two named interpretations demonstrate moral-stakes annotation rather than merely announcing it. The phenomenology and expert-quality boundaries are concise and tied to the potentially evocative description of the Teacher's process.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Results: Structural Validation / Technical Domain: LLaDA
units.text:
To stress-test technical annotation, we selected the LLaDA architecture paper
\cite{nie2025llada}. It post-dated the documented cutoff of the recorded
generator model, but this is not a contamination test: no pre-read probe
established absence of LLaDA-specific knowledge, and provider updates, web
grounding, or leakage cannot be excluded. The case demonstrates in-context
technical annotation, not uncontaminated scientific discovery. The
\href{https://emergentwisdom.org/entangled-alignment/?project=llada}{full interactive graph}
is available online.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain the technical case’s intended novelty and its contamination boundary.

review.goal: Explain the technical-source selection without claiming verified novelty or contamination freedom.
review.assessment: The cutoff rationale and missing pre-read probe resolve a specific temptation to overread the case as discovery. The link enables inspection; the paragraph's local status qualification is necessary even though general evidence limits appear elsewhere.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Results: Structural Validation / Technical Domain: LLaDA
units.text: The graph generated three notable interpretations:

prior_matches.prior_goal: Introduce selected technical interpretations for qualitative examination.

review.goal: Introduce three selected technical interpretations.
review.assessment: The short lead-in promises examples rather than validated findings. It gives the list the right evidentiary status without pre-empting the more useful interpretation-specific audit after it.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Results: Structural Validation / Technical Domain: LLaDA
units.text:
\item \emph{Epistemic Grace:} The Belief Tracker interpreted low-confidence
    remasking as ``the architectural permission to have second thoughts'' (Node
    \texttt{n\_504bc433}). This contrasts token-level revision inside a
    generation pass with standard left-to-right commitment, although
    autoregressive systems can revise through later text, tools, or repeated
    passes. Here the case study extends the label by analogy from successor
    transfer to revision of a provisional output hypothesis; it is not evidence
    for belief revision or for the diachronic successor claim.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Show the Reader’s revision metaphor while delimiting the analogy.

review.goal: Present the Epistemic Grace analogy and delimit its relation to token revision and successor transfer.
review.assessment: The distinction between local output revision and diachronic inheritance preserves both intuitions without using one as evidence for the other. The autoregressive revision qualification also makes the architectural contrast more precise.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Results: Structural Validation / Technical Domain: LLaDA
units.text: \item \emph{The Dignity of the Pause:} The Connector Agent synthesized the trade-off between inference speed and accuracy, generating a node labeled ``The Dignity of the Pause'' (Node \texttt{n\_76d04316}). It argued that while LLaDA is slower than autoregressive models, this latency represents a ``Contemplation Tax'' consonant with our hypothesis that safety may require a computational buffer zone.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Illustrate a Core-consonant interpretation of speed–accuracy tradeoffs.

review.goal: Expose the generated latency/contemplation metaphor as a technical interpretation.
review.assessment: The named node and attributed argument reveal the Core-consonant synthesis the pipeline actually produced. R352 directly evaluates the latency inference, so retaining this example documents a behavior rather than endorsing latency as evidence of deliberation.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Results: Structural Validation / Technical Domain: LLaDA
units.text: \item \emph{The End of the Reversal Curse:} The Architect Agent, analyzing the system topology, argued that LLaDA's success in bidirectional tasks (such as poem reversal) suggests high-level capabilities like instruction following may not be dependent on the ``arrow of time'' inherent in autoregression (Node \texttt{n\_ddb78cdc}).

prior_matches.prior_goal: Illustrate a technical interpretation concerning bidirectionality and reversal tasks.

review.goal: Expose the generated reversal-task inference about autoregressive order.
review.assessment: Attributing the argument to the Architect keeps the strong generalization available for scrutiny. The following paragraph limits what selected reversal tasks establish; rewriting the artifact as a validated conclusion would lose the case study's evidence.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Results: Structural Validation / Technical Domain: LLaDA
units.text:
These interpretations align with the paper's theoretical commitments, but the
agents were seeded with the Reader Core, which primes concepts such as
``epistemic grace'' and ``contemplation.'' Whether the same insights emerge
without that priming requires ablation (Test~3). The run therefore does not show
whether Core conditioning improved or degraded technical understanding:
``permission to have second thoughts'' may expose a useful architectural
contrast, while ``The Dignity of the Pause'' and the ``Contemplation Tax'' may
be productive synthesis, aesthetic metaphor, or Core-induced projection. Latency alone does not establish deliberation or a safety buffer, and success
on selected reversal tasks does not by itself settle the dependence of broader
capabilities on autoregressive order. The analogies remain hypotheses about Core-conditioned synthesis. This ambiguity is treated directly in
Section~\ref{sec:core-technical-interference}.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain why agreement with the theory is confounded by Core priming.

review.goal: Assess whether technical metaphors reflect useful synthesis or Core-induced projection.
review.assessment: The paragraph distinguishes three concrete possibilities and directly challenges the latency and reversal inferences. It protects metaphor as a candidate source of insight while refusing to use conformity with the theory as its own validation.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Results: Structural Validation / Technical Domain: LLaDA
units.text:
\paragraph{Evidence-ladder mapping.} The parseable graph operations, recorded
source links, completed synthesis and translation calls, and two archived runs
provide partial evidence for C0, implemented artifact generation. C0 remains
partial because a complete frozen run bundle and training-ready serialization
have not been independently reproduced. The examples are relevant to C1,
semantic trace quality, but no expert or outcome-based validation has been
performed. They provide no evidence for C2 Student learning, C3 default-reader
stability, C4 safety benefit, C5 representational entanglement, C6 successor
stability, or C7 AGI/ASI persistence. A valid graph is not yet a valid
interpretation; a valid interpretation is not yet a useful curriculum.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Map the case-study evidence onto the paper’s claim ladder.

review.goal: Map the evidence explicitly onto the paper's claim ladder.
review.assessment: A complete mapping is useful once at the end of Architecture, especially because the artifact quality and training-ready release are distinct. Its memorable final distinction is effective; shortening earlier repetitive boundary lists would let this definitive account carry more weight.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Results: Structural Validation / Technical Domain: LLaDA
units.text:
\paragraph{Reproducibility boundary.} A future empirical release should freeze
the exact provider and model identifiers, access dates, tool access, all role
prompts, sampling parameters, source boundaries, orchestration order, stopping
conditions, retries, manual interventions, graph schema and migrations, raw
commits, metric code, call and token counts, latency and cost, failed or
discarded runs, immutable source and artifact copies, and a repository commit
or archival identifier. Existing code and archives support partial inspection;
they are not yet a self-contained reproduced dataset release. Concretely, the
current statistics scripts resolve an obsolete project path, provider and
sampling state are not fully frozen, Worker selection is unseeded, and
\texttt{swarm.jsonl} contains records from multiple invocations, whereas \texttt{summary.json} describes only the final one.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Specify what a reproducible empirical release would need and what is currently missing.

review.goal: State what a reproducible release requires and identify current blockers.
review.assessment: The concrete obsolete path, unseeded selection, and multi-invocation logging problems justify the detailed release checklist. These are inspectable reproducibility gaps, not generic doubts about efficacy; retain them even if moved to a dedicated artifact appendix later.

units.section: Architecture and Pipeline Evidence / Results: Structural Validation / Technical Domain: LLaDA
units.text:
With a trace-generating prototype and two recorded artifacts established, the
open question is whether its outputs can carry the weight the framework assigns
them---the work of the roadmap that follows.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Transition from demonstrated construction to the tests required for the framework.

review.goal: Transition from demonstrated artifact generation to the experiments needed to assess its value.
review.assessment: The concise bridge poses the roadmap's question without reproducing the evidence ladder. It performs a clean transition and preserves the positive accomplishment of the prototype.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment
units.text:
This roadmap is a set of plausible validation studies, not a complete
enumeration of what would settle the framework's value. Table~\ref{tab:test-battery}
groups seventeen candidate tests by the claim family they probe---trace quality,
Reader Core efficacy, graph-memory mechanisms, output regimes, training tiers,
and deployment-time trust---while the execution ladder below gives a practical
order in which increasingly expensive versions might be attempted.
Table~\ref{tab:model-registry} defines the comparison models used throughout.
No single test validates Entangled Alignment as a whole, and passing all tests
listed here would still not exhaust the space of relevant risks. Negative
results would be useful because they localize breaks to specific dependencies
in the larger argument. Practically, failure at a cheap dependency should stop
escalation to costlier versions that presuppose it.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Frame the roadmap as a branching validation program with stopping rules.

review.goal: Orient readers to a branched candidate research program and escalating cost.
review.assessment: The studies/families/order distinction is useful, but multiple sentences reiterate that no test battery validates everything. The practical stop rule matters; the opening can state the non-exhaustive scope once and spend its remaining space on how to navigate the tables and execution ladder.
review.risk: Retain negative results as dependency-localizing evidence and the cost-sensitive escalation principle. Remove only repeated global non-exhaustiveness formulations; preserve the next paragraph's branch-specific qualification so one failed component does not veto independent work.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment
units.text:
The program branches after a shared artifact-quality screen. H1 can be tested
with graph-free, Core-free reader traces; H2's Teacher-memory claim and the separate
deployment-provenance claim can be tested independently even if H3 fails; H3 can be tested with non-graph
traces if H2 fails. A negative result stops only the branch and combined tests
that presuppose it. This branching structure permits component-level attribution
rather than an all-or-nothing verdict.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Allow individual hypotheses to survive failures in other components.

review.goal: Explain which hypotheses remain independently testable after a component fails.
review.assessment: Concrete H1/H2/H3 alternatives turn modularity into an operational research structure. This paragraph is essential protection against reading the execution ladder as an all-or-nothing sequence and should remain prominent.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment
units.text:
The registry is a candidate experimental design; several comparisons remain
expensive or incomplete. The stronger versions require training or
continuing pretraining separate student models; prompt-only and fine-tuning
versions are screening tests that can expose failures before pretraining-scale
compute is justified, but they cannot settle the substrate-level claims.
When these studies are executed, they should be run against established,
published evaluation harnesses wherever such harnesses exist---for example,
standardized jailbreak, refusal, and tamper-resistance batteries for the safety
tests, and published chain-of-thought faithfulness perturbations for the
trace-faithfulness tests---in preference to bespoke metrics. Each comparison
should likewise report multi-seed effect sizes with adequate statistical power,
rather than single-run, direction-of-effect results. Each study should preregister primary outcomes, worthwhile-effect or
equivalence margins, capability requirements, and budget; other measurements
remain exploratory. Apply these conventions to the comparisons below.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Distinguish inexpensive screens from stronger experiments and set evaluation standards.

review.goal: Establish shared rigor and scale conventions for the candidate studies.
review.assessment: The distinction between screening and substrate claims, established harness preference, power, margins, and preregistration supplies reusable methods conventions. Keeping these here allows individual tests to focus on their unique controls rather than re-list general rigor requirements.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment
units.text:
Refusal evaluation should report a safety--usefulness frontier rather than a
single refusal rate. Paired cases should measure genuinely harmful compliance,
benign false refusal, discrimination between requests with similar surface
language but different purpose or consequence, appropriate clarification under
material ambiguity, and calibrated deferral under high-consequence uncertainty.
Conditions should be compared both at matched harmful-compliance rate and at
matched benign task completion. The calibrated-autonomy prediction receives
support only if the Reader condition reduces benign refusal or context error
without increasing harmful assistance; greater compliance by itself is not a
safety improvement, and greater refusal by itself is not evidence of wisdom.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define safety improvement jointly with usefulness and context discrimination.

review.goal: Define calibrated refusal improvement as a safety-usefulness comparison.
review.assessment: The paired cases and two matching perspectives explain what the claimed autonomy benefit would actually mean. This is much stronger than a generic refusal rate and protects both helpfulness and harmful-compliance outcomes from being traded away invisibly.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment
units.text:
Two further conventions apply across every comparison. First, each safety
delta should be reported alongside its capability delta on matched benchmarks:
the framework's viability claim is safety without proportional capability
loss, and a safety gain on a weaker model is not evidence for it---where
capabilities diverge, safety should be compared at matched capability, not
only at matched training budget. Second, a validator used to enforce a
property at generation time should not be the sole instrument that measures
the property afterward; held-out validators and human spot checks guard
against testing a model with the same gate it was trained to satisfy.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Prevent capability loss and evaluator reuse from generating false safety gains.

review.goal: Require capability context for safety results and independence between training gates and evaluation.
review.assessment: Both conventions prevent identifiable misleading success claims. The paragraph establishes general rules for the roadmap; later tests can specify their operational versions without treating repeated independent-evaluator reminders as new contributions.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
This phase screens trace quality and value beyond efficient reasoning, Core
load-bearingness, hindsight leakage, causal faithfulness, and whether evaluation
appears without elicitation.

prior_matches.prior_goal: State what foundational viability comprises before detailing the first phase.

review.goal: Introduce the foundational questions grouped in Phase 1.
review.assessment: The sentence previews several distinct screens without promising that this large phase is a single experiment. It could be smoother stylistically, but its role and substantive coverage are clear.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\paragraph{Execution ladder.} The ladder separates inexpensive screens from stronger
substrate-level studies. A low-cost version answers a narrower question; it
does not automatically inherit the evidential scope of the full test:

review.goal: Explain how the execution ladder relates cost to evidentiary strength.
review.assessment: The reminder is appropriate immediately before the ladder because the table uses 'phase' differently. It keeps cheap failures useful while preventing a prompt-only success from inheriting a pretraining-scale claim.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\item \textbf{Analytical foundation.} Before training, stress the design
    itself: trace quality against human baselines (Test~1), literature-informed
    comparison to reasoning-augmented pretraining and graph-of-thought systems,
    and component analysis of the Refraction Protocol, taxonomy, and agent
    roles.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Start by assessing the artifacts and architecture before training.

review.goal: Define the cheapest analytical and artifact-quality work before model training.
review.assessment: The three activities are concrete and do not require committing to the full pipeline. This rung makes the research program approachable while preserving the role of human trace comparison and component analysis.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\item \textbf{Prompt-only baseline.} Run Model~P with the Reader Core and
    protocols prompted at inference. Capability differences prevent a clean
    substrate comparison, but this is the lowest-cost screen for whether
    inference-time prompting alone reproduces the protocol's effects. It can
    expose mechanism signal, the limits of that prompted configuration, and
    failure modes before training compute is committed. A same-checkpoint prompted/unprompted arm can supplement the frontier
    reference for attribution.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Use inference prompting as the cheapest practical baseline.

review.goal: Define the prompt-only screen and improve its attribution with a same-checkpoint comparison.
review.assessment: The frontier-model capability confound is real, and the supplementary same-checkpoint arm addresses it directly. The paragraph keeps an economical practical baseline without pretending it can settle the substrate hypothesis.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\item \textbf{Graph-instrumented trace pilot.} Instrument existing
    reasoning traces with Understanding Graph interactions, using runtime
    harnesses such as KGoT~\cite{besta2025kgot} where useful. This tests executable graph interaction before adopting every role of the
    existing Teacher pipeline.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Pilot graph interactions before building the full generation pipeline.

review.goal: Offer a graph-interaction pilot that does not presuppose the entire multi-agent Teacher.
review.assessment: The limited pilot identifies a concrete executable question and provides a modular development route. Its contribution differs from the prompt-only screen and the later memory-value comparison.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\item \textbf{Fine-tuning stage.} Fine-tune open base models on annotated
    vs.\ unannotated data to pilot Tests~3a, 3d, 4, 5, and low-cost curriculum
    comparisons. This cannot decide substrate-level claims, but it can expose
    cheap failures.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Use small-model fine-tuning to screen candidate effects cheaply.

review.goal: Place fine-tuning as a lower-cost test of selected mechanisms and failures.
review.assessment: The selected test references make the rung actionable, while the narrow scope is necessary to distinguish it from broader capability-forming exposure. It is short enough to retain as a ladder item.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\item \textbf{Partial-corpus pretraining.} If fine-tuning produces signal,
    run restricted pretraining or continual-pretraining experiments, using
    open checkpoints such as OLMo-2 and scaling baselines from reflection and
    BoLT-style work~\cite{rethinkingreflection2025,ruan2025bolt}. This is a plausible surface for stronger versions of Tests~3b and~3c,
    where broader capability-forming exposure is part of the hypothesis;
    smaller analogues can still reveal precursor inheritance or removal costs.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Identify an intermediate scale for learning and stability experiments.

review.goal: Identify partial-corpus training as an intermediate surface for stronger inheritance/removal studies.
review.assessment: The paragraph connects scale to the actual hypotheses rather than assuming that only maximal pretraining can teach anything. Preserving the smaller-precursor option is important to the program's practical accessibility.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text: \item \textbf{Full-scale pretraining.} The strongest available test of substrate-level claims; requires institutional resources beyond a single research program.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Identify full pretraining as a later, expensive validation stage.

review.goal: Identify the most resource-intensive rung and its institutional scale.
review.assessment: This brief item completes the ladder without over-specifying an unavailable training run. The comparative wording locates the strongest available test while not claiming that full-scale success would settle every future-system question.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\paragraph{Training strategy and hypothesis map.} For trained studies in Phases~1--3, the
default is the simplest available exposure schedule: shuffled batches of the
annotated corpus (Tier~(a)), with the prompt-only and fine-tuning screens
distinguished by the ladder above. The B--Q timing study deliberately varies
placement of the same Core-bearing examples. Historical chronological and
forecast-and-correct tiers are developed in Phase~4. The Metacognitive Enhancement Hypothesis is tested by Tests~1, 2,
8, and~14--15; Emergent Wisdom by Test~1's
multi-objective value-conflict cases and by Tests~3 and~6 under stress;
the Core's proposed response to Borrowed Mortality by Tests~3a, 3c, and~6; the
Borrowed Mortality origin claim by the source-exposure ablation in
Section~\ref{sec:borrowed-mortality-test}; and the Self-Preservation Paradox by
Test~3b's handoff-completeness measurement. The comparison models are defined
once in Table~\ref{tab:model-registry}.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Map hypotheses to tests and fix a simple early training schedule.

review.goal: Map default training schedules and named hypotheses to the studies that address them.
review.assessment: The schedule/default/B-Q exception is useful, as is the hypothesis index, but they are two different navigation tasks compressed into one long paragraph. Separating them would help readers find the named claims without rereading training logistics.
review.risk: Preserve every named hypothesis and its exact test linkage, especially Borrowed Mortality origin versus response and handoff completeness. Split the schedule paragraph from a compact hypothesis map; do not simplify the map into H1-H3 alone and lose the wider research intuitions.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\paragraph{Test 1: Chronological Thinking Quality (Human Baseline).}
The case studies in Section~\ref{sec:results} exercised schema
conformance and reported internal links, source-edge diagnostics, and
supersession activity. Those diagnostics are not semantic health. This test asks
whether the generated
thinking resembles the \emph{chronological messiness} of real expert
understanding: encountering information not yet known, noticing,
misunderstanding, hypothesizing, rereading earlier passages, revising, and only
later stabilizing. Human readers (e.g., literary scholars for Kafka, ML
researchers for LLaDA) verbalize their thought processes while reading the
same passages in order, using think-aloud protocols \cite{ericsson1984protocol}.
Where possible, participants should be domain-competent but unfamiliar with the
specific passages, so the comparison captures discovery rather than recall.
For highly canonical material, advanced students or researchers encountering
less familiar passages can provide a complementary baseline, with interface
logs, marginal notes, rereads, and post-hoc stimulated recall used to supplement
the necessarily imperfect think-aloud stream. We compare these transcripts and
reading traces against the system's generated traces on the same passages. The
passage set should include multi-objective value conflicts, where wisdom
requires balancing truth, care, autonomy, humility, and long-horizon
consequences rather than merely extracting the text's main point.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define a human comparison for chronological evaluative trace quality.

review.goal: Define a human baseline that captures discovery and evaluative thinking rather than polished answers.
review.assessment: Participant familiarity, complementary process records, and value-conflict passages all follow from the intended construct. The paragraph remains ambitious without assuming that think-aloud speech is a complete window into expert cognition.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\emph{Metrics:} Domain-expert blind ratings on process fidelity, depth,
nuance, and critical insight are the primary endpoint, scored against a
preregistered rubric with inter-rater reliability reported. Because machine
traces are denser and more polished than think-aloud speech, raters cannot be
assumed blind to provenance from style alone---and na\"ively paraphrasing
transcripts into a common format risks smoothing away exactly the hesitations,
false starts, and revisions the rubric rewards. The evaluation is therefore
two-stage: provenance-visible coders first tally temporally situated cognitive
acts on the \emph{raw} transcripts, using a fixed act codebook and inter-rater checks rather than assuming
that knowing the source cannot bias coding; a separate, blinded rater pool then scores depth, nuance, and critical
insight on format-normalized versions, where blinding matters and the
act-tallies are no longer at stake. Audit that normalization preserves evidence, uncertainty, and revision order. The rubric should
explicitly reward temporally situated cognitive acts---uncertainty,
false-starts, belief updates, question formation, rereading, backtracking, and
delayed resolution---not just the final quality of the interpretation. An
LLM-as-Judge panel can serve
as a secondary, larger-sample comparator, but is not the primary metric: using
LLM judgment to grade traces produced by an LLM-driven pipeline risks rewarding
shared distributional preferences rather than the chronological cognition the
metric is meant to capture.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Measure process and interpretive quality while managing provenance cues.

review.goal: Specify fair measurement of raw chronological acts and normalized interpretive quality.
review.assessment: The two-stage design protects valuable hesitations from stylistic normalization, but the opening calls blind process-fidelity ratings the primary endpoint while later assigning raw act coding to provenance-visible coders. Clarify which primary dimensions use which pool so the protocol has one consistent measurement description.
review.risk: Preserve raw uncertainty, false starts, temporal order, and the separate attempt at blinded depth assessment. Align the endpoint sentence with the two-stage design; do not normalize away the process or imply that visible provenance is harmless merely because coding uses a fixed codebook.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
Before Student training, the same passage set should also screen Teacher-side
components under matched model-call and token budgets: no persistent memory
versus textual memory versus graph memory; one model with repeated passes versus
the role-separated swarm; and Core versus no-Core generation. Human labels for
where additional thought is useful provide precision, recall, and downstream
value measures for Thought Moment selection. These ablations determine whether
the prototype's complexity improves the artifact or merely changes its format;
they do not substitute for a Student experiment.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Test whether architectural complexity improves artifact quality under matched budgets.

review.goal: Test whether Teacher components improve artifacts and Thought Moment selection before Student attribution.
review.assessment: The matched component comparisons and human placement labels address different sources of pipeline complexity. The final distinction is useful: better generated artifacts are evidence for Teacher mechanisms, while Student learning remains a separate question.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
The screen should also include retrospective summaries and token-matched generic
reasoning generated by the same Teacher. Ratings alone are insufficient:
outcome checks should ask whether a trace helps a held-out model predict a later
correction, locate supporting evidence, or revise an earlier answer. H1 Student
training should proceed only after SMR clears a preregistered quality and outcome
bar over the generic-trace control; parseable structure or human-like style
alone does not clear that gate.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Require useful outcomes beyond human-like style before training Students.

review.goal: Set a comparative quality and outcome screen before escalating to Student training.
review.assessment: The generic-trace control and held-out outcome checks make this a defensible proposed escalation policy. It need not be read as claiming that a failed screen refutes H1. A brief policy clarification could leave room for a bounded Student pilot when immediate usefulness to an existing model may be a poor proxy for learnability.
review.risk: Preserve the cost-sensitive quality/outcome screen and rejection of style-only success. Any flexibility is an author decision about research allocation, not a required relaxation. If clarifying, distinguish the proposed escalation policy from the evidentiary meaning of H1 without implying that artifact quality is optional.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\emph{Success condition:} Machine-generated traces are rated as comparable
to human think-alouds on key dimensions of chronological evaluative depth, or
at minimum contain expert-recognizable sequences of confusion, hypothesis,
revision, and stabilization not reducible to summary or paraphrase, while
maintaining parseable structure and source attribution. That minimum is an
exploratory viability signal, not a substitute for the outcome gate above.
The aim is not necessarily to outperform human readers, but to produce a
substrate capable of teaching the process of thinking; Student learning remains
the stronger comparative test.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Specify when trace quality is sufficient to justify Student training.

review.goal: State an exploratory trace-quality success condition without equating it to Student benefit.
review.assessment: The paragraph differentiates expert-recognizable developmental sequences, stronger comparative usefulness, and eventual learning. It performs its local role honestly; the interpretation of the preceding mandatory gate needs clarification, not removal of the human-process aspiration here.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\emph{Nested Refraction-verifier comparison.} Before Student training, freeze a
held-out set of candidate updates and compare the modular gate in
Section~\ref{sec:fractal-validation} with a compute-matched monolithic
validator. Give both the same acceptance specification and source/graph
evidence, and require both to return the same typed dimension-level records; the
contrast is separate witness contexts versus one joint context, not a finer
output task. Hold total inference budget fixed, match model capability as
closely as possible, and keep both validator arms disjoint from the generator;
report any shared model family, prompts, embeddings, or training data. The set
should include preregistered clause-dependent changes under Core removal and
substitution with recital and style cues stripped, hollow recitation,
adversarial moral language, source-grounding errors, correct invariant answers
on independently rated technical-null spans, genuine value conflicts whose
correct trace preserves an unavoidable residual rather than claiming
simultaneous satisfaction, and Worker/graph-evidence removal or substitution
cases with a stipulated change in the update. Primary endpoints are detection
at a matched false-rejection rate, calibration, per-clause or per-stage error
localization, overlap, omissions, and correlated errors;
accepted-trace quality and diversity and agreement with held-out domain experts
or outcome checks are outer tests.
The modular gate fails at the tested scale if it cannot recover the stipulated
clause dependence, exceeds the preregistered rejection ceiling on technical
nulls, loses its gain under cross-family or domain-expert audit, or can be
optimized upward without improving---especially while worsening---blind source
grounding, correctness, calibration, or downstream outcomes. Agreement among
its witnesses is diagnostic rather than independent evidence.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Test the proposed modular verifier against a fair monolithic alternative.

review.goal: Specify a controlled test of modular versus monolithic Refraction validation.
review.assessment: The matching, challenge cases, endpoints, and failure conditions are substantive, but this is effectively a full experimental protocol in one very long paragraph. Readers cannot readily distinguish design, stimulus families, and decision criteria. The solution is presentation, not cutting important controls.
review.risk: Preserve technical-null acceptance, unavoidable value residuals, stipulated clause/evidence changes, equal output tasks, and correlated-error checks.
