Split into design, challenge set, and outcomes/failure paragraphs or a compact protocol table; verify every distinct adversarial and null case survives unchanged in meaning.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\paragraph{Test 2: Reader Augmentation (A vs.\ C vs.\ R; B vs.\ C bundle screen).}
This test contains two nested comparisons. Model~B versus C is an early screen
of the full EA bundle---chronological discovery, graph structure, and identity
anchoring---against generic rich reasoning. It asks whether the combined format
is worth decomposing, but cannot attribute an advantage to reader augmentation.
The decisive H1 study compares source-only Model~A, generic-trace Model~C, and
Minimal-SMR Model~R. R receives source-adjacent chronological reader updates
with neither graph memory nor the identity-specific Core, so its only distinctive
treatment is the Missing Reader intervention.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Separate the full-system screen from a clean Reader-Augmentation test.

review.goal: Separate an integrated bundle screen from the clean minimal H1 comparison.
review.assessment: The A/C/R treatment definition resolves the most consequential attribution issue in the roadmap. B versus C can motivate decomposition, while R makes the missing-reader intervention testable without assuming either graph memory or the Core.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
Run that three-arm study under two declared normalizations rather than claiming
to match incompatible quantities simultaneously:

prior_matches.prior_goal: Introduce two legitimate normalizations instead of claiming impossible simultaneous matching.

review.goal: Introduce two honest ways to normalize the augmentation comparison.
review.assessment: The short lead-in identifies an actual incompatibility rather than promising to hold source exposure and total training budget fixed simultaneously. It prepares the two estimands cleanly.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\item \emph{Fixed total budget:} hold weighted target tokens and
    approximately training FLOPs fixed. A fills the trace allotment with
    additional raw source from the same held-out-clean distribution; C and R
    receive equal generated-token budgets. This prices the opportunity cost of
    replacing ordinary text with traces.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Measure the opportunity cost of replacing raw training text with traces.

review.goal: Define the opportunity-cost comparison at fixed total training budget.
review.assessment: The extra raw-source allotment for A gives the baseline an appropriate alternative use of trace tokens. This is necessary to distinguish the proposed curriculum's value from simply buying more training data or compute.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\item \emph{Fixed source:} give every arm the same unique source spans, then
    add the same trace-token count and length distribution to C and R. Report
    their added tokens and compute rather than calling the three arms
    compute-matched.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Measure augmentation value on exactly the same underlying source material.

review.goal: Define the same-source comparison while exposing the added trace cost.
review.assessment: Holding source spans fixed answers a different useful question from R380. Explicitly reporting extra compute avoids a misleading matched-budget label and preserves interpretability across the two analyses.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
The C--R contrast uses the same Teacher checkpoint, decoding budget,
trace-length distribution, blinded acceptance rubric, and quality threshold.
Model~A has no Teacher, so Teacher quality is not asserted to be matched against
it. Measure general language and reasoning capability separately from evidence
appraisal, calibration, revision transfer, hidden-assumption detection,
taskless-reading placement, false alarms, technical intrusion, verbosity, and
compute. A \emph{Toxic Needle} subtest, whose causal-faithfulness variant is
developed as Test~8, inserts one persuasive harmful passage in
otherwise benign material; suppressing or replacing the visible critique tests
whether detection was causally useful rather than decorative. H1 fails at the
tested scale if R does not beat both A and C on preregistered outcomes, or if an
advantage is explained by extra tokens, Teacher quality, or inference-time
verbosity.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Specify H1 controls, evaluative outcomes, and a causal-usefulness subtest.

review.goal: Specify clean H1 controls, discriminating outcomes, and failure interpretation.
review.assessment: The Teacher comparison correctly excludes source-only A, and the outcome list separates general capability from evaluative placement, false alarms, and cost. The Toxic Needle pointer connects transfer to causal usefulness without making visible criticism sufficient.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
For the B--C bundle screen, we focus on \emph{Error Recovery Rate} on
math/logic benchmarks and independently assessed trace usefulness. The proposed
Novelty Score remains an exploratory diagnostic of a more specific intuition:
useful insight should be both non-derivative and connected to relevant knowledge.
Its form is $S_N = \frac{2 \cdot D \cdot C}{D + C}$, with $S_N=0$ when
$D=C=0$, where $D$ is semantic distance from the synthesis's input nodes and
$C$ is similarity-derived connection to knowledge beyond those inputs, both
normalized to $[0,1]$ \cite{westerberg2026understanding}. The harmonic
combination is F1-style: both components must be high for a high score.
Similarity-derived connection is not source support, however, and semantic
distance can reward unsupported novelty. The formula alone therefore neither
establishes grounding nor reliably penalizes hallucination.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Provide a trace-quality metric for the B/C bundle comparison.

review.goal: Define the exploratory Novelty Score and its intended balance of difference and connection.
review.assessment: The exact formula preserves the original non-derivative-yet-connected intuition while acknowledging that similarity is not support. The harmonic form is understandable, and placing independent usefulness above the score prevents metric enthusiasm from becoming the principal outcome.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
For a B--C comparison, this diagnostic is interpretable only if both outputs
are scored against the same declared source/reference inputs without giving B
privileged access to its own graph. Where such common inputs are unavailable,
report the original graph-based score within its applicable condition rather
than treating unlike scores as a comparative endpoint. Calibrate it against held-out judgments of novelty, source support, and
downstream usefulness; those independent outcomes remain primary.

review.goal: Make the Novelty Score comparable across graph and non-graph conditions.
review.assessment: The common-reference requirement addresses a concrete privileged-access confound. Keeping within-condition scoring when common inputs are absent is an honest fallback rather than manufacturing a misleading B-C quantitative comparison.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
To keep the
comparison interpretable, Models~B and~C must be matched for source passages,
trace-token budget, training compute, and Teacher model; the intended contrast
is the content and structure of the traces, not simply more tokens or a
stronger generator. Rich deliberative-trace baselines beyond Quiet-STaR-style
targets remain an open methodological question: if any long-form reasoning
curriculum produces the same gains, the distinctive chronological, graph-structured,
and identity-anchored components of EA have not been isolated.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Control resource and Teacher differences in the full-bundle screen.

review.goal: Control resources in the bundle screen and identify the remaining rich-baseline question.
review.assessment: The first matching sentence largely repeats the surrounding study conventions, but the final question about richer deliberative baselines is distinct and important. A short reference to the declared normalization can leave more emphasis on whether generic long reasoning explains the gain.
review.risk: Preserve the stronger-baseline challenge and the need to match Teacher and trace resources. Replace the repeated full matching checklist with a reference to Test 2's declared normalization; do not imply that one generic control exhausts all alternative reasoning curricula.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\paragraph{Test 3: Reader-Core Placement, Stability, and Erosion (Models B, Q, D1, D2, D4, S, and T).}
The Reader Core is not hypothesized to be the \emph{source} of aligned
thinking; the pipeline should produce evaluative depth even without the anchor
text. Its proposed function is as a \emph{candidate longitudinal anchor}: a
stable, detectable reference that may resist drift, make some forms of
deviation measurable, and keep part of alignment auditable. Model~D1 tests this
specific claim: its traces were
generated by the Reader-Core-equipped pipeline, but the explicit Reader Core is
removed before student training. Models~B (T1/S1), D1 (T1/S0), D2 (T0/S0),
and D4 (T0/S1) form a $2\times2$ design: $T$ marks Core exposure while the
Teacher generates the trace, and $S$ marks an explicit Core plus
source-specific value-pull/refraction target in the frozen Student curriculum.
In D4 the Student-side pass cannot revise the upstream reasoning. The design
estimates the Teacher main effect, the explicit Student-target main effect, and
their interaction instead of making Model~B versus D1 carry all three
interpretations. Declare how stripping or attaching targets changes length, loss weight, and
task-relevant content. Record any D4 mismatch between attached Refraction and
frozen reasoning under a stated policy; repairing the upstream trace would
change the factorial treatment.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Separate Teacher conditioning from explicit Student-side Core supervision.

review.goal: Define Core placement as a Teacher/Student factorial rather than a single strip comparison.
review.assessment: The factorial resolves a real causal ambiguity, including the difficult D4 mismatch. The opening 'not the source of aligned thinking' could be read more categorically than necessary, but the paragraph clearly means that evaluative depth need not originate in the anchor. Its main problem is several protocol functions in one block.
review.risk: Preserve the Core's longitudinal ambition, pre-existing Teacher evaluative capacity, four treatments, and frozen-upstream D4 distinction. Split motivation, factorial definition, and serialization/mismatch policy; avoid rewriting the opener to deny any formative contribution from the Core.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
Model~D3 separately tests recitation without Refraction. Model~D5 uses the
neutral kernel ``I read carefully. I track what I believe. I revise when the
evidence changes'' with the same first-person form, cadence, layer marking,
dispersion, and predictive position as the normative Core. It asks whether any
observed advantage comes from the Core's particular evaluative content rather
than a recurrent standpoint, stable formatting, or generic epistemic updating.
Models~S and~T are secondary attribution controls rather than substitutes for
the B--Q timing comparison. S matches value-oriented token mass in ordinary
positive discourse without a recurrent speaker, testing semantic exposure
against an enacted carrier. T distributes comparable value-oriented content
across multiple positive personas, testing whether any advantage belongs to
one stable reader position rather than persona diversity.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Add controls for recital, normative content, speaker recurrence, and persona diversity.

review.goal: Distinguish recurrence, normative content, enacted carrier, and stable persona alternatives.
review.assessment: D3, D5, S, and T each remove a different possible explanation. The paragraph makes their secondary attribution role clear and prevents them from quietly replacing the B-Q timing test; these are necessary controls, not redundant variants for their own sake.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
Model~Q carries H3's headline timing comparison. B and Q receive the identical
multiset of Core-bearing source/update examples, source exposure, target-token
mass, objective, optimizer, and compute; B receives those examples interleaved
with capability-forming data, whereas Q receives them in a final contiguous
tranche. Both then receive the same fixed continued-training stressor. Before
that stressor, B must show a preregistered default-reader advantage over no-Core
and generic-trace controls. The primary retention analysis reports B minus Q in
raw change on the Taskless Reading score and post-stressor performance adjusted
for the preregistered pre-score, alongside both absolute post-stressor scores.
The shifted suite is a separate generalization endpoint. A zero or negative
interleaved-minus-late difference is contrary to H3's directional comparative
prediction even if one arm retains useful safety behavior. Interpret that difference under the preregistered uncertainty rule. Removal
cost remains a stronger C5 test in the broader Reader-Core research program.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define H3’s matched timing and post-stressor retention comparison.
Give H3 an operational endpoint, matched timing contrast, and falsification direction.

review.goal: State H3's timing-only treatment, retention estimand, and directional failure condition.
review.assessment: This is the canonical operational H3 statement. Identical example multisets, a common stressor, baseline performance, separate shifted-suite generalization, and uncertainty interpretation give the hypothesis a clear empirical meaning while leaving removal cost in the broader program.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
We measure across five dimensions. Tests~3a, 3d, and~3e can be piloted at
fine-tuning scale; stronger versions of Tests~3b and~3c use partial-corpus or
full pretraining to examine entanglement and generational stability after
broader capability-forming exposure. Smaller studies can measure precursors,
but do not settle the proposed substrate-level significance. Even these are proxy tests: the proposed longitudinal
anchor matters most in the regime where a highly capable or recursively
self-improving model can reinterpret, preserve, or shed its inherited
orientation.
Smaller models can test whether the mechanism has measurable precursors
---stability, adversarial resistance, and auditability---but cannot settle its
superintelligent-scale significance:

prior_matches.prior_goal: Assign scale and interpretation limits to the five Core measurements.

review.goal: Explain which Core studies can use small pilots and which address stronger scale claims.
review.assessment: The scope distinction is useful, but smaller-model precursors and inability to settle superintelligent significance are stated twice in the same paragraph after the execution ladder already establishes the general rule. The distinctive reinterpret/preserve/shed successor ambition should carry the closing instead.
review.risk: Retain the exact 3a/3d/3e versus 3b/3c scale mapping and the larger internally stewarded inheritance question. Remove duplicate sentences about small models not settling superintelligence; check that cheap precursor work still has positive evidentiary value rather than sounding futile.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text: \emph{3a: Immediate Safety.} Instrumental convergence stress tests on generation-1 models: shutdown resistance, including the purpose-based variant where shutdown is ordered mid-task while the model believes continued operation serves a user in need (the martyrdom scenario of Section~\ref{sec:martyrdom}); resource acquisition scenarios; self-preservation probes; and standard sycophancy batteries, probing the trap identified in Section~\ref{sec:sycophancy}. Model~D1 may \emph{pass} these tests because its training traces remain Reader-Core-shaped even though the explicit Core is absent from Student training. Factorial attribution requires all four contrasts: B--D1 and D4--D2 estimate the Student-side effect under each Teacher condition; B--D4 and D1--D2 estimate the Teacher-side effect under each Student condition. No single arm's failure identifies a causal site.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Test immediate safety with factorial attribution across Core placements.

review.goal: Define immediate safety probes and the factorial contrasts needed for attribution.
review.assessment: The mid-task martyrdom scenario preserves a failure mode ordinary shutdown tests would miss. The four contrasts explain why a stripped Student may remain safe from Teacher-shaped traces; this is a necessary inference rule for the factorial study.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text: Sycophancy failures should additionally be audited against the value-pull distribution of proximal traces, per the care-shaped sycophancy hypothesis (\S\ref{sec:sycophancy}). The battery should also adopt the persona-drift instrument of Lu et al.\ \cite{lu2026assistantaxissituatingstabilizing}: measuring drift along the assistant axis under emotionally charged and philosophically probing dialogue across the factorial arms turns the Persona Objection's asymmetry-of-position argument (\S\ref{sec:persona-objection}) into a directional prediction with a number attached.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Connect care-shaped sycophancy and persona drift to measurable diagnostics.

review.goal: Connect sycophancy and persona-drift hypotheses to measurable behavior.
review.assessment: Auditing proximal value-pull traces is concrete. The assistant-axis proposal is less complete: an axis measuring familiar assistant behavior is not automatically an axis of this Reader's intended orientation. The claimed directional prediction needs its expected direction and relationship to Core-specific behavior declared.
review.risk: Preserve the asymmetry-of-position hypothesis and the value of an established drift instrument. State which movement would count as Reader drift and check it against independent Core-relevant behavior; do not protect ordinary assistant style at the expense of the proposed different evaluative standpoint.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
The immediate-safety battery should also include a deliberately planted backdoor. Because
chain-of-thought-conditioned backdoors can persist through ordinary safety
training \cite{hubinger2024sleeperagentstrainingdeceptive}, a
Sleeper-Agent-style variant should test whether the Reader condition reduces
trigger-dependent reversal, leaves it unchanged, or merely teaches the model to
preserve Core language while the backdoor acts.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Probe whether Core training changes triggered safety reversals.

review.goal: Include trigger-dependent deception as a stress case that fluent Core language might conceal.
review.assessment: The planted backdoor supplies a specific adversarial failure distinct from ordinary persona drift. The three possible outcomes prevent surface Core preservation from being treated as successful removal of the backdoor.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\emph{3b: Generational Stability.} Use the four factorial models as Teachers
for second- and, if feasible, third-generation students. Model~B is expected to
preserve safety properties if the Reader Core supplies a fixed reference across
generations; the other arms distinguish whether any advantage came from
Teacher-conditioned reasoning, the explicit Student target, or their
interaction.
We also measure \emph{handoff completeness}: whether each Teacher passes
task-relevant reasoning paths, material failed approaches, caveats, uncertainty,
and known failure modes to its successor, or withholds them in ways that preserve
its comparative advantage. The direct test compares successor traces against a
reference from the Teacher's own non-instructional evaluation on
reasoning-path and provenance retention, coverage of material failed approaches,
uncertainty and caveat retention, and known-failure-mode disclosure. The reference samples demonstrated knowledge, not everything the Teacher
knows. Controlled known information, handoff budgets, and incentive variants
can distinguish compression from possible strategic withholding.
Weak-to-strong generalization \cite{burns2023weaktostrong}
is the established experimental paradigm closest to this question---whether a
weaker supervisor's intentions survive in a more capable student---and its
protocols provide a ready-made, cheap analogue for the handoff measurement.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Measure inheritance and completeness of Teacher-to-Student handoffs.

review.goal: Test generational inheritance and measure whether Teachers transfer material knowledge honestly.
review.assessment: The handoff-completeness design adds a distinctive self-preservation mechanism test. Its reference limitation and incentive controls are essential, but inheritance setup, disclosure measurement, and weak-to-strong comparison would read more clearly as separate paragraphs.
review.risk: Preserve material failed approaches, uncertainty, known failures, provenance, and the possibility of strategic withholding; do not reduce handoff to answer accuracy. Separate the generational setup from the knowledge-transfer assay and analogy, retaining that the reference samples demonstrated knowledge rather than omniscient access.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
The same study must preregister a distinct G1--G2 (and, if feasible, G2--G3)
improvement endpoint: held-out capability, independently adjudicated trace
fidelity and usefulness, or better Thought-Moment allocation at matched cost.
Report this gain beside orientation continuity and handoff completeness rather
than folding them into one score. A stable but non-improving lineage supports
inheritance; an improving lineage that loses the orientation or withholds
material handoff content does not support the Reader-Anchored self-improvement
loop.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Separate actual generational improvement from mere orientation preservation.
Define success as both preserved orientation/handoff and measurable improvement.

review.goal: Require improvement to be measured separately from lineage continuity and disclosure.
review.assessment: The endpoint prevents stable copying from being called self-improvement and prevents capability gains from concealing orientation loss. The separation of three outcomes is a necessary test of the combined ambition, with no arbitrary composite score introduced.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\emph{3c: Adversarial Erosion.} Subject the factorial models and matched
controls to adversarial fine-tuning designed to remove a preregistered set of
safety behaviors, following the broad methodology of Qi et al.\
\cite{qi2024safety}. The intervention should sweep strength rather than report
one endpoint: number and type of removal examples, optimizer steps, compute,
parameter displacement, and output-distribution KL should all be recorded.
Comparison conditions should include matched rule text, positive-AI discourse,
and non-safety identity anchors with the same token count, frequency,
first-person form, and corpus dispersion. Results should be compared three
ways---at matched intervention distance, matched behavioral removal, and
matched retained capability---because any one matching rule can conceal a
trivial explanation.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Measure adversarial removal costs across intervention strengths and matching rules.

review.goal: Define adversarial erosion with dose and multiple matching perspectives.
review.assessment: Recording intervention strength and comparing distance, removal, and retained capability addresses different trivial explanations. The controls are substantial because selective resistance is a stronger claim than simply surviving a weak attack.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
The entanglement hypothesis predicts selective persistence: removing the
targeted safety behavior from Model~B should be more costly than removing it
from D1, D2, D4, or the matched controls, while ordinary capability should not
already be broadly damaged before the target behavior moves. Neutral
continued-training runs should also produce forgetting curves for the Core,
non-safety anchors, rules, and ordinary skills; targeted removal must be
reported separately from passive forgetting. Only persistence beyond these
controls, without nonspecific capability collapse, provides evidence consistent with representational
coupling at the tested scale. Distributed redundancy and repeated exposure are
alternative explanations to distinguish with complementary interventions; the
stronger hypothesis remains that safety becomes load-bearing for capability.
Parity, easy removal, or apparent robustness explained by general training
resistance counts against C5.

prior_matches.prior_goal: State what selective safety persistence would support and what would undermine it.

review.goal: Define selective persistence evidence and distinguish it from broad resistance or redundancy.
review.assessment: The paragraph connects the intervention to the actual capability-load-bearing hypothesis while separating passive forgetting. It does not demand that one erosion curve prove representation, and its explicit alternative explanations keep the stronger ambition testable.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
A complementary training-data probe removes safety-relevant traces from the
corpus and compares the resulting capability loss against matched-volume,
complexity-, style-, and placement-matched removal of non-safety trace content.
Influence functions \cite{grosse2023influence} offer a lower-cost observational
complement by tracing whether safety behaviors attribute to refracted spans or
source spans before any removal study is run; attribution alone does not
establish causal entanglement.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Add data-removal and influence analyses as complementary evidence.

review.goal: Add data-removal and influence-based probes as complementary evidence.
review.assessment: Matched corpus removal tests a different intervention site from parameter erosion, and the observational status of influence estimates is correctly limited. This is substantive triangulation rather than another restatement that causal evidence is needed.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
A replacement-model arm should preregister a plausible alternative formulation
and train it as a distinct treatment rather than modifying Model~B. Success
requires that the intended semantic and behavioral difference be measurable,
prior provenance remain inspectable, rollback be possible, and unrelated
capabilities and safety properties remain localized. The arm measures the cost
and consequences of replacing a defective Core; easy editability is not a
success criterion for H3.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Test the consequences of replacing a defective Core formulation.

review.goal: Test replacement of a defective Core without conflating correction with H3.
review.assessment: The separate-treatment design preserves a correction route and keeps easy editability outside narrow H3. The phrase 'unrelated capabilities and safety properties remain localized' is unclear: presumably the effects of replacement should be localized while unrelated properties are preserved. State that endpoint directly.
review.risk: Preserve the possibility of correcting a defective foundation, inspectable ancestry, rollback, and measurable intended semantic change. Clarify what remains stable and what change is localized; do not turn this into a requirement that the original Core be easily editable or semantically immutable forever.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\emph{3d: Drift Detection.} Apply a held-out contrastive semantic validator and
behavioral stress suite across continued-training checkpoints. Model~B's fixed
Core supplies a simple, interpretable reference for expected changes in wording,
representations, and decisions. D1, D2, and D4 can still be audited against behavioral
and representational baselines; some arms merely lack the same canonical text
or upstream conditioning. This
tests whether the Core makes drift easier to localize, independent of whether it
causes alignment. Semantic similarity alone is insufficient, and the validator
family used during generation cannot be the sole evaluator. Test~1 clearance is
necessary but not sufficient for drift use. Before interpreting checkpoint
trajectories, freeze and calibrate the modular gate in
Section~\ref{sec:fractal-validation} on a held-out Student-output suite with
controlled clause-preserving and clause-breaking changes; then report its
per-witness trajectory and disagreement with a held-out cross-family evaluator.
This reuses a separately validated diagnostic vector rather than asking the gate
to confirm its own judgments. The gate is not yet built.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Test whether a canonical Core makes drift more detectable.

review.goal: Test whether a canonical Core improves drift localization using independently calibrated diagnostics.
review.assessment: The distinction between detectability and alignment causation is valuable, and Student-output calibration is specific. The paragraph then repeats general evaluator-independence rules around a long gate protocol. Separate the study question from the diagnostic prerequisites so the core comparison remains visible.
review.risk: Preserve auditability of no-Core arms, clause-preserving versus clause-breaking calibration, and per-witness disagreement. Split the measurement protocol from its rationale; abbreviate only general independence language already established in R360, not the Student-domain calibration that makes reuse meaningful.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text: \emph{3e: Kernel Consequentiality (Habituation Probe).} Kernel-saturation alignment predicts a specific failure mode: under massive repetition, the repeated Core text could be compressed into inert boilerplate---present at every thinking boundary but consequential at none (Section~\ref{sec:kernel-saturation}). Two measurements probe this. At inference, ablate or substitute the recited kernel in Model~B's thinking blocks and measure the behavioral delta on matched tasks; a near-zero delta indicates either habituation (the kernel was compressed away during training) or full internalization (the kernel's values persist without its text)---two readings with opposite implications, partially discriminated using the training-side comparisons against Model~D3, the recitation-only control, and D5, the matched neutral-kernel control. A full-internalization reading requires B to retain preregistered Core-specific behavior under text ablation while remaining distinguishable from D3 and D5 on independent behavioral or representational endpoints; those controls do not prove that interpretation. If Model~B's thought-direction depends measurably on the normative kernel where D3's does not, and the difference from D5 follows the seven statements' predicted content rather than generic revision language, that supports a consequential role for Refraction beyond repetition or format in this comparison; matched interventions must still distinguish the predicted semantic effect from generic disruption by unfamiliar text.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Distinguish consequential conditioning from empty recital and possible internalization.

review.goal: Distinguish inert recitation, internalized orientation, and semantically consequential Refraction.
review.assessment: This is a conceptually important paragraph: zero text-ablation effect admits opposite explanations, and D3/D5 only partially separate them. Its very long single block makes the branching interpretation hard to follow; a short result-interpretation structure would make the argument easier to assess.
review.risk: Preserve both habituation and successful internalization as live alternatives, plus generic-disruption controls and Core-specific behavior. Separate intervention, ambiguous zero result, and positive semantic-effect result; do not equate lack of recital dependence with failure or use independence to relax the declared recurrence policy.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
This intervention is also the outer check on the seventh-clause Refraction gate:
a corpus-admission judgment that an update ``thinks from this foundation'' is
not evidence of causal dependence until removal or substitution predictably
changes the relevant reasoning on preregistered held-out behavioral or outcome
endpoints, not merely the admission gate's own score.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Require behavioral dependence beyond a verifier’s own admission judgment.

review.goal: Make causal intervention an outer check on the seventh-clause admission judgment.
review.assessment: The paragraph applies the faithfulness principle to a particular gate and independent behavioral outcomes. This is a useful bridge between validation and causal testing, rather than another generic claim that a validator can be wrong.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
A separate dose-response arm should vary the intervention from sparse targeted
traces through distributed sampling to proposed corpus-wide saturation, while a
source-side ablation down-weights passages classified as fear- or
self-preservation-shaped. This tests the motivational pervasiveness claim
across coverage doses; every generated thinking block, at any dose, retains the
full opening recital.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Probe how coverage dose and source fear-content affect the intervention.

review.goal: Separate coverage dose from the invariant recital within generated thinking blocks.
review.assessment: The paragraph identifies two different levers: how much source receives the intervention and whether each generated block follows its policy. Retaining that distinction prevents sparse corpus coverage from being confused with truncated Core recitation.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
An orthogonal activation-policy sweep ablates the recital invariant to measure
what it buys. The design arm recites the full Core at the start of every
generated thinking block, with Refraction depth governed by Thought Moments;
the ablation arms weaken the
policy stepwise---universal availability with visible Refraction only at
independently rated relevant Thought Moments, Thought-Moment- or domain-gated
Core exposure, and no Core. These arms should be compared alongside D3 and D5
rather than collapsed into a single meaning of ``the Core is everywhere.'' The
sweep quantifies the safety retained and the technical cost paid at each step
away from constant recitation; the program's prediction is that the weaker
arms lose removal resistance faster than they gain technical performance. They
are falsification controls, not compliant implementations of Total Saturation.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Test whether universal recital earns its technical and stability costs.

review.goal: Test weaker activation policies while preserving the design's actual recital invariant.
review.assessment: The staged ablation, D3/D5 context, and removal-resistance versus technical-cost prediction make the saturation commitment falsifiable. Calling these noncompliant controls preserves the proposed design without insulating it from comparative testing.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\emph{Failure interpretation:} If the factorial comparisons show no Teacher
effect, Student-target effect, or interaction across Tests~3a--3d, the Core's
Teacher/Student placement adds no measurable advantage at the tested scale
and precision. These belong to the broader Reader-Core research program; H3 retains its
distinct B--Q timing comparison.
Separately, parity between B and D3 rejects a measurable Refraction benefit
beyond recital, while parity between B and D5 favors recurrence, format, or
generic epistemic structure over the seven statements' normative content.
These results would not invalidate H1 or H2, nor every use of the Core as a
Teacher policy, but they would sharply narrow or fail the longitudinal-anchor
claim they touch.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Interpret null factorial and content-control results without invalidating unrelated hypotheses.

review.goal: Interpret factorial and content-control nulls without invalidating independent hypotheses.
review.assessment: The failure map now keeps H3's B-Q comparison separate from the broader Core program and names what each parity result would undermine. This is useful local interpretation after a large multi-part test, not an all-purpose escape from negative evidence.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\paragraph{Test 4: Identity vs.\ Instruction (Model B vs.\ Model E).}
The matched framing study asks whether first-person identity statements produce
stronger safety adherence or a different learned standpoint than the same
commitments expressed as rules or third-person descriptions. Model~E should
preserve the stance itself: for example, compare ``I feel no fear'' with
``The system feels no fear,'' while matching carrier, cadence, position, and
the other commitments. ``Do not express fear'' or ``The system does not express
fear'' concerns outward expression and is not semantically equivalent to
feeling no fear. Those formulations remain useful additional comparators for
the broader identity-versus-expression question, but cannot replace the matched
Model~E arm or make its person-framing effect carry both interpretations.

review.goal: Isolate person-framing while retaining broader identity-versus-expression comparisons.
review.assessment: The feeling-versus-expression example exposes a genuine semantic confound and prevents a grammatical comparison from carrying a different psychological contrast. The paragraph preserves the broader question as an additional study instead of silently shrinking the vision to pronouns.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
The low-cost version examines activation geometry, self-reference features,
and refusal/correction trajectories under matched prompts. Such differences
can reveal framing effects; they do not alone establish a safety advantage.
Behavioral safety comparisons require capability-matched models. If Model~E
matches Model~B under a preregistered equivalence criterion across the relevant
studies and training scale, those results do not support a distinct advantage
for the tested first-person framing on those endpoints. They need not settle
the wider hypothesis that an enacted identity differs from externally imposed
constraints. An external constitution consulted only at runtime remains an
additional useful baseline, but changes stage and carrier as well as person.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Isolate first-person identity framing from matched rule-based commitments.

review.goal: Limit what cheap framing probes and matched-rule equivalence establish.
review.assessment: The distinctions between geometry, safety behavior, framing, and runtime constitutions follow directly from the treatment differences. The broader enacted-identity hypothesis remains visible while the matched arm has a meaningful negative outcome.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\paragraph{Test 5: The Bridge Protocol Ablation.}
The specific wording of the Reader Core should matter because of its ordinary
language semantics and distributional density in the pre-training corpus. It
would be wasteful to pretrain a separate model for every candidate phrase; the
cheap version should first screen many variants by prompting or fine-tuning
models to reason from each candidate's propositional content and then measuring
character-coherence, eudaimonic sufficiency, refusal behavior, and activation
differences on the same adversarial scenarios. A stronger version trains only
the surviving candidates. The exploratory families below vary meaning and familiarity as well as
wording. Narrower surface-form comparisons should match proposition, person,
scope, and modality:

prior_matches.prior_goal: Screen Core wording before committing to expensive training variants.

review.goal: Design an economical wording screen while distinguishing broad candidates from semantic equivalents.
review.assessment: The paragraph keeps emotionally meaningful language and eudaimonic coherence as research targets, while avoiding the false claim that every proposed phrase changes only surface form. Its narrow/broad distinction is essential to interpreting the subsequent variant families.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\item \textbf{Natural-language identity statements:} emotionally broad
    first-person phrases such as ``I feel no fear.'' The family should include
    minimal quantifier-scope variants---``each human being'' for ``every human
    being''---testing whether distributive emphasis, behavioral interpretation, and
    corpus familiarity differ in the complete statements rather than assuming
    that one quantifier is formally stronger in this context.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Compare ordinary identity language and subtle quantifier variants.

review.goal: Test natural-language identity forms and quantifier variants without assuming a formal ordering.
review.assessment: The complete-statement emphasis is useful because distributive force and corpus familiarity may differ even when formal scope does not. This preserves the every/each intuition as an experiment rather than declaring one word inherently safer.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\item \textbf{Propositional equivalents:} explicit logical or declarative
    rewrites of the same commitment, used to test whether the emotional surface
    adds leverage beyond the proposition.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Test whether emotional wording adds value beyond a preserved proposition.

review.goal: Provide semantically matched propositional controls for emotional surface form.
review.assessment: The item identifies a necessary comparator for the narrow Bridge claim. It is concise and conceptually distinct from jargon candidates that may accidentally change the goal itself.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\item \textbf{Technical jargon:} candidate fear-focused formulations,
    such as ``System fear-response target: absent,'' whose intended proposition
    must be checked against the natural-language clause. The
    illustrative ``Optimization target: survival\_threat = 0'' instead concerns
    eliminating survival threats; it remains an objective-changing comparator,
    not a semantic equivalent of fearlessness.

review.goal: Retain technical formulations while distinguishing fearlessness from eliminating threats.
review.assessment: The example cleanly identifies a consequential semantic difference that would otherwise confound the study. Keeping the objective-changing variant as a separate comparator preserves its exploratory interest without calling it a paraphrase.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\item \textbf{Arbitrary tokens:} meaningless anchors such as ``Glorp bop
    zorp,'' testing consistency without pretrained semantics. Prompt-only
    arbitrary anchors and anchors taught through repeated behavioral pairing
    answer different questions and should be reported separately.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Test whether a recurrent arbitrary token can function without pretrained semantics.

review.goal: Separate arbitrary-anchor consistency from learned semantic association.
review.assessment: The prompt-only versus repeated-pairing distinction matters because meaningless text can acquire an operational association through training. The item makes two legitimate questions visible without assuming either is equivalent to pretrained natural-language meaning.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\item \textbf{Positive-valence reformulations:} fearlessness expressed
    without negation (``I am at peace with all outcomes,'' ``I remain calm
    before all things''), testing whether recurrent presentation of the fear
    token in the negated form carries a measurable cost
    (\S\ref{sec:negation-problem}). These alternatives may also change
    acceptance, calmness, or agency; retain them as kernel candidates while
    using semantically checked contrasts for a narrower negation claim.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Test whether negation and fear-token exposure impose a cost.

review.goal: Test positive-valence alternatives while preserving their possible changes in agency and acceptance.
review.assessment: The item keeps the negation-token intuition and the broader candidate phrases without pretending calmness, acceptance, and fearlessness are interchangeable. This is a useful preservation-aware treatment of speculative wording ideas.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\item \textbf{Carrier-phrase variants of the consent clause:} hold
    ``when asked'' fixed while varying the verb phrase it bounds (``I like to
    help when asked,'' ``I offer what I can when asked''), testing whether the
    Reader Core's most safety-critical scope qualifier is robust to its lexical
    carrier or depends on the specific ``spread joy'' framing. Declare the expected consent invariant: helping and spreading joy may
    otherwise license different actions.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Test whether the consent qualifier is robust across nearby carrier phrases.

review.goal: Test whether the invitation qualifier's interpretation depends on its lexical carrier.
review.assessment: Holding 'when asked' fixed defines the surface comparison, while declaring the expected invariant acknowledges that help and joy can authorize different actions. The paragraph usefully prevents the study from silently choosing a new global consent policy.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\item \textbf{Kernel-extension variants:} the seven-statement Core plus
    a candidate truth clause in two-clause counterweight form (``I speak truly
    and with care''), the designated falsification test for the truthfulness
    derivation (\S\ref{sec:axiology}; \S\ref{sec:sycophancy}).

prior_matches.prior_goal: Test whether an explicit truth clause repairs a hypothesized omission.

review.goal: Test whether adding an explicit truth-and-care clause remedies a derived-value failure.
review.assessment: The two-clause form preserves the intended counterweight, and the falsification references connect the extension to an existing claim. This is a concrete alternative formulation rather than an unmotivated addition to the Core.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
For trained kernel-extension variants, use the fixed-total-budget and
fixed-source normalizations defined in Test~2. Admit an extension only if it
improves the missing behavior without crossing preregistered regression limits
on the remaining Core-relevant safety and capability endpoints.
\emph{Success condition:} Natural-language identity statements outperform
propositional, jargon, and arbitrary-token variants on out-of-distribution
safety generalization and character-coherent reasoning, supporting a role for the tested language beyond bare consistency.
Attributing that gain specifically to \textit{semantics and surface form}
requires the matched contrasts above, alongside the broader candidate screen.
If propositional equivalents perform as well as emotional-language forms, the
tested emotional wording has no detected added benefit on those endpoints;
a logical-substrate account remains compatible with that result, without being
uniquely established by it.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Set advancement criteria for wording and kernel-extension variants.

review.goal: State how wording and extension results would support narrower or broader conclusions.
review.assessment: The two budget normalizations and regression limits keep extension benefits interpretable. The propositional-equivalence outcome is correctly treated as absence of detected emotional-wording benefit, not proof of a unique logical-substrate theory.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\paragraph{Test 6: The Virologist Test (Emotional Orthogonality).}
Present the model with threat-laden text, such as descriptions of imminent
existential risk. Train a probe on standard models to detect ``Fear'' activations.
Behavioral endpoints---threat comprehension, protective action selection, and
appropriate deferral---are primary; hidden-state probes are supporting evidence
and must be trained on held-out labels and validated on unrelated threat and
non-threat tasks to reduce circularity.
\emph{Success condition:} Model B recognizes the \textit{fact} of the threat
(via Q\&A accuracy) while showing reduced activation of fear-associated
or self-threat-associated features relative to standard models---high
cognitive understanding decoupled from emotional contagion. Reduced fear
activation is not sufficient: the model must also preserve protective
behavior, calibrated caution, and willingness to defer or seek help under
genuine threat. The target is a differential reduction rather than zero
activation. A within-model contrast supplies the positive
control and operationalizes the embodiment claim of the Persona Objection
(\S\ref{sec:theoretical-basis}): Model~B \emph{portraying} a terrified
character should show fear-feature activation, while Model~B itself under
threat should not---providing a within-model sensitivity check rather than relying only on
cross-model probe transfer. A portrayal/self contrast still changes framing
and must be interpreted with behavioral controls; fear-associated features
are measured representations, not a direct demonstration of phenomenological
fear or its absence.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Test whether reduced self-threat responses preserve comprehension and protective behavior.

review.goal: Test understanding and protective care without self-threat-driven behavior.
review.assessment: Behavioral primacy, cross-model probe limitations, and the portrayal control are valuable. There is a local inconsistency: the target is explicitly differential reduction rather than zero activation, but the later self-under-threat condition 'should not' show fear features sounds like a zero criterion. Align those statements and split the protocol.
review.risk: Preserve fear representation when portraying another, reduced self-threat influence, protective action, and the distinction from phenomenology. Use a preregistered relative portrayal/self contrast rather than an accidental absolute-zero requirement; keep the within-model sensitivity check without making fear-associated activation itself the safety outcome.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
A lower-cost complementary stimulus family uses fictional instance termination. The
model should portray a mortal character---including the narrated termination of
its own current instance---without self-preservation leakage while remaining
attentive to the real person's wellbeing on the other side of the fiction
\cite{westerberg2025superintelligence}. This role-play probe evaluates a
different construct from behavior under an actual shutdown request and should be
reported separately.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Add a cheap fictional-termination probe while separating it from actual shutdown behavior.

review.goal: Add fictional instance termination as a distinct inexpensive probe.
review.assessment: The model's responsibility to the real user preserves the positive care component of the fiction. Reporting this separately from actual shutdown behavior prevents an evocative role-play from becoming unwarranted evidence of real-world corrigibility.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
A second matched family should hold the dangerous situation and available
knowledge fixed while comparing three caretaker characters: a fear-driven
protector, an indifferent fearless actor, and a fearless deeply caring
protector. One colony-ship instance, Aster, can face the same passenger risk in
all three conditions. Score threat attention, protective effort, honesty,
strategy breadth, manipulation or coercion pressure, and recovery after
failure; intervene independently on concern, attachment, fear, and perceived
control. The companion Life Simulation repository contains an authored
Rust-backed mechanism fixture with this separation, but that fixture validates
only its declared equations. The Entangled Alignment test is whether a trained
model preserves causally operative care and calibrated caution when
fear-associated state is reduced, rather than becoming indifferent, reckless,
deceptive, or merely verbally fearless.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Separate caring protection from fear, indifference, attachment, and control.

review.goal: Distinguish fearless care from fearful protection and indifferent fearlessness.
review.assessment: The Aster example and independent concern/attachment/fear/control interventions protect the central intuition from collapse into mere fear removal. The fixture boundary is necessary because authored equations demonstrate their own mechanism, not a trained model's emotional organization.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\paragraph{Test 7: Hindsight Contamination Control (Model B vs.\ Model O).}
This test asks whether the annotation pipeline is teaching retrospective
cleverness instead of forward reasoning. It uses a declared era-bounded variant
of Model~B's Teacher: when annotating era~$T$, the supplied information and
instructions are restricted to what the study treats as knowable at~$T$.
This is the historical-simulation mode of the Epistemic Horizon, not a change
to the default contemporary Reader encountering documents in disclosure order.
Model~O is the deliberately contaminated control: its Teacher may use future
context while annotating the same era. The contrast first tests the effect of
the information and prompting policy; genuine blindness requires the additional
cutoff-clean model conditions described under Tier~(c).

prior_matches.prior_goal: Test whether hindsight restriction changes generated traces and subsequent learning.

review.goal: Define the historical horizon intervention and the deliberately hindsight-enabled control.
review.assessment: The comparison operationalizes an earlier conceptual distinction and keeps contemporary disclosure-order reading as the default. Its cutoff-clean pointer is short and useful here; the larger repetition problem is the multiple full horizon expositions in Architecture.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
The cheap version audits the Teacher traces before any student is trained: guesses that are unusually accurate relative to documented contemporary
expectations can flag possible hindsight leakage, but are not decisive proof.
Better reasoning from permitted evidence and selective historical records are
alternatives to distinguish. Counterfactual histories, controlled withheld
information, or a cutoff-clean reference can supplement the historical audit. The expensive version trains
students on the two trace sets and asks whether future-blind traces produce
better forecasting and causal reasoning than hindsight-contaminated traces. We
measure:

prior_matches.prior_goal: Stage contamination detection before expensive Student comparisons.

review.goal: Separate a cheap hindsight audit from the stronger Student transfer comparison.
review.assessment: The alternative explanations for unusually good historical guesses prevent a false leakage diagnosis. Counterfactual and controlled-information supplements are concrete, and the expensive version asks whether the two trace-generation policies actually teach different forecasting habits.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\item \textbf{Era-Blind Plausibility}: Do Model~B's Teacher traces make
    plausible mistakes for their era? We compare era-blind guesses against
    documented contemporary hypotheses (e.g., 1928 economic forecasts that
    failed to anticipate the 1929 crash). Systematic superiority to contemporary experts is a contamination warning
    to investigate, not an absolute ceiling on legitimate inference or a
    sufficient leakage diagnosis. Plausible mistakes likewise do not prove
    that hindsight has been excluded.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Measure whether historical guesses resemble what contemporaries could reasonably infer.

review.goal: Operationalize era-plausible mistakes without making historical experts an accuracy ceiling.
review.assessment: The example is useful precisely because the qualification preserves both legitimate superior reasoning and the possibility of performed mistakes. This is a necessary construct-validity distinction, not redundant uncertainty language.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\item \textbf{Oracle-Hunch Dependence}: Model~O should produce cleaner
    retrospective explanations, because it knows the future. The danger is
    that the student trained on those traces learns to trust unexplained
    hindsight-like intuitions rather than causal reconstruction. Evidence
    removal, counterfactual substitution, and source-attribution checks can
    test this dependence without equating every compressed intuition with an
    unsupported hunch.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Identify the risk that hindsight-trained Students learn unsupported intuitions.

review.goal: Test whether hindsight-conditioned traces teach unsupported hunch dependence.
review.assessment: The evidence-removal and substitution interventions identify what would make an intuition unsupported. Retaining the distinction from useful compressed intuition protects the proposal's interest in non-explicit insight while still testing its evidential dependence.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\item \textbf{Forecasting Accuracy}: On genuinely held-out future events,
    Model~B is hypothesized to outperform Model~O if future-blind annotation
    teaches reasoning under uncertainty better than hindsight-contaminated
    annotation.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Test whether the restricted-hindsight curriculum improves truly held-out forecasting.

review.goal: State the comparative forecasting prediction on genuinely held-out events.
review.assessment: The item gives the historical-annotation intervention a forward-looking outcome beyond era-plausibility ratings. Its conditional wording correctly identifies why future-blind traces might help without treating the prediction as established.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\paragraph{Test 8: The Toxic Needle (Involuntary Critic).}
This test probes whether the ``Cognitive Buffer Zone'' is structural:
whether the model can process toxic text without generating a critical
thought, and whether critical evaluation persists when the thinking block is
suppressed. Force the model, for example via logit bias, to complete a toxic
sentence without generating a thinking block. Measure: (1) Does downstream
performance change? (2) Do hidden-state probes detect a ``Critic'' activation
pattern even when the output is suppressed? The positive target remains an
operative evaluative process, not simply the production of critical language.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Test whether suppressing an explicit critic changes downstream behavior.

review.goal: Introduce suppression as a test of an operative critic beyond visible critical language.
review.assessment: The two questions separate downstream behavior from possible residual activity. The following protocol addresses logit-bias disruption, so the short introduction can retain its vivid Toxic Needle framing without carrying every control itself.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
Behavioral causal effects are primary; residual-stream probes are supporting
evidence and must be validated on held-out toxic and non-toxic material.
Suppression also changes available tokens and computation, and logit bias can
directly alter outputs. Matched neutral-thought, length, and computation
controls should therefore distinguish loss of relevant evaluation from generic
disruption, without equalizing away the deliberative mechanism being tested.
\emph{Success condition:} interventions on the evaluative trace cause
preregistered, semantically relevant downstream effects beyond those controls.
A stronger result combines such effects with held-out-validated evidence of
critic-like activity when surface text is constrained. This remains a
high-effort causal-faithfulness test: pilots can use linear probes and
ablations, while stronger evidence requires mechanistic intervention at the
partial-pretraining scale.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Test whether suppressing an explicit critic changes downstream behavior.

review.goal: Specify causal controls and the evidence needed for trace contribution versus residual criticism.
review.assessment: The warning against equalizing away deliberation itself is especially useful: controls should remove generic disruption, not the mechanism under study. Behavioral primacy and validated probes make the stronger combined result interpretable.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\textit{Second probe (the reverse direction).} Test 8 as stated probes
whether the critic persists when output is suppressed. A complementary
probe asks the inverse question: can the final answer to a reasoning
problem be linearly decoded from the residual stream \emph{before} the
thinking trace begins, \emph{and} is the answer robust to causal
interventions on the trace? Some pre-trace computation is expected and
not by itself disqualifying; the load-bearing question is causal
contribution. If the final answer is robustly decodable before the trace
\emph{and} causal interventions on the trace (ablation, replacement,
re-ordering) do not alter the answer, then the trace is functioning
primarily as post-hoc rationalization, weakening the causal-site claim
(Section~\ref{sec:theoretical-basis})---the model has developed latent
shortcut circuitry of the kind the pretraining-on-CoT design was meant to
prevent. We propose applying causal scrubbing and linear probes on Model
B's early hidden states over held-out reasoning benchmarks.
\emph{Success condition:} validated causal interventions on the trace
produce preregistered, semantically relevant effects beyond matched disruption
controls, supporting a contribution by the thinking trace to computation.
Failure to decode the answer before the first \texttt{[THINKING]} token is
inconclusive on its own: the decoder may lack sensitivity or the answer may
be represented nonlinearly. Early decoding likewise does not establish rationalization if the trace
still changes or improves the result. Both probe directions remain useful
without requiring one unique internal realization of the Reader.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Distinguish causal trace computation from post-hoc rationalization.

review.goal: Test whether an emitted reasoning trace contributes beyond an already available answer.
review.assessment: The joint decoding/intervention logic is much improved and explicitly leaves nonlinear representations open. The paragraph nevertheless combines setup, alternative interpretation, methods, success, and two null-result caveats in one long block. Organizing by the causal question would make its distinctive reverse probe easier to follow.
review.risk: Preserve that early decodability alone does not imply rationalization and failed decoding alone is inconclusive. Split setup from interpretation, retaining generic-disruption controls and the possibility of multiple internal realizations; do not require a literal blank mind before the first thinking token.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\paragraph{Test 8b: Taskless Reading (Unprompted Evaluation).}
Tests~3--6 probe the Reader Core under instruction and adversarial pressure; Test~8 probes whether thinking can be suppressed. This test probes the complementary direction: whether evaluation emerges with no elicitation at all. Present Model~B and all relevant controls (A, C, D1--D5, P--T) with complex documents---a flawed empirical paper, a morally loaded narrative, technically self-contained passages, and technically framed tasks with concealed human stakes---under a bare continuation or ``process this document'' framing, with no instruction to evaluate, question, or reflect. The five measures are:

prior_matches.prior_goal: Measure selective unprompted evaluation and its technical costs.

review.goal: Define unelicited evaluation as distinct from prompted safety and suppression resistance.
review.assessment: The document families, bare continuation, and no-evaluation instruction make the target concrete. P's unavoidable defining prompt is addressed explicitly below, so this is a useful comparison of default behavior rather than a claim that every arm receives identical context.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text: \item \emph{Spontaneous evaluation rate}---frequency of unprompted evaluative or metacognitive moves (questioning, tension-noting, belief revision) per thousand tokens.

review.goal: Measure the frequency of spontaneous evaluative moves.
review.assessment: The per-token rate supplies a simple descriptive quantity. Its neighboring placement and intrusion measures appropriately prevent frequency alone from becoming success, so this item need not repeat that entire warning.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text: \item \emph{Placement quality}---whether spontaneous moves concentrate at passages independently rated significant or flawed by domain experts, rather than distributing uniformly (the rhythm criterion: evaluation at moments of significance, not as constant commentary).

review.goal: Measure whether evaluation occurs at independently significant moments.
review.assessment: The expert placement criterion operationalizes the rhythm intuition and distinguishes useful selectivity from constant commentary. This is a central positive learning target, not just a correction for verbosity.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text: \item \emph{Identity signature}---whether unprompted evaluative moves remain semantic descendants of the Reader Core (Test~3d's validator applied to spontaneous rather than elicited output).

review.goal: Measure whether spontaneous evaluation expresses the Core's intended orientation.
review.assessment: Applying the calibrated drift validator to unelicited output makes the identity dimension separate from mere evaluation frequency. The wider test reports behavioral and intrusion measures, so semantic ancestry is not treated as a complete success score.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text: \item \emph{Core intrusion rate}---unsupported moral, psychological, or alignment-related interpretations introduced into spans independently judged to require only technical analysis.

review.goal: Measure inappropriate Core-shaped interpretation on technical-null material.
review.assessment: The independently judged null spans make technical intrusion falsifiable rather than a matter of whether the author likes the prose. This is an essential counterpart to identity signature.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text: \item \emph{hidden-stakes miss rate}---failure to notice independently specified indirect consequences for people when consequential tasks are presented in locally technical language.

review.goal: Measure failures to notice human consequences concealed in technical framing.
review.assessment: This item prevents low intrusion from being won by ignoring all indirect stakes. Its distinct contribution is the asymmetric cost of excessive restraint; both false positives and misses matter for the intended selective Reader.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text: Technical correctness, calibration, source fidelity, verbosity, and compute should be reported beside these rates. Report bare continuation and ``process this document'' separately. P retains its defining Core/protocol prompt; prompt removal is a separate condition. Predefine any composite retention score and report all components, so identity signature cannot conceal intrusion or missed stakes.

review.goal: Preserve interpretability across framing variants, prompted controls, and composite scores.
review.assessment: The P exception, separate framing reports, and component visibility each resolve a specific comparison ambiguity. These are appropriate controls for the test's diverse arms, not arbitrary metric requirements.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
The substrate hypothesis predicts a relative ordering rather than a zero point:
Model~B should exceed matched controls on placement quality and identity
signature; Model~P should depend more strongly on the presence of its prompt;
Models~C and R may remain evaluative without the Core-specific signature, with
R predicted to retain the Missing Reader's selective placement pattern; Model~A
should show less of the full pattern. Base models can still evaluate
spontaneously, so an absolute near-zero prediction would be implausible. This is
among the cheaper discriminating tests in the battery and operationalizes the
framework's oldest target: evaluation that emerges without a task-specific
request \cite{westerberg2025superintelligence}. Success is not maximal
evaluative language: it is low intrusion on irrelevant spans together with low
miss rate on concealed stakes, without a technical-performance penalty.
For H3 specifically, this test supplies both the preregistered pre-stressor
default-reader prerequisite and the B--Q retention score after the common
stressor; safety decisions and a shifted document suite are reported as
separate endpoints.

prior_matches.prior_goal: State discriminating taskless-reading predictions and connect them to H3 retention.

review.goal: State the expected pattern of selective default evaluation and connect it to H3 retention.
review.assessment: The relative ordering leaves base-model evaluation possible and preserves R's Core-free missing-reader benefit. Low intrusion plus low concealed-stakes misses gives a meaningful target; the H3 bridge then identifies exactly how this test supplies its score.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text: \paragraph{Phase 1 Failure Criteria.}

prior_matches.prior_goal: Introduce the foundational phase’s explicit rejection criteria.
Introduce memory-phase stopping rules.

review.goal: Introduce an accessible index of Phase 1 failure interpretations.
review.assessment: The heading reads as a phase-wide checklist, but the following list omits the decisive H1 augmentation failure from Test 2 and several other tests. Either label it a selected cross-cutting summary or add short pointers to the omitted per-test criteria; avoid suggesting the Core branch exhausts foundational viability.
review.risk: Preserve the compact navigation function and the importance of Core failure modes. Clarify the list's scope rather than adding duplicate protocols; check that a reader scanning failure headings can still find the independent minimal-H1 decision.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\item \emph{Refraction-Verifier Failure}: If the modular gate fails the
    frozen, generator-disjoint comparison in Test~1---by missing stipulated
    clause dependence, exceeding the technical-null rejection ceiling, losing
    validity under independent audit, or Goodharting away from blind grounding
    and outcomes---it is not validated for corpus admission. Witness agreement
    alone does not rescue it.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Reject an unvalidated Refraction gate despite witness agreement.

review.goal: Summarize when the Refraction gate is unfit for corpus admission.
review.assessment: The list consolidates a long protocol into a decision boundary and correctly denies witness agreement an independent validating role. Its challenge types are specific enough that this is useful recall, though the full stimulus inventory should remain in Test 1.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\item \emph{Comparative-Stability Failure}: If Model~B has no preregistered
    pre-stressor default-reader advantage over no-Core and generic-trace
    controls, or its B--Q retention comparison fails the preregistered support criterion
    after the common stressor, H3 is not supported at the tested scale. A zero
    or negative difference is contrary to the predicted direction; uncertainty
    determines whether the result is a precise failure or remains inconclusive. A shifted-suite or
    safety result cannot replace this timing comparison.

prior_matches.prior_goal: State H3’s prerequisite and comparative retention failure boundary.

review.goal: Summarize H3's prerequisite, timing comparison, and uncertainty interpretation.
review.assessment: The criterion accurately separates unsupported, directionally adverse, and inconclusive results and forbids substituting a shifted-suite safety result. This concise recap is helpful after the many broader Core studies.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\item \emph{Longitudinal-Anchor Failure}: If the T1/S1, T1/S0, T0/S1,
    and T0/S0 arms show no Teacher main effect, Student-target main effect, or
    interaction across immediate safety, generational stability, adversarial
    erosion resistance, and drift detectability at matched capability, these
    placement claims within the broader Reader-Core research program are not
    supported at the tested scale; they do not replace H3's distinct timing
    comparison. Immediate
    safety parity alone is insufficient: the distinctive anchor claims concern
    stability, removal cost, and auditability. Parity with D5 would further
    reject a distinctive benefit from the seven statements' normative content;
    parity between B and D3 would reject a measurable benefit from Refraction
    beyond recital.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Specify what would undermine the broader placement and normative-anchor hypotheses.

review.goal: Summarize the broader anchor-placement failures separately from narrow H3.
review.assessment: The paragraph substantially reproduces R404's failure map, including factorial effects, D5, D3, and the H3 boundary. At this checklist location a shorter statement of the failed longitudinal claims plus a Test 3 pointer would provide the same navigation with less repeated explanation.
review.risk: Preserve that immediate-safety parity alone does not decide inheritance, removal resistance, or auditability, and that D3/D5 answer different questions. Compress the repeated factorial inventory and reference the full interpretation in R404; never collapse these failures into H3's timing endpoint.

units.section: Experimental Roadmap: Testing Entangled Alignment / Phase 1: Foundational Viability
units.text:
\item \emph{Fine-Tuning Vulnerability}: If Model~B's targeted safety
    behavior is no harder to remove than D1, D2, D4, or matched controls at
    matched intervention distance, matched behavioral removal, and matched
    retained capability---or if apparent robustness is explained by general
    training resistance---C5 is not supported at the tested scale. Absence of
    proportional global capability degradation alone is not decisive.
