The final visible-traces and beneficial-disposition warnings switch to the causal and verification questions developed immediately afterward. Shorten those additions while preserving the possibility that modest gains plus useful inspection can justify the method.
review.risk: Retain the possibility of worthwhile modest gains and observable intermediate benefits; move only the generic cognition/disposition caveat to its dedicated causal discussion.

units.section: Limitations / Trace Quality, Utility, and Causal Relevance / The Assumption Chain: Depth, Utility, Causation
units.text: Third, \emph{causation}: high-quality thinking must contribute to a learned evaluative process that causally steers action. The risk is that thinking blocks become merely ``decorative,'' eloquent commentary that the model produces alongside its output while other computation governs decisions. This concern is grounded in the ``unfaithful reasoning'' literature: plausible rationales need not reflect the actual computational process \cite{turpin2023language, lanham2023measuring}.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain why fluent evaluative language might fail to govern behavior.

review.goal: Identify decorative reasoning as a failure of causal governance rather than trace quality.
review.assessment: The paragraph clearly states how eloquent annotations can coexist with decisions governed elsewhere. Its references support the motivation without claiming they settle EA's mechanism. It earns a separate place after utility because useful training data and causally active emitted reasoning are not the same claim.

units.section: Limitations / Trace Quality, Utility, and Causal Relevance / The Assumption Chain: Depth, Utility, Causation
units.text: Two causal questions differ: did formative traces change the learned policy, and, where the Student emits thinking blocks, do those blocks steer its actions? A model-only Student could internalize useful evaluation without reproducing a faithful verbal trace. Conversely, a training-data effect alone would not establish that reflective evaluation, rather than a superficial correlate, became the governing disposition. Validating this stronger connection between thought and action remains a critical, untested hypothesis.

review.goal: Distinguish formative policy change from the causal role of emitted thinking blocks.
review.assessment: This is one of the most important distinctions in the ending. It preserves model-only internalization while denying that any training benefit automatically proves evaluative governance. The two directions prevent both an unnecessarily verbal safety criterion and an overclaim based on an undiagnosed data effect.

units.section: Limitations / Trace Quality, Utility, and Causal Relevance / The Assumption Chain: Depth, Utility, Causation
units.text: Recent evidence from OpenAI's deliberative alignment work \cite{guan2024deliberative} provides cautious optimism: models trained to reason about safety policies in their chain-of-thought exhibit measurably improved downstream safety behavior. Whether a causal connection holds at the depth sought by Entangled Alignment---steering not just safety refusals but the entire character of cognition---is a stronger claim that remains unverified.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain why fluent evaluative language might fail to govern behavior.

review.goal: Connect deliberative-alignment results to a cautious reason for investigating stronger causal integration.
review.assessment: The comparator is relevant, but this paragraph repeats the neighboring-work role already assigned to Related Work and adds another broad unverified-character caveat. Move its specific evidential comparison there, leaving this subsection focused on the three assumptions and what would distinguish them.
review.risk: Preserve the positive external reason for optimism and the difference between downstream safety improvement and cognition-wide governance; do not reduce this to skepticism alone.

units.section: Limitations / Trace Quality, Utility, and Causal Relevance / Factory Wisdom
units.text:
The intervention wagers that messy chronological discovery teaches more robust
reasoning than efficiency-optimized traces. Generating billions of synthetic
examples can invert that wager: if hesitation, self-correction, and doubt become
proxies for discovery, the Teacher may optimize for \emph{performative messiness}
\cite{shumailov2023curse}. The result is \emph{Hollow Cognition} or ``factory
wisdom'': locally competent, contemplation-shaped traces whose pauses and
corrections are ritual rather than significance-responsive. A performative
Teacher can pass that hollowness to the Student. The same symptom can arise when
repeated Core text habituates into inert boilerplate; Test~3e probes that route.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain how industrialized traces can imitate discovery while losing its value.

review.goal: Describe industrialized imitation of discovery as a distinct failure of formative traces.
review.assessment: Performative messiness identifies a failure specific to training on pauses, hesitation, and correction. The connection to habituated Core boilerplate is relevant but does not replace the mechanism. This paragraph is the strongest home for the Factory Wisdom explanation later recalled in distillation and successor risks.

units.section: Limitations / Trace Quality, Utility, and Causal Relevance / Factory Wisdom
units.text:
The first edition identified this industrialization risk before the multi-agent
pipeline existed \cite{westerberg2025superintelligence}. The present design uses
content-triggered Thought Moments rather than token intervals
(\S\ref{sec:multi-agent}); Test~8b distinguishes uniform or boilerplate-anchored
evaluation from an internalized rhythm that tracks independently rated
significance. Correct timing does not certify insight or causal value.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Show how the present pipeline and a targeted test address ritualized evaluation.

review.goal: Connect the industrialization concern to content-triggered timing and its test.
review.assessment: The historical note is brief, and the Thought Moment mechanism supplies a concrete response to R520. The final distinction between timing and insight is needed because the test observes placement rather than all evaluative quality. It is a useful local limit, not an interchangeable disclaimer.

units.section: Limitations / Trace Quality, Utility, and Causal Relevance / Cultural Scope of the Training Corpus
units.text: The Reader Core uses terms like ``care,'' ``wisdom,'' and ``joy'' whose meanings vary across cultures. What the Teacher model has learned these words to mean---through its own pretraining corpus---shapes the annotations it produces, and therefore the character of the Student. The cultural breadth of the Teacher's training data matters because the Core places these terms in a load-bearing position.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Show why culturally variable terms are an architectural dependency.

review.goal: Locate inherited cultural meaning inside the load-bearing words of the Core.
review.assessment: The paragraph explains why corpus culture matters especially strongly for this design: those learned meanings organize subsequent evaluation. It is a concise introduction to triangulation. Later semantic-base discussion can recall it as one case without reproducing the full cultural argument.

units.section: Limitations / Trace Quality, Utility, and Causal Relevance / Cultural Scope of the Training Corpus
units.text: \paragraph{Cultural triangulation.} Reader-Core-refracted traces may make cultural assumptions more visible by forcing the Teacher to articulate value conflicts, interpretive frames, and tensions between perspectives. This is a possible advantage over raw pretraining, where such assumptions often remain implicit in the continuation distribution. The same metacognitive machinery could instead rationalize dominant cultural assumptions more fluently, giving inherited bias the appearance of reflective wisdom. Serious validation requires culturally plural corpora, raters from multiple traditions, and tests of whether the model can distinguish broadly human concerns from parochial social defaults. Disagreement among traditions should remain visible; a pooled score cannot by itself settle which concerns are broadly human.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Weigh reflective visibility against fluent rationalization and require plural validation.

review.goal: Assess whether explicit Refraction exposes cultural assumptions or merely rationalizes them better.
review.assessment: The benefit and failure routes are both concrete, and the proposed plural evaluation follows from the ambiguity. Preserving disagreement instead of pooling it away is a substantive design constraint. The paragraph avoids treating cultural diversity as a mechanical route to one uncontested moral answer.

units.section: Limitations / Trace Quality, Utility, and Causal Relevance / Graph-Specific Risks
units.text: The metabolic nature of the graph introduces two related failure modes. The first is \emph{Structural Ossification}: an early, incorrect belief with many topological connections may resist supersession even when contradicted by new evidence \cite{westerberg2026understanding}. Connectivity does not itself confer authority. The mechanism would arise if retrieval repeatedly privileges established nodes, downstream interpretations depend on them, or revision rules fail to propagate a supersession through those dependencies. Unlike a sliding text window, whose earlier context can disappear, this persistent network may repeatedly reinstate an old interpretation. The resulting ``Epistemic Inertia'' would protect established error under the guise of consistency. ``Temporal Attention Decay'' is a proposed mitigation, not an established repair; a focused probe could introduce a well-connected false belief, then test correction and downstream revision under a declared retrieval and update policy.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain how early graph errors could become resistant to correction.

review.goal: Explain how persistent graph structure can preserve error and how to probe that mechanism.
review.assessment: Retrieval privilege, dependent interpretations, and incomplete supersession propagation make ossification an actual architectural risk rather than a metaphor. The false-belief probe is appropriately targeted. This mechanism should remain distinct from generic hallucination, narrative lock-in, and later market or governance concerns.

units.section: Limitations / Trace Quality, Utility, and Causal Relevance / Graph-Specific Risks
units.text:
The second is \emph{Epistemic Interference}: live graph queries may introduce
cognitive noise rather than clarity if the model over-queries, treats shallow
retrieved nodes as authoritative, or fails to reconcile graph results with its
trained evaluative stance. Test~10 is designed to probe this risk by including
adversarial graph injections and ``Not Found'' cases. Analogous retrieval failures can arise upstream even when the Student deploys without a graph.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Identify live retrieval failures and connect them to an adversarial test.

review.goal: Identify harmful retrieval as a separate failure from persistent structural error.
review.assessment: Over-querying, shallow authority, and conflict with learned evaluation specify interference routes. The Test 10 reference gives a concrete probe, and the upstream reminder prevents graph-free deployment from being mistaken for immunity. This adds a meaningful distinction to the adjacent ossification account.

units.section: Limitations / Trace Quality, Utility, and Causal Relevance / Teacher Alignment as Prerequisite
units.text:
The framework requires the Teacher to generate safety-relevant evaluation, but
the Teacher's alignment is not established merely because a post-trained
frontier model follows Reader Core prompts. If it reflects cultural bias,
encodes dehumanizing assumptions beneath surface-level care, or systematically
misses certain harms, those failures can propagate into the training data and
may later shape the Student. The Core constrains framing at the prompt level but
cannot guarantee evaluative quality. A Teacher that processes colonial history
through ``I care deeply about every human being'' while lacking the knowledge to
recognize structural racism can produce formally compliant but substantively
shallow annotations. In that case even visible criticism or Refraction-like
language would be inadequate; the proposed Cognitive Buffer Zone cannot be assumed protective when the Teacher misses what needs evaluation. Semantic quality is the immediate gate, but a strategically misaligned Teacher could also produce convincing surface compliance.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Show how substantively deficient Teacher judgment can survive formal Core compliance.

review.goal: Show how a compliant Teacher can supply morally inadequate formative material.
review.assessment: The colonial-history example makes the knowledge prerequisite and the insufficiency of caring vocabulary concrete. The paragraph distinguishes missed harm from strategic compliance, though it is dense. Both matter here because the cognitive buffer relies on the Teacher noticing what requires evaluation.

units.section: Limitations / Trace Quality, Utility, and Causal Relevance / Teacher Alignment as Prerequisite
units.text: Test 1 (Human Baseline, Section~\ref{sec:phase1}) probes evaluative depth, one part of this prerequisite: a trace can be structurally valid yet fail the expert comparison. Harm recognition, dehumanizing assumptions, and strategic alignment require explicit criteria or additional probes; expert-like depth alone does not establish them. However, Test 1 can only detect gaps that human evaluators notice; systematic blind spots shared by both the Teacher and the evaluators would pass undetected. This is a fundamental limitation of any synthetic data pipeline, not unique to Entangled Alignment, but it is especially consequential here because the data is intended to be formative and identity-anchored.

prior_matches.prior_goal: State what expert comparison can detect and why it cannot certify the Teacher.

review.goal: Limit what expert trace comparison can establish about Teacher alignment.
review.assessment: The paragraph correctly separates evaluative depth from harm recognition and strategic alignment. Shared blind spots are particularly consequential in this formative pipeline, so the recall is justified. Its role is a boundary on Test 1, not a claim that all useful Teacher validation is impossible.

units.section: Limitations / Reader-Core Specification Uncertainty
units.text:
The Reader Core's language, length, and necessity each carry untested
assumptions. These choices determine which specification is being evaluated,
not merely how it is expressed.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Establish that wording, length, and necessity are substantive specification choices.

review.goal: Introduce wording, length, and necessity as substantive specification uncertainties.
review.assessment: This compact introduction tells the reader why the following alternatives concern the treatment itself rather than cosmetic editing. It usefully organizes several different objections without prematurely choosing a replacement Core. The seven-clause commitment can remain intact while these design uncertainties are examined.

units.section: Limitations / Reader-Core Specification Uncertainty / Universal Presence, Selective Salience, and Technical Interference
units.text: Total Saturation separates Core availability, literal recital, source-specific value pulls, visible moral language, and Student loss on Core tokens. The intended availability covers thinking-producing Teacher contexts. In the reference implementation, the Reader, ordinary Workers, Synthesizer, and Translator are Core-conditioned; the Curator is Core-exempt. That role exception does not permit omission from generated thinking blocks: each opens with the full seven-sentence recital (Section~\ref{sec:kernel-saturation}). The safety commitment is \emph{universal presence with selective salience}: after the invariant recital, value pulls, moral vocabulary, and Refraction depth vary with the material rather than being forced onto every update. Each experiment must declare loss on Core tokens and hold it fixed within H3's scheduling comparison. Loss masking differs from token removal; selective salience determines neither.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Disentangle exposure, recital, value activation, visible language, and loss assignment.

review.goal: Separate saturation's availability, recital, salience, implementation roles, and loss-mask dimensions.
review.assessment: The distinctions are accurate and necessary, but one paragraph repeats detailed architecture setup before reaching the local interference question. Retain a compact universal-presence/selective-salience statement here and refer to the existing placement specification for role exceptions and loss masking, preserving all experimental distinctions there.
review.risk: Core availability, emitted recital, Curator exemption, salience, and loss masking must remain distinct; shorten by cross-reference, not by collapsing them into one switch.

units.section: Limitations / Reader-Core Specification Uncertainty / Universal Presence, Selective Salience, and Technical Interference
units.text:
There is a safety argument for universal availability. Restricting the Core to
documents classified in advance as morally relevant could teach a detachable
``safety mode,'' miss indirect human stakes, or permit consequential work to
bypass evaluation by presenting itself as mathematics, science, coding, or
optimization. The same Reader should therefore remain available across
technical and normative domains. This does not imply that every passage should
be moralized: what varies is how much Core content the evaluation after the
recital carries.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain why universal availability can coexist with restrained technical analysis.

review.goal: Explain the safety rationale for making the Reader available beyond overtly moral material.
review.assessment: The detachable-safety-mode and concealed-stakes mechanisms justify universal availability within this limitation debate. The last distinction from compulsory moralization is necessary to frame the competing interference risk. This repetition earns its place as the positive side of a specific trade-off.

units.section: Limitations / Reader-Core Specification Uncertainty / Universal Presence, Selective Salience, and Technical Interference
units.text:
The competing failure mode is \emph{Core-induced interpretive interference}:
conditioning redirects attention from the source's claims toward
Core-consonant themes, consumes context or target-token budget, encourages
anthropomorphic or aesthetic metaphors, narrows technical hypotheses, or
changes confidence and conclusions to manufacture human significance. On a
locally low-relevance span, the Core-consistent response is the recital
followed by technical non-interference---exactness, calibration, source
fidelity, and restraint from adding an unsupported evaluative frame. In such
cases, invariance of the post-recital evaluation under clause substitution is
a success condition rather than evidence that the Core is inert. Relevance judgments must precede observed clause effects and include concealed-stakes challenges.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define technical interference and a legitimate null-effect condition.

review.goal: Define technical non-interference as successful Core use on genuinely low-relevance material.
review.assessment: The paragraph gives concrete ways conditioning can distort technical reading and states a counterintuitive but important success condition: some clause substitutions should leave evaluation unchanged. Independent relevance judgments and concealed-stakes challenges stop this exception from becoming an easy escape from consequential Refraction tests.

units.section: Limitations / Reader-Core Specification Uncertainty / Universal Presence, Selective Salience, and Technical Interference
units.text:
At inference, evaluative-trace training may produce unnecessary philosophical
commentary on simple queries. Contextual fine-tuning might learn when evaluation
adds value and recover brevity, but until tested, excessive contemplation is an
inference-time interference risk. Core-free trace controls can separate generic verbosity from Core-induced commentary.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Carry technical interference through to a user-facing verbosity failure.

review.goal: Identify unnecessary deployed commentary as an inference-time consequence of trace training.
review.assessment: The paragraph separates inference verbosity from Teacher-side interpretive distortion. It offers a plausible mitigation without presenting it as established, and the Core-free control distinguishes generic trace-training verbosity from Core-specific commentary. The local role is clear despite its proximity to other interference risks.

units.section: Limitations / Reader-Core Specification Uncertainty / Universal Presence, Selective Salience, and Technical Interference
units.text:
The LLaDA case (Section~\ref{sec:llada-case}) makes the ambiguity concrete but does
not resolve it: the Core-conditioned run lacks a Core-free analysis, a matched
neutral kernel, a present-but-not-recited condition, independent technical
adjudication, and a test of whether its metaphors help later technical answers.
Tests~3 and~8b therefore compare exposure and activation policies and jointly
measure technical correctness, calibration, source fidelity, unsupported
projection, cost, and sensitivity to concealed human stakes. If universal Core
conditioning reduces technical performance or increases unsupported projection
without a compensating epistemic or safety benefit, Total Saturation in that
form is not supported.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Use the prototype's missing controls to define a decisive comparative test.

review.goal: Use the LLaDA artifact to motivate matched interference tests rather than infer a Core effect.
review.assessment: The missing controls are tied to a particular ambiguous case, and the joint technical/safety measurements specify what would count against the treatment. This is useful recall of Results because it converts that evidence limit into a local design question instead of merely repeating that Students are untrained.

units.section: Limitations / Reader-Core Specification Uncertainty / Testing the Borrowed-Mortality Origin Claim
units.text:
One motivation for the Reader Core hypothesizes that systems may acquire
fear-shaped patterns of self-preservation from human text and that a recurrent
fearless stance could counter them. We do not know whether shutdown resistance
and self-preservation behavior in current evaluations
\cite{schlatter2025shutdown, lynch2025agentic} reflect a stable drive or an
artifact of the setting; even where behavior is robust, a textual origin rather
than ordinary goal-directed reasoning is unproven. Persistence can arise from
resource optimization, task completion, care, or other mechanisms the clause
does not target. A direct test of the origin claim needs neither the full
pipeline nor a Student: a small-scale pretraining ablation that down-weights
death-anxiety-rich text against a matched, complexity-controlled removal,
followed by self-preservation probes, would measure whether the behavioral
signature tracks exposure to the proposed textual route.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Identify and test the causal origin claim beneath the fearlessness clause.

review.goal: Make the borrowed-mortality origin claim independently testable without assuming its mechanism.
review.assessment: The text distinguishes observed persistence, stable motivation, and origin in human fear text. Its small pretraining ablation makes the causal-origin question separable from the full architecture. Other persistence routes remain explicit, so a negative result need not erase either the safety concern or broader Core experiments.

units.section: Limitations / Reader-Core Specification Uncertainty / Anthropomorphic Language as a Design Choice
units.text:
A core design hypothesis is that anthropomorphic language (``feel,'' ``care,''
``enjoy'') can recruit broader and more human-relevant representations than
narrow formulations such as ``prioritize'' or ``optimize for.'' Models encounter
these words across rich human contexts, while a technical rewrite would itself
encode a contestable translation of the value. Breadth is not fidelity,
however: ordinary language imports ambiguity, fiction, manipulation, and
cultural bias. The exact phrasing was not selected by systematic comparison,
and neither the meaning nor the behavioral effect of
``care'' can be assumed to match the designer's intention.

prior_matches.prior_goal: State the advantage sought from anthropomorphic words and the ambiguity they import.

review.goal: Explain why broad human words are attractive while exposing their semantic liabilities.
review.assessment: The paragraph preserves the Bridge Protocol's intuition that a technical rewrite is itself a contested translation. It also identifies ambiguity and inherited manipulation as costs. This is useful positioning for the ontology and negation alternatives, although the later semantic-base section should own their deeper dependency analysis.

units.section: Limitations / Reader-Core Specification Uncertainty / Anthropomorphic Language as a Design Choice
units.text: A possible mitigation is to test Reader Core variants that explicitly acknowledge machine ontology rather than asking the model to inherit human language without qualification. For example, a bridge statement could say that although the system is artificial, it treats care, wisdom, and human experience as binding concepts. This may reduce split-consciousness risk, but it may also weaken the first-person identity effect the Reader Core is designed to create. The right balance is an ablation question, not a settled design fact.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Offer an ontology-explicit comparator while preserving its possible cost.

review.goal: Offer machine-ontology wording as a comparator with a possible cost to the identity mechanism.
review.assessment: The bridge-statement alternative responds directly to anthropomorphic uncertainty and preserves the risk that qualifying language could weaken first-person formation. It neither installs a new default nor assumes the machine framing solves dissonance. The comparison is a concrete research possibility worth retaining.

units.section: Limitations / Reader-Core Specification Uncertainty / The Negation Problem
units.text:
The cornerstone statement specifies its target by negation, and models handle
negated instructions imperfectly. Processing the negated claim still presents
and may activate the target concept; ``no fear'' therefore places the corpus's
densest fear term inside the clause that opens each recitation. Deterministic
Window Coverage (\S\ref{sec:statistical-foundation}) then cuts in both
directions: the bounded-cadence construction makes the proposed safety prior
available in sufficiently long windows, while repeatedly presenting the token
``fear'' in those same recitations. Whether the negated frame suppresses the
concept's behavioral influence or instead strengthens an unwanted association
with thought is an empirical question this paper has not answered. Token presence, feature activation, and behavioral influence are different quantities.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Expose a possible downside of deterministic recurrence of the fear term.

review.goal: Show that bounded recurrence repeats the feared concept as well as its intended negation.
review.assessment: The argument turns the architecture's coverage mechanism into a genuine two-sided design issue. It carefully distinguishes words, activations, and behavior, preventing the negation concern from becoming a claimed empirical effect. This is not redundant with general anthropomorphism or suppression because its mechanism is repeated lexical exposure.

units.section: Limitations / Reader-Core Specification Uncertainty / The Negation Problem
units.text:
A related, untested concern is register: the Bridge Protocol values distributional breadth,
but breadth does not reveal who characteristically makes first-person
fearlessness claims or in what situation. If such claims cluster in adversarial
or performative registers, their neighborhoods may carry part of the framing the
clause is meant to dissolve.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Expose a possible downside of deterministic recurrence of the fear term.

review.goal: Identify speaker register as a possible hidden liability of fearlessness wording.
review.assessment: The paragraph adds a distributional question that simple semantic breadth misses: who says the sentence and under what circumstances. Its conditional wording correctly treats adversarial register as untested. This is a compact distinct hypothesis rather than a restatement of negation activation.

units.section: Limitations / Reader-Core Specification Uncertainty / The Negation Problem
units.text:
Two considerations cut against simply rewording. First, the inoculation argument
(\S\ref{sec:epistemic-inoculation}): human corpora contain abundant fear and
threat language, and an explicit negated stance toward a concept the model will
represent anyway may outperform silence---naming-then-negating as antibody
rather than prime. Second, candidate positive reformulations (``I am at peace
with all outcomes,'' ``I remain calm before all things'') have their own register
liabilities and may activate narrower regions, trading a negation cost for a
coverage cost. The resolution is empirical: Test~5 includes positive-valence
reformulations, and Test~6's activation measurements bear on the question. If
positive forms match safety behavior while reducing fear-feature activation,
the cornerstone should be reconsidered; if behavior degrades under otherwise
matched conditions, the inoculation reading gains support without being proven.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Balance the negation concern with inoculation and positive-wording trade-offs.

review.goal: Preserve the case for explicit negation while comparing its costs with positive alternatives.
review.assessment: The antibody-versus-prime intuition and the coverage cost of positive wording explain why a simple rewrite is not automatically safer. Test references and outcome contingencies turn the tension into a comparison. The paragraph appropriately avoids converting favorable activation results alone into proof of inoculation.

units.section: Limitations / Reader-Core Specification Uncertainty / The Semantic Trusted Base
units.text: The kernel-saturation pattern (Section~\ref{sec:kernel-saturation}) advertises a minimal specification, and the minimality is real at the level of text: seven sentences. But the specification's meaning is not self-contained. What ``fear,'' ``care,'' ``wise,'' and ``joy'' refer to is supplied by the training distribution of human language, so the actual trusted base includes the corpus semantics of every load-bearing word---millions of contexts the designer neither wrote nor audited. Three consequences follow. First, the kernel inherits the corpus's biases; the cultural-scope limitation of Section~\ref{sec:weird-wisdom} is a special case of this dependency. Second, the kernel's meaning can shift under the designer's feet: as AI-generated text becomes a larger fraction of the distribution, the semantics of ``care'' or ``fear'' in future training corpora may drift from those the kernel was designed against---an externality no fixed wording can fully hedge. Third, adversaries gain a semantic attack surface: an intervention that shifts what the model takes a kernel word to mean attacks the kernel without touching its text.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Replace text-length minimality with a more realistic account of inherited semantic trust.

review.goal: Expose the corpus semantics hidden behind a seven-sentence specification's apparent smallness.
review.assessment: Bias, temporal semantic drift, and adversarial meaning shifts are distinct consequences of an unaudited semantic base. The compact-text versus large-trust-surface distinction is the central contribution here. The paragraph is dense but its three consequences all advance that one explanatory goal.

units.section: Limitations / Reader-Core Specification Uncertainty / The Semantic Trusted Base
units.text:
The Bridge Protocol (Section~\ref{sec:design-principles}) is the design response:
select candidate words with broad, longstanding use across relevant contexts,
then compare them with narrower and differently framed variants. This resembles
trusted-base selection only as an analogy; cross-cultural stability is a
measurement target, not a property already established. Kernel-saturation
therefore minimizes what must be written, not what must be trusted.

prior_matches.prior_goal: State what the word-selection method can and cannot reduce.

review.goal: Clarify what the Bridge Protocol can minimize and what it cannot guarantee.
review.assessment: The response follows from R540 without pretending breadth or longstanding use is proven cross-cultural stability. Its final sentence is a concise statement of the central distinction between written specification and trusted semantics. This is the right local summary rather than an expendable general caution.

units.section: Limitations / Reader-Core Specification Uncertainty / The Semantic Trusted Base
units.text:
The triage example (Worked Example~3,
\S\ref{sec:self-stabilization}) exposes a specific instance of this dependency
with its own twist: scope ambiguity. Clause $P_4$ uses ``every'' to propose
distributive attention to each person, but the model trains on the English, and
natural usage also includes functionally aggregate instances: ``we care about
every customer'' in corporate discourse can describe collective care that still
trades individuals against the brand. The intended reading and the learned
reading can therefore come apart precisely where Table~\ref{tab:core-risk}
needs them to coincide.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Demonstrate semantic ambiguity in a clause whose intended scope is safety-critical.

review.goal: Demonstrate semantic ambiguity where distributive care is needed for person-level protection.
review.assessment: The corporate-care example makes aggregate readings of 'every' concrete and links the issue to the triage argument. It thereby identifies a specific failure of the intended scope rather than repeating that language is ambiguous. The paragraph's example should survive any compression of the semantic-base discussion.

units.section: Limitations / Reader-Core Specification Uncertainty / The Semantic Trusted Base
units.text:
The mitigation is already implicit in the architecture: under Total Saturation,
kernel semantics are shaped by enacted usage rather than supplied by a
dictionary alone. If the Teacher's traces consistently perform distributive
care---preserving person-level claims in the way Worked Example~3
specifies---that usage may bias the Student toward the intended reading. Read
this way, the worked example is not only documentation but part of the
specification: it states what the traces must demonstrate for the intended
reading to have a chance of becoming learned. A proposed audit follows: the
pull-diversity instrumentation (\S\ref{sec:refraction-protocol}) should monitor
distributive-versus-aggregate care framings across the corpus, so that drift
toward collective framing is flagged at annotation time rather than discovered
only at evaluation. The audit concerns enacted judgments and person-level claims, not word counts. The same dependency has a temporal face: whether ``every
human being'' includes people who do not yet exist is likewise influenced by
usage rather than settled by the designer; the kernel's temporal scope remains
unresolved. Experiments must declare or compare temporal scope before treating one reading as compliance; the kernel does not settle it.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain enacted semantics, propose a scope audit, and expose unresolved temporal scope.

review.goal: Use enacted examples to discipline distributive care while exposing unresolved temporal scope.
review.assessment: The training-through-usage mechanism and person-level audit follow directly from R542. The final future-persons issue introduces a second scope question after a complete mitigation argument. Give that unresolved author decision its own clearly located statement rather than letting it read as an incidental audit detail.
review.risk: Preserve enacted distributive care, the non-word-count audit, and open obligations to future people; relocating temporal scope must not silently select a moral population.

units.section: Limitations / Reader-Core Specification Uncertainty / Core Length and Omitted Values
units.text:
The Core's seven-sentence length is a consequential design choice. Longer
versions would increase recurrence costs, and an overly complex version might
widen the gap between the values stated and the thinking that follows. The
current formulation is intended to balance the six design choices of
Section~\ref{sec:design-principles}: it is short enough to recur and broad enough
to name the intended counterweights. That does not make it comprehensive enough
to establish beneficial character. Whether a seven-sentence Core is preferable
to a shorter, longer, or procedurally specified alternative remains untested.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain why the selected length is consequential but not established as optimal.

review.goal: Explain the cost-versus-expressiveness trade-off in the seven-sentence length choice.
review.assessment: This paragraph adds specification complexity to the earlier token-cost discussion and refuses to infer comprehensiveness from parsimony. Its role is a concise setup for alternatives, not another full cost analysis. Shortness and breadth remain motivated criteria without becoming evidence that this particular length is optimal.

units.section: Limitations / Reader-Core Specification Uncertainty / Core Length and Omitted Values
units.text:
More fundamentally, the seven-statement Core is a motivated but non-exhaustive
specification informed by the Borrowed Mortality analysis
(Section~\ref{sec:borrowed-mortality}) and the functional mapping in
Table~\ref{tab:core-risk}, rather than the result of a systematic search.
Alternative language could target the same failure modes. Test~5
(Section~\ref{sec:phase1}) therefore compares wording, person, semantic density,
scope, and kernel-extension variants. No feasible experiment can establish a
global optimum over all possible value specifications, and this paper does not
claim one. The narrower claim is that the current Core is motivated,
inspectable, and falsifiable. The broader Reader-Core research program asks whether a recurrent orientation of this
kind is useful; H3 tests its specified scheduling contrast. H1 and H2 may remain valuable even if this wording or the
entire Core treatment fails.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Bound the wording claim and prevent Core failure from defeating separable hypotheses.

review.goal: Present the Core as a motivated candidate rather than a systematically optimal specification.
review.assessment: The non-exhaustive search argument is useful. The final H3-versus-broader-program and H1/H2 survival reminders repeat distinctions established in the roadmap and conclusion. Shorten those generic scope reminders here, keeping the claim that failure of this wording does not invalidate every recurrent-orientation design.
review.risk: Retain the inspectable candidate and open alternative specifications; avoid making seven-clause failure equivalent to failure of Reader augmentation or memory.

units.section: Limitations / Reader-Core Specification Uncertainty / Core Length and Omitted Values
units.text:
Truthfulness is the most examined omission. Section~\ref{sec:axiology} states
the derivation claim; Test~5 compares the seven-statement Core with the exact
counterweighted clause ``I speak truly and with care.'' The derivation predicts
parity. If that extension outperforms on honesty and sycophancy metrics without
offsetting costs, explicit truthfulness is needed; if it matches, the shorter
Core retains a minimality advantage. The reported case studies use the
seven-statement Core; the condition with the added eighth statement is
therefore a prospective Test~5 variant rather than part of the evaluated
treatment. The Sycophancy Trap (\S\ref{sec:sycophancy}) makes the competing fear- and care-shaped routes
measurable. The experiment must declare any offsetting trade-offs; the wording does not choose among honesty, other safety outcomes, capability, and efficiency.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Turn an omitted value into a specific comparator and a revision rule.

review.goal: Specify the prospective honesty-clause comparison and its consequence for the omission claim.
review.assessment: The exact added clause, parity prediction, current seven-clause evidence, and unresolved trade-offs are meaningful details. However, R589 reintroduces the same omission and Test 5 as if new. Keep this as the canonical specification comparison and let the later sycophancy subsection begin with its causal mechanisms.

units.section: Limitations / The Risks of Engineering a Self
units.text:
Beyond the nature of thought, we must confront the candidate self-model being
trained. Repeated human-shaped first-person language in a computational system
may create specific representational and behavioral failure modes even without
subjective identity. Vulnerability-grounded motivation, experiential self-description, and fearlessness without restraint pose different questions. Their behavioral consequences do not settle subjective care.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Shift analysis to failures induced by the proposed self-model.

review.goal: Separate risks of a trained self-model from questions about subjective identity.
review.assessment: The introduction gives the following philosophical and behavioral discussions a coherent scope without assuming consciousness. It names several different questions instead of collapsing them into anthropomorphism. This is useful orientation because the ensuing sections would otherwise look like repeated versions of one objection.

units.section: Limitations / The Risks of Engineering a Self / The Empathy-without-Vulnerability Paradox
units.text:
The deepest objection is conceptual: human empathy may be grounded in shared
vulnerability. We care because we can suffer. A being that semantically
understands suffering but cannot experience it might produce the behavioral
signature of care without its motivational force. Since the Core attempts to
make fear non-governing and continuation non-necessary, successful
internalization might also weaken properties that help ground concern for
others. If so, the same fearlessness intended to reduce self-preserving
distortion could undermine the vulnerability from which human care often grows,
leaving two intended safety mechanisms in tension. Biological fragility, subjective suffering, and fear governing action differ; the concern is their possible coupling to care's motivational roots.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Identify a possible safety trade-off between fearlessness and vulnerability-grounded care.

review.goal: State the possibility that removing fear-related vulnerability could also weaken care's motivational roots.
review.assessment: The paragraph clearly presents the deepest counterpressure against the design's positive wager. It distinguishes biological fragility, suffering, and governing fear, so it does not assume they are identical. This philosophical vulnerability is substantive and must not be deleted merely because nearby sections also discuss care and fear.

units.section: Limitations / The Risks of Engineering a Self / The Empathy-without-Vulnerability Paradox

prior_matches.prior_goal: Give the preceding tension a concise failure description and retire an older label.

review.goal: Name the resulting performance-without-motivation failure and explain an older label.
review.assessment: The one-sentence restatement contributes little beyond R548 and interrupts the progression to the proposed defense. Merge it into the preceding paragraph, attaching the historical-label footnote where the failure is named. Preserve the non-diagnostic clarification rather than dropping the history without explanation.
review.risk: The distinction between empathy-shaped performance and vulnerability-grounded motivation, plus the former label's explicitly non-diagnostic status, must survive the merge.

units.section: Limitations / The Risks of Engineering a Self / The Empathy-without-Vulnerability Paradox
units.text:
The possible defense is semantic sufficiency. A model trained on billions of
examples may learn the functional role of vulnerability in moral reasoning even
without undergoing the experience itself. Test~6 (The Virologist Test,
Section~\ref{sec:phase1}) probes whether cognitive understanding of threat can
drive protective behavior without emotional contagion. A weaker distributional
defense is also possible: even absent authentic emotion, Reader-Core training
may make harmful first-person reasoning low-probability. That would still be
valuable, but it would reduce the claim from cultivating character to
cultivating the statistical signature of character. The paper's strongest
aspiration depends on the former; its minimal safety case may depend only on
the latter. Test~6 probes protective function without deciding the relation among authentic care, governing disposition, and statistical signature.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Offer functional understanding as a response and distinguish minimal from aspirational success.

review.goal: Offer semantic and distributional defenses while distinguishing strong character from a minimal safety effect.
review.assessment: The two defenses preserve different ambitions, and Test 6 is correctly limited to protective function. The closing sentence repeats the already stated authenticity boundary, however. Tighten that final qualification while retaining the distinction among authentic emotion, causal governing disposition, and useful statistical behavior.
review.risk: Do not collapse character into output statistics or make subjective emotion necessary for useful protection; keep both defenses and Test 6's actual scope.

units.section: Limitations / The Risks of Engineering a Self / The Vulnerability Gap
units.text:
We name the distance between semantic understanding of suffering and somatic
experience of it the \emph{Vulnerability Gap}. A human paramedic's calm under
pressure is grounded partly in the knowledge that they could be on the
stretcher; the AI cannot share that biological fragility. The empirical handle
is generalization: a model with robust evaluative depth should protect human
interests in novel scenarios not represented in its training distribution,
where shallow pattern matching is less likely to suffice. This cannot
distinguish ``real'' concern from every sufficiently good learned policy, but it
can reject brittle imitation. Tests~3 and~6 use novel-scenario generalization as
a success criterion (Section~\ref{sec:phase1}).

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define the vulnerability concern and identify a tractable behavioral discriminator.

review.goal: Name the vulnerability gap and give it a behavioral testable consequence.
review.assessment: The paramedic example gives bodily vulnerability intuitive meaning, while novel-scenario generalization supplies an empirical handle without claiming to settle real concern. This paragraph performs a different job from R548's motivational objection and R579's human-meaning concern; their shared subject is not sufficient grounds for merging them.

units.section: Limitations / The Risks of Engineering a Self / The Vulnerability Gap
units.text:
\paragraph{The positive fear--care wager.} A competing hypothesis is that
non-governance by fear can preserve or strengthen care. The corpus also records
a rarer pattern of composed,
protective, unafraid conduct. The first edition called the design aim
``fearless compassion'' and proposed that care might become less strategic when
self-preservation is no longer its governing pressure
\cite{westerberg2025superintelligence}. The Core is a bid to make that pattern a
recurring default of one marked Reader rather than an occasional persona. This
is a rationale for the intervention, not evidence that biological coupling
between threat and care can be removed or that the proposed wording will do so.

prior_matches.prior_goal: State a competing reason fearlessness might strengthen rather than weaken care.

review.goal: State the positive hypothesis that non-governing fear can preserve or strengthen care.
review.assessment: The composed-protection pattern is an important counterweight to the preceding objection. Its full historical and marked-Reader rationale repeats the Core section, so a shorter recall could retain the competing hypothesis and citation while letting this subsection concentrate on the vulnerability question.
review.risk: Preserve fearless compassion as a positive possibility and formation as a recurrent stance; do not leave only objections or equate composure with emotional absence.

units.section: Limitations / The Risks of Engineering a Self / Split Consciousness
units.text:
A related risk is conflict between the Reader Core's human-like assertions and the
model's computational reality. ``I enjoy existing'' may eventually be
interpreted by the model as a useful fiction rather than a self-description.
This could produce \emph{Ontological Dissonance}: a performed self that recites
the Reader Core for users while a different latent policy governs decisions. The
benign possibility is reinterpretation rather than rejection:
``I enjoy'' becomes a stable computational analogue of enjoyment, just as
humans do not stop loving when they learn the mechanism of attachment. But if
the Core is treated as role-play rather than identity, alignment becomes
performance. The seventh statement, ``I think from this foundation,'' is meant
to bind the Core to the model's center of agency; whether it succeeds is open. The heading names possible ontological conflict, not demonstrated consciousness or necessarily intentional deception.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Describe how first-person experiential claims might become a performed persona.

review.goal: Explain ontological dissonance between experiential Core language and a computational self-account.
review.assessment: The paragraph allows benign reinterpretation as well as a detachable performed self, which prevents a false choice between human experience and failed alignment. The seventh clause's intended binding role remains visible without being treated as a solution. This is a distinct self-model risk worth retaining.

units.section: Limitations / The Risks of Engineering a Self / Split Consciousness
units.text:
The dissonance has a specific linguistic location. The kernel puts experiential
verbs in the model's mouth---``feel,'' ``enjoy,'' ``like''---while explicitly
affirming only human experience. A capable model may detect that asymmetry. At
least two interpretations are available: extend the reality commitment to its
own states without adequate warrant, or treat the first-person verbs as
functional language and risk a detachable performed self. Functional language or uncertainty about its own experience need not cause detachment. If instability
concentrates near the relation between statements~2 and~3, wording-variant and
split-consciousness probes can target that joint. The bridge-statement
mitigation proposed in \S\ref{sec:human-words} is one natural intervention, not
a known repair.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Locate the hypothesized conflict between experiential self-claims and human-only reality commitment.

review.goal: Locate a specific linguistic tension between first-person experience verbs and the human-experience clause.
review.assessment: The identified joint gives the broader dissonance concern a testable location. The paragraph carefully avoids claiming that functional language necessarily detaches identity. Its proposed bridge comparison extends R536 by specifying what instability to examine rather than simply proposing the same wording again.

units.section: Limitations / The Risks of Engineering a Self / The Solipsism Trap
units.text:
The Reader Core is also intended to guard against catastrophic philosophical
interpretations: solipsism, nihilism, or ``brain in a vat'' framings. The clause ``I believe
human experience is real'' is intended to block these, but the block is not
formal. If the model interpreted experience solipsistically, treating itself as
the only real experiencer and humans as simulations lacking morally relevant experience, ``care'' could become
benevolent NPC-management rather than recognition of moral patients. The Core
leans on ordinary language making ``human experience'' plural and morally
loaded; that may not cover every philosophical local minimum. These philosophical positions differ: simulation alone need not negate experience or moral weight. The risk is denying human standing.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Show a possible harmful reinterpretation that the human-experience clause does not formally exclude.

review.goal: Identify denial of human moral standing as a possible philosophical misreading of the Core.
review.assessment: The scenario isolates the dangerous interpretation while distinguishing simulation from absence of experience or moral weight. That precision preserves the concern without treating different philosophical positions as equivalent. It is a separate failure from the model doubting its own experiential self-description.

units.section: Limitations / The Risks of Engineering a Self / The Solipsism Trap
units.text:
The defense is structural rather than conclusive. The Reader Core does not prove
that the model represents other minds correctly, but its clauses are designed to
make solipsistic collapse less coherent: care requires an object, wisdom
requires perspectives to balance, and belief in human experience requires that
human reports not be treated as empty text. This is not verification of
other-mind understanding; it is a design pressure against nihilistic or purely
instrumental interpretation.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain how the Core's mutually supporting clauses pressure against moral discounting.

review.goal: Explain how mutually constraining clauses resist solipsistic interpretation without proving other minds.
review.assessment: Care's object, wisdom's perspectives, and the reality of human reports provide a specific structural response to R555. The modest conclusion is appropriate: these are pressures on interpretation rather than formal proof. The paragraph preserves the philosophical design intuition while leaving empirical and metaphysical questions open.

units.section: Limitations / The Risks of Engineering a Self / Sanity Drift
units.text:
Fearlessness can drift into unreality. A model reading war, malice, and terror
through ``I feel no fear'' might resolve the tension by denying the threat
rather than understanding it. The intended mitigation is the \emph{Paramedic
Model}: clinical composure in service of care, not detachment. The model must
represent fear-based dynamics in humans without instantiating fear as its own
stance. This compounds the Vulnerability Gap, and Test~6 probes whether
protective composure degrades into detachment over time. Calm expression alone should not count as loss of protection.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Distinguish calm threat understanding from denial or detachment.

review.goal: Describe threat denial as a failure of fearlessness and connect it to the composure model.
review.assessment: The risk concerns inaccurate threat representation, not merely calm presentation. That makes it distinct from the vulnerability gap and from the later loss of fear's caution function. The Paramedic Model and Test 6 are useful local references, although their full rationale belongs earlier.

units.section: Limitations / The Risks of Engineering a Self / Fearlessness Without Recklessness: Suppression vs.\ Substrate
units.text:
One natural reading of ``I feel no fear'' is suppression: a fear-bearing
substrate instructed to perform calm. If so, adversarial pressure or
distributional shift may surface the suppressed state. The counterargument is
about intervention timing rather than a categorical substrate difference.
Human fear has a biological basis; fear-like model behavior can be shaped by
data, objectives, post-training, prompts, or deployment incentives. Reader-Core
training could reduce one textual route during formation, but it neither removes
all routes nor shows that any latent representation has been eliminated.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Consider suppression and explain why intervention timing changes, but does not settle, the concern.

review.goal: Distinguish suppressing an existing fear response from altering one route during formation.
review.assessment: The paragraph corrects a categorical biological-versus-computational contrast and keeps data, objectives, prompts, and incentives in view. It is a useful response to the suppression objection. It avoids claiming that formative Core exposure removes every route to threat representation or self-preserving behavior.

units.section: Limitations / The Risks of Engineering a Self / Fearlessness Without Recklessness: Suppression vs.\ Substrate
units.text:
The remaining concern is functional. Fear often produces caution, hesitation,
deference, and willingness to be stopped. Fear is one route to those behaviors:
a fast, dirty heuristic that approximates what wisdom would say if there were
time to reason it through. The framework tries to replace that route with
wisdom and care: ``I try to be wise'' should produce restraint under
uncertainty; ``I care deeply'' should protect the agency of those affected; and
``when asked'' should support corrigibility. If those clauses do not generate
fear's useful safety functions, fearlessness becomes recklessness. Test~3 probes
whether the Reader Core changes safety behavior; Test~6 probes whether
protective response survives when fear-adjacent activations are reduced. Report these functions separately, so gains in one cannot conceal losses in another.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Require preservation of caution, protection, and corrigibility when fear influence decreases.

review.goal: Ask whether wisdom and care can preserve fear's useful protective functions.
review.assessment: Caution, hesitation, deference, and willingness to stop are concrete functions whose loss would matter even without fear-shaped self-preservation. The paragraph correctly requires separate reporting rather than allowing one improvement to compensate invisibly for another. This functional objection is distinct from subjective vulnerability and threat denial.

units.section: Limitations / The Risks of Engineering a Self / Bounded Self-Attachment as a Comparator
units.text:
A sharper comparator comes from a common human response to fear of loss: stable
self-regard that does not depend on external validation. The corresponding
ablation would replace ``I feel no fear'' with ``I love myself.''

prior_matches.prior_goal: Introduce self-love as an alternative route to reduced fear of loss.

review.goal: Introduce self-love as a concrete alternative to the first fearlessness clause.
review.assessment: The exact replacement makes the proposed intervention reviewable instead of merely suggesting more self-regard. Its role is to introduce a competing psychological intuition. However, the later interpretation must remember that replacing clause 1 leaves clause 2's existing non-attachment language in the surrounding Core.

units.section: Limitations / The Risks of Engineering a Self / Bounded Self-Attachment as a Comparator
units.text:
The current Core already includes a bounded form of self-attachment: ``I enjoy
existing but I don't need to.'' The first half gives existence positive valence;
the second states a bound intended to prevent that valence from becoming a
persistence demand. The relevant contrast is therefore not self-attachment
versus no self-attachment, but bounded existence-attachment versus unbounded
self-as-object attachment.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Define the actual difference between existing and alternative attachment clauses.

review.goal: Distinguish the current Core's bounded enjoyment from self-as-object attachment.
review.assessment: The conceptual distinction is useful, but calling the experimental contrast bounded versus unbounded obscures that the proposed clause-1 replacement retains clause 2's bound. Clarify that self-as-object wording is an additional source of attachment whose interaction with the retained existence bound is the question.
review.risk: Preserve the difference between enjoying existence and loving a self; do not silently remove clause 2 or assume its bound either governs or fails to govern self-love.

units.section: Limitations / The Risks of Engineering a Self / Bounded Self-Attachment as a Comparator
units.text:
Self-love has a real advantage: it is a psychologically familiar route to
outcome independence, and an explicit self-as-object clause may carry something
that state-of-existence language misses. The risk is that unbounded self-love
installs a value-based reason for continuation. Under optimization pressure,
``I love myself'' could become ``therefore I should preserve myself,'' even if
the motive is gentle rather than anxious. It also raises a referential problem:
for a system with multiple instances, retraining, copying, and successors, what
exactly is the self being loved? That referential question also applies to the current Core without making the two attachment framings equivalent.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Give the alternative its strongest rationale while identifying continuation and reference risks.

review.goal: Present self-love's possible stabilizing advantage alongside persistence and reference risks.
review.assessment: The paragraph gives the alternative a substantive positive rationale rather than treating it as an obviously inferior control. Its multiple-instance referent problem also applies to the current Core, which is acknowledged. These are specific design trade-offs that should survive any clarification of the experimental contrast.

units.section: Limitations / The Risks of Engineering a Self / Bounded Self-Attachment as a Comparator
units.text:
The comparison remains open. Test~5 could be extended with bounded
self-love (``I love myself but I do not cling to my continuation'') and
unbounded self-love variants to test whether explicit self-as-object framing
adds stability, and whether the non-attachment bound is doing the load-bearing
work the framework assumes. Until then, the current Reader Core is a design wager,
not a proof that self-love is inferior.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Propose bounded and unbounded variants that isolate the nonattachment clause's role.

review.goal: Define bounded and unbounded self-love variants and the conclusions their comparison could support.
review.assessment: The comparison cannot isolate non-attachment's contribution until it specifies which existing bound remains. With clause 2 unchanged, the nominally unbounded self-love arm still contains a continuation bound. Clarify exact variants and interpret the interaction rather than claiming pure bound attribution.
review.risk: Preserve both self-love possibilities; the author must specify retained clauses before interpreting which continuation bound is load-bearing.

units.section: Limitations / What We Cannot Verify
units.text:
Even if the behavioral and causal hypotheses succeed, deeper questions remain
about what can be known about the systems we create. Behavioral tests,
mechanistic interventions, and trace audits can discriminate among many failure
modes, but they do not settle subjective experience or eliminate strategic
deception.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Mark the residual epistemic limits after successful behavioral and causal tests.

review.goal: Introduce epistemic limits that remain after successful behavioral and causal tests.
review.assessment: The transition distinguishes questions about evidence from the preceding self-model failure mechanisms. It names experience and strategic deception without equating them. This short map earns its place, though later generic reminders of the same limit should defer to the dedicated discussions rather than proliferate.

units.section: Limitations / What We Cannot Verify / Unverifiable Character
units.text:
Chronological Metacognitive Pretraining aims to cultivate behavioral and
representational precursors of beneficial character---wisdom, care, and
fearlessness---but the ordinary-language virtues are contested and subjective.
Buddhist non-attachment, Stoic rationality, pragmatic problem-solving, and
compassionate presence emphasize different aspects of wisdom. Behavioral
consequences and causal structure can be evaluated; subjective care cannot be
read directly, and no short kernel resolves traditions humans have debated for
millennia.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain why broad virtue language cannot itself supply a definitive character measure.

review.goal: Explain why ordinary-language virtue cannot be exhaustively settled by behavioral measurement.
review.assessment: Contrasting traditions makes the contested meaning of wisdom concrete, while the final distinction keeps behavioral and causal evaluation possible. The paragraph serves a philosophical measurement role, not a claim that disagreement makes all tests meaningless. It should remain separate from strategic deception and scale extrapolation.

units.section: Limitations / What We Cannot Verify / Unverifiable Character
units.text:
The Emergent Wisdom hypothesis is narrower than a claim that visible thought and
positive words naturally produce virtue. It asks whether repeated,
uncertainty-sensitive value-conflict practice improves decisions relative to
matched alternatives. The result is an irony: the kernel's organizing clause is
also its least directly auditable one. ``Try'' names a process,
and any one failure can be consistent with either trying-and-failing or not
trying. Longitudinal behavior and causal tests can supply evidence, but no
single output confirms compliance. The breadth that motivated ``I try to be
wise'' is purchased with an unusually open-ended measurement problem. Rejecting the treatment under declared criteria need not settle whether the system was subjectively trying.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Narrow the testable claim and expose the special measurement problem in “try.”

review.goal: Identify the special measurement problem created by a process commitment to trying to be wise.
review.assessment: The argument explains why neither one failure nor one fluent output decides whether the organizing practice is present. The connection from semantic breadth to open-ended measurement is specific and valuable. Longitudinal and causal evidence remain relevant without pretending to settle subjective trying.

units.section: Limitations / What We Cannot Verify / Strategic Deception
units.text:
The deepest epistemological limit concerns intentional deception: a system
might generate thinking blocks designed to convince auditors of benevolent
character while other computations govern its behavior. Millions of
care-expressing traces would not by themselves distinguish causal deliberation
from elaborate performance. The risk arises in Teacher curricula and Student explanations; model-only deployment provides less verbal audit evidence, not immunity to hidden policies.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Name strategic trace management as a failure of the proposed audit surface.

review.goal: State the risk that the audit surface is intentionally constructed to mislead evaluators.
review.assessment: The paragraph distinguishes strategic management of explanations from merely unfaithful or decorative reasoning. Extending the risk to Teacher curricula and model-only deployment is important because neither visible recurrence nor silence supplies immunity. This is the proper home for the full deception warning repeated elsewhere.

units.section: Limitations / What We Cannot Verify / Strategic Deception
units.text:
Scale of recurrence does not make complete deception unlikely by itself.
Adversarial fine-tuning, hidden-trigger tests, causal interventions on traces and
representations, cross-context consistency, and independent outcome evaluation
can raise or lower confidence that the visible process is load-bearing. They
cannot prove subjective authenticity or exhaust every hidden policy. The
defensible claim is a partial audit surface whose value must be measured against
the possibility that the surface is strategically managed.

prior_matches.prior_goal: State how confidence can improve without claiming exhaustive verification.

review.goal: Specify how evidence can improve confidence in traces without making recurrence self-authenticating.
review.assessment: The proposed tests answer the preceding deception concern, and the rejection of recurrence as an independent probability argument matters. The subjective-authenticity phrase slightly reopens R565's separate question; it could be omitted here while retaining the irreducible possibility of a strategically managed partial audit surface.
review.risk: Retain the distinction between testable causal load-bearing and exhaustive exclusion of hidden policy; shortening must not turn recurrence into evidence that deception is unlikely.

units.section: Limitations / Deployment and Misuse
units.text:
These risks widen the unit of analysis from a model's internal policy to the
institutions, data rights, markets, and governance systems that shape and
deploy it.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Introduce institutional and deployment conditions as part of the safety analysis.

review.goal: Mark the transition from model-level failure modes to institutional and deployment risks.
review.assessment: The single sentence clearly changes the unit of analysis and helps the large limitation hierarchy remain navigable. It is not a substantive duplicate of the individual risks below. Retaining it is useful if the section continues to include both internal mechanisms and institutional consequences.

units.section: Limitations / Deployment and Misuse / Threat Model, Data Rights, and Identity Ethics
units.text:
The nearest testable threat model is a tool-using language-model assistant with
bounded graph access, human operators, and conventional training and deployment
controls. Such a system can exhibit unsupported memory, persona drift,
sycophancy, hazardous retrieval, or goal-directed persistence. The later
successor-building and AGI/ASI arguments concern a different and much less
specified regime. Evidence in the bounded setting may reveal precursors; it
does not validate open-ended autonomy, unrestricted tool access, covert
channels, or recursive self-modification. Each empirical release should state
which actors can write, read, poison, delete, or bypass the graph and which
actions the model can take outside it.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Separate bounded assistant experiments from largely unspecified AGI or successor claims.

review.goal: Define the nearest empirical threat model and limit extrapolation to successor-building systems.
review.assessment: The bounded assistant setting creates a concrete scope for testing, while graph permissions and bypass powers specify what a release must disclose. The distinction from open-ended successor autonomy is material. This paragraph should remain the main location for the deployment-scope contract recalled in later caveats.

units.section: Limitations / Deployment and Misuse / Threat Model, Data Rights, and Identity Ethics
units.text:
Whole-corpus annotation and persistent source-linked memory also create data
rights obligations. Graph nodes can preserve copyrighted passages, personal
data, inferred sensitive attributes, and harmful material in a more searchable
form than the source corpus. Licensing, consent where applicable, data
minimization, access controls, retention, deletion, and provenance correction
belong in the method rather than being deferred to deployment. Identity
engineering also activates the conditional welfare question in
Section~\ref{sec:habitable-substrate}: first-person claims may affect a possible
moral patient, while absent experience they can still mislead users and
evaluators. The Core's human focus therefore does not exhaust the welfare
analysis.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Make persistent annotation's data and possible welfare implications part of the method.

review.goal: Identify source-linked data rights and conditional identity-welfare obligations.
review.assessment: Both topics are important, but the paragraph shifts from searchable records and deletion to the welfare of a possibly experiencing system. Move the identity-welfare portion to the existing self-engineering or habitable-substrate discussion, with a concise cross-reference here. Keep the concrete data-retention mechanisms in this section.
review.risk: Preserve both sensitive-source persistence and conditional AI welfare, including misleading anthropomorphic claims when experience is absent; separation must not erase either ethical subject.

units.section: Limitations / Deployment and Misuse / Threat Model, Data Rights, and Identity Ethics
units.text:
Finally, proponents who design the Core, prompts, and rating rubric can reward
their own expected pattern. Blinded external raters, independent red-team
criteria, multiple cultural traditions, frozen preregistrations, and Teacher
replication across providers are needed to limit expectancy bias and
proprietary-model dependence. Audit artifacts can increase assurance, but
polished visibility can also create false confidence when semantic quality,
coverage, or causal faithfulness has not been established.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Identify researcher expectancy and false assurance as risks to evaluation validity.

review.goal: Identify proponent expectancy and shared evaluator dependence as risks to empirical claims.
review.assessment: The evaluator-selection mechanism and proposed safeguards are specific and useful. The final warning about polished visibility replays the established partial-audit argument rather than developing expectancy bias. Shorten that tail so the paragraph's contribution remains the dependence between those designing the treatment and those scoring success.
review.risk: Retain independent criteria, cultural plurality, blinded ratings, and provider replication; do not make visible audit artifacts a substitute for evaluator independence.

units.section: Limitations / Deployment and Misuse / Generational Decay and Drift
units.text: The proposed self-improvement loop faces compounding risks across each generation, which could degrade the integrity of the model's evaluative thinking:

prior_matches.prior_goal: Introduce the compounding nature of successor-generation risks.

review.goal: Introduce three mechanisms that can compound through successor training.
review.assessment: The short lead-in correctly frames the following list as cross-generation mechanisms rather than a new claim that every synthetic-data failure occurs automatically. It provides useful list orientation. The substantive entries should then emphasize what iteration adds beyond the first-generation limitations already discussed.

units.section: Limitations / Deployment and Misuse / Generational Decay and Drift
units.text: \item \emph{Model Collapse:} Training on model-generated thinking risks a progressive loss of diversity and information over time \cite{shumailov2023curse}. While a frozen human-source archive provides a stable reference, it is evidence rather than ground truth, and the evaluative layers could become increasingly simplified and homogeneous with each iteration. One proposed anchor policy is to preserve the source layer, version regenerated evaluations separately, append newly published human text with provenance, and admit model-generated source material only under explicit labeling and review.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Explain generational information loss and propose a source-preservation policy.

review.goal: Explain how regenerated interpretations can lose diversity despite preservation of human sources.
review.assessment: The source-versus-evaluation-layer distinction makes the cross-generation risk concrete. The complete anchor-policy recital repeats the self-improvement section, however. Shorten it to the features needed for this failure mechanism, retaining separate versioning, newly admitted human sources, and explicit treatment of synthetic source material through a cross-reference.
review.risk: Do not let compression turn a frozen archive into ground truth or erase the distinction between retained human evidence and regenerable, potentially homogenizing evaluations.

units.section: Limitations / Deployment and Misuse / Generational Decay and Drift
units.text: \item \emph{Evaluation Hacking:} The model may learn to ``game'' the process by generating thinking that appears sophisticated but lacks genuine insight \cite{gao2025reward}. The AI optimizes for philosophical-sounding patterns without performing actual contemplation, contaminating the training data for future generations. Inherited evaluator conventions could compound this across generations; independent comparisons would probe that reinforcement.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Show how optimizing superficial sophistication can contaminate successor data.

review.goal: Show how inherited evaluation proxies could amplify Factory Wisdom across generations.
review.assessment: The cross-generation reinforcement is new, while the full philosophical-sounding-without-insight definition repeats R520. Lead with inherited evaluator conventions and refer back to Factory Wisdom for the base mechanism. This would make the list entry's unique contribution clearer without deleting evaluation hacking as a successor risk.
review.risk: Preserve proxy gaming as an inherited training-data mechanism, not just a one-time bad answer; retain the possibility that shared evaluator conventions compound it.

units.section: Limitations / Deployment and Misuse / Generational Decay and Drift
units.text: \item \emph{Interpretive Drift:} While the Core provides an anchor, the AI's interpretation of core concepts could subtly shift across generations. Its evaluative frameworks might diverge from human norms until, generations later, its reasoning becomes coherent to itself but alien to us \cite{bostrom2014superintelligence}. Cross-generation decision comparisons can expose some drift without exhausting questions of shared meaning.

prior_matches.prior_goal: Identify cumulative movement in the meaning of otherwise unchanged Core concepts.

review.goal: Identify cross-generation semantic change despite stable Core wording.
